title: `Vec.extend_from_slice` and the `try_` writers (`try_push`, `try_insert`, `try_reserve`, `try_resize`, `try_extend_from_slice`) borrow their receiver shared in MIR: auto-par runs appends to one buffer as concurrent tasks (the proto3 encoder of fixtures/protobuf_proto/proto_map_field_roundtrip crashes or decodes out of bounds in 56 of 9,000 runs on three workers), and `karac check` lets a `ref` parameter be appended to.
detail: MEASURED by the kata thread's corpus sweep (mir-llvm default vs KARAC_THREADS=1 KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0): proto_map_field_roundtrip failed once with `runtime error: index out of bounds at source.kara:20:16` (Doc.decode(d.encode())). KARAC_AUTO_PAR_DEBUG showed `statements as tasks: Doc.encode@11`; KARAC_MIR_DUMP showed each task capturing `ref Vec[u8]` out and calling `Vec[u8].extend_from_slice(&(*(*_1).0), ..)`, a shared borrow, where push takes `&mut`. The MIR receiver mode for a native method comes from crate::ast::is_mutating_collection_method plus a short list (src/mir/lower.rs), and extend_from_slice and the try_ forms were in neither. A built binary at default settings, three concurrent loops of 3,000 runs each under load: 56 failures (index out of bounds, segfaults, one abort); built with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0: 0 of 9,000; the auto-par binary at KARAC_THREADS=1: 0 of 9,000. Separately, check: `fn add(v: ref Vec[i64], w: ref Vec[i64]) { v.extend_from_slice(w); }` was accepted (core_ref_write's MUTATING_BUILTINS lacks it too), while `v.push(1)` is refused.

fix: bdf62fdac0 makes borrowck's liveness linear in practice: gen/kill bit sets per block and a fixpoint over the blocks in postorder (src/mir/borrowck.rs liveness_with, postorder), where it had iterated Vec<Local> sets in reverse block order. On mini_inflect's new_tab (26,420 blocks over 1,700 locals once auto-par adds its tasks) the old order took 491 rounds to settle and postorder takes 3. Measured on this container, release karac with llvm: compile_mir 49.5 s -> 1.4 s on the auto-par build; `karac build` of corpus/apps/cli/mini_inflect 15.4 s wall, output identical to expected.out. Of several named holders in a live set, borrow_errors now names the one declared last, so the diagnostics are independent of set order (core_strict_check 401/401). The rest of the auto-par build cost (opt + emission over the doubled bodies of the in-order twins) is a different cause, filed as its own row.
title: An auto-par build (the default) of apps/cli/mini_inflect (6,994 lines) takes 84 s against 9.5 s with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0: compile_mir (MIR to LLVM IR) 61.8 s against 0.38 s, for 365,133 LLVM instructions against 177,690; the binaries run alike (0.08 s, same output).
detail: MEASURED by the kata thread's corpus sweep (review thread, 2026-10-28; mir-llvm default vs KARAC_THREADS=1 KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, release karac at c336ac98fa plus a9f56911ac): mini_inflect timed out at 60 s by default and passed in 10 s sequential, the one sweep difference not explained by B-2026-10-28-4/-5. Reproduced: `karac __mir-llvm-run` 82.5 s default, 84.9 s KARAC_THREADS=1, 9.6 s KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0; `karac build` 83.6 s vs 9.5 s. KARAC_MIR_TIME=1 on the auto-par build: compile_mir 61784 ms, opt + emission (4 units) 16809 ms, finish_build 1262 ms (838 bodies) + 548 ms (401 bodies); with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0: opt + emission 6029 ms, compile_mir 383 ms, finish_build 455 ms (404 bodies). So the doubled body count (the in-order twins of B-2026-10-26-17 and the task closures) doubles the instructions, but compile_mir grows 160x: something in the MIR-to-LLVM translation is superlinear in what auto-par adds. Not bisected; the measurements ran beside a background gate on a 4-core container. ADR-2's build-time bar (geomean <= 1.5x, none > 2x) was met before threads and auto-par went default-on.

fix: 71d0bd3bdf: STDLIB_PROGRAMS parses each baked source at its own prelude::stdlib_span_base(i) (usize::MAX/2 + i<<24, above the gated modules' range) instead of offset 0, so the default bodies desugar copies from a baked trait into an impl type their expressions under spans past any program's text. tests/baked_stdlib_span_base.rs pins benches 86 partition_list and 165 compare_version through `karac check`, and asserts no expression type lands in a 64 KiB comment prefix of a program with a user `impl Hasher` (after desugar). Control at b2f2ba9ccb: the two bench tests and the overlap test fail; with the fix 3 passed. The impl-order remainder (copies of one default body sharing spans across impls) is B-2026-10-28-9.
title: `karac check` refuses correct programs at offset-specific places: the baked stdlib (STDLIB_PROGRAMS, e.g. hash.kara) is parsed at offset 0, so a trait default body desugar copies into an impl records expression types under spans that collide with the user's expressions; frozen benches 86 partition_list and 165 compare_version stopped building at a1e167c756
detail: MEASURED by the kata thread during the ADR-2 re-measure (review thread, 2026-10-28) at main b2f2ba9ccb. Two frozen M2 benches fail `karac build`: katas/1-100/86-partition-list/bench/partition_list (`value 'node' moved here, used again here` on a `shared struct` handle) and katas/101-200/165-compare-version-numbers/bench/compare_version (`cannot move a non-Copy value out of a collection element` at `b[i]` over a Vec[i64], 39:29). Both are correct programs; their non-bench variants check clean. Bisected (git bisect run over 7fad5e51e7..b2f2ba9ccb, debug karac check) to a1e167c756, which appends runtime/stdlib/source/table_hash.kara with `impl Hasher for TableKeyBytes` to every program. The root is older. STDLIB_PROGRAMS parses each baked source with crate::parse (offset 0), unlike GATED_STDLIB_PROGRAMS (gated_span_base). desugar::synthesize_trait_default_methods copies Hasher's default bodies (write_u8 ... write_isize, hash.kara lines 25-34) into the impl with those spans, and the typechecker records `self: TableKeyBytes` at hash.kara's offsets (1276, 1335, 1406, ... len 4). In 165, `b[i]` is at offset 1406 len 4, so use_classifier::core_moves_out_of_place read its type as TableKeyBytes (non-Copy) and recorded a move out of the element. Removing 3 bytes anywhere above it makes the error vanish. Any program can hit this at whatever offsets the baked default bodies occupy, and any user `impl Hasher` (or other baked trait with default bodies) could before a1e167c756. The remainder, two impls of one trait sharing the copied bodies' spans with each other, is B-2026-10-28-9.

fix: 6074183596 and 51711b08d7. The first shrinks the executor that auto-par links, in runtime/src/mir_task.rs. Its maps hash with one multiply (IdHasher) instead of SipHash under RandomState. Cancellation sorts with one small heapsort over (id, index) pairs instead of a stable sort per element type, and cancel_where takes a &dyn Fn. The reactor's park and wait are reached only through REACTOR, which fd_wait sets, so a program with no descriptor wait links neither, nor epoll_ctl / epoll_wait (tests/mir_task_pool_lean.rs pins this). The second replaces std::thread::available_parallelism, which every program calls and which walks cgroups through /proc, with linux_cores: the affinity mask capped by cgroup v2 cpu.max or the v1 cfs quota. Bisected over runtime/src from 7fad5e51e7, threads-on-by-default (72ce9e026c) alone had added 16 KB to the smallest binary. Measured afterwards at 51711b08d7, release karac, over the 520 benches of the 10-28 run: linked size against legacy has geomean 1.194 (it was 1.240 in that run) and max 1.417 (it was 1.51). On the frozen M2 set (517 built) the geomean is also 1.194. two_sum brute force is 474,912 B against 511,928 B, with 400,328 B under KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0. powx-n's bench, which has no task, is 374,840 B against 387,088 B. The remaining ~18% on auto-par binaries is the executor itself (task_run, worker_loop, teardown).

detail:
MEASURED by the shared drop schedule after bdf62fdac0, release karac with llvm on a quiet 4-core container: KARAC_MIR_TIME=1 karac build corpus/apps/cli/mini_inflect/source.kara gives finish_build 838 bodies, 365,077 LLVM instructions in 4 codegen units, opt + emission 7.4 s; with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, 404 bodies and opt + emission 2.7 s. compile_mir itself is 1.4 s. The extra bodies are the one-worker twins of B-2026-10-26-17 (Thread C, 45524985d1) plus the task closures, so the volume, not any one pass, is what costs: a fix shrinks what is emitted twice (Thread C is prototyping a dual-module build, so the twins are optimized apart and emitted once each) or emits the twins only for functions with a parallel site on the hot path. The binaries run alike (0.08 s, same output). Owner: Thread C (twins); the drop schedule has nothing pending in mir_aot.rs, mir/mod.rs or call.rs. UPDATE (Thread C, 94c9eb83dd, min of 3 on this host): in order 7.59 s, twins 20.79 s, dual 20.08 s. KARAC_MIR_TIME=1: finish_build 401/428/404 bodies, compile_mir 2.1 s, opt + emission 7.9 s (parallel, 4 units) beside 12.7 s (in-order, 4 units, both modules at once on 4 cores; alone it is about 2.7 to 5 s). The dual module's in-order module rides a second thread, and a reachable-only variant (19.7 s) was dropped for a static-initialisation bug (B-2026-10-28-1's close), so the lever left is the parallel module's own optimisation cost: about 2.8x the in-order module's for 7% more instructions.

UPDATE (Thread C, 10-29, release karac with llvm on a 4-core container). Single-threaded opt-18 + llc-18 on the KARAC_MIR_LL dumps with the build's pipeline: parallel module 7.4 + 5.9 s, in-order module 6.8 + 4.5 s, so 1.18x, not 2.8x. The largest functions match except `new_tab`: `new_tab#resume` has 51,722 instructions in the parallel module (it spawns 25 tasks: statement auto-par over its independent `let`s) against 42,336 for `new_tab#seq`. Extracted alone (llvm-extract-18), it costs opt 1.76 s + llc 1.89 s against 0.52 + 0.71 s, with MemCpyOpt (34%), DSE (24%) and InstCombine (14%) leading -time-passes. The unit holding it took 9.1 s on a core shared with the other module's units. The unit schedule (src/backend/mir_aot/split.rs, `KARAC_MIR_UNIT_SCHEDULE`) weighs units by cost and gives the costliest a core first, so that unit now runs alone (6.3 to 6.9 s): median build 14.8 to 13.2 s, interleaved. What is left is that one unit. A build cannot go below it while `new_tab` is a coroutine: either the cost gate declines statement auto-par in a function like this one (it runs once, and the binaries run alike in 0.08 s), or the coroutine's resume shrinks. Front end 1.2 s, three finish_builds 1.4 s and compile_mir 1.6 s (0.45 s in order) are the rest. The unit schedule landed in 2da8ab72e2. Next lever (agreed 10-29 by the kata thread, which owns the cost gate, and the drop schedule): the gate admits `new_tab` as designed, and `stmt_tasks` in src/mir/lower.rs (Thread B) spawns every statement of an admitted group, weight-0 ones included; lowering a group as at most about 4 tasks of consecutive chunks would collapse the 25-way resume. The drop schedule looks at the frame layout if the resume is still the long pole after that. UPDATE (drop schedule, 7078626bba): an admitted statement group now runs as at most 4 tasks, its heavy statements shared out in order and the light ones riding along (the kata thread's suggestion). Release, 4 cores, median of 3 interleaved builds: 18.8 s to 17.7 s; new_tab#resume 53,617 to 48,057 instructions (575 switches, 1,046 memcpys). So the task count was not most of it: the resume is the whole of new_tab (about 9,000 calls) as one state machine, every local in the frame, and that shape is what MemCpyOpt and DSE pay for. The lever left is the coroutine shape of a long function with one early group (a join that blocks with work-helping instead of suspending, or only the group's span as the coroutine), a design question for the review thread.

fix:
9a4a2338b8 (with c443cbdc2b) removes both parts on this host. c443cbdc2b starts the pool with the first task beside the root, not with the root, so a program that reaches no site stays one thread, and the main thread runs that task inline until a worker takes it; each worker starts the next before it looks for work, so the main thread pays for one thread's creation, not one per core. The nap's spin length made no difference (4096, 256 and 0 spins within 0.05 ms on either program), so it stays.

The multi-threaded loss on grain_intake was glibc's free: once a second thread exists it takes the arena's lock (an atomic, for a fast bin) for every chunk its seven-deep tcache cannot take, and grain_intake frees about 140,000 chunks (123,373 of them straight from compiled code, callgrind). GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.malloc.tcache_count=4000 alone took it from 11.89 to 10.80 ms at four workers, the same as the pool with no workers started (10.86). 9a4a2338b8 keeps up to 64 freed chunks per 16-byte class (chunks up to 512 bytes) on per-thread lists in the runtime, switched on when the workers start and off on one worker, under any sanitizer (dlsym of __asan_init and the rest) and with KARAC_ALLOC_CACHE=0. karac_alloc_fallible and karac_free_buf use them, and a native build of a program that runs tasks renames its compiled code's malloc and free to karac_malloc / karac_free after the LLVM passes; the in-order module of a dual build keeps libc's.

Four workers, 4-core cloud VM, interleaved medians, before / after (in-order build):
- C's probe (four work() statements as tasks, KARAC_AUTO_PAR_SIZE=0), 401 rounds: 2.079 / 1.785 ms (1.603-1.680).
- apps/pipeline/grain_intake, 201 rounds: 12.18 (lists off 11.46) / 10.24 ms (10.16), ratio 0.99.
- apps/pipeline/milk_collect (the review thread's probe, 0.599 in C's floor run), 201 rounds: 8.71 (lists off 8.30) / 7.78 ms (7.47), ratio 0.96.

Left: the probe's +0.18 ms is one thread creation on the main thread's path, which only a later start would hide, and a later start serialises a coarse site's tasks behind an inline one (no preemption). `karac run` (the JIT) does not rename its compiled code's malloc/free; only the runtime's own allocations use the lists there. Corpus on mir-build over par, stmt-par, taskgroup and apps: 424/424 apps, the five other failures fail the same with KARAC_ALLOC_CACHE=0; mir-llvm-asan and mir-llvm-tsan on stmt-par 37/37 each.
title: A native program that reaches an auto-par site pays a fixed cost for going multi-threaded: about 0.2-0.3 ms per worker to start the pool on a 4-core cloud host (the cost of bare thread creation there), plus multi-threaded malloc, mutex and wake overhead, about 1.5 ms in all on apps/pipeline/grain_intake already at two workers; it grows with the core count
detail: MEASURED by Thread C at 94c9eb83dd's karac, 4-core cloud VM, medians of interleaved rounds. (1) Probe: a main of four `let x = work(1000);` statements, built with KARAC_AUTO_PAR_SIZE=0 so the group runs as tasks (six karac_mir_task calls in the IR), 400 rounds: in-order build 2.374 ms, auto-par at KARAC_THREADS=1 2.316, =2 2.693, =4 3.027. A bare Rust program that spawns and joins three threads with 8 MiB stacks took 2.937 ms against 2.310 ms for none on the same rounds, so the pool's start at four workers (+0.65..0.71 ms) is this host's thread creation (runtime/src/mir_task.rs start_workers: one thread per worker past the first, each taking its own glibc malloc arena). (2) apps/pipeline/grain_intake, 120 rounds: in order 14.76 ms, auto-par at 1/2/3/4 workers 14.70 / 16.34 / 15.88 / 16.11. The loss is already whole at two workers, and under callgrind the four-worker run executes only 2% more instructions (73.7M against 72.2M, of which malloc/_int_malloc/_int_free +1.1M as glibc leaves its single-thread path, mir_task::nap +0.34M), with CPU/wall about 1.06: the time is waiting (thread start, a parked worker's wake at each site, real mutexes on program state), not work. strace -f at four workers: 726 sched_yield from napping workers' spin (POOL_SPINS 4096, a yield every 64), 12 futex. (3) The cost is per program, not per site, and a site cannot see it: grain_intake's sites hold about 4% of its instructions (close_week's group 2.7%, about 120 us a call, which would repay a spawn by itself), so a cost-model refusal at lowering does not fit (B-2026-10-28-14). On a many-core host the start is one thread per core. Candidate directions, none measured: start workers later (once the program has run a while, or when a site's tasks are still queued after the first worker took one), start them off the main thread, or cut the nap spin. Numbers and method in the shared folder at thread-c-patches/b-28-14/notes.md. Owner: the shared drop schedule (runtime/src/mir_task.rs).

fix: FIXED by 14e6159356. src/manifest.rs parses `[package].import` and a dependency entry's `alias`, both validated as identifiers (a keyword or a hyphen is refused), and refuses two `[dependencies]`/`[dev-dependencies]` entries that claim one import name (`kara-data` and `kara_data` without an alias). The module loader (src/cli/build_cmds.rs `dep_import_names`, src/module.rs) registers each dependency under the name the root package writes for it: the root's `alias`, else the dependency's `[package].import`, else its name with `-` mapped to `_`. Two dependencies declaring one `[package].import` are refused there. A dependency that writes a different name for a shared package (its own alias) has those imports renamed to the registered one, in the tree and in the project-mode combiner, which re-parses each file (`ProgramTree::rename_dependency_import`). A local module still hides a dependency of the same import name, and an alias reaches it. Pinned by tests/package_import_names.rs (7 tests: hyphen, import key, alias past a local module, a dependency's own alias, both collision errors, identifier validation); all 7 fail at the parent commit.
title: The manifest keys design.md §4 promises for import names are not implemented: a dependency's `alias = "..."`, the optional `[package].import = "..."`, and the rule that a hyphen in a package name maps to `_` in the import path (`kara-data` is imported from `kara_data`); kara-data's `import data` depends on all three
detail:
MEASURED at 29e3371f72: `grep -n alias src/manifest.rs` finds no dependency `alias` key, and there is no `import` key in `[package]` (an unknown `[package]` key is a warning). design.md §4 Packages and manifests (29e3371f72) states: a hyphenated package name is imported with each `-` as `_`; `[package].import` declares a different import name; a dependent's `alias` overrides both; two dependencies that differ only by `-` against `_` are an error at the manifest. The resolver must match a path's first segment against those import names. Fix shape: parse both keys in src/manifest.rs, compute each dependency's import name there, and have the resolver's dependency lookup use it; pin with a two-package fixture (a hyphenated dependency imported by its mapped name, one with `import`, one with `alias`, and the collision error).

title: `Ok((n, it.map(..).collect()))` and `Some((n, it.map(..).collect()))` pass `karac check` but the MIR build refuses them (an expression whose type does not lower, UnsolvedParam(C)): a `collect` that is a tuple element inside an enum constructor keeps its target type unsolved; in a bare tuple, or directly inside `Ok`, it builds
detail:
Repro (kara-katas apps/cli/mini_pandas, `quantile` returned its frame and the labels):

```
fn labels(qs: Vec[f64]) -> Result[(i64, Vec[String]), String] {
    Ok((qs.len(), qs.iter().map(|q| q.to_string()).collect()))
}

fn main() {
    let qs: Vec[f64] = [0.25, 0.5].to_vec();
    match labels(qs) {
        Ok((n, l)) => println(f"{n} {l}"),
        Err(e) => println(e),
    }
}
```

`karac check` passes (karac at 38befdc4f6). `__mir-run` stops:

```
error[mir]: build: 2:19 in `labels`: an expression whose type does not lower (UnsolvedParam("C")) is not lowered yet
```

Measured variants, same binary:
- `-> Option[(i64, Vec[String])]` with `Some((qs.len(), ...collect()))`: the same error at 2:21.
- `-> (i64, Vec[String])` with the bare tuple `(qs.len(), ...collect())`: builds, prints `2 [0.25, 0.5]`.
- `-> Result[Vec[String], String]` with `Ok(...collect())`: builds.
- `-> Option[Vec[String]]` with `Some(...collect())`: builds.

So the typechecker solves `collect`'s `C` from the return type through the enum constructor and through the tuple separately, but the solution does not reach the MIR builder when both are nested. The workaround in `quantile` binds the `Vec[String]` with a type annotation first.

Expected: prints `2 [0.25, 0.5]`.
fix: cd5a50673e. The checker typed an `Ok` / `Err` / `Some` payload in synthesis mode unless it was one of a few narrow shapes, so a tuple payload holding a bare `collect()` left `collect`'s target `C` unsolved: `karac check` passed and the MIR build met `UnsolvedParam("C")`. A bare tuple worked because the tuple arm already pushes each slot into a bare `collect()` element. On the MIR pipeline the payload slot is now pushed into a tuple literal holding a bare `collect()` at any depth (src/typechecker/exprs.rs, `tuple_literal_has_bare_collect`), and a tuple element that is itself such a tuple takes its slot too, which the nested case `Some(((0..n).collect(), (n, ...collect())))` needed. The row's program prints `2 [0.25, 0.5]`. Pinned by tests/mir_collect_in_payload.rs (Ok, nested Some, Err); on main before the fix it fails with all three `UnsolvedParam("C")` errors. Full gate green (19584 passed, 0 failed).

f59be6dac3 src/mir/concat.rs: `candidate`'s walk from the borrow to the add skips a successor whose block only aborts (terminator Abort, no statement mentioning the taken String), since an abort runs no drop; it still needs exactly one other successor. A program with an isolating group turns a failed check into a call of the panic native (lower.rs `diverge`), so there the edge still stops the pass. Unit test a_checked_right_side_still_appends_in_place (fails without the change). Kata 1006's parse arm built: 1.05 s to 0.13 s, the text-building probe 1.18 s (KARAC_MIR_CONCAT=0) to 0.059 s against Rust's 0.051 s. `karac __mir-run` is unchanged: the interpreter's String.add still copies (23.7 s on the arm).
title: `s = s + (n - x).to_string()` copies `s` on every add, so building a string in a loop is quadratic: the concat pass (src/mir/concat.rs) gives up when a checked operation on the right side (here `n - x`'s overflow test) branches between the borrow of `s` and `String.add`
detail: MEASURED at f03a023547 (release karac, runtime archives rebuilt there). Kata 1006's parse arm writes the expression `n*(n-1)/(n-2)+...` with `text = text + ops[(x - 1) % 4] + (n - x).to_string();`. Built, a program that only builds those texts (1,000 n up to 1000, 200 random n up to 10000, four of 10000) ran in 0.99 s against 0.051 s for the same Rust (`text = text + ops[i] + &(n - x).to_string()`, rustc -O); callgrind: 96% of instructions in memcpy, 74% of them under karac_mir_string_from (79,984 calls, two per iteration), i.e. `String.add` copying the left side. `text = text + x.to_string()` and `let s = (n - x).to_string(); text = text + s` both append in place (no string_from in the IR); only the form whose right side has a checked op between the borrow `_r = &text` and the add copies. Cause: concat.rs `candidate` walks from the borrow to the add through blocks with exactly one successor, and the overflow check's SwitchInt has two, one to an Abort. Proposed fix: skip successors that only abort (an abort runs no drop, the pass's own premise). With it the program runs in 0.059 s (KARAC_MIR_CONCAT=0: 1.18 s), the kata arm 1.05 -> 0.13 s, output unchanged; a unit test pins it (a_checked_right_side_still_appends_in_place, fails without the change). `karac __mir-run` is not changed by it (23.7 s on the arm either way): the interpreter's String.add copies regardless.

title: `if c { a = x } else { b = y }` (an assignment ending each arm, no `;`) gets a correct `;` fix-it for the first arm only, and `karac fix` refuses to apply it: the parser does not recover as if the `;` were there, so the fixed file reports three errors to the original two and the safety check rejects the edit; one arm alone (`if c { a = x }`) is fixed
fix: d9df626fe4. src/parser.rs `expect`: a `;` expected and a `}` found that closes the block records the insertion as before and then parses on as if the `;` were there. The repro reports one `Expected Semicolon` per arm with its insertion and no `else` cascade, and `karac fix` applies both in one run (prints `true false`); the match-arm form now needs one run instead of two. Pinned by tests/missing_semicolon_recovery.rs.

title: `prefix ?? default` on a bare (borrowed) `Option[String]` parameter is refused as "'??' requires an `Option` or a `Result` on the left, found 'ref Option[String]'" with the help "an unwrapped value needs no fallback — drop the '?? ...'", which is wrong advice; the same on `Option[i64]` checks and runs, and `prefix.clone() ?? default` is the fix the message should offer
fix: FIXED by 03e92379b1, with B-2026-10-29-10. A bare `prefix: Option[String]` parameter reads as `ref Option[String]` under D5, and `infer_nil_coalesce` (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs) accepted a `ref` wrapper only when the whole wrapper was `Copy`. Anything else fell to "'??' requires an `Option` or a `Result` on the left" with the help to drop the `??`. A `ref` `Option`/`Result` is now always read as the wrapper. A `Copy` payload is copied out, so `r ?? 0` on a bare `Result[i64, String]` parameter checks and runs, printing what the hand-worked output says. A non-`Copy` payload is refused with "'??' on a borrowed 'Option[String]' would move its 'String' out of the borrow" and a machine-applicable `.clone()`, so `karac fix` writes `prefix.clone() ?? "x".to_string()`. Pinned by tests/mir_nil_coalesce_borrowed.rs, whose refusal test also asserts the old "needs no fallback" help is gone.

title: A function-typed parameter in Rust's spelling, `f: impl Fn(i64) -> i64` or `f: fn(i64) -> i64`, gets only a bare parse error (`Expected RightParen, found LeftParen` at the `(`; `Expected type, found Fn` for `fn`) with no hint that Kāra writes `Fn(i64) -> i64`, and no fix-it, so `karac fix` leaves it
fix: 38876d470b. src/parser/types.rs `fn_type_head` recognises Rust's spellings of a function type: `impl Fn(..)` / `impl FnMut(..)` / `impl FnOnce(..)` get "`impl Fn(..)` is Rust syntax: in Kāra a function type is written `Fn(..) -> T`, with no `impl`" with an edit deleting `impl `; `fn(..)` gets "`fn(..) -> T` is Rust's function-pointer type" with `fn` to `Fn`; `FnMut` / `FnOnce` get the rename to `MutFn` / `OnceFn`. The type then parses as Kāra's, so nothing cascades, and one `karac fix` run repairs a parameter or return type (the row's repro prints 5). A Rust spelling is taken only when its `(` follows. Pinned by tests/rust_fn_type_fix.rs. A `MutFn` parameter written from `impl FnMut` still needs `own` to be called, which the typechecker's own diagnostic says.

title: A closure that passes a captured `String` to `replace`, `replacen`, `split`, `find` or `strip_prefix` on its parameter (`|s| s.replace(old, new)`) is typed as consuming the capture, so it is once-callable and `.map(...)` or any `Fn` slot refuses it; all five take `Str` (strings.md), and `starts_with`, `contains` and `ends_with` with the same capture pass
fix: 80e76392cf. Same fix as B-2026-10-28-28: `builtin_read_only_arg_method` (src/typechecker/closures.rs) knew only `contains` / `starts_with` / `ends_with`; every `String` / `Str` method except `extend` now reads its arguments, so `|s| s.replace(old, new)`, `replacen`, `split`, `find` and `strip_prefix` keep the closure `Fn` and `map` accepts it. Pinned by tests/core_closure_string_method_args.rs (`a_capture_passed_to_replace_keeps_the_closure_fn`, `every_str_argument_method_reads_its_capture`).

title: `s.bytes().collect()` is refused with a message that spells out the rewrite ("iterator adaptors/terminals require an explicit `.iter()` — write `s.bytes().iter().collect(...)`") but the diagnostic carries no fix, so `karac fix` leaves it for a hand edit
fix: FIXED by 803f7ede31. The three sites that refuse an iterator adaptor or terminal on a collection with the "require an explicit `.iter()`" hint (method_user_impl.rs for a fixed Array and for Vec/VecDeque, stdlib_seq.rs for a Slice) now attach the insertion of `.iter()` after the receiver as a machine-applicable fix (`iter_hint_fix`): after a method call's closing paren (`s.bytes()`), or at the end of a place, call or index. The row's repro gains the fix and `karac fix` makes it check. Pinned by tests/iter_hint_fix.rs (Slice from `s.bytes()`, Vec binding, fixed Array, field; fixed file runs on __mir-run). Control arm on 0c8ba8aa7f's src: 0 passed, 1 failed.

title: A borrowed parameter or match binding put in an array literal where an owned `Vec[String]` is wanted (`count([key].to_vec())`, `key` a bare `String` parameter or a `Some(key)` arm on a borrowed `Option[String]`) gets only `expected 'ref Vec[String]', found 'Vec[ref String]'`, with no hint and no fix, while the same through a `Some(ref key)` binding gets borrow_projection_copy's message and a machine-applicable `.clone()` (closed with the parameter's `own` fix, the D5 remedy, rather than `.clone()`)
fix: FIXED by c3fb7ea323. The same change as B-2026-10-29-14: an array literal's `to_vec()` where a `Vec[String]` is wanted checks its elements against `String`, so r3's `count([key].to_vec())` with `key` a bare parameter reports "cannot give away parameter `key`" with the `own` fix, and r1's `Some(key)` arm on a bare `by: Option[String]` reports "cannot give away `key`, bound out of parameter `by`" with `own` on `by`; `karac fix` applies either in one run. The fix is the parameter's `own`, the D5 remedy every other give-away offers, rather than the `.clone()` the row proposed; the message names `.clone()` as the alternative. Pinned by tests/to_vec_give_away_fix.rs.

title: The MIR compiled backend runs kata 5's expand-around-center seq bench 1.22x legacy's instructions and 1.45x its cycles, turning a kata that beat Rust (0.95x) into one that trails it (1.17x rustc -O, 1.28x overflow-checked rustc, 1.43x clang -O3)
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro (6P+12E, macOS), karac 0.1.0-dev.13686+g04628b0eb unless stated. Instruction and cycle counts are exact per-process counters (scripts/pmc.c); every sink matches. The MATCHED pair is one compiler and one lean/full archive pair at dd86e3955 (d216abeade^, the last commit where `karac build` defaulted to legacy and `--mir` also existed), so the legacy-vs-MIR delta there has no archive or commit confound.

bench/expand_around_center.kara, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, sink 500000:

    build                         instructions    cycles
    dd86e3955 legacy              11.284 G        1.33 G
    dd86e3955 --mir               13.799 G        1.93 G   (+22% / +45%)
    04628b0eb (v2 default)        13.799 G        1.81 G

kara-katas bench.sh, seq lane, hyperfine means: kara 327.7 -> 410.7 ms (+25%) against its 2026-07-28 legacy recording, while c 286.5 -> 287.9, rust 345.9 -> 351.3, rust_ovf 324.1 -> 321.2, go 419.9 -> 421.0 stayed flat in the same run. Nothing between the switch and today has moved the instruction count. The par lane carries the same loss (28.7 -> 38.2 ms; rayon 26.4 -> 26.9). Not yet located inside the kernel: the next step is a MIR dump of `expand` (two-index byte compare in a while loop over a String's bytes) against legacy's IR.
fix:
3344983712: an index call whose upper half a loop guard already proved is checked for its sign alone. src/mir/guard_bounds.rs finds `X.index(&(*r), h as usize)` where `r` is a shared reference written at most once, `n` is assigned once by `len` on the same `X`, and walking up through single-predecessor blocks reaches a branch taken only when a flag implying `h <s n` holds (Lt/Gt, copies, `&` of flags, joins that set it), with `h` unwritten in between. codegen (seq.rs checked_elem, `upper_proven`) then emits `h >= 0` instead of `h as usize <u len`, which LLVM drops for a counter it sees stay non-negative, as legacy's `vidx.oob.neg` was. `KARAC_MIR_GUARD_BOUNDS=0` restores the full check.

MEASURED on Linux x86 (this container), kata 5's seq bench, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, cachegrind instructions: 15.03G before -> 12.53G after; legacy (dd86e3955) 12.52G. Output identical. Not re-measured on macOS (the row's cycles column is a Mac number).

Pins: tests/mir_guard_bounds.rs (proved index compares `sge` with the pass on, `ult` with it off; a negative index under the same guard, an index into a different vector, and a counter written after the compare all still panic with "index out of bounds", interpreted and built).

title: The MIR compiled backend runs kata 2's add-two-numbers seq bench 1.15x legacy's instructions and 1.17x its cycles, so kara drops from clang -O3 parity (1.01x) to 1.23x C; CORRECTED 2026-10-31: the cost is refcounting the `shared struct ListNode` on each traversal step, not Vec access
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro (6P+12E, macOS), karac 0.1.0-dev.13686+g04628b0eb unless stated. Instruction and cycle counts are exact per-process counters (scripts/pmc.c); every sink matches. The MATCHED pair is one compiler and one lean/full archive pair at dd86e3955 (d216abeade^, the last commit where `karac build` defaulted to legacy and `--mir` also existed), so the legacy-vs-MIR delta there has no archive or commit confound.

bench/iterative.kara, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, sink 4000000:

    build                         instructions    cycles
    dd86e3955 legacy              21.455 G        2.76 G
    dd86e3955 --mir               24.738 G        3.22 G   (+15% / +17%)
    04628b0eb (v2 default)        24.843 G        3.50 G

Wall clock agrees across three runs: 2026-07-28 legacy kara 698.8 ms vs c 692.2; 2026-10-18 legacy (g4ea06e27b) kara 620.7 vs c 607.8; today kara 730.5 vs c 592.0 (rust 1037.1, go 455.6). Kara still beats rustc -O (0.70x), so the loss is against C and Go only. The kernel is a digit-list add over Vec[i64] with carry, so per-element Vec access/push on the MIR path is the first suspect (cf. the fixed B-2026-10-12-36 / B-2026-10-15-36 family).

CORRECTION 2026-10-31 (drop schedule, Linux x86, cachegrind, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0): legacy 11.33G, MIR 12.31G. malloc/free instructions are identical in both (8.9G), so allocation is not it, and the Vec suspect is refuted: the kernel walks two `shared struct ListNode` lists. Program code alone is legacy main 2.14G vs MIR karac.main 3.16G. MIR's node is 32 B {strong, weak, val, next} and each step `a = n.next` increments the next node's count and decrements the current one's (with the branch to the free chain), on both lists, and each built node pays an init, a dec of the node temp and a dec of the old tail; legacy's 16 B node does none of that in this loop. Fix direction: borrowed traversal (the list roots outlive the loop, so a step through `n.next` can borrow rather than own), i.e. RC elision for a walk under a live root; not a local codegen tweak.

PART LANDED 2026-10-31, 5c91ea5617 (drop schedule): rc_pairs now follows a retain's copy moved into another whole local (`_42 = retain(node); tail = move _42; ...; drop(node)`), so the tail-built list's `tail = node` no longer takes and gives back a count per node. Kata 2's bench on Linux: 12.31G -> 12.16G instructions (karac.main 3.16G -> 3.01G; legacy main 2.14G, malloc/free identical). STILL OPEN, the remainder: each step of the two walked lists does `n = take(a); a = clone(n.next); drop(n)`, one increment and one decrement per node per list, which legacy's uncounted 16 B node never paid. Removing them needs a borrowed-walk analysis: a cursor that starts from a borrowed parameter's list and only advances along `next`, in a loop whose every write goes to nodes made fresh in this body (`tail` here), can borrow instead of own. That is design-sized; per the review thread it waits for after 0.9.0.
fix: 5c91ea5617 (part landed earlier; the rest is under the bar). Re-measured 2026-11-02 by the kata thread on x86 with valgrind callgrind (GRID_BLIND_SPOTS rule 80), karac release at 433a916e3e with its archives rebuilt there, against legacy dd86e3955 built in this container, bench/iterative.kara with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs byte-equal: MIR 11.955G against legacy 11.332G, 1.055x, inside the 1.15x bar the review thread set for these re-bench rows. The 10-31 x86 figures (12.31G, then 12.16G after 5c91ea5617) were cachegrind, which over-counts skipped branches. The remaining 5.5% is the walk the row describes, one increment and one decrement per node per list on `a = n.next`. Removing it needs a borrowed-walk RC elision (a cursor that only advances along `next` under a live root), which is design-sized and not scheduled; a later re-bench that finds kata 2 above the bar should file it as its own row. The M5 cycles figure (1.17x at 04628b0eb) predates 5c91ea5617 and wants a Mac re-run.

title: Kata 4's auto-par binary executes a constant +207M instructions (+37%) whenever it has two or more workers, and two workers buy no speedup at twice the CPU: 6.9 ms at 18 workers against rayon's 4.1 ms and the legacy karac_par_reduce build's 3.9 ms
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro, karac g04628b0eb, which already contains B-2026-10-28-15's pool-start fixes (c443cbdc2b, 9a4a2338b8). bench/binary_search_partition.kara (K=10M independent median calls summed), sink 20019970000000; exact counters via scripts/pmc.c, two reps each:

    KARAC_THREADS   instructions   cycles    hyperfine wall / user
    seq twin         556 M          67 M     16.1 ms / 14.5 ms
    1                556 M          67 M     16.9 ms / 14.7 ms
    2                763 M         128 M     17.0 ms / 28.0 ms
    4                763 M         130 M     10.8 ms / 29.2 ms
    18               770 M         157 M      6.9 ms / 35.8 ms

The extra instructions do not grow with the worker count, so this is not spinning: it is ~20 instructions per loop iteration paid on the parallel path (the in-order module runs at one worker). At two workers the cycles double with no wall gain, so the two threads run at about 0.6x the seq IPC, consistent with a contended shared line (ExecLock's flag or the reduction state). bench.sh par lane: kara 3.9 -> 5.9 ms against its 2026-07-28 karac_par_reduce recording, rayon 4.0 -> 4.1, go-par 5.9 -> 6.2, C pthreads 3.2 -> 3.4. The same kata's seq lane is at parity with legacy (564 M vs 556 M instructions). Kata 1 brute_force (27.6 -> 29.8 ms) and kata 5 (see B-2026-10-28-33) par lanes are within their seq-side losses, so the per-iteration cost shows most on a fine-grained reduction like this one.
fix:
5b6aab2a3c (src/mir/lower.rs, src/mir/counters.rs, src/backend/mir/mod.rs; pinned by tests/mir_auto_par_narrow_run.rs). MEASURED on Linux x86_64 (4 vCPU), cachegrind and wall medians of 15, bench/binary_search_partition.kara:

    build                         instructions   wall, 2 workers   wall, 4 workers
    seq twin                      600 M          50.2 ms (1 worker)
    auto-par before (5f89bbef22)  1,086 M        56.1 ms           41.3 ms
    auto-par after                866 M          43.4 ms           33.9 ms

Cause: the task kept its signed sum as an i128 total plus i128 least and greatest prefix, updated per term (add/adc, two cmp/sbb, four cmovs and stack spills: ~41 instructions per term, two terms per iteration). The task now keeps the run and its prefixes in the sum's own type (a checked add and two compares per term) and folds into an i128 base only when the run would overflow; the join's (total, least, most) is unchanged. The fold path still pinned six registers, so codegen now weighs any switch on a checked operation's overflow flag as taken 1 in 2000 (counters::overflow_tests, KARAC_MIR_COLD_OVERFLOW=0 to compare): 996 M with the narrow run alone, 866 M with the weights. Two workers now beat the in-order build (1.16x) where they lost before.

Not done: the remaining +266 M is the in-order overflow check's own per-term tracking (about 10 per iteration) plus the task's loop costs. One of those costs is filed as B-2026-10-29-50. The macOS screen was not re-run here.

title: Every compute-only binary is about 250 KB larger on the MIR backend: a seq kata binary is 337 KB at g04628b0eb against 85 KB from legacy, and the auto-par one 404 KB
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro (6P+12E, macOS), karac 0.1.0-dev.13686+g04628b0eb unless stated. Instruction and cycle counts are exact per-process counters (scripts/pmc.c); every sink matches. The MATCHED pair is one compiler and one lean/full archive pair at dd86e3955 (d216abeade^, the last commit where `karac build` defaulted to legacy and `--mir` also existed), so the legacy-vs-MIR delta there has no archive or commit confound.

Same source, same lean archive, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0: kata 2 iterative 84,664 B legacy vs 369,784 B --mir at dd86e3955; kata 5 84,760 vs 369,928; kata 4 84,632 vs 369,608. At g04628b0eb the seq builds are 336,648-336,984 B and the auto-par builds 403,848-403,928 B. kara-katas results.json binary_bytes moved +302 KB on every seq row of katas 1, 2, 4 and 5 and +84 KB on the par rows; the comparators are byte-identical. This undoes the 2026-06 lean-floor work (the ~33 KB floor). Not yet attributed to symbols: next step is `nm -size-sort` of a hello-world on both sides to name what the MIR runtime pulls in.

RUNTIME MEMORY moves with it: kata 1's auto-par brute_force and its hash_map build peak at 2.4 MiB RSS against 1.4 / 1.3 MiB on their 2026-07-28 legacy recordings (seq builds of katas 2 and 4 are flat, 1.0 MiB), so the pool's thread stacks and per-thread caches cost about 1 MiB once a program reaches an auto-par site.
fix: 1f4c30c7de. The binary-size half. A MIR compute program linked std's panic hook and DWARF backtrace symbolizer (gimli, addr2line, miniz_oxide, rustc_demangle) because every native it imports reached a Rust panic: the print path (FMT/OUT RefCells and LocalKey::with, Vec growth, std::io::stdout/stderr, OnceLock), run_main's std::thread fallback, the abort report's String/format!/error trace, vec_reserve's expect, karac_mir_exit's std::process::exit, pooled_first's env::var and a cgroup slice index, and on Linux __emutls_get_address, which the executable exports (libgcc_s defines the same symbol), so its HashMap code was a GC root. Now stdout/stderr go through write(2) (fatal::write_all, errno read directly) over a panic-free buffer whose thread-local copies a pthread key frees; main's fallback thread is a pthread; exit is libc's; emutls is Apple-only; and karac_mir_abort_at writes the plain report itself, reaching the full one (panic(msg) text, error trace, log drain, panic handler) through a pointer that only the natives setting those parts store (black_box keeps LTO from calling it directly). Reports stay byte-identical to the interpreter's. Linux x86_64: hello-world 353,064 -> 63,664 B stripped; katas 2, 4, 5 365,944 -> 67,760 B; kata 1 brute_force (auto-par, pool linked) 71,768 B. Pinned by tests/mir_panic_free_floor.rs (no RUST_BACKTRACE note in a print/Vec program or an overflow abort; a formatted panic still reports in full). Full gate green; TSan tests pass against rebuilt TSan archives; corpus mir-build 1015/1020 (the 5 are kata 985 entries with no expected.out on main) and mir-llvm-asan clean after re-running load timeouts alone. NOT verified on macOS, where the row was measured. Remainders filed: a Map/Set program still links the hook (B-2026-10-29-41), and the RSS half (B-2026-10-29-42).

title: Compiling a 40-line kata now takes about 158 ms and 68 MB peak against 92 ms and 24 MB in July, slower and larger than rustc -O on the same program (102 ms, 32 MB), and `karac run` of kata 1's 1.8 ms hash_map program takes 106 ms
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro, kara-katas bench.sh compile rows (hyperfine cold, --prepare rm), compile time / peak RSS, with rustc and clang flat in the same runs:

    kata          2026-07-28 legacy     dd86e3955 legacy   dd86e3955 --mir   g04628b0eb
    1 brute       92.9 ms / 23.9 MB     -                  -                 171.4 / 70.0
    2 iterative   92.0 / 24.1           131.5 / 78.7       172.9 / 94.8      158.1 / 67.8
    4 bsp         96.3 / 24.6           -                  -                 184.4 / 70.1
    5 expand      97.5 / 24.3           137.4 / 78.6       165.6 / 93.6      182.4 / 69.3

So most of the growth predates the MIR switch (legacy itself went 24 -> 79 MB between July and 2026-10-22), the switch added ~30% time and ~20% memory, and the trend since is down (95 -> 68 MB). Kata 3's compile, last recorded 2026-09-08, is flat in time (147 -> 155 ms) but 30 -> 67 MB. The interp lane of kata 1 (`karac run hash_map.kara`) went 41.9 -> 105.9 ms: on v2 that command builds before it runs, so it is this row's compile latency, not interpreter speed.
fix: 6bae6aa8d2 (Thread A). The front-end share: the library prune (`src/mir/library_prune.rs`) kept most of the library for every program. Words in comments counted (a file's header comment is the tail of the item before it), every free function was kept whole and `vec_extend_deque` and its kin named VecDeque/Set/Map/SortedSet/SortedMap, and impls of the built-in Set/SortedSet/SortedMap/VecDeque were kept as impls of a type the library does not define. Comments are now blanked before words are read, a free function over a library type is kept when its name or every such type is reached, and those four collections' impls go with their names. Two holes the over-keeping hid are closed: an imported gated module's words count (std.log, std.path), and a renamed library item (`Json__lib`) is reached by its own name. Kept library pieces on kata 2: 263 -> 165. MEASURED on the cloud box, release `--features llvm`, medians of 9-15 against f7f2075954: kata 2 iterative.kara check 110 -> 79 ms (peak 91 -> 85 MB), build 466 -> 330 ms (129 -> 115 MB); kata 1 `karac run hash_map.kara` 370 -> 222 ms (110 -> 102 MB). Build typecheck 92 -> 54 ms, ownershipcheck 38 -> 14 ms. Verified: corpus and kata `karac check` sweeps identical to the baseline, the full corpus on mir-interp against the control (16936 vs 16938 pass; the one new failure, the renamed-library case, is fixed in the commit; the other is kata 756's 56 s program timing out on the control too), full gate green. What remains is not front end and has its own rows: the build running the front end twice (B-2026-10-31-7) and process startup plus link (B-2026-10-31-8, numbers sent to the drop schedule thread).

title: INVALID (premise refuted): auto-par on kata 1's hash_map two-sum, a 2 ms program, is faster in wall time than its KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 twin (2.66 vs 3.09 ms median over 1500 interleaved runs on 4-core Linux; 1.8 vs 2.1 ms on the M5 Pro) at about 1.6x the CPU, so item 13's wall-time gate is right to accept it; the seq-lane row was cross-lane only because bench.sh built hash_map without KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro, karac g04628b0eb, exact counters via scripts/pmc.c, sink -20 on every build. bench/hash_map.kara: K=10 calls of a one-pass Map[i64, i64] two-sum over N=5000, summed with `for _ in 0..10`.

    build                          instructions   cycles     hyperfine wall (30 runs)
    default (auto-par)             31.18 M        15.27 M    1.8 ms +- 0.1, user 2.0 + sys 2.1 ms
    KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0               26.80 M         7.04 M    2.1 ms +- 0.2, user 1.3 + sys 0.4 ms

The default binary carries karac_mir_task_spawn. The wall difference is inside the noise of a 2 ms process, while the CPU doubles and system time quintuples (thread creation). kata 1's bench.sh documents this approach as seq-only because the legacy runtime's gate declined it ('per-call work too light'), so its seq-lane row is now silently cross-lane. BENCH.md's rule for a wasteful activation is a cost-model fix, not a kata change: ten calls of ~2.7M instructions each should not clear the M4 cost gate (0563970557, M4 item 13). For contrast, the matched pair at dd86e3955 shows the seq path itself is fine: legacy 31.64 M, --mir 32.72 M, today's seq twin 26.94 M.
fix: Measured at 8f3182f638 on a 4-core Linux container: bench/hash_map.kara built by default (auto-par, carries karac_mir_task_spawn) and with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, 1500 runs of each interleaved. Auto-par: median wall 2.66 ms (p25 2.44, p75 2.96), user 3.42 ms, sys 1.00 ms. Sequential: median 3.09 ms (p25 2.77, p75 3.79), user 2.60 ms, sys 0.45 ms. Auto-par is about 14% faster in wall time at about 1.6x the CPU, and the row's own M5 numbers point the same way (1.8 +- 0.1 vs 2.1 +- 0.2 ms). Item 13's cost gate judges by wall time ("none may run slower"), so a minimum-work threshold would make this kata slower by the gate's own measure; no compiler change (review-thread ruling 2026-10-30). The real defect was the kata's bench lane: bench.sh built hash_map without KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, so its seq-lane row ran the auto-par binary. Thread C is giving kata 1's hash_map, and the other seven katas in the same state, a KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 seq lane as part of the x86 feed re-run.

title: A `fold` whose result is the payload of an enum-variant constructor in tail position is refused: in `fn total(v: Vec[i64]) -> Val { Val.I(v.iter().fold(0, |a, x| a.wrapping_add(*x))) }` the fold takes the function's return type `Val` as its accumulator ("expected 'Val', found 'i64'" at the `0`, "no method 'wrapping_add' on type 'Val'"), though `let a = Val.I(..)` and `Some(Val.I(..))` check
fix: FIXED by 62fb839cf8. The expected type published for a generic call (`pending_expected_call_return`, B-2026-08-05-19) is now keyed by the call's span. A non-generic enum's constructor (`Val.I(..)`) never took it, so the first generic call inside its payload did: `fold` seeded its accumulator `B` with the function's return type `Val`. Keyed, only the call being checked takes it; `Some(Val.I(..))`, `let b: Box[i32] = Box { v: 5 }` and `let u: u8 = id(200)` still seed. Pinned by tests/core_expected_type_tails.rs `expected_type_stays_with_a_variant_constructor` (check, __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run). Control: on ffd1d7d49a's src the test fails.

title: An `if` or `match` whose type is known (a function's tail, or a `let` with an annotation) does not pass it into its branches, so `strs.iter().map(|s| s.chars().skip(n).collect()).collect()` in a branch is E0238 "cannot infer type parameter 'C'" for the inner collect, though the same expression checks as the function's tail, after `return`, or as a typed `let`'s whole initializer
fix: FIXED by d2677b5af5. The desugar that gives a map closure's inner `collect()` the element type of the annotation (B-2026-10-14-7, B-2026-10-21-50) now walks every value tail of the annotated value: a block's tail, both branches of an `if` / `if let` and every `match` arm. So a function's return type and a typed `let`'s annotation reach `strs.iter().map(|s| s.chars().skip(n).collect()).collect()` in a branch as they do at the bare tail. Pinned by tests/core_expected_type_tails.rs `expected_type_reaches_branch_tails_of_a_mapped_collect` (the row's repro, the match arm, the typed let, a block and an if-let/else-if/match nest; check, __mir-run and __mir-llvm-run). Control: on ffd1d7d49a's src the test fails.

title: The fix for a Rust closure return type (`|r: i64| -> Vec[String] { ..collect() }`) deletes `-> Vec[String]` and leaves a closure whose body cannot infer (E0238 "cannot infer type parameter 'C'", then "no method 'join' on type parameter 'C'"); when the closure is a `let`'s whole initializer with every parameter typed, the fix could move the type onto the binding as `let row: Fn(i64) -> Vec[String] = |r: i64| ..`, which checks and runs
fix: 0a5d255d8a. src/parser/stmts.rs `move_closure_return_to_binding`: when the closure is the whole initializer of an unannotated one-name `let`, every parameter is typed and the body's tail is a `collect`, `sum` or `product` call, the arrow's fix also writes `: Fn(T..) -> R` onto the binding (the repro becomes `let row: Fn(i64) -> Vec[String] = |r: i64| { .. };` and prints `b,d`). Any other closure keeps the delete-only fix, since its body infers and it may be a `MutFn` or `OnceFn`, which an `Fn` annotation would refuse. Pinned by tests/closure_return_type_fix.rs.

title: The turbofish fix on a `collect::[Vec[String]]()` in the middle of a chain (`"(" + it.collect::[Vec[String]]().join(", ") + ")"`) deletes the type arguments and leaves `no method 'join' on type parameter 'C'`; B-2026-10-24-13 made the fix two-sided only when the call is a `let`'s whole initializer, and a mid-chain call has no binding to move the type to
fix: 0a5d255d8a. src/parser/exprs.rs `reject_method_turbofish`: a turbofish on `collect` / `sum` / `product` whose call is followed by `.` or `?.` (its result is the receiver of a further call) no longer offers the delete; the message says the type cannot be inferred from its use and names the typed `let` to bind it with (`let v: Vec[String] = it.collect();`), at the turbofish. Took the row's second option: hoisting the chain into a fresh `let` would reorder evaluation. `Vec[String].from_iter(..)`, the one spelling that names the type at the call, checks but does not lower (filed as B-2026-10-29-40), so it is not offered either. The pin in tests/turbofish_fix.rs that held the delete for `.collect::<Vec<char>>().len()` is flipped.

title: `let v: Vec[Option[String]] = [None].to_vec();` passes `karac check` but does not build on MIR: `an expression whose type does not lower (Type(UnknownParam("T"))) is not lowered yet`, also as a function's `return [None].to_vec();` with a `Vec[Option[String]]` return type; `let none: Option[String] = None; [none].to_vec()` builds
fix: af7bbf1e39. The receiver `[None]` was synthesized with its nodes typed `Option[T]`, Option's own parameter, and the context-decides step in `check_expr` bound that `T` to `String` and recorded it as the `to_vec` call's own `T`, so check passed with the receiver's nodes and the call's substitutions still naming a parameter of no signature in scope (`UnknownParam("T")`). When the context decides a method call's type (src/typechecker/exprs.rs), the receiver's nodes that still name such a parameter now take what the context bound it to (`refine_foreign_params_under`), the call's recorded substitutions do too, and a parameter the receiver named is no longer recorded as one of the method's. The row's program prints `1` and `1`; `[None, None].to_vec()`, `[None, Some(3)].to_vec()` and `return [None].to_vec()` build, and `Some(None).clone()` into an `Option[Option[String]]`, which built invalid MIR (`field 0 of Option has the wrong type`), runs. Pinned by tests/mir_none_in_a_receiver.rs, which fails on main before the fix with the row's message. A longer chain whose result names none of the receiver's parameters, `[None].iter().map(|x| x.clone()).collect()`, is refused by `karac check` itself ("cannot infer type parameter 'T' ... bind the result with a type annotation"), so check and MIR agree there. Full gate green (9780 + 9844 passed, 0 failed).

title: `for n in v { out.push(n ?? String.new()); }` over a `Vec[Option[String]]` (so `n` is `ref Option[String]`) passes `karac check` and is refused only by the MIR build ("cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place: take a copy with `.clone()`"); check should report it with the `.clone()` fix, and B-2026-10-28-32 is the same `??` on a bare parameter refused by check with the wrong help
fix: FIXED by 03e92379b1. `infer_nil_coalesce` (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs) read a borrowed wrapper only when the whole wrapper was `Copy`, and never asked whether a value-typed operand was a borrowed place, so a bare `for` element `n` over a `Vec[Option[String]]` passed the check that the MIR build refused. It now treats a `ref` `Option`/`Result` and a borrowed place (`core_receiver_is_borrowed`: a `for` view, a field behind a borrow) alike. A `Copy` payload is copied out, as the build already did. A non-`Copy` payload is refused at the operand by `reject_nil_coalesce_out_of_borrow` with "'??' on a borrowed 'Option[String]' would move its 'String' out of the borrow: take a copy with `.clone()` first (core-semantics §3.7)", and a machine-applicable `.clone()` when the wrapper supports it, so `karac fix` writes `n.clone() ?? String.new()`. Checking all 237 corpus programs that use `??` found none newly refused. Pinned by tests/mir_nil_coalesce_borrowed.rs: `nil_coalesce_refuses_a_borrowed_non_copy_payload` (check plus the `karac fix` round trip), `nil_coalesce_runs_on_a_cloned_operand`, and `nil_coalesce_copies_a_copy_payload_out_of_a_borrow`, on every backend. Control arm on the base: 1 passed (the cloned program, which ran before too), 2 failed.

70e887275e src/mir/lower.rs: the `for` lowering recognises `v.iter()` / `v.iter_mut()` (no arguments, after an optional 2-tuple `.enumerate()`) whose object is a `Vec`, and sends it down the direct Vec path, which reads `v` by position in the same order, instead of looping through the library `VecIter.next`. tests/mir_vec_iter_loop.rs pins a plain loop with continue/break, an `iter_mut` loop writing in place, and an enumerated loop and a temporary Vec, each with the built body free of `VecIter`. Probe on 1e7 elements under `karac __mir-run`: 10.0 s to 1.14 s, level with `for w in v` (1.17 s). Corpus subset of 1386 entries on mir-interp: the same 23 failures before and after, none from this change.
title: `for x in v.iter()` over a `Vec` calls the library `VecIter.next` once an element, so in the MIR interpreter it runs 8.5 times slower than `for x in v` over the same Vec
detail: MEASURED at 8b6e8a9088 (release karac). Since 544e1a32ef `v.iter()` returns the library `VecIter` (runtime/stdlib/source/collections.kara), and the `for` lowering in src/mir/lower.rs sends any iterable whose type implements `Iterator` through its own `next`, so the direct Vec path, which reads by position, never sees `v.iter()` or `v.iter_mut()`. Probe, `karac __mir-run`, a sum over 1e7 i64: `for w in v.iter()` 10.0 s, `for w in v` 1.17 s, a while loop over an index 2.6 s, a range loop 1.18 s. Found writing kata 1011, whose arms loop with `.iter()`; mir-llvm inlines `VecIter.next` and is not affected.

fix: 70e887275e (found by bisect, not written for this row). Re-measured on Linux, cachegrind instruction counts at KARAC_THREADS=4, on the bench in corpus/katas/1001-1100/1011-capacity-to-ship-packages-within-d-days/bench/ship_within_days. At the row's 8b6e8a9088, rebuilt here: default build 7,228,445,978, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 build 6,238,725,721, reproducing the row's 7,228M / 6,239M. At 7a4500f1a3: 6,238,689,439 and 6,238,689,462. Bisect over 8b6e8a9088..7a4500f1a3 (rebuilding karac and its lean archive at each step) names 70e887275e, "a `for` over `v.iter()` / `v.iter_mut()` on a Vec reads by position" (B-2026-10-29-11), as the first commit where the default build runs the in-order count. Its parent 024b145747 still ran 7,228M. A program whose candidates are all refused still ships the recording build's MIR, which differs from the in-order build's by the candidates' forwarding blocks; after 70e887275e that costs this bench nothing measurable.
title: Kata 1011's bench built with auto-par on (the default) runs 1.23 times the time and 16% more instructions than with `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0`, though nothing fans out
detail: MEASURED at 8b6e8a9088 (release karac, runtime archives rebuilt there). kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1011-capacity-to-ship-packages-within-d-days/bench: eight interleaved runs, default build median 1.167 s, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` build 0.950 s; `time` user equals real, and `karac query concurrency` reports no loop or statement group fanned out; `KARAC_THREADS=1` still 1.125 s. Cachegrind: 7,228M instructions and 80.9M branch mispredicts against 6,239M and 73.5M. The two `KARAC_MIR_LL` dumps differ only by empty forwarding blocks in `days_needed` and `ship_within_days` (the statement parallel groups' join points) and by main's `collect` lowering, so the extra work is in how the inlined greedy loop is laid out after those blocks, not in a spawn. Owners: auto-par (drop schedule / Thread B).

title: A keyword used as a binding name (`let and = op == "&";`) gets E0003 with a fix renaming the binding to `r#and`, but each use (`if and { .. } else { .. }`) gets the same E0003 with no replacement, so `karac fix` leaves the binding renamed and every use not; the uses also cascade into "'else' is a reserved keyword" at the `else`, and a use inside a closure is reported twice
fix: 9d11090195. src/parser.rs `recover_keyword_as_ident` now records each keyword it recovers as a binding name (`escaped_bindings`); a later use of that keyword as the condition or scrutinee before a `{` (`if and { .. }`) is that binding, so it is retyped and given the same `r#and` edit. One `karac fix` run now leaves a program that checks (the repro prints `false true`), the `else` cascade is gone, and a use inside a closure is reported once. Took the rename-every-use remedy rather than suggesting a plain name. Pinned by tests/keyword_binding_uses_fix.rs.

title: `total([a, b].to_vec())` with `a` and `b` borrowed parameters and `total(ps: Vec[P])` is E0200 "expected 'ref Vec[P]', found 'Vec[ref P]'" with no help and no fix, while the same values pushed one by one (`v.push(a)`) get "cannot give away parameter `a`" with a machine-applicable `own` on the parameter
fix: FIXED by c3fb7ea323. Where a `Vec[E]` (or a borrow of one) is wanted and `[..].to_vec()` has an element naming a bare parameter or a binding out of one, check_expr now checks each element against `E` (`d5_give_away_to_vec`, src/typechecker/exprs.rs), so each such element gets the same "cannot give away parameter `a`" diagnostic and `own` fix as `vec![a, b]` and `v.push(a)`, in place of one `Vec[ref P]` mismatch over the literal. The row's repro reports `a` and `b`, and `karac fix` writes `a: own P, b: own P`; the program then prints 3. Copy elements are unchanged. Pinned by tests/to_vec_give_away_fix.rs. Control arm on 0c8ba8aa7f's src: 0 passed, 1 failed.

title: The MIR backend never ported legacy's partial-unroll hint (`llvm.loop.unroll.count 4` on pure-scalar counted `while` loops, B-2026-07-08-24), so kata 70's Fibonacci recurrence runs 1.58x legacy's instructions; adding the one hint to MIR's IR closes 89% of the gap
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro by the legacy-vs-MIR corpus screen (Kara/mir_screen/, outside both repos: screen.tsv, README.md, kernels/<kata>/). Exact instructions via scripts/pmc.c, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs identical on every variant. 'leg' = karac dd86e3955 legacy backend; 'MIR' = the same karac with --mir or today's g04628b0eb. Attribution is by IR edit: MIR's KARAC_MIR_LL IR through stock LLVM 18 opt default<O2> + llc tracks karac's own build within ~1% on 45 of 48 tail/control sources, so an edit's delta is the mechanism's cost.

bench/climbing_stairs.kara: leg 3.738G, MIR 5.896G (karac) / 5.192G (stock pipeline). Hot loop: legacy unrolled 4x, ~5 instr/iter; MIR 7 instr/iter, not unrolled, with `mov` shuffles the unroll would remove.

    MIR IR as emitted                                  5.192G
    + counter-overflow check removed                   5.192G   (no effect)
    + `!llvm.loop !{unroll.count 4}` on climb's back edge   3.903G   (cycles 606M vs legacy 591M)

Legacy: `while_loop_wants_partial_unroll` (codegen/control_flow_bce.rs, gate: counter bounded in the guard, constant step, scalar-only body) -> `attach_unroll_count_metadata(back_edge, 4)`. MIR ports only the full-unroll hint (src/mir/counters.rs `unroll_full_latches`). Also ruled out: legacy's monotone llvm.assume (switched off, legacy unchanged), MIR's compare-form counter check vs sadd.with.overflow (identical), KARAC_MIR_OPT=3, KARAC_MIR_CODEGEN_UNITS=1.
fix:
FIXED by 721602d810. `counters::unroll_partial_latches` ports legacy's gate to the MIR CFG (innermost loop; guard `i < n` or `i <= n`, any bound; `i` written only at its start and by a constant step >= 1; a body touching only scalar locals) and codegen marks those back edges `llvm.loop.unroll.count 4` when no full-unroll hint applies. `KARAC_MIR_UNROLL_PARTIAL=0` drops only these hints. Pinned by tests/mir_unroll_partial.rs (fires on a `<=` recurrence and a strict runtime bound; not on an element-access loop, a loop with a call, or a <=32-trip constant loop, which keeps unroll.full).

Measured on the M5 (exact instructions, scripts/pmc.c): kata 70 5.89G -> 4.27G, cycles 945M -> 726M (legacy 3.74G). Same-binary A/B over all 341 kara-katas bench sources (Kara/mir_screen/ab_partial.tsv): 0 output mismatches; the hint fires on 8 sources and none regresses (5-run minimums, on/off): #70 0.724, #179 0.783, #89 0.865, #53 0.894, #68 0.983, #248/#140/#139 1.000. The remaining 14% of kata 70's gap is karac's pipeline vs stock opt+llc on this module (3.90G in the IR-edit run).

title: MIR checks the full upper bound on indexes legacy proved in range from the loop guard, and the extra checks push kata 139's 4-trip inner loop over LLVM's peel budget: 2.03x legacy's instructions, 97.8% of it recovered by removing two bounds checks
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro by the legacy-vs-MIR corpus screen (Kara/mir_screen/, outside both repos: screen.tsv, README.md, kernels/<kata>/). Exact instructions via scripts/pmc.c, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs identical on every variant. 'leg' = karac dd86e3955 legacy backend; 'MIR' = the same karac with --mir or today's g04628b0eb. Attribution is by IR edit: MIR's KARAC_MIR_LL IR through stock LLVM 18 opt default<O2> + llc tracks karac's own build within ~1% on 45 of 48 tail/control sources, so an edit's delta is the mechanism's cost.

bench/word_break.kara: leg 2.563G, MIR 5.197G (stock 5.192G). The inner j loop (trip <= 4) is peeled 4x on legacy (pw folds to 1/5/25/125, bounds checks gone) and by 1 on MIR.

    opt -unroll-threshold=400, no edit          3.274G  (peel fires)
    dp[j] upper-bound check forced true         3.017G
    s[off+j] bounds check forced true           2.758G
    both removed                                2.622G  (97.8% of the gap)

Legacy's frontend proved `j <= ii-1 <= win < dp.len` and emitted only `j < 0` (`vidx.oob.neg`); MIR emits `idx <u len` on every Vec index. The s[off+j] check is in legacy's IR too but its O2 removes it; in MIR's IR it survives even when peeled, and legacy-style monotone assumes alone did not remove it (that half's cause is a hypothesis). Anomaly: also removing base[ln]'s check loses the peel again (3.739G).

CORRECTED 2026-10-30: the IR-edit numbers above were measured on KARAC_MIR_LL dumps, which carry no target triple or data layout (karac sets them after the dump, mir_aot::compile_module), so opt used LLVM's default layout and cost model. Re-measured with the real header and -mcpu=apple-m1 (MIR 5.210G as emitted, = karac's own 5.20G): dp[j] check removed 4.759G, s[off+j] removed 4.550G, both removed 2.892G (87% of the gap to legacy's 2.564G), -unroll-threshold=400 3.420G. TRIED AND DROPPED: a MIR non-negativity dataflow (a signed local proved >= 0 through a guard edge, stated as assume(x >= 0) at its `as usize`): under the real target LLVM then rewrites dp[j]'s check onto the pre-decrement phi (j_in <u 26) and folds neither half, and the build is 3% worse (5.22G -> 5.37G); stating `ln >= 0` as well loses the peel, since base[ln]'s `ln <u 5` is the compare LLVM peels to decide. The fix needs the upper halves proved, as legacy did on the AST (bce_length_pin.rs, B-2026-07-17-1): a length pin (dp filled to win + 1, s to n, by counted push loops and never resized) plus linear bounds through the loops (j <= ii - 1 <= win - 1; off = ro % (n - win) with ro >= 0, so off + j < n), eliding the check in MIR rather than hinting LLVM.
fix: 594852a575. src/mir/range_bounds.rs, a forward interval dataflow over the elaborated body, proves the upper half that legacy's bce_length_pin.rs proved on the AST. It follows integer locals whose address is never taken mutably, the exact results of checked operations past their overflow test, and the length of each local vector whose every mention is a new/with_capacity/filled that makes it, a receiver borrow of a call, its Drop or its storage markers (push adds one; index_mut, presize, reserve and a few others keep it; any other &mut call forgets it). It also tracks equalities len(v) = i + c, which is how a push loop's length follows its counter. Loops widen only the slots they write, and only where their back edges push, so a counter the loop does not move keeps the value it entered with; narrowing passes then recover the guards' bounds. An index whose interval ends below the vector's least length joins guard_bounds::upper_proven_indexes, so codegen checks only its sign. KARAC_MIR_RANGE_BOUNDS=0 turns it off. On kata 139 both of the row's sites are proved: dp[j] with j in [0,23] against len 25, and s[off+j] with off+j in [0,4998] against len 5000. base[ln] keeps its check (ln is unbounded), so the row's anomaly does not arise. MEASURED on Linux x86, callgrind, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0: 5.74G instructions with the proof off, 4.10G with it on, and legacy (741fbf08c --legacy) 3.48G, so the ratio goes from 1.65x to 1.18x; output 2602274054 in all three. The whole corpus on mir-build, proof on and off, gives identical pass and fail sets (17648 pass / 881 fail). Compile time is within noise on freight_audit, cumulus and kata 139. Pins: mir::range_bounds unit tests (the six DP indexes proved; a short fill, a pop and a truncating callee are not, and each still panics) and tests/mir_guard_bounds.rs (the IR for the DP has six sign checks and no <u len; with the proof off it has the six <u len checks back; the unfollowed indexes keep <u len and panic built).

title: MIR never ported legacy's binary-search midpoint assume (B-2026-06-16-1) and passes a Slice through memory, so `len` reaches IPSCCP only after inlining: kata 153's search loop runs 14 instructions per iteration against legacy's 9 (1.55x), and the same shape regresses katas 34, 35, 74 and 275
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro by the legacy-vs-MIR corpus screen (Kara/mir_screen/, outside both repos: screen.tsv, README.md, kernels/<kata>/). Exact instructions via scripts/pmc.c, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs identical on every variant. 'leg' = karac dd86e3955 legacy backend; 'MIR' = the same karac with --mir or today's g04628b0eb. Attribution is by IR edit: MIR's KARAC_MIR_LL IR through stock LLVM 18 opt default<O2> + llc tracks karac's own build within ~1% on 45 of 48 tail/control sources, so an edit's delta is the mechanism's cost.

bench/binary_search.kara: leg 423.8M, MIR 657.4M (stock 669.1M). MIR's extra per-iteration checks: the `lo + (hi-lo)/2` overflow check, nums[mid] and nums[hi] bounds checks; plus nums[lo] after the loop.

    A: a second default<O2> on unmodified MIR IR   543.1M (-126M, 54%); `-passes=ipsccp` alone on the once-optimized IR removes 3 of the 4 checks
    B: + legacy's assume(mid >= lo), assume(mid < hi), double O2   454.9M (-88M, 38%; loop = legacy's 9 instr)

Legacy passes the slice by value `{ptr, i64}` and gets hi < len in one O2; MIR calls `kara.find_min(ptr %ret, ptr %arg)` and wraps each overflow flag in alloca/memmove/switch i8 (which of these hides the constant is a hypothesis). Deleting the nums[mid] check WITHOUT the assume is worse (686.9M): LLVM loses mid < len and the csel loop turns into branches. Double O2 across 36 tail sources helps only 8, five of them binary searches (#153 0.83, #34 0.87, #35 0.88, #74 0.92, #275 0.88), so this is the binary-search cluster's mechanism, not a general pipeline fix. Remaining 8-13%: with_capacity+push fill loop not unrolled (hypothesis; it is the whole 18.9M gap of sibling linear_scan).
fix: FIXED by b8ad892458 (2026-10-30). mir::midpoint finds a binary search's midpoint (a `lo < hi` guard, then on its straight line in, `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`, `(hi - lo) / 2 + lo` or `>> 1`, or `(lo + hi) >> 1`, or `(lo + hi) / 2` on an unsigned type; lo and hi not written between) and the backend states `assume(lo <= mid)` and `assume(mid < hi)` right after it, as legacy's B-2026-06-16-1 did. A module that states one runs its default<O2> pipeline twice (`karac.midpoint` named metadata gates it; the facts meet the check only after the search is inlined): the assumes alone change nothing (657M -> 657M on 153), the second run folds the checks. Knobs: KARAC_MIR_MIDPOINT=0, KARAC_MIR_MIDPOINT_REOPT=0. Kata 153 binary_search 657M -> 442M (legacy 424M); same-binary A/B over 341 bench sources: 0 output mismatches, fires on 8, 35 search_insert 0.663, 34 search_range 0.674, 153 0.674, 275 hsearch 0.753, 300 lisscan 0.882; 154, 302, 162 fire within 1%. 34 and 35 now run fewer instructions than legacy. Kata 74 is NOT this mechanism: its search is closed (`lo <= hi`) and indexes `m[mid / cols][mid % cols]`; stating `lo <= mid <= hi` there fired and changed nothing (4.31G either way), so it moved to its own row (B-2026-10-30-36). Pinned by tests/mir_midpoint.rs (signed ranges either side of zero, unsigned, a search past the end that must still panic: negative-controlled, a false `mid > hi` fact makes it run past the end) and src/mir/midpoint.rs's unit tests (the signed `(lo + hi) / 2` of B-2026-08-30-6 and a `lo <= hi` guard are refused).

title: MIR heap-copies every string literal a function returns and builds `a + " " + b` one realloc per operand (copying a dead left operand), where legacy returned a borrowed static and allocated a `+` chain once: kata 273 runs 2.31x legacy's instructions and 2.3x its mallocs
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro by the legacy-vs-MIR corpus screen (Kara/mir_screen/, outside both repos: screen.tsv, README.md, kernels/<kata>/). Exact instructions via scripts/pmc.c, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs identical on every variant. 'leg' = karac dd86e3955 legacy backend; 'MIR' = the same karac with --mir or today's g04628b0eb. Attribution is by IR edit: MIR's KARAC_MIR_LL IR through stock LLVM 18 opt default<O2> + llc tracks karac's own build within ~1% on 45 of 48 tail/control sources, so an edit's delta is the mechanism's cost.

bench/spell_seq.kara: leg 8.325G, MIR 19.223G (stock gap 11.60G); mallocs (DYLD interposer) 12.5M vs 28.5M. The byte-hash loop is identical on both (8 instr/byte); the gap is allocation churn in number_to_words / group_name / *_name.

    1. `return "One"` lowers to `call @karac_mir_string_from` (malloc + copy) on 30 sites; legacy `ret {ptr @str, 3, 0}` (cap 0 = borrowed, drop skips it). Edit to the borrowed aggregate: 19.905G -> 14.644G (45%), mallocs 28.5M -> 19.6M
    2. `t + " " + small_name(r)`, `piece + " " + out`: one push_str -> vec_reserve -> realloc per operand, and `piece` copied by string_from though dead; legacy sums the lengths, mallocs once, memcpys inline. Edit: -> 10.301G (37%), mallocs back to 12.5M (= legacy)
    3. push_str out of line -> inline fast path: -> 9.817G (4%)

13% unexplained (hypotheses: inexact reserve, 24-byte String temporaries via alloca+memmove, recursive group_name not inlined). Related but distinct: B-2026-10-28-30 (s = s + x in a loop), already in the measured build.

PART 1 FIXED by 5e8165275e (2026-10-28): String.from(<literal>) now borrows its static bytes (cap 0) for every destination, not only never-moved locals; KARAC_MIR_BORROW_LITERALS=0 copies. Kata 273 spell_seq 19.97G -> 14.82G (string_from calls in IR 32 -> 1); same-binary A/B over 341 sources: 0 output mismatches, 15 improve > 3%, none regress. STILL OPEN (part 2, ~37% of the original gap): a `+` chain grows one push_str/reserve/realloc per operand and copies a dead left operand with string_from; legacy summed the lengths and allocated once.
fix: FIXED by de113d6d66 (2026-10-29), part 2; part 1 was 5e8165275e. mir::concat now (a) takes a left side that has a drop flag by clearing the flag at the add (kata 273's `piece`, whose flag-guarded drop sat at a join the add did not dominate, so it was copied with string_from), and (b) fuses `(x + a) + b` into one n-ary String.add, which the backend grows once by the summed lengths (a borrowed left allocates once, sized for every operand); KARAC_MIR_CONCAT_FUSE=0 keeps the adds apart. Kata 273 spell_seq: 14.82G -> 10.35G instructions (19.97G before part 1; legacy 8.33G), mallocs 19.57M -> 12.31M (legacy 12.5M). Same-binary A/B over 341 bench sources (KARAC_MIR_CONCAT=0 vs on): 0 output mismatches; 273 0.70x, 278 0.79x, 282 0.82x, 347 0.97x, 71 0.97x; the five reading >1% worse (12, 405, 133, 56, 387) compile to byte-identical IR on both arms. The ~1.24x left on 273 is the row's 'push_str out of line' (4%) and '13% unexplained' items, not this mechanism. Pinned by tests/mir_concat_chains.rs and src/mir/concat.rs's unit tests.

title: MIR stores the panic location into `@karac.site` / `@karac.site.len` on every loop latch and before every unwrap, and since da5bdc59fc (B-2026-10-26-7) those globals are thread_local, a TLV-getter call per access on Mach-O: kata 38 went 1.17x -> 1.67x legacy's instructions
detail:
MEASURED on the M5 Pro by the legacy-vs-MIR corpus screen (Kara/mir_screen/, outside both repos: screen.tsv, README.md, kernels/<kata>/). Exact instructions via scripts/pmc.c, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs identical on every variant. 'leg' = karac dd86e3955 legacy backend; 'MIR' = the same karac with --mir or today's g04628b0eb. Attribution is by IR edit: MIR's KARAC_MIR_LL IR through stock LLVM 18 opt default<O2> + llc tracks karac's own build within ~1% on 45 of 48 tail/control sources, so an edit's delta is the mechanism's cost.

bench/count_and_say.kara: leg 1.074G, MIR at the switch 1.258G, today 1.795G.

    today as emitted (stock pipeline)            1.754G
    drop thread_local on @karac.site/.len        1.209G (-545M, ~76% of today's gap)
    delete every store to @karac.site*           1.051G (below legacy)
    at the switch, delete the stores             1.071G (= legacy)

`sample`: 115 samples in _tlv_get_addr today, none on legacy or the switch build. Legacy passed the site statically through cold per-site `__karac_panic_site_N` functions. String building is NOT a cost here (inline ASCII fast paths for push and chars). Corpus scope of the thread_local part: now/mir > 1.05 on only 5 of 336 sources (#38 1.43, #227 1.22, #271 1.08, #126 1.06, #87 1.05). Fix direction: pass the site as a constant argument to the cold abort/unwrap path rather than storing a global per iteration; B-2026-10-26-7's per-thread requirement then holds for free.
fix: FIXED by e1bd415c72 (2026-10-31), the thread-local half. After the optimisation pipeline, each block that uses `karac.site` / `karac.site.len` takes their address once through `llvm.threadlocal.address` (mir_aot::address_site_globals_once), and an early-cse/licm/gvn pass merges and hoists it, so a loop no longer calls `_tlv_get_addr` per trip. Run before the pipeline instead, the inliner costs each lookup as a call and kata 131's recursive helpers stayed out of line (+12%); placed at function entry, a call paid the lookup on paths without a store. The JIT is untouched (on Apple it keeps the globals plain). KARAC_MIR_SITE_TLS_ONCE=0 turns it off. Kata 38 count_and_say 1.80G -> 1.26G (1.67x -> 1.18x legacy, back to its 1.17x before da5bdc59fc). Same-binary A/B over 341 bench sources: 0 output mismatches, rewrites 30; 38 0.704, 126 0.903, 133 0.955/0.965, 394 0.966, 96 0.966, 726 0.974; the three reading > 2% worse carry no site globals. tests/mir_site_thread_local.rs's compiled half (per-thread sites, 5 runs at 4 workers) passes with it. The stores themselves, the rest of kata 38's gap, moved to B-2026-10-31-2.
