title: A `FileSystem` provider whose handle methods (`read_handle`, `write_handle`, `close`) use a resource overridden where the provider is bound is refused only by the MIR build (`error[mir]: providers: ... uses `Stdout`, which is overridden ...`); §14.11 (b2655d3ef) requires `karac check` to report it as a structured diagnostic naming the method and the resource
fix: FIXED by 084367df50. A `FileSystem` (or `Network`) provider's handle method that uses a resource overridden where the provider is bound (a `with_provider` call or a `providers` block) is reported by `karac check` as E0422 at that binding, naming the method and the resource (`MemFs.close` uses `Stdout`, which is overridden where the `with_provider[FileSystem]` call is; ..., core semantics §14.11). `providers::file_handlers` records it as a refusal instead of failing the build, `source_effect_errors` reports it (now also run for programs naming `with_provider` or `providers`), and `par_check` keeps refusing the program on every backend with the same text. Pinned by tests/mir_provider_refusals.rs (both binding forms, and the socket twin); tests/mir_provider_overrides.rs's MIR-run refusal still holds.

title: `for x in mut v { .. }` (mutable iteration written with `mut` before the iterable) gets E0003 "'mut' is a reserved keyword and cannot be used as an identifier", with no fix and no pointer to `v.iter_mut()`, then two cascade errors: "Expected expression, found RightBrace" at the closing `}` of `main` and a false "file contains both top-level statements and an explicit `fn main()`" on the next statement
fix: c602325768. src/parser/exprs.rs (the `for` parser): a `mut` right after `in` is reported as "`mut v` after `in` is not Kāra: a `for` loop iterates for writing with `v.iter_mut()`, which binds each item as a `mut ref`" and skipped, so the loop parses and neither the "Expected expression" nor the false top-level-statements error follows. When the iterable is a name, path, field, call or index the fix deletes the `mut` and appends `.iter_mut()`; for a larger expression (`mut 0..3`) there is no fix. Pinned by tests/rust_mut_spelling_fix.rs (the row's repro prints 2 after the fix).

title: A struct item left unclosed (`struct A { x: i64,` with no `}`) before the next item reports only E0003 "'struct' is a reserved keyword and cannot be used as an identifier; write `r#struct` to use it as an ordinary identifier" at the NEXT `struct`, so the one error points at the wrong line and suggests a wrong remedy; the missing `}` is never named
fix: c24082c6ee. src/parser/generics.rs `at_next_item`: an item keyword first on its line (`fn`, `struct`, `enum`, `trait`, `impl` but not `impl invariant`, `const`, `extern`, with or without `pub` / `shared`) ends a struct's field list, and src/parser/items.rs reports "unclosed `{` of struct `A`: its `}` is missing before the item on line N" at the struct's `{` (1:10 in the repro), with no `r#` hint; the next item parses as itself. No fix is offered, since where the `}` belongs is the author's call. Pinned by tests/unclosed_struct_recovery.rs, including that a keyword field name on the fields' own line stays the keyword diagnostic.

FIXED by 4ff0c29ccf. Closed as written by B-2026-10-29-19's fix: the bit counts now return i64 (src/typechecker/method_numeric.rs), so `x.count_ones()` compares with an i64 directly and no cast or fix-it is needed. The row's repro (`let k = set.count_ones(); if k < len {..} else if k == len {..}` with i64 len) checks clean and prints "eq" on karac run; a u8 `total += x.count_ones()` into an i64 accumulator also checks.
title: Comparing `x.count_ones()` (a `u32`) with an `i64` is refused with E0208 and no machine-applicable fix, though `as i64` widens without loss and E0200 already offers that cast
detail: MEASURED at 8b6e8a9088 (release karac). Kata 1012's sets arm, natural form: `let k = set.count_ones(); if k < len { .. } else if k == len { .. }` with `set` and `len` i64. `karac check` gives E0208 `cannot compare 'u32' and 'i64': mixing signed and unsigned integers is a type error -- cast one operand with `as` so both have the same signedness` twice, and `karac check --output=json` carries no replacement; `karac fix` says `no fixable diagnostics`. The comparison arm (`reject_mixed_signedness_compare`, src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs) only words the cast, while the arithmetic arm's E0200 inserts ` as <wide>` when `int_cast_preserves_all_values` holds and the operand's extent is known. Here `u32 as i64` preserves every value, and the operand is an identifier (or, written inline, a MethodCall, whose extent `args_close_span` gives). The kata writes `set.count_ones() as i64`. Owner: the checker's diagnostics (Thread A).

fix: FIXED by 4ff0c29ccf. Per the ruling in 0a350a4e3d (docs/library/core-types.md, "Bit counts"), count_ones, count_zeros, leading_zeros and trailing_zeros return i64 on every integer type (src/typechecker/method_numeric.rs); shift amounts and pow exponents stay u32. Pinned by tests/typechecker.rs bit_intrinsics_return_i64_on_every_width (an i64 binding accepted on every width, a u32 binding refused) and corpus/fixtures/codegen/numerics/e2e_chained_width_sensitive_int_intrinsic (expected_from=decision). The 33 corpus files and 33 katas (kara-katas ee136cfe) that wrote `as i64` after a bit count lost the cast in the same push. Control arm on 7ae45ec869's src: the typechecker test failed 0/1 and the corpus pair failed 0/2.
title: `count_ones`, `count_zeros`, `leading_zeros` and `trailing_zeros` return `u32`, while design.md says Kāra code uses `i64` for every size, length, count and index, so every use beside a length needs `as i64`
detail: MEASURED at 8b6e8a9088. src/typechecker/method_numeric.rs types the four bit intrinsics as `u32` (`Rust's iN::{count_ones,..}`). design.md's type table says `isize`/`usize` are for FFI only and `Kāra code uses i64 for every size, length, count and index, I/O included`, and § Indexing: `Sizes, lengths and indices all use i64, so no cast is needed between an index and other integers`. A bit count is a count. In the corpus every use of `count_ones()` beside other integers is written `count_ones() as i64` (43 corpus files name `count_ones()`; the katas' uses are `as i64` or `% 2` on the bare value). docs/library names none of the four. A spec call (review thread): keep Rust's `u32`, or return `i64` as the table says; the second makes B-2026-10-29-18's shape type-check as written.

title: Under a `Network` override, TLS, WebSocket, `UdpSocket` (ruled cc02f4f3e) and the `Server.serve` family must be refused by `karac check` with `E_PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED` naming the call and `Network` (§14.12); today they are accepted and reach the real network, and a `Network` provider's handle method that uses a resource overridden at the binding site is refused only by the MIR build
fix: FIXED by 084367df50. Under an override of `Network` (a `with_provider[Network]` call or a `providers` block), a call of the library's UDP, TLS, WebSocket or server functions (`UdpSocket.*`, `TlsListener.*`, `TlsStream.*`, `WebSocket.*` that reach the network, `Server.serve` and its family) is refused by `karac check` as E0421 (`E_PROVIDER_UNSUPPORTED`, core semantics §14.12), naming the call and `Network`, at the call, whether it is made in the override, in a callee, or on a socket opened outside it; every backend refuses it too (`par_check`). Mechanism: effect inference charges `Network` to such a call in a program that binds it (check's stand-in library bodies included), so the code making one is copied per override; `providers::specialise` records the call under a bound `Network` as a refusal instead of failing, the library's own calls among those functions not reported again. Second half: a `Network` provider's handle method that uses a resource overridden where the provider is bound is reported by the check as E0422 (shared with B-2026-10-29-15). Calls a provider serves (TCP, the HTTP client), a `WebSocket` helper that does not reach the network, and UDP outside every override still check and run. Pinned by tests/mir_provider_refusals.rs (control arm at 11649a8102: 5 of 6 fail, the sixth is the still-accepted guard).

title: `karac test` on a package refuses a program that uses a v2-only library item (`NetError`, `NetworkProvider`) with `E0104 undefined type`, where `karac build` of the same package builds: the test runner's tree check resolved each module without the library the build appends (B-2026-10-24-43 fixed only the build), and that library read only the production files, not the `_test.kara` companions
fix: 927b03363c: `test_front` (src/cli/test_cmd.rs) builds `PackageLibrary::of(&tree)` and passes it to `resolve_modules` and `typecheck_modules`, as the build does, and `PackageLibrary::of` (src/cli/build_cmds.rs) reads each module's merged `_test.kara` companion too, so a test file's words (a `NetworkProvider` fake) bring their library module in. Pinned by tests/mir_network_provider.rs `provider_network_fake_in_a_test_file_leaves_the_build_alone`, which runs a package whose test file names `NetError` and declares a `Network` fake under `karac test` and `karac test --interp`, and checks `karac build` of the package keeps the plain socket natives.

title: The implicit numeric widening of a CALL's result is dropped when the call initializes an annotated `let` (`let x: f64 = f()` with `f() -> f32`, `let n: i64 = g()` with `g() -> i32`, a method call alike), is a function's return value (`return f()` or a tail `f()` in a `-> f64` function) or is an `if` arm: `__mir-run` prints the right value, while `__mir-llvm-run`, `karac run`, `karac build` and `__mir-llvm-asan` read a half-written slot (1.5 prints as 5.28426686e-315, -7 as 4294967289 or stack junk under ASan); an argument, a field, a `push` and an assignment widen correctly
fix: 46a1f3e2e3. `expr_into_here` (src/mir/lower.rs): a call or method call whose own type the slot widens losslessly (design.md §5) writes a temporary of its own type, which is then widened into the slot, instead of writing its narrower bytes straight into it. Covers the annotated `let`, a `return`, a tail, an `if` arm, an assignment and an argument; the interpreter's `i32` into `f64` (printed `-7` for `-7.0`) is fixed by the same change. Pinned by tests/mir_call_result_widening.rs (2 tests, interpreter plus compiled at -O0 and -O2): control 0 passed, 2 failed; with the fix 2/2.

title: Rust-style angle-bracket generics in a type (`-> Result<(), String>`, `let v: Vec<i64>`, `x: Option<i64>`) get a bare token error ("Expected LeftBrace, found LessThan", "Expected Equal, found LessThan", "Expected RightParen, found LessThan") with no pointer to Kāra's `Result[(), String]` and no fix; in a method of an `impl` the parser also reports a false "Expected expression, found RightBrace" at the `impl`'s closing brace
fix: 028b93b8ce. src/parser/types.rs `angle_generic_args`: a `<` after a type's path is reported once, "`Result<..>` is Rust's spelling: Kāra writes generic arguments in brackets, `Result[..]`", with a multi-edit fix rewriting each of the list's angle brackets (`>>` closing two lists becomes `]]`), and the tokens are rewritten the same way so the list parses as Kāra's: the false "Expected expression, found RightBrace" at the end of an `impl` is gone. Each closer must match its opener; an unbalanced list (`Vec<i64)`) is reported with no fix. The type after `as` is exempt (`x as i64 < y` is a comparison). Pinned by tests/rust_angle_generics_fix.rs; a scan of every corpus source with `karac check` found the message on none.

title: On macOS, `karac run` of a program with several pool workers can report ANOTHER task's source location for a panic: the JIT keeps `@karac.site` / `@karac.site.len` process-wide because RuntimeDyldMachO cannot link thread-locals, and B-2026-10-26-7's comment says that sharing 'costs speed only' — it also makes the reported place a race, and tests/mir_site_thread_local.rs's `karac run` assertion passes by chance on a Mac
detail:
MEASURED 2026-10-28 on the M5 (macOS, arm64), the program in tests/mir_site_thread_local.rs (four tasks calling pick(k).unwrap() at line 7 in a loop; task 3 then unwraps None at line 10). `karac run`, 5 runs per arm, reported location counted:

    KARAC_THREADS=4, as built today                    7:17 x5            (wrong: another task's site)
    KARAC_THREADS=4, KARAC_MIR_BORROW_LITERALS=0       10:17 x1, 7:17 x4  (wrong 4/5 BEFORE 5e8165275e too)
    KARAC_THREADS=1, either arm                        10:17 x5           (correct)

The compiled binary (`karac build`) reports 10:17 every time: its globals are thread_local. Only the JIT strips thread_local on Apple (src/backend/mir/mod.rs compile_mir_ir_for_jit). So the test's `karac run` half is a race on a Mac: it passed in two local gates by luck and fails deterministically after 5e8165275e changed the timing. CI runs on Linux, where the JIT keeps the thread-locals, so CI is unaffected. Fix direction: give the JIT a per-thread site without a TLS relocation (e.g. a runtime accessor returning a pointer to a thread-local slot), or report the site from the aborting task's own frame; until then the test's JIT assertion should be Apple-gated with this id.
fix:
a4ea53a5ee: there is no longer a global to share. The place of the program's call into a library body that can abort is an argument of that body (B-2026-10-31-2's fix), so the JIT's Apple-only stripping of `thread_local` from `karac.site` / `karac.site.len` (compile_mir_ir_for_jit) is deleted along with the globals, and an abort on one worker can only report its own task's call.

MEASURED on Linux: tests/mir_site_thread_local.rs now asserts the IR holds no `@karac.site` and runs the four-worker program built x5 and under `karac run` x5 (KARAC_THREADS=4), each reporting main.kara:10:17. The race never reproduced on Linux (the JIT kept the thread-locals there), so the Linux run proves the mechanism, not the Mac symptom: macOS confirmation is left to the scheduled CI run, which runs that test's `karac run` half.

title: An unsuffixed integer literal inside `Vec.filled(n, 0)` does not take its element type from the expected type when the call is a METHOD argument (`d.push(Vec.filled(2, 0))` with `d: Vec[Vec[u64]]`, a struct field's `c.d.push(...)`), a tuple element under an annotated `let`, or an `Option` payload (`let o: Option[Vec[u64]] = Some(Vec.filled(2, 0))`): each is refused as `Vec[i64]`, with no fix-it although the help names the suffix; a `let` annotation, a free-function argument and a `vec![...]` struct field all infer `u64`
fix: FIXED by 5dd03bfb7d. An associated-function call with a bare numeric or list literal among its arguments (`ctor_with_literal_args`: `Vec.filled(n, 0)`) is now checked against its slot where the slot is known: a method argument (`Vec.push`'s element, and the generic method pass-1 arm of B-2026-10-19-32), a tuple element under an annotated `let`, and a `Some`/`Ok`/`Err` payload. The literal takes the slot's element type, so the help's fix-it is no longer needed, and it is range-checked there (`m.push(Vec.filled(2, 300))` into `Vec[Vec[u8]]` reports "integer literal 300 out of range for 'u8'"). Pinned by tests/core_expected_type_tails.rs `expected_type_reaches_a_constructors_literal_arguments` (both repros' shapes plus the range refusals). Control: on ffd1d7d49a's src the test fails.

title: `d.push(Vec.filled(n, None))` with `d: Vec[Vec[Option[T]]]` clones its `None` from a stack slot too small for an `Option[T]` on the compiled backends: `__mir-llvm-asan` reports a stack-buffer-overflow READ of 32 bytes in `clone.Option[Vec[u8]]` (16 for `Option[i64]`) from `kara.main`; the interpreter, a `let`-annotated `Vec.filled(3, None)`, a free-function argument, `Some(4)` in the same place and a `None` bound by a typed `let` first are all clean
detail:
Found writing apps/cli/mini_read_sas (kara-katas), a port of pandas' read_sas: `Sas7.read` makes one column per string variable with `ch.s.push(Vec.filled(nrows, None))` into `s: Vec[Vec[Option[Vec[u8]]]]`. All 2,857 lines matched pandas on `__mir-run`, `__mir-llvm-run` and a `karac build` binary, but the ASan lane stopped at the first read job with the report below. The likely shape: the bare `None` argument is lowered with its own (unit-like, 1-byte) type before `Vec.filled`'s `T` is unified with the element type that `push` expects, so the slot passed to `Vec.filled` is smaller than the `Option[T]` it clones n times. Without ASan the over-read is of neighbouring stack bytes, which happen to make a `None` here, so `__mir-llvm-run` prints the right answer; a larger or differently laid-out frame could read a `Some`.

Repro (karac at cc02f4f3e8):

```
fn main() {
    let mut d: Vec[Vec[Option[Vec[u8]]]] = Vec.new();
    d.push(Vec.filled(3, None));
    println(f"{d[0].len()} {d[0][2].is_none()}");
}
```

`__mir-run`: `3 true`. `__mir-llvm-asan`:

```
ERROR: AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow on address 0x7f92a72ff0e1
READ of size 32 at 0x7f92a72ff0e1 thread T1
    #0 __asan_memmove
    #1 clone.Option[Vec[u8]]
    #2 kara.main
```

With `Vec[Vec[Option[i64]]]` the same line reads 16 bytes. Clean on every backend: `let v: Vec[Option[i64]] = Vec.filled(3, None)`; `takes(Vec.filled(3, None))` with `fn takes(v: Vec[Option[Vec[u8]]])`; `d.push(None)` into `Vec[Option[i64]]`; `d.push(Vec.filled(3, Some(4)))`; and `let e: Option[Vec[u8]] = None; d.push(Vec.filled(3, e))`, which is the app's workaround (with a comment citing this row). Same expected-type path as B-2026-10-29-24 (a method argument one level down), which the type checker refuses for an integer literal and here lets through with the wrong layout.
fix: e5f935eb0b. The checker leaves the bare `None` as an `Option[()]`; the builder now builds a value whose type has such `()` holes at the type its slot names (`operand_filling_holes` / `fills_unit_holes`, src/mir/lower.rs): the value argument of `Vec.filled` takes the element type of the call's own type, the repeat literal `vec![None; n]` / `[None; n]` its element type, and a call argument its parameter type. Pinned by tests/mir_unsolved_value_types.rs (2 tests, interpreter plus `__mir-llvm-asan`, incl. `Option[Vec[u8]]`, `Option[(i64, String)]` and `vec![None; 4]`): control 0 passed, 2 failed (stack-buffer-overflow); with the fix 2/2. The app's workaround in mini_read_sas can go.

title: (v1) A `Request` a program builds with `Request.new` / `with_header` / `with_body` is never freed, on either MIR backend: each call appends to a process-wide table of built requests that nothing shrinks, so a client that builds requests in a loop (a poller, a crawler, a retrying client) grows without bound
detail:
Since 58db33e78c (core-semantics §14.12, the HTTP half of a Network provider) `Request` is `struct Request { __id: i64 }`: 0 is the served request, and an id above 0 indexes a table of built requests, `BUILT_REQUESTS` in runtime/src/mir_io.rs (`karac_mir_http_request_new` / `_set`) and `built_requests` in src/mir/interp.rs. `Request` has no `Drop`, so no entry is ever removed; `with_header` and `with_body` take `self` by value and push a new entry each time, so the chain `Request.new(..).with_header(..).with_body(..)` leaves three.

Measured on a built binary (debug karac at 58db33e78c), a loop of `Request.new("GET", f"http://api.test/items/{i}?page=1").with_body("x")` reading `r.url()`: 200000 iterations, max RSS 62028 KB; 400000 iterations, 108460 KB, about 240 bytes per iteration that never come back.

The review thread (06:07Z) ruled this a v1 item: fixed after the program-rooted defaults and before the kata bench re-run. Shape of the fix: a `Drop` for `Request` that frees its entry (id 0 excluded), with the builders reusing the moved-in entry instead of pushing a copy; LSan on the `mir-llvm-asan` lane is the instrument.
fix: a1b960dd5d. `Request` has a builtin `Drop`: a request a program built frees its slot in the table of built requests (runtime/src/mir_io.rs `karac_mir_http_request_release`, reached through `io_drop` as a socket's close is; src/mir/interp.rs `("Request", "drop")`), and the next request takes the freed slot; the served request (id 0) frees nothing. Correction to the detail: `with_header` and `with_body` already changed a built request in place on both backends, so the chain held one entry, not three; the leak was that entry, never freed. Measured on a built binary, the detail's loop now peaks at 11 MB of resident memory at both 200000 and 400000 iterations (62 MB and 108 MB before). Pinned by tests/mir_network_provider.rs `provider_network_built_requests_are_freed` (a 40 MB bound read with `wait4`, plus the interpreter's output).

title: Inside a subtrait's generic default method, `let (i, u) = self.tag(u)` calling a SUPERTRAIT's generic default `tag[T](self, t: own T) -> (i64, T)` is refused with "cannot infer type parameter 'T'; add a type annotation to this binding"; annotating the binding (`let p: (i64, U) = self.tag(u)`) or calling `tag` from the same trait's default checks and runs
fix: FIXED by 8b40f7b792. `dispatch_trait_method_on` instantiated a trait method's own generic parameters only for a receiver through `impl Trait` or a bound with associated-type bindings; on `Self` in a default body (and on a bare bounded type parameter) a generic method's signature was used with its parameters left as the names `T`, so `let (i, u) = self.tag(u)` reached the binding as `(i64, T)`. A generic method on such a receiver now goes through `check_call_args_with_substitution_full`, so `T` is solved from the argument. Taken from Thread A's queue with its agreement (10-30). Pinned by tests/core_supertrait_generic_defaults.rs (the repro, a bounded `show[T: Clone + Display]`, a generic default calling another, and the same calls on `S: Shape`; check, __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run). Control: on 86011ab591's src the test fails.

title: An unsuffixed literal on the left of `<<` / `>>` with a non-constant count is typed `i64` whatever the context: `r | (255 << b)` with `r: u64` passes `karac check` and fails as invalid MIR ("binary operands of different types u64 and i64") on every backend, and `r + (255 << b)` is refused
detail:
Found writing kara-katas apps/cli/mini_read_sql (SQLite's `<<` on a negative i64 fills the vacated bits: `r = r | (18446744073709551615 << (64 - b))` with `r: u64`). Measured at af329e798c, release karac.

Repro:

    fn fill(r: u64, b: i64) -> u64 {
        r | (255 << b)
    }

    fn main() {
        println(f"{fill(1, 4)}");
    }

`karac check`: All checks passed. `karac run` / `karac __mir-run`: `error[mir]: invalid MIR: fill: bb1[1]: binary operands of different types u64 and i64` (exit 1); `__mir-llvm-run` the same (exit 3). Expected: 4081 (design.md, Division, remainder and shifts: "n may have any integer type, and the result has the type of x", and an unsuffixed literal takes its type from the context, here `u64`).

The same probe with `let x = <expr>; x` in a function over `r: T, b: i64`:

| expr | T = u64 | T = u32 | T = i32 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `r \| (255 << b)` | check passes, invalid MIR | 4081 | 4081 |
| `r & (255 >> b)` | check passes, invalid MIR | 1 | 1 |
| `r \| (1 << b) \| 2` | check passes, invalid MIR | 19 | 19 |
| `r ^ (1 << 3)` (constant count) | 9 | 9 | 9 |
| `r + (255 << b)` | refused: cannot mix integer types 'u64' and 'i64' in arithmetic | refused (u32/i64) | refused (i32/i64) |
| `r == (1 << b)` | refused: cannot compare 'u64' and 'i64' | refused | not measured (the probe returned a bool) |

So the literal shift is typed `i64` before the context reaches it. The bitwise operators then accept the mix (a named `x: i64` in `r | x` is correctly refused, so the acceptance is specific to the literal shift), which is unsound at u64; the arithmetic and comparison operators refuse it, which is a false positive. `let m: u64 = 255 << b;`, `(255 << b) as u64`, `255u64 << b` and a named `let ones: u64 = ...; ones << b` all work.

Workaround in mini_read_sql `bit_op`: the mask is a named `u64`. Related, both fixed: B-2026-10-23-12, B-2026-10-27-19.
fix: ef433a7c5b. The literal tree beside a typed peer was promoted to the peer's type by span only (`promote_int_literal_operator_tree`, src/typechecker/exprs.rs), so the typed HIR kept `255 << b` at `i64` and the MIR build refused `r | (255 << b)`; it now records each node by id too. The B-2026-10-15-51 promotion (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs) covered only `& | ^`; it now covers `+ - * / %` and the comparisons, so `r + (255 << b)`, `r == (1 << b)` and `r + (2 + 3)` with `r: u64` check and run, each leaf and intermediate range-checked at the peer's type (`r + (300 << b)` with `r: u8` is "out of range for 'u8'"). Pinned by tests/core_shift_literal_takes_peer_type.rs (control at the base: 0 passed, 4 failed; with the fix: 4 passed).

title: For `!x` on an integer, `karac check` says "use `not` instead" and its JSON `replacement` is `not `, while `karac fix` correctly writes `~x`: a reader of the message or the JSON gets a fix that then fails typecheck
fix: 08ffa923e1. `karac check --output=json` now takes the same look-ahead `karac fix` takes (src/cli/fix_cmds.rs `complemented_bangs`, sharing `complement_integer_bangs`), so the replacement for a `!` on an integer is `~` and on a bool `not `; src/cli/diag_json.rs renders it. The parser's message names both: "use `not` for a bool, `~` for an integer's bitwise complement". Pinned by tests/bang_complement_json.rs.

title: `m[k]` (and `ref m[k]`) on a `Map[K, dyn T]` is wrong compiled: the index stores a POINTER to the map's value into a `ref dyn T` destination, which is the two-word `dyn` pair itself, so LLVM treats the found-key path as unreachable; `__mir-llvm-run` aborts with `key not found` on a key that is there, `__mir-llvm-asan` SEGVs. The interpreter, `m.get(k)` and `v[i]` on a `Vec[dyn T]` are right
fix: 4d4e122e46: the index (`m[k]`, `ref m[k]`, `mut ref m[k]`) now writes a `dyn` value's pair into its `ref dyn T` destination, as `get` does through `store_found`, through a new `lend_value` in src/backend/mir/table.rs; `entry_or_insert`/`entry_or_insert_with`, an `Occupied` entry's payload, `or_insert`/`or_insert_with` and `values()` (a `Vec[ref dyn T]`) had the same address-for-pair store and take it too. Any other value type still gets the slot's address. Pinned by tests/mir_dyn_tables.rs (on the CI llvm list): `m[k]`, `ref`/`mut ref m[k]` with `mut ref self` calls through them, `get` and `values()` on a `Map[String, dyn Show]` and a `SortedMap[i64, dyn Show]`, on the interpreter and compiled at -O0 and -O2; clean under `__mir-llvm-asan`. Control: with the dyn branch of `lend_value` disabled the compiled program aborts `key not found` at the first `ref m["x"]`.

title: A call through `dyn Display` (or another library trait the MIR library does not carry: `Debug`, `Hash`, `Eq`, `Ord`) is not dispatched: `d.to_string()` on `d: dyn Display` fails at run time on the interpreter (`print cannot show Dyn {..}`) and is refused by the compiled backends (`printing a dyn ... is not lowered yet`), for a struct with its own `impl Display` as for a number; `karac check` accepts it, and `f"{d}"` is refused by check
fix: cb4fa14b71. A `dyn Display` value (or a `dyn` of a trait under `Display`) now dispatches through its method table: `d.to_string()`, `f"{d}"` and `println(d)` on __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run and __mir-llvm-asan, for a struct with its own `impl Display` and for a number, string, bool and char. The builder reads `Display` from the checker's stdlib (runtime/stdlib/display.kara) when the MIR library does not carry it, so `dyn_slots` finds the `to_string` slot (src/mir/lower/dyn_trait.rs `checker_library_trait`). A primitive's slot is the generated library function `dyn_display_to_string[T: Display]` (runtime/stdlib/source/dyn_display.kara), since its `to_string` is a native. A generic `[T: Display]` body's `x.to_string()` on a primitive, which had no resolved callee, now falls to the builtin method. `print_operands` prints a `dyn Display` through the slot call into a scoped String. Checker half: `type_supports_display` accepts a `dyn` whose trait is `Display` or under it, so the f-string is no longer refused. Pinned by tests/mir_dyn.rs `mir_dyn_display_shows_through_its_to_string_slot` (interpreter, then compiled at -O0 and -O2); the control arm without the src change fails it (0 passed; 1 failed). Scope of the title's other traits: `Debug` has no method callable even on a concrete type yet (`fmt_debug` is "no method", `{x:?}` is reserved), and `Hash` (generic `hash[H]`), `Eq` and `Ord` (a `Self` parameter) have no dispatchable slot, so a `dyn` of them has nothing to call.

title: On the MIR compiled backend, `String.contains` with a needle of at most 16 bytes calls `memchr` and then `memcmp` at every place the needle's first byte occurs, so on a two-letter haystack (a binary string, where that byte is every other one) it costs 3.2 ns per haystack byte: 9.4x C `strstr` and 7.2x Rust `str::contains`; kata 1016's bench is 8.5x C
detail: MEASURED on a 4-core container, karac 56c60bdf7c (archives ce706dd131). Kata 1016 (Binary String With Substrings Representing 1 To N, kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1016-binary-string-with-substrings-representing-1-to-n) asks, for 200 random 1,000-bit strings and every n up to 400, whether `s.contains(f"{x:b}")` holds for each x from n down to n / 2 + 1: 2,251,192 searches for needles of 1 to 9 bytes over 424,572,466 haystack bytes in all. Medians of eight interleaved runs: C (`strstr`) 0.234 s, Go 0.227 s, Rust (`format!` + `str::contains`) 0.366 s, Rust with overflow checks 0.336 s, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build` 1.986 s and plain `karac build` 1.981 s; Python takes 1.95 s. Under callgrind the Kāra binary runs 17.8 billion instructions: 27.4% in `__memcmp_avx2_movbe`, 22.8% in `__memchr_avx2`, 25.8% inclusive in `karac_mir_fmt_spec` (the `{x:b}` half, filed as B-2026-10-29-33) and about 12% in malloc and free. A probe that searches one 1,000-bit string 425,000 times for an absent 9-byte needle (`100001011`, so every search reads the whole string) takes 1.351 s as a `karac build` binary, against 0.144 s for C `strstr` (behind a compiler barrier) and 0.187 s for Rust `str::contains`. The inline scan is `str_contains` in src/backend/mir/seq.rs (B-2026-10-15-55, B-2026-10-19-26): `memchr` for the first byte, then `memcmp` of the rest at each hit, with no budget, so a first byte that occurs at half the places costs two libc calls per two haystack bytes. The runtime's copy (runtime/src/mir.rs `contains`, for longer needles) has the same scan with a compare budget that hands over to two-way search; the inline one never hands over. HYPOTHESIS (not tried): a short needle wants a scan that does not call out per candidate, such as comparing a word-sized window, or glibc's `memmem`, whose short-needle path is what makes `strstr` fast here.
fix: 28baa4f6a0. The compiled short-needle scan made a memchr and a memcmp call at every hit of the needle's first byte. runtime/src/mir.rs contains now keeps the memchr scan only while that byte is rare: once it has turned up more than once per 16 bytes, a needle of up to 256 bytes goes to find_short, a Horspool search keyed on the hash of the window's end byte pair (glibc memmem's short-needle path) that calls nothing per window; the scan itself walks raw pointers. src/backend/mir/seq.rs str_contains sends a 2-to-16-byte needle in a haystack over 64 bytes to that runtime search; 1-byte needles and short haystacks stay inline. MEASURED on a 4-core x86 container, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 builds, hyperfine means, control built at 83c7cf6133 with fresh archives: the row's probe (one 1,000-bit string, absent needle 100001011, 425,000 searches) 1.354 s to 0.335 s (C strstr was 0.144 s in the row, so about 2.3x C now, from 9.4x); kata 1016's bench 1.568 s to 0.638 s, same output (B-2026-10-29-33's {x:b} fix was already in both arms; callgrind of the fixed binary puts 63% of its 5.5G instructions in the search itself and 3.7% in karac_mir_fmt_spec, so what remains against C's 0.234 s is the search, a per-byte loop where strstr compares 16 positions at a time); a 9,690-byte English-like text with rare first bytes 54.7 to 58.2 ms (sigma 6 to 9 ms); 2,000,000 searches of words under 32 bytes 62.7 to 62.7 ms. Pinned by the runtime unit test find_short_agrees_with_a_naive_search (alphabets of 1 to 4 letters and all 256 bytes, needles across the 256-byte limit) and tests/mir_build.rs mir_long_haystack_contains_agrees_with_the_interpreter (compiled at -O0 and -O2 against the interpreter on binary, three-letter and English haystacks). Gate green; TSan suites pass three of three on rebuilt TSan archives.

title: `f"{x:b}"` (any format spec but `{v:N}` / `{v:0N}`) re-parses its spec text on every call: `karac_mir_fmt_spec` copies the spec into a String, runs `FormatSpec::parse` and formats through a second String, 130 ns per call against 38 ns for Rust `format!("{:b}")` and 22 ns for C (malloc and a bit loop)
detail: MEASURED on a 4-core container, karac 56c60bdf7c (archives ce706dd131). A loop formatting `f"{x:b}"` for x = i % 400 + 1 over 2,251,192 values (the count kata 1016's bench formats) and summing the lengths takes 0.292 s as a `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build` binary, Rust `format!("{:b}", x)` 0.085 s, and C with a malloc, a bit loop and a free 0.050 s; `f"{x}"` in the same Kāra loop takes 0.009 s. In kata 1016's bench `karac_mir_fmt_spec` is 25.8% of the instructions, inclusive (see B-2026-10-29-32 for the rest). runtime/src/mir.rs `karac_mir_fmt_spec` takes a fast path only through `padded_int` (`{v:N}` and `{v:0N}`); every other spec goes through `String::from_utf8_lossy(spec).into_owned()`, `FormatSpec::parse` and an intermediate `String` before `string_of` copies it out. HYPOTHESIS (not tried): the spec is a compile-time constant, so it could be parsed once (at lowering, or cached by pointer), and the common integer radix forms (`b`, `o`, `x`, `X`) written straight into the output.
fix: 6f860bee0b. runtime/src/mir.rs `karac_mir_fmt_spec` keeps the specs it has parsed in a thread-local cache keyed by their text (`parsed_spec`), and writes a 64-bit integer through the new `FormatSpec::write_magnitude` (src/format_spec.rs) into a reused buffer before `string_of` copies it out, so no spec copy, parse or intermediate String per call. The interpreter's `apply_magnitude` goes through the same writer, so both backends keep one rendering; a unit test (`integer_writer_matches_the_format_based_rendering`) checks it against the format!-based rendering it replaced over 20 specs and 9 values. Measured on a 4-core container, three runs each, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 builds: the row's loop (`f"{x:b}"` for x = i % 400 + 1, 2,251,192 times) 0.42 s to 0.12 s, against the row's Rust 0.085 s on its machine; a mix of `x`, `>8`, `08b`, `X` and `.3` specs 2.9 s to 1.2 s, output identical. 128-bit, float and string specs use the cache but still format through a String.

title: `ref mut m` in a pattern (Rust's order for Kāra's `mut ref m`) is reported as "'mut' is a reserved keyword and cannot be used as an identifier" plus a cascading "Expected expression, found RightBrace" at the next `}`, with no fix; `mut m` in a pattern already gets a Rust-syntax diagnostic and a fix
fix: c602325768. src/parser/patterns.rs: after `ref`, a `mut` followed by a name is reported as "`ref mut m` is Rust syntax -- in Kāra write `mut ref m`" with an edit swapping the two words, and the binding is parsed as `mut ref m`, so the cascade at the next `}` is gone in the `if let` and match-arm forms. Pinned by tests/rust_mut_spelling_fix.rs (both forms run after the fix).

title: A comparison does not give a constructor or tuple operand the other operand's type, so a `ref` to a Copy value inside it is refused: with `n: ref i64` from `for n in v.iter()`, `value == Some(n)`, `Some(n) == value`, `value != Some(n)` and `pair == (n, 5)` fail "cannot compare 'Option[i64]' and 'Option[ref i64]'" (or the tuple form) with no fix-it, though `let w: Option[i64] = Some(n)`, `same(value, Some(n))` and `vec![Some(n)]` into a `Vec[Option[i64]]` all read `n` as an `i64`
detail: MEASURED on karac 56c60bdf7c, `karac check` and `karac __mir-run` alike. Found writing kata 1017's differential (kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1017-convert-to-base-2), which loops `for n in ns.iter()` over a `Vec[i64]` and compares `value_of(form)` (an `Option[i64]`) with `Some(n)`. Probe: `let ns = vec![1, 2, 3]; for n in ns.iter() { let value: Option[i64] = Some(2); if value == Some(n) { .. } }` reports `cannot compare 'Option[i64]' and 'Option[ref i64]'` at the `==`; the reverse order and `!=` report the same, and `let pair = (2, 5); if pair == (n, 5)` reports `cannot compare '(i64, i64)' and '(ref i64, i64)'`. In the same loop `let w: Option[i64] = Some(n);`, a call `same(value, Some(n))` to `fn same(a: Option[i64], b: Option[i64])`, and `let v: Vec[Option[i64]] = vec![Some(n)];` all check and run (`__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run` print the expected lines), so an expected type reaches a constructor's argument everywhere but a comparison operand. core-semantics §5.10 reads a `ref` to a Copy value as the value "wherever a T is expected", naming an operator operand and a field or element of a literal; and a comparison already types one operand from the other for a literal (`x == 3` with `x: i32`) and for an underdetermined variant (`c == None`, the `is_underdetermined_variant` block at the top of `infer_binary`, src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs). That this case should check is my reading of §5.10, not a recorded decision; B-2026-10-12-22 settled the different case of a library result that is itself `Option[ref V]` (`m.get(k) == Some(n)`), which stays refused. The kata writes `Some(*n)`, which §5.10 allows as the explicit read. HYPOTHESIS (not tried): in `infer_binary`, check a constructor-call or tuple operand against the other operand's (concrete) type, as the `??` fallback does for a string literal, instead of inferring it alone; failing that, a fix-it inserting `*` before the argument.
fix: FIXED by 6bbbaf1fb5. In `infer_binary`, a comparison operand that is a `Some`/`Ok`/`Err` call or a tuple literal of places and literals is checked against the other operand's type when the two differ only by `ref`s to `Copy` values (or a variant parameter nothing decided), and takes that type, so `value == Some(n)`, `Some(n) == value`, `value != Some(n)`, `pair == (n, 5)` and `r == Ok(n)` with `n: ref i64` read `n` as the value (core-semantics §5.10). A `ref String` is not `Copy` and `o == Some(w)` stays refused; B-2026-10-12-22's `m.get(k) == Some(n)` with `n: i64` is unchanged (the library side is the ref). Pinned by tests/core_expected_type_tails.rs `comparison_reads_a_copy_ref_in_a_constructor_operand` (check, __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run). Control: on ffd1d7d49a's src the test fails.

title: A call whose result type nothing fixes passes `karac check` when it is an operand of `==` and fails in the MIR builder: `s.chars().filter(..).collect() == t` (t: String) and `v.iter().map(..).collect() == w` (w: Vec[i64]) report "All checks passed" and then `an expression whose type does not lower (UnsolvedParam("C"))` under __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run and build; `karac fix`'s turbofish fix produces exactly this shape
detail: MEASURED on karac 56c60bdf7c (and a fresh check on main 2f07ada7cb's tree with the same binary). Found writing kata 1023's skeleton arm (kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1023-camelcase-matching). Probe a.kara: `let s = "aBcD"; let t: String = "BD".to_string(); let ok = s.chars().filter(|c| c.is_ascii_uppercase()).collect() == t;` -> `karac check` and `check --output=json` report no diagnostic; `karac __mir-run`, `__mir-llvm-run` and `karac build` all stop at `error[mir]: build: 4:14 in main: an expression whose type does not lower (UnsolvedParam("C")) is not lowered yet`. Probe b.kara, the same with `v.iter().map(|x| x * 2).collect() == w` over `Vec[i64]`, behaves identically. Control c.kara: `v.iter().collect().len()` IS refused by check (E0236 `no method 'len' on type parameter 'C'`), and design.md § Type inference makes an unsolved variable an error at the end of the body. The comparison cannot fix C by itself: `PartialEq[Rhs = Self]` takes an Rhs (design.md §9, `impl PartialEq[Str] for String`), so `collect() == t` is genuinely underdetermined and the spec answer is the refusal (`cannot infer ...; annotation needed`), not inference. Cause, read not tried: `check_unsolved_call_results` (src/typechecker/items.rs, B-2026-10-22-36, 9b8845bf54) checks only the RECEIVER of a method call that is itself a call, because a call's own recorded type can predate the context that fixes it (its commit says checking every call result refused 321 corpus programs); an operand of a binary operator is not a receiver, so it is never looked at. HOW IT IS REACHED: the natural first draft was `.collect::[String]() == capitals`; the parser's turbofish diagnostic (`reject_method_turbofish`, src/parser/exprs.rs) says to remove the type arguments and annotate the binding, and `karac fix` applies only the removal, leaving `.collect() == capitals`, which then passes check and fails to build. In a non-binding position (here the binding is the `bool` of the comparison) the fix cannot carry the type to an annotation, so either it should not be machine-applicable there, or check must refuse what it leaves. HYPOTHESIS (not tried): extend the end-of-body check to operands of comparison and arithmetic operators whose recorded type keeps an unbound parameter, re-measuring the corpus-wide false-positive count the B-2026-10-22-36 commit cites. The kata binds the capitals with `let caps: String = ...collect();` as the diagnostic says, which builds and runs.
fix: 9d8dfb194d: `karac check` now refuses a call result whose type nothing fixes when it is an operand of a comparison or arithmetic operator (design.md § Type inference: an unsolved variable is an error at the end of the body), as it already did for a method receiver, so `s.chars().filter(..).collect() == t` gets the annotation diagnostic at check instead of failing in the MIR builder (src/typechecker/items.rs `check_unsolved_call_results`). Only an operand whose type is a bare unsolved parameter is refused; a nested one the other side fixes (`i64.parse("3").ok() == Some(3)`, `f(x) == Ok(true)`) still checks. Pinned by tests/core_unsolved_operand_type.rs; control: the base accepts the row's program, the fix refuses it; the check sweep is unchanged.

title: `karac check` refuses moving a binding after a non-escaping closure that only reads it ("moved inside a loop" with no loop in the program); both MIR backends accept it and print the right answer
fix: 39fd8d115b: a `let f = |..|` closure that only reads a capture no longer pairs its body's read with a later move of that capture when every use of `f` comes before the move: the body runs where `f` is called (src/rc_predicate.rs `let_closure_runs_before`, with src/cfg.rs recording each closure body's blocks and each `let`-bound closure). A call or use of `f` after the move, a moved `f`, and a loop that both calls `f` and moves the capture are still refused. Pinned by tests/core_closure_read_before_move.rs (check and MIR output). Five RC-fallback pins in tests/ownership.rs and tests/rc_fallback.rs held a closure that was never called; they now call it after the consume, so they still pin the capture/consume pairing.

title: The MIR interpreter's `Str.bytes()` copies the whole string into a fresh snapshot on every call, so code that calls `s.bytes()` once per step pays the string's length each time: 2,000 one-byte reads through `bytes()` on a 100,000-letter string take 3.3 s under `__mir-run` and nothing measurable under `__mir-llvm-run`
fix: d86cab30a8. src/mir/interp.rs: the `"bytes" =>` arm keeps its last four snapshots by the text they copy (`bytes_snapshots`, BYTES_SNAPSHOTS_KEPT), and a string asked for its bytes again unchanged gets the same read-only `Slice[u8]` snapshot instead of a fresh `Vec` of every byte; `sweep_snapshots` keeps those four, and changed text gets a new snapshot (a snapshot cannot outlive a change to its string: the borrow checker refuses the push while one is held). The row's probe, 2,000 `byte_at` calls on a 100,000-letter string: the calls add 0.16 s over the no-call run under a debug karac, against 2.8 s under a release karac from main 10-28 (different builds, so a rough control). Pinned by tests/mir_interp_bytes_snapshot.rs (reuse, a change between calls, six strings in turn).

title: `s.parse::<i64>()` gets E0001 whose machine fix deletes `::<i64>`, so `karac fix` leaves `s.parse()`, which E0236 then refuses for want of a type (with no edit), though the type was in the source until the first fix removed it; the edit could write `i64.parse(s)`
fix: d9c29910ec. src/parser/exprs.rs `reject_method_turbofish`: a turbofish on `parse` with one type argument and no call arguments, after a `.`, is fixed to the associated call Kāra writes, `RECV.parse::<T>()` to `T.parse(RECV)` (two edits: `T.parse(` before the receiver, and `.parse::<T>()` to `)`), and the message names that spelling. The repro becomes `let v = i64.parse(piece).unwrap();` and prints 42; a parenthesized receiver keeps its parentheses around the call. Pinned by tests/turbofish_fix.rs; the two pins that held the delete (`"4".parse::<i64>()` there and in tests/parser.rs `method_turbofish_is_named_and_deleted`) are flipped.

title: `Vec[String].from_iter(it)` (an associated call on a type written with its generic arguments) passes `karac check` and fails `karac run` / `karac build` with "an expression with no recorded type is not lowered yet"; `let v: Vec[String] = Vec.from_iter(it)` runs
fix: FIXED by bd4d547c50. The qualified impl-table branch of `Type[Args].method(..)` (src/typechecker/method_identifier_receiver.rs) checked the arguments against a signature whose own generic parameters it never solved, so `node_call_subs` held the impl's `T` but not the method's `I`, and the typed HIR stopped on the unsolved parameter. It now pins the impl parameters from the written type arguments first, and when the method has parameters of its own it routes the call through `check_call_args_with_substitution_full` with the receiver substitution in scope, which solves them and checks their bounds against the pinned arguments (`Vec[String].from_iter(ints)` reports `I.Item = String` is not satisfied). Pinned by tests/mir_qualified_generic_calls.rs: `Vec[String].from_iter`, `Set[i64].from_iter` and a user `Bag[i64].of[I: Iterator[Item = T]]` run on every backend; control arm at the base was 0 passed, 2 failed.

title: A MIR binary that uses a Map or Set still links std's panic hook and backtrace symbolizer: kata 1's hash_map is 358,680 B on Linux against 71,768 B for its brute_force
detail: MEASURED on Linux x86_64 at 1f4c30c7de, which made the print path, run_main, exit, vec_reserve and the plain abort report panic-free (B-2026-10-28-36): katas 1 brute_force, 2, 4 and 5 now build to 68-72 KB with no `RUST_BACKTRACE` note in the binary, and kata 1's hash_map (KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 or not, same size) to 358,680 B with it. Its runtime imports are karac_hash_seed_ready, karac_hash_word, karac_hash_word_state, karac_mir_map_insert_hv and karac_mir_map_free beside the lean set. A section-level reachability walk of the lean archive's object (relocations, roots = the program's imports) finds two anchors: (1) karac_hash_word -> karac_hash::seed::init_once -> random_pair's SystemTime::now().duration_since (Timespec::sub_timespec's expect); the seed's std::env::var and Box::new (handle_alloc_error) reach panics too; (2) karac_mir_map_insert_hv -> mir_map::insert, whose assert!(at < TOMB) and Vec pushes (dead, hashes; capacity_overflow) reach core::panicking. Making these panic-free (clock_gettime / getenv / malloc on unix in hash/src/seed.rs; panic-free growth and an abort in place of the assert in runtime/src/mir_map.rs) is expected to bring a Map program to the same floor. Set and the other table natives not yet walked.
fix: b8cb6d95f0. Three panics stayed reachable from the table paths and each kept std's panic hook and DWARF symbolizer (about 250 KB) in the binary. (1) The hash seed read KARAC_HASH_SEED through std::env::var and the clock through SystemTime; on unix it now calls getenv, malloc and clock_gettime directly (hash/src/seed.rs), with the per-process key still random and the KARAC_HASH_SEED pin unchanged. (2) walk_index took % by the table length, whose zero case panics; it uses checked_rem (hash/src/lib.rs). (3) The table's side vectors grew through Vec and indexed slices, keeping the capacity-overflow and bounds panics; they are now LeanVec (runtime/src/lean_vec.rs), a Copy-only buffer that grows through karac_realloc_or_panic and aborts with a message on an out-of-bounds index, also replacing the print buffers' own Buf. Measured stripped on Linux: kata 1 hash_map 358,680 B to 71,768 B (now equal to its brute_force), a program inserting, removing and walking a Map, a Set and a SortedMap 359 KB to 80 KB, outputs identical. tests/mir_panic_free_floor.rs::mir_table_program_links_no_panic_hook pins it (expected output from a Python mirror). Gate green; lib:map/lib:set/lib:sortedmap corpus 153/153 on mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan; both TSan archives rebuilt and the TSan tests pass. macOS not measured (no target here).

title: A MIR program that reaches an auto-par site peaks about 1 MiB higher in RSS than its legacy build: kata 1's auto-par brute_force and hash_map at 2.4 MiB against 1.4 / 1.3 MiB
detail: Split out of B-2026-10-28-36, whose binary-size half 1f4c30c7de fixed; this half was not touched there and is NOT re-measured here. As recorded on the M5 Pro (macOS) at g04628b0eb: kata 1's auto-par brute_force and its hash_map build peak at 2.4 MiB RSS against 1.4 / 1.3 MiB on their 2026-07-28 legacy recordings, while the seq builds of katas 2 and 4 are flat at 1.0 MiB, so the pool's thread stacks and per-thread caches cost about 1 MiB once a program reaches an auto-par site. Next step: measure on Linux with KARAC_THREADS=1 and =N, and attribute the delta between worker stacks (1 GiB reserved each, committed as touched), per-thread allocator arenas and the executor's own tables.
fix: 0e42c916c4. Measured on Linux at 2f99e4ed9d first (peak RSS from wait4, min of 5): kata 1's auto-par brute_force peaked at 3.0 MiB and hash_map at 2.95 MiB, against 2.1 / 2.15 MiB in order and 2.4 / 2.4 MiB for legacy 741fbf08c1. The extra 0.85 MiB was the same at KARAC_THREADS=2, 4, 8 and 16 and unchanged under MALLOC_ARENA_MAX=1, so it was neither worker stacks nor allocator arenas. The cause: an auto-par loop's tasks took every Copy capture by value, so each of the 16 tasks held its own copy of the 40 KB input array. An auto-par loop's group is joined before the loop ends, so a fixed array its tasks only read is now borrowed (closure_value, src/mir/lower.rs). After the fix: brute_force 2.4 MiB and hash_map 2.55 MiB, at legacy's level; user CPU unchanged (929 vs 953 ms, min of 8). Pinned by tests/mir_auto_par_array_capture.rs (each loop's environment holds `ref Array[i64, 1000]`, with the array written between the two loops; in-order output on the interpreter and built). The macOS figures in the title were not re-measured.

title: `karac check` still refuses moving a binding after an iterator adapter's closure that only reads it (`h.iter().filter(|u| mask[*u % 2]).count(); let m2 = mask;`, "moved inside a loop"); B-2026-10-29-37's fix covers only a `let`-bound closure, and both MIR backends run the program correctly
fix: faedb308f5: the use classifier records the closure literals passed to a method of a function-level statement's receiver chain when nothing the statement leaves behind can hold them (the `let`'s value and the chain's root receiver have types built only from scalars, strings, the standard collections, Option and Result; an expression statement's value drops at the `;`), and the RC/UAM predicate skips a read in such a body when the consume lies outside the statement and the statement is not reachable from it (src/use_classifier.rs `record_statement_closures`, src/rc_predicate.rs `statement_closure_runs_before`). The row's `.filter(..).count()`, `.map(..).sum()` and `.filter(..).map(..).collect()` forms check and print the right answer. An iterator kept past the move, a move before the chain, a closure pushed into a `Vec[Fn(..)]`, and the pair inside a loop are still refused. Pinned by tests/core_adaptor_closure_read_before_move.rs; control: base 1 passed 1 failed, fix 2 passed; check sweep (corpus, kara-katas) unchanged.

title: A closure whose annotated parameter borrows (`|x: ref String|`), passed to an owning slot (`OnceFn(own T) -> U`: `Option.map`, `Result.map`, `into_iter().map`, a user generic), leaves the call's result type unsolved: "cannot infer type parameter 'U'"
fix: 3bf606519c: `unify_fn_param` (src/typechecker/inference.rs) now binds through a `ref` on the closure's side against an owned slot parameter, so a closure whose parameter borrows, passed where the slot hands the value over (`OnceFn(own T) -> U`), solves `T` and with it the slot's return. `Result.map(|x: ref String| x.len())`, `into_iter().map(|x: ref String| ..).collect()` and a user generic `ap(x, |s: ref String| s.len())` check and run. Legality is unchanged: `is_subtype` already accepted the pair (a weaker mode, core-semantics §4.7). Pinned by tests/core_borrowing_closure_solves_its_result.rs (check and MIR output); control: the base refuses the Result.map and user-generic forms, the fix accepts them. Thread B's five Option/Result map fixtures that regressed under D5 closures pass.

title: `karac fix` has no `own` fix for a closure's bare parameter given away by an `own self` method (it offers `#[derive(Copy)]`), by a writing method (it says `mut ref`), by `return x` / `let y = x; y` (the caller gets E0516 instead), or by a returned closure that captures it (E0509 at the store)
detail:
Found migrating B-2026-10-28-24's corpus list with `karac fix` once D5 closures were on. Three shapes where a closure's annotated bare parameter is given away get no machine fix, or the wrong one; the right fix in each is the parameter's `own`, which the closure's other give-away diagnostics already offer:

1. A method taking `own self` called on the parameter: `|t: S, k: i64| t.take() + k` (corpus fixtures/own_params/SRC). Ownership E0515 "cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place: this method takes `self` by value", whose replacement is `#[derive(Copy)]` on `S`; `karac fix` inserted it. The same holds for a function's bare parameter, `fn f(t: S) -> i64 { t.take() }`.
2. A method that writes its receiver: `|vv: Vec[i64]| vv.pop()` (fixtures/codegen/closures/test_e2e_closure_option_returning_method_tail). "`vv` is a shared `ref`, so `vv.pop` ... cannot modify it. Borrow it as `mut ref`", with no machine fix; for a closure that takes the vector, `|vv: own Vec[i64]|` is the fix.
3. The parameter handed back by `return x` or through a binding (`|x: R| { return x; }`, `|x: R| { let y = x; y }`, fixtures/codegen/families/b_2026_10_01_14/e2e_closure_handing_back_its_by_value_param_runs_its_body_once). `d5_closure_tail_gives_away` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) walks only the tail, so the closure is not reported and the caller gets E0516 "cannot drop the temporary value ... while `r` still borrows it", with no machine fix.
4. A closure that returns a closure capturing the parameter: `let make = |s: String| |x: i64| x + s.len(); fs.push(make(..))` (tests/mir_closure_results.rs). E0509 "a view of a temporary value is stored in an escaping closure ..." at the push, with no machine fix; the parameter's `own` is the fix.

These were migrated by hand in B-2026-10-28-24's commit.
fix:
864e30b6f9. Each of the four shapes now carries the parameter's `own` as its machine fix.
(1) An `own self` method on a bare parameter: the typechecker records the receiver in the new `core_own_param_receivers`, together with the `own ` insertion point and whether the parameter is a closure's. The C3 refusal in src/ownership/rc_promote.rs then offers `own` instead of `#[derive(Copy)]`, for closure and function parameters alike. One deliberate exception: a type with `.clone()` keeps the existing `.clone()` fix (B-2026-10-25-25's pin in core_strict_check.rs), because that edit is local while `own` changes the signature.
(2) A closure's writing method: core_ref_write binds an annotated bare closure parameter with a new `Origin::ClosureParam`. Its E0517 now says the parameter borrows and carries `|vv: own ...|`.
(3) and (4): `d5_closure_tail_gives_away` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) now also walks every `return v` outside a nested closure, follows a block's `let y = x;` alias to a tail `y` (reported at the `x`), and treats a tail closure as giving away every outer parameter its body names (inner parameters shadow).
Control: with the base binary, `karac fix` inserts `#[derive(Copy)]` for shape 1 and leaves shapes 2-4 with no fix. With the fix, all five programs check after one `karac fix` and run with the expected output.
Fixtures: tests/core_fix_own_given_away_params.rs, 2 tests. The negative test covers a shadowed function parameter, an inner closure parameter shadowing the outer one, and a Copy parameter. Check sweep: corpus and katas unchanged.

title: `method_param_modes` is keyed by `"Type.method"`, so a type with two impls of one operator trait (`impl Add for Col` with a borrowing `rhs: Col` and `impl Add[Flags] for Col` with `rhs: own Flags`) gives every `col + x` the LAST impl's parameter modes: `a + b` then `a + b` is refused as a use of moved `b`, though the impl `a + b` calls borrows it and the MIR build runs it
fix: FIXED by d07ed81b82. The typechecker records, beside `user_operator_calls`, `user_operator_impls`: for a type with more than one impl of the operator's trait with that method, the chosen impl's own `Type.method#k` (k = its place among them in source order, src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs record_user_operator). src/ownership.rs keys each trait impl method's self and parameter modes by `Type.method#k` too (TraitImplOrdinals), and src/use_classifier.rs operator_key reads that key first for binary, unary and compound-assignment operators. tests/core_d5_user_types.rs d5_two_operator_impls_on_one_type_keep_their_modes: `a + b` twice borrows through `impl Add for Col` in either impl order, and a second `a + f` through `impl Add[Flags]` (`own Flags`) is still a use of moved `f`. The effect checker still keys an operator call by `Type.method` (src/effectchecker/inference.rs), which merges two impls' effects; not seen to matter yet.

title: A program's own `struct Mask` is read as the SIMD scalar `Mask` by D5 (`COPY_SCALARS` in src/d5_params.rs lists "Mask" by name), so a bare `m: Mask` parameter is not rewritten to `ref Mask` and every call moves its argument: `count(m)` twice is refused as a use of moved `m`, and the same struct renamed `Bits` checks and runs
fix: FIXED by d07ed81b82. src/d5_params.rs borrow_bare_params: a program struct or enum named like a built-in scalar in `COPY_SCALARS` (`Mask`, `Vector`) shadows it, and unless it is `Copy`, `shared` or `sync` its name is taken out of the copied set, so a bare parameter of it borrows. tests/core_d5_user_types.rs d5_a_program_struct_named_mask_borrows: the row's repro, the same struct as `Bits`, an `enum Vector`, and a `Mask` right operand of `Mul`, each checked and run on __mir-run.

title: With a program `impl Mul[Col] for f64`, every `f64 * f64` in the program is attributed to that impl's `f64.mul` by the effect checker: a helper doing `*x * k` that the impl calls is reported as a mutual recursion group with `f64.mul`, and the impl's effects flow to every float multiplication
fix: 1b299d7160. `effectchecker::is_lowered_builtin_operator_call` recognises the `f64.mul(a, b)` the lowering writes for a built-in operator on two primitives: its callee carries the first argument's span, which `lowering::call_path` gives it and no written path has. `collect_calls_in_expr` (src/effectchecker/inference.rs) neither pushes such a call nor walks its callee path, which had read as a value reference to the program's `impl Mul[Col] for f64` under the same `method_bodies` key and was the edge behind the false recursion note. The concurrency walker (src/concurrency/effects_collect.rs) skips it too. The row's repro now checks clean, and a public `area(w, h) = w * h` beside a printing impl declares nothing. tests/effects_operator_impls.rs pins both; they fail on 71d681381d. The same work found the converse, that a mixed-type operator was never charged its impl at all: B-2026-10-29-51, fixed in the same commit.

title: A `let` closure whose parameter is typed `Str` still moves a `String` argument in `karac check` (`let skip = |n: Str| ..; skip(n); n.len()` is "moved here, used again here"); `|n: String|` and `fn skip(n: Str)` check, and `__mir-run` runs all three
fix: fb03e6df09: a function value's view slot borrows. `modes_of_fn_params` (src/use_classifier.rs), which reads the parameter modes of a call through a closure binding or a function-typed value off its type, mapped only `ref` / `mut ref` to a borrow, so a `Str` slot (lowered `StringSlice`) took its `String` argument by move. It now maps `StringSlice` and `Slice[T]` to `Ref` and `mut Slice[T]` to `MutRef`, as `param_modes_from_signature` does for a function's parameters. Pinned by tests/core_closure_view_param_borrows.rs (`|n: Str|` with a `String`, `|s: Slice[i64]|` with a `Vec`; check passes and the MIR interpreter prints `true b` / `3 3`). The control (the binary before fb03e6df09) refuses the `Str` case with "value 'n' moved here, used again here". Writing the negative case found that a call through a `let` closure never moves an owned argument in check at all: B-2026-10-30-2.

title: An auto-par task's loop takes its run's bounds as plain captures, so LLVM knows nothing of the counter's range: kata 4's `k % R` becomes a signed 64-bit magic division in the task (about 10 instructions) where the in-order loop, knowing 0 <= k < 10M, uses a 32-bit unsigned one (about 5)
detail: MEASURED on Linux x86_64 at 5b6aab2a3c, bench/binary_search_partition.kara, objdump of the built binary. In-order loop: `mov %edx,%eax; imul $0x10624dd3,%rax,%rax; shr $0x26,%rax; imul $0x3e8,%eax,%eax; sub`. Task loop (main.ap0 inlined): `movabs $0x20c49ba5e353f7cf; imul; mov; shr $0x3f; sar $7; add; imul $0x3e8; sub; neg`, with the counter itself reloaded from the stack. Each task gets `lo` and `hi` as captures, and the spawn computed them from the loop's own range, so `lo >= start` and `hi <= end` hold. Nothing tells LLVM that (no llvm.assume, no range metadata on the capture loads), so it cannot narrow the remainder or the counter's arithmetic. This is about 5 of the remaining 27 instructions per iteration over the in-order build (866 M vs 600 M) after B-2026-10-28-35. Suggested remedy (unverified): when the loop's start is a non-negative constant or a value already known non-negative, assume 0 <= lo <= hi <= end in the task.
fix: 30e4af977d: an auto-par task now clamps its run's captured lo and hi to the bounds the lowering knows: a `for`'s literal or constant-`let` start and end, or a counting `while`'s end and its counter's `let` on the way in when no statement in between names the counter (src/mir/lower.rs, `counter_start`, `bound_const`, the chunk's clamp). The clamp is a no-op that LLVM reads as the counter's range, and it can only shorten a run. `KARAC_AUTO_PAR_RANGE=0` leaves the bounds unstated. MEASURED on Linux x86_64, release, kata 4's bench (binary_search_partition), callgrind, two workers: 865.6M -> 855.6M instructions, against 599.7M in order. objdump: the task's `k % R` went from the signed 64-bit magic (`movabs; imul; shr $63; sar $7; add`) to an unsigned one (`shr $3; mulx; shr $4`). It is not the in-order loop's 32-bit form: LLVM 18 does not narrow the urem when the loop exits at a non-constant `k < smin(hi, 10M)`. That remainder is B-2026-10-31-3. Pinned by tests/mir_auto_par_range_facts.rs (the clamps in the IR, absent under KARAC_AUTO_PAR_RANGE=0, and the in-order output at four workers).

title: An operator whose operands differ in type (`v * 2.0` on `impl Mul[f64] for V`, `2.0 * c` on `impl Mul[Col] for f64`) is never charged its impl's effects: a public function whose body is `v * 2.0` passes `karac check` with no declaration while the impl prints, though `v.mul(2.0)` in its place is asked for `with writes(Stdout)`
fix: 1b299d7160. The typechecker's `user_operator_calls` now reaches the effect checker: it is a new parameter of `effectcheck_with_typecheck_tables`, which `Pipeline::effectcheck_phase` (src/cli.rs) and the test helpers pass, and `EffectChecker::with_user_operator_calls` stores it. The `Binary` arm of `collect_calls_in_expr` charges the impl the table names for that operator. The probe now reports `scale` as well as `twice`, and `2.0 * c` on a printing `impl Mul[Col] for f64` asks its public caller for `with writes(Stdout)`. tests/effects_operator_impls.rs pins both shapes plus a declared caller that passes; both fail on 71d681381d. Effect entry points that do not pass the table (`effectcheck_with_typecheck_data`, the effect-graph route) still leave such an operator uncharged, as they leave a bound call charged every impl.

title: Check reads a bare `dyn Trait` parameter as owned (d5_params skips `dyn`) while the MIR builder borrows it, so `fn keep(v: mut ref Vec[dyn Shape], s: dyn Shape) { v.push(s) }` passes check and MIR refuses it
detail:
Found landing the dyn front end. Under D5 a bare parameter borrows unless its type is copied or a counted handle (core-semantics §4.1). The MIR builder's `param_mode_ty` (src/mir/lower.rs) applies that to a `dyn Trait` parameter: it is lowered as `ref dyn Trait`. The strict check's rewrite (`borrows` in src/d5_params.rs) matches only Path, Tuple and Array types, so a `TypeKind::Dyn` parameter stays owned there: the check moves the caller's argument and lets the body store it. The two disagree in both directions:

1. `fn keep(v: mut ref Vec[dyn Shape], s: dyn Shape) { v.push(s) }` called as `keep(mut v, Sq { s: 3 })`: check passes; `karac run` refuses at the MIR build with "cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place". Before the dyn front end, the router shape `fn add(mut ref self, h: escaping dyn Handler) { self.routes.push(h) }` failed the same way; `escaping` parameters are now owned in MIR (`fn_param_owned`), so only the bare form is left.
2. `let s: dyn Shape = Sq { s: 2 }; show(s); show(s);` with `fn show(s: dyn Shape) -> i64`: check reports "value 's' moved here, used again here" at the second call; `karac __mir-run` borrows and prints 4 twice.

The spec reading is MIR's: a bare `dyn` parameter borrows, `escaping dyn` (or `own dyn`) owns it. The fix is a `TypeKind::Dyn` arm in `borrows` that returns true unless the parameter's type span is in `Program::escaping_fn_types`, plus the corpus/kata migration for any program that stores a bare `dyn` parameter (expect `escaping`).
fix: d423e29660: the strict check's D5 rewrite (`borrows` in src/d5_params.rs) gains a `TypeKind::Dyn` arm, so a bare `s: dyn Shape` parameter reads as `ref dyn Shape`, the mode the MIR builder's `param_mode_ty` already gave it. `own dyn Shape` stays owned, and so does `escaping dyn Shape`: the item rewrite (`param_borrows`) skips a parameter whose type span is in `Program::escaping_fn_types`. Pinned by tests/core_dyn_param_borrows.rs: `show(s); show(s)` checks and prints `4` twice, `own dyn` and `escaping dyn` parameters can be stored, and storing a bare one is refused with the `s: own dyn Shape` fix-it. The control (the binary before d423e29660) refuses the first with "value 's' moved here, used again here" and accepts the last. Corpus and kara-katas check sweeps and the `dyn` corpus run under mir-interp are unchanged.

title: A call through a `let` closure never moves an owned argument in check: `let take = |n: own String| n.len(); take(n); take(n)` passes check, and `__mir-run` refuses it ("use of _3, which may have been moved")
detail: Found writing B-2026-10-29-49's negative fixture. With `let take = |n: own String| n.len(); let n = "b".to_string(); let k = take(n);` a later read of `n` (`println(f"{k} {n}")`), or a second `take(n)`, passes `karac check`; the MIR builder's move check refuses both with "move check main: bb9[0]: use of _3, which may have been moved or never initialized". The same holds with a consuming body (`|n: own String| { let m = n; m.len() }`) and with the pre-flip spelling `|n: String|` under `KARAC_D5_CLOSURES=0`, so it predates B-2026-10-28-24. The call is classified in `use_classifier.rs` (`fn_typed_callee_modes`, which maps a function value's non-`ref` slot to `Own`) and in the legacy state machine (`arg_is_borrow_position`), so the place to look is why the `Own` mode does not reach the use-after-move predicate for a closure binding's call (a closure is a nameable callee with no `callee_param_modes` entry).
fix: f9f5e22871. The framing was right, but the cause was a name collision. The `take` in the row's program is the stdlib's `fn take[T: Default](dest: mut ref T)` (runtime/stdlib/mem.kara), so `callee_modes_for_call` found an entry under the closure binding's name and read `take(n)` as a borrow; `fn_typed_callee_modes` was never reached. Renamed to `eat`, the same program was already refused. The fix: a local binding or parameter now shadows a function of the same name in both check pipelines. In src/use_classifier.rs, a callee that is in `param_types` / `local_types` takes its own type's modes (and skips the imported-name read default). In src/ownership/expr_check.rs, a callee in `states` / `param_types` takes the function-value consume default instead of the table's modes. The reverse direction is covered too: a borrowing local closure named like an owning user fn borrows. Control: the base binary accepts the read-after, call-twice and `take: Fn(own String)` parameter forms; the fix refuses all three with "value 'n' moved here, used again here", matching MIR. Fixtures: tests/core_local_callee_shadows_fn.rs (2 tests, including the borrowing negative). Check sweep: corpus and katas unchanged.

title: `mir::concat` moved the left side of `a + b` into the add while a closure still borrowed it: `let f = || println(a); let b = a + "y"; f()` printed freed bytes (compiled) and the MIR interpreter stopped on a read through a reference to an uninitialized value
detail: Found 2026-10-29 while extending the pass for B-2026-10-28-42 part 2. take_concat_lefts checked only that nothing but the add's own borrow `_r = &_t` mentioned `_t` before the add and nothing but drops after it; a borrow taken EARLIER and read after the add (a closure capture `_2 = &_1`) was invisible to both checks, so the add took `_t`'s buffer while the capture still pointed at it. Reproduction (main at 1d1b2b104c): fn mk() -> String { String.from("ab") + "c" } fn main() { let a = mk(); let f = || println(a); let b = a + "yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"; f(); println(b); } -> compiled prints garbage then abcyyy..; KARAC_MIR_CONCAT=0 prints abc; `karac __mir-run` reports `print through a reference to an uninitialized value`. Kāra has no `&` expression, so a closure capture is the user-visible way to hold such a borrow. Present since the pass landed in 37548799f9 (2026-10-19).
fix: FIXED by de113d6d66 (2026-10-29): take_concat_lefts takes `_t` only when every other borrow of it ends at the call it is made for (`_b = &_t` moved into its block's call, used nowhere else, with a result that holds no borrow), so a closure capture that outlives the add makes the add copy. Pinned by tests/mir_concat_chains.rs (`captured`, compiled vs interpreter; negative-controlled: removing the check fails it) and the unit test a_left_a_closure_borrows_is_copied.

title: A closure that writes a provider, made into a `Fn` value (`twice(|| { Clk.bump(); Clk.now() })` under `with_provider`), is refused by MIR: "a closure that writes `R`'s provider, made into a `Fn` value, is not lowered yet"
detail: `karac check` accepts a non-escaping `Fn` value whose body writes a bound resource; every MIR backend refused it in `src/mir/providers.rs` `carry_request`, because a `Fn` value borrows its environment shared and the borrow checker read the carried `mut ref` provider behind it as read-only (E0517 once the refusal was lifted). tests/mir_build.rs mir_closures_inside_with_provider_reach_the_provider pinned the refusal (`apply(|| { Clk.bump(); tick() })`), and the corpus fixture mir_closures_inside_with_provider_reach_the_provider__writes expected error:codegen. Found writing the v1 integration pin. A stored (escaping) callback that reaches the provider stays refused, as §14.5 requires (B-2026-10-30-7).
fix: FIXED by d0e0acb943. src/mir/providers.rs carry_request no longer refuses a carried closure that writes a provider through a shared (`Fn`) environment; the carried `mut ref` stays in its captures, and src/mir/borrowck.rs through_shared_ref lets a deref of a `mut ref` field of a carried closure type (providers::is_carried) be written through the environment lent shared. The loan is kept, so a stored (escaping) callback that reaches the provider is still refused (§14.5, B-2026-10-30-7). tests/mir_build.rs mir_closures_inside_with_provider_reach_the_provider now runs the writing closure on the interpreter and compiled (flipped from the refusal); the corpus fixture __writes expects its output; tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs provider_fn_value_writes_the_provider covers a generic and a `Fn` parameter.

title: `karac test` refuses a package `karac check` and `karac build` accept: its per-module typecheck reports type errors (`map` on a `Vec` from `split`, an `escaping Fn` push, `Map.get(Str)`) that the v2 check of the combined source does not
detail: src/cli/test_cmd.rs `test_front` ran the legacy per-module `typecheck_modules` and stopped on any type error, while `karac check` (package_check_on, `refuses_only_by_type`) and the build defer a type-only refusal to the strict v2 check of the amalgam. The v1 integration pin (tests/fixtures/v1_service) failed `karac test` with five such errors, some attributed to main.kara for code in main_test.kara, though check passed and every backend ran main.
fix: FIXED by d0e0acb943. src/cli/test_cmd.rs test_front: under the v2 runner (`core_places`) a per-module type error no longer stops the run; the strict v2 check of the combined source decides, as for `karac check` and the build (refuses_only_by_type). Pinned by tests/mir_v1_service.rs (its package used split/map, an escaping Fn push and Map.get(Str), which the per-module pass refused).

title: A closure that reaches a provider and is run by the runtime under `with_provider` (`tg.spawn(|| Clk.now())`, a `sort_by` comparison, a `retain` predicate) fails on every MIR backend: "TaskGroup.spawn: no body for closure DefId(..)"
detail: core semantics §14.9 lets tasks and branches inside a `with_provider` use the provider. `src/mir/providers.rs` carried a closure's providers only where it is erased to a `Fn` value or called directly; a closure handed to a native the runtime runs (TaskGroup.spawn, sort_by, retain, get_or_init) kept its plain type, and its body, which needs the bound resource, was removed with no copy made. The interpreter reported "no body for closure" and the LLVM backend "no body for `closure#N()`". It also hit a task spawned through a function taking the closure (`both(|| Clk.now())`).
fix: FIXED by d0e0acb943. src/mir/providers.rs carry_native: a closure that reaches a bound resource and is an argument of a native the runtime runs (no MIR body, not with_provider or a resource method, outside library bodies) is passed as its copy carrying the providers. A task that writes a provider-rooted resource's provider is refused by name (task_writes) until the check enforces §14.9 (B-2026-10-30-6). tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs: provider_tasks_read_the_provider, provider_reached_from_natives_and_par, provider_tasks_writing_the_provider_are_refused.

title: `karac check` lets two tasks inside a `with_provider` write the provider at once (core semantics §14.9): `tg.spawn(|| { Clk.bump(); .. })` twice, or one task beside the spawner's own `Clk.bump()`; MIR refuses a task that writes a provider-rooted resource's provider meanwhile
detail: §14.9: "A branch that writes `R` conflicts with any other that uses it (§11.2), with `R` as the place", and readers need a `CrossTask` provider (`E_NOT_CROSS_TASK` at the `with_provider`). `karac check` reports neither for tasks. Since the fix for B-2026-10-30-5 carries the provider into tasks, `src/mir/providers.rs` `task_writes` refuses any task that writes the bound provider of a provider-rooted resource ("a task that writes `Clk`'s provider is not run yet"), which is stricter than §14.9 (one writing task with no other user is legal). A task writing an override of a program-rooted resource (a `Network` fake) ran before and still runs, unchecked. Once the check enforces §14.9 that refusal can go. Pinned by tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs provider_tasks_writing_the_provider_are_refused.
fix: fcd68a7848 checks §14.9 for tasks in the MIR effect pass (`src/mir/effects/task_providers.rs`), which `karac check` and every run share. A `TaskGroup.spawn`'s task borrows the provider of each provider-rooted resource its closure needs, `mut ref` when it writes it, from the spawn until the group's `Drop` (§9.5), or to the end of the body when the group is borrowed. Refused, E0424 (`TaskProviderConflict`, class EffectConflict): a second task of the group using a provider a live task writes, a looped spawn of a writing task, and the spawner using the provider while a writing task lives, or writing it while a reading task lives. A function that spawns into a group it is lent counts as a spawn at its call (escaping-task summaries), and an inner `with_provider` in a task supplies its own provider. With check enforcing it, provider specialisation's blanket `task_writes` refusal is gone (agreed with Thread B), so one writing task runs. Pins: corpus/core/err_provider_tasks_write, corpus/core/ok_provider_task_writes (prints 22); tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs `provider_tasks_writing_the_provider_are_refused` (flipped: check refuses it now), `provider_one_task_writes_the_provider`, `provider_tasks_sharing_a_written_provider_are_refused` (two tasks, looped, spawner writes, lent group). Program-rooted overrides are not checked before specialisation; that remainder is B-2026-10-30-10.

title: `karac check` misses §14.5 when the provider is bound out of sight: a callback that reaches a resource stored through an `escaping` parameter in a function called under `with_provider`, or in a test under `#[with_provider(..)]`, passes the check and is refused by the MIR borrow checker as E0509 "a view of (*_1) is stored in an escaping closure"
detail: src/provider_escape.rs reports `provider_escape` ("cannot be passed to an `escaping` parameter: a provider cannot leave its scope") only for a closure written inside the `with_provider` closure itself. `fn audit() with reads(Clk) { bus.reg(|| Clk.now()); .. }` called as `with_provider[Clk](F{..}, || audit())`, passes `karac check`, and the same registration in a `#[with_provider(FileSystem, MemFs.new)] test` passes the front end of `karac test`; MIR refuses with a borrow-check message that names a MIR local and, under `karac test`, a line of the combined source. Pinned by tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs provider_stored_callback_is_refused (PREDICTS this row).
