fix: e104887c31. `check_core_provider_escape` (src/provider_escape.rs) now carries the provider scopes a caller binds. New `scopes_bound_by_callers` collects every function called inside a `with_provider[R]` / `providers {}` binding (a test's `#[with_provider]` lowers to one), then walks the call graph breadth-first over each body's callees: by bare name or `Type.method` for calls, and by method name for method calls. Each function inherits its callers' scopes. A callback in such a function that uses R and is stored, returned or passed to an `escaping` parameter is now refused in `karac check` (E0600). The message names the caller ("a caller of `audit` binds"), or, when the closure sits in a test body, "this test's `#[with_provider]` binds". Control: the base binary accepts both the bus-with-a-Stdout-override program and the test project; the fix refuses both. Fixtures: tests/core_provider_escape_through_callers.rs (2 tests, one including the no-override negative). Two of Thread B's pins were flipped because check now refuses earlier: tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs provider_stored_callback_is_refused (per backend), and tests/mir_v1_service.rs v1_service_stored_callback_under_a_fake_names_its_file (accepts the JSON file/line form). Check sweep: corpus and katas unchanged.

title: `karac test` reports a MIR build error at a line of the combined package source (`borrow check __test__root__103_..: 292:5: ..`), not at the file and line it came from
detail: src/cli/test_v2.rs `cmd_test_v2` builds the amalgam of the package and its test companions; a MIR error is a plain string with amalgam spans and the build_error event carries it verbatim, with no `file`. A registration in the v1 integration pin's main_test.kara was reported at 292:5. Diagnostics from the v2 check (E0423) are mapped back already.
fix: FIXED by 71d1ac24b9. src/cli/project_v2.rs remap_build_error now maps every `L:C` place in a MIR build error (after a space or at the start, ending at `:`, `)`, a space or the end) through the package's source map, not only `L:C in `f``: a borrow-check refusal reads `borrow check f: src/main_test.kara:12:5: .. (borrow at bb5[1] at src/main_test.kara:12:18)`. Unit test remap_build_error_names_every_place_by_file; tests/mir_v1_service.rs v1_service_stored_callback_under_a_fake_names_its_file pins it under `karac test` on both executors.

title: `fn make() -> dyn Shape with reads(Clock) { .. }` gives the function the clause and the `dyn` return type none, silently; the clause reaches a `dyn` return only through an alias or a wrapper (`-> Option[dyn Shape with reads(Clock)]`)
detail: design.md § `dyn Trait` lets a `with` clause stand on any `dyn` type and lists a return as a coercion position, but a trailing `with` after a return type is parsed as the function's own clause, as it is after `-> Fn(..) -> R`. Measured at e722d66535: `fn make() -> dyn Shape with reads(Clock) { Loud { s: 1 } }` (Loud.area prints) checks clean, while `type Gauge = dyn Shape with reads(Clock); fn make() -> Gauge { Loud { s: 1 } }` and `-> Option[dyn Shape with reads(Clock)]` are refused at the coercion (`returned value coerces Loud to dyn Shape with reads(Clock), but Loud.area has effect writes(Stdout)`). Nothing tells the author which reading was taken. A spec decision (parenthesised return types, or a diagnostic when the function's clause follows a `dyn` return) is the review thread's; the parser change follows it.
fix: 9421ed2be2 adds the `return_clause_on_fn` lint (W0290), per the review thread's ruling on this row. In return position a trailing `with` still belongs to the function. The lint fires when a bare `dyn` or function return type with no clause of its own is followed by the function's clause, on functions and trait methods. Its message names both spellings: `-> (dyn T with X)` gives the clause to the value, and `-> (dyn T) with X` keeps it the function's. The parser records parenthesized return types (`Program::paren_return_types`), so the second spelling states the function reading on purpose and is silent, and `karac fmt` keeps those parentheses. `#[allow(return_clause_on_fn)]` silences it. design.md § `dyn Trait` already describes the rule. Pinned by tests/return_clause_on_fn.rs (7 tests: dyn, function type, trait method, both parenthesized spellings, a non-dyn return, allow, fmt). A `karac check` sweep over corpus/ found no program that trips it.

title: `karac check` passes two `TaskGroup` tasks that both write an override of a program-rooted resource (`with_provider[Stdout](cap, ..)` with each task printing), which the run refuses with a MIR borrow-check E0516 naming internal places (`main.c0{Stdout=Cap}: bb7[3]: mutable borrow of (*_2)`)
detail: The fix for B-2026-10-30-6 (fcd68a7848) checks core semantics §14.9 for tasks in the MIR effect pass, before provider specialisation, and only for provider-rooted resources: a program-rooted resource may be at its default in a body, which tasks share freely (two tasks may both print), and whether a body runs under an override is known only once providers are specialised. Probe: a `Cap` implementing `StdoutProvider` with `write(mut ref self, s: Str)` counting calls; `with_provider[Stdout](Cap { n: 0 }, || { let tg = TaskGroup.new(); let a = tg.spawn(|| { println("a"); 1 }); let b = tg.spawn(|| { println("b"); 2 }); a.join() + b.join() })`. `karac check`: All checks passed. `karac run`: error[mir]: borrow check main.c0{Stdout=Cap}: 10:17: bb7[3]: mutable borrow of (*_2) while it is borrowed mutably (borrow at bb4[3] at 9:17) [E0516]. So the race is caught, but by the post-specialisation borrow checker, with a message that names MIR places, and check does not report it. A fix could run the same task check per specialised instance (the override is known there), or mark in the effect pass which bodies run under an override of a program-rooted resource (the with_provider closures and providers blocks, and what they reach).
fix: 8f3182f638 takes the review thread's preferred option: the MIR effect pass marks which bodies can run under an override of a program-rooted resource (`Analysis::overridden` in src/mir/effects/task_providers.rs): the closure a `with_provider[R]` call is given, a body with a `providers` block binding `R`, and everything those call or make. In those bodies the §14.9 task check from B-2026-10-30-6 covers `R` as it does a provider-rooted resource, so `karac check` reports the probe as E0424 with the §14.9 wording ("this task uses `Stdout` while the task spawned at line 14, which writes `Stdout`, may still run"), before specialisation. A body that also runs at the default is checked all the same, since its tasks race under the override; tasks printing outside every override still run; the library's own bodies are not checked for an override. Pins: corpus/core/err_provider_override_tasks_write; tests/mir_provider_callbacks.rs `provider_tasks_writing_an_override_are_refused` (through a helper the override's closure calls) and `provider_tasks_printing_at_the_default_run`. A check sweep over every corpus program with a provider and tasks found no new refusal.

title: `karac check` accepts `*r = other` through a `mut ref dyn Trait`, which design.md § dyn Trait makes an error (the new value may have another type and size); MIR runs it
detail: Found probing the dyn check gaps after B-2026-10-29-45. `fn swap_in(r: mut ref dyn Shape) { *r = Ci { r: 2 }; }` called on a `dyn Shape` holding `Sq { s: 3 }` passes `karac check`, and `__mir-run` prints 12 (the `Ci`'s area). design.md § dyn Trait: "A `mut ref dyn Trait` cannot replace the value it views: `*r = other` is an error, because the new value may have another type and size. Assign the owned `dyn Trait` itself, which drops the old value first." The typechecker's `*r = v` arm (src/typechecker/items.rs) refuses only a `ref T` target.
fix: 72540f41c6. The typechecker's `*r = v` arm (src/typechecker/items.rs) now refuses a `mut ref dyn Trait` target with E_DYN_REPLACE_THROUGH_VIEW, citing design.md § dyn Trait: the new value may have another type and size. Its help names the two legal routes: assign the owned `dyn` itself, or call a `mut ref self` method through the view. Control: the base binary accepts the program, and MIR runs it and prints 12. Fixtures: tests/core_dyn_view_and_stdlib_supertraits.rs, `a_mut_ref_dyn_cannot_replace_the_value_it_views`, with the owned-assignment negative `assigning_the_owned_dyn_itself_replaces_it` (runs to 12). One case was flipped: the kata thread's tests/mir_dyn_effects.rs fixture wrote `*s = Loud { .. }` through a `mut ref dyn` to make a callee change a local's concrete type. Its swap_in now only calls through the view, and `local_written_by_callee` became `local_lent_to_a_callee`, which is accepted: under the rule, a callee lent the local cannot change its type or its effects. Check sweep: corpus and katas unchanged; corpus `dyn` subset unchanged.

title: `E_DYN_NOT_DISPATCHABLE` never judges a standard-library supertrait: `trait T: PartialEq` makes `dyn T` legal although `PartialEq.eq` names `Self` outside the receiver
detail: Found probing the dyn check gaps. `dyn_first_undispatchable` (src/typechecker/dyn_dispatchable.rs, 4bc6c9d802) looks a trait's declaration up in the program's own items only, so a baked standard-library trait was skipped as "not judged". `trait T: PartialEq { fn n(ref self) -> i64; }` with `let x: dyn T = A { v: 1 };` passes check and runs. design.md § dyn Trait requires every required method of the trait and of its supertraits to be dispatchable; `eq(ref self, other: ref Self)` is not. The library's declarations are in `crate::prelude::STDLIB_PROGRAMS`.
fix: 72540f41c6. `dyn_first_undispatchable` (src/typechecker/dyn_dispatchable.rs) now falls back to `crate::prelude::STDLIB_PROGRAMS` for a trait the program does not declare. A baked standard-library supertrait is therefore judged like a program's own: `trait T: PartialEq` makes `dyn T` E_DYN_NOT_DISPATCHABLE, naming `eq` "(from its supertrait `PartialEq`)". When the offending method is the library's, the help says "Drop the supertrait `PartialEq`" rather than "Give `eq` a default body" (src/typechecker/dyn_trait.rs). Control: the base binary accepts the program and runs it. Fixtures: tests/core_dyn_view_and_stdlib_supertraits.rs, `a_standard_library_supertrait_is_judged_for_dispatchability`, plus the negative `dyn_display_and_dyn_iterator_stay_usable` (`dyn Named: Display`, `dyn Display`, `Vec[dyn Iterator[Item = i64]]` check and run). Check sweep and corpus `dyn` subset unchanged.

title: A plain `dyn Trait` MOVED into a `TaskGroup.spawn` closure passes `karac check` and runs, so a concrete value holding a `shared` handle (non-atomic count) crosses a task boundary
detail: Found probing the dyn check gaps. `let j: dyn Job = J { c: Cell { n: 3 } };` (`Cell` a `shared struct`) and `g.spawn(|| { let k = j; k.run() })` pass `karac check`, and `__mir-run` prints 3. design.md § dyn Trait: `dyn Trait` is not `CrossTask`; only `dyn Trait + CrossTask` may cross, each coercion checking the concrete type; "a view follows the view rules". The typechecker's capture check (src/typechecker/cross_task_check.rs) skips every `DynCrossTask` failure, because a task may VIEW a `dyn` value and that pass sees no capture modes; the ownership pass's `closure_captures` has them (`Own` here), but nothing re-checks. A read-only capture (`g.spawn(|| j.run())`) stays legal under the view rules.
fix:
15479807f6. The typechecker's spawn capture check (src/typechecker/cross_task_check.rs) still defers a plain `dyn` capture, since a task may view one and that pass sees no capture modes. It now records each deferral in the new `TypeCheckResult.core_dyn_task_captures`, keyed by the closure's span. The ownership pass's `core_move_errors` (src/ownership/rc_promote.rs) reads `closure_captures` for that closure and refuses a capture whose mode is `Own`, with the new `OwnershipErrorKind::DynMovedIntoTask` (code E_NOT_CROSS_TASK). The message says the value behind the `dyn` may hold a `shared` handle; the help is "write `dyn Job + CrossTask` ... or let the task borrow `j`". The `Own` mode covers a move by the body and the §9.5 move of a value that drops before its group.
Control: the base binary accepts both moving forms and the row's program.
Fixtures: tests/core_dyn_moved_into_task.rs. `a_task_cannot_take_a_plain_dyn_by_move` covers the body move and the declared-after-group case. `a_task_may_view_a_plain_dyn_or_move_a_cross_task_one` checks that a view and a move of a `dyn Job + CrossTask` both check and run.
Check sweep: corpus and katas unchanged.

title: design.md § `as` casts promises `redundant_cast` (an identity cast) and `lossless_cast` (an `as` whose widening is implicit where it stands, its fix removing the `as`), but neither lint exists, so `x as i64` with `x: i64` passes silently and `karac fix` cannot drop it; and `true as bool`, which the same table calls the identity, is refused with E0210
fix: FIXED by 8bd1a4d307. Both lints are in the registry (src/lints.rs) and emitted from the typechecker's Cast arm (`lint_unneeded_cast`, src/typechecker/exprs.rs) as W0291 (E0291 when denied). `redundant_cast` flags an `as` to the type its operand already has; `check_cast_pair` now accepts `bool as bool`, the table's identity. `lossless_cast` flags a lossless integer or float widening where check_expr wants the target type (a binding, argument, return or field). Each carries a fix deleting the `as` and its type when the operand ends at its own span (a place, call, method call or index). Integer to `f64` is not flagged, since an operator's operand needs that `as`, nor is a literal operand. The row's repro now warns three times and `karac fix` removes all three. Pinned by tests/cast_lints.rs; control arm on fc37308403's src: 0 passed, 1 failed. A scan of about 14,800 corpus files found 310 warnings in 217 files and none in library code; three of them fixed with `karac fix` still print their expected output. `karac lint --list`, which design.md names, is still an unknown command; that is left to the doc owner.

title: A resource method with a bare `self` is charged `writes(R)`, not `reads(R)` as core-semantics §14.2 says: `karac query effects` reports `writes(UserDB)` for the README's own `fetch_users`, whose comment says `reads(UserDB)`, and the automatic-parallelism analysis serialises two reads of one resource as a write conflict, while the `par` check accepts the same pair
fix: 1a5e7ccb08: the front-end effect checker seeds `R.m(..)` with the receiver's verb, and took a bare `self` for an owned one on any path that had not rewritten bare parameters as borrows (`karac query effects` and `karac query concurrency` read the source without the check's D5 rewrite, while the MIR par check already read `mut ref self` alone as a write). Under D5 a bare `self` is now `reads(R)` whatever the path; `mut ref self` stays `writes(R)`; `own self` (which §14.2 forbids through a resource) and a bare `self` with `KARAC_D5=0` keep `writes(R)`, so E0412 still fires with D5 off. The row's repro now reports `a`/`b` `reads(UserDB)`, `c` `writes(UserDB)`, and `report`'s statements 0 and 1 as a parallel group ("concurrent reads on same resource"); README.md's example reports `fetch_users` `reads(UserDB)`, `fetch_orders` `reads(OrderDB)`, and a group "independent reads on different resources". Pinned by tests/resource_receiver_verbs.rs (2 tests); tests/effectchecker.rs `test_resource_receiver_contradiction_owned_self_reads_only` flipped (a bare `self` with a `reads(Cfg)` clause is consistent, no E0412).

title: `karac fmt` drops every comment: `// top`, a comment line inside a body and a trailing `// note` all vanish from its output, so formatting any real file loses its comments
fix: FIXED by 99e4590cf5. The formatter now lifts comments out of the source: the gaps between lexer tokens, plus the `///` and `//!` tokens. It writes each comment back at the next line boundary past its offset, which is before an item, statement, field, variant, impl or trait member, match arm, or closing brace (src/formatter/comments.rs). A comment that ended a line of code goes back on the end of that line. An own-line comment keeps its own line, and the blank line before or after it. Anything left over is written at the end of the file, so a comment can move but is never lost. Imports and impl methods keep their source order when a comment sits among them. `karac fmt` and `karac::format_source` (the LSP's format) both go through `format_program_with_comments`. The same commit also quotes `test "name"`, which had lost its quotes, and drops the `;` the formatter added after `if`/`for`/`match` statements; both are part of B-2026-10-30-29, which stays open for the rest of its list. Swept over the 20,031 corpus files fmt accepts: no comment lost, and no new re-parse or idempotence failure (596 files fail to re-parse, the same count as the base, which is B-2026-10-30-29's work). Pinned by tests/fmt_comments.rs.

title: `karac query ownership app.kara` (a bare file, as the other kinds accept) fails with `error: cannot read 'app': No such file or directory`, splitting the file name at its dot
detail:
Found in the dogfood rehearsal (karac at 57d9695f4e, release build from a fresh clone): README.md's query table lists `ownership` beside `effects`, `concurrency`, `cost-summary`, `monomorphization` and `affected-by`, which all accept `app.kara`. `karac query ownership app.kara` prints `error: cannot read 'app': No such file or directory (os error 2)` and exits 1. `karac query ownership app.kara.total` works. `karac help` says per-function kinds take `<file>.<function>`, but `effects` and `concurrency` are per-function kinds too and accept the bare file, listing every function.

Expected: `ownership` on a bare file lists every function as the others do, or at least says it wants `<file>.<function>` rather than reporting a missing file named `app`.
fix: FIXED by 76b022a676. `karac query ownership app.kara` (a bare `.kara` target) now prints `{"functions":[...]}`, each function's object in name order, the way `effects` and `concurrency` treat a bare file. `app.kara.f` still gives the one function (src/cli/args.rs, src/cli/query_cmd.rs). Pinned by tests/cli_rehearsal.rs karac_query_ownership_on_a_bare_file_lists_every_function. Seen while testing, filed separately: the query reports a declared `s: own String` as mode "ref", because the mode comes from usage (base does the same).

title: `karac run` with no file inside a project fails with `error: missing file argument`, while `karac check`, `karac build` and `karac test` with no file all work on the project
detail:

Expected: `karac run` with no file runs the project's entry (`src/main.kara`), as `cargo run` does.
fix: FIXED by 76b022a676. `karac run` with no file, inside a project (a kara.toml found walking up from the current directory, and a src/main.kara present), runs that src/main.kara; program arguments still go after `--`. `--no-manifest` and running outside a project keep the error, which now carries a help line (src/cli/args.rs). Pinned by tests/cli_rehearsal.rs karac_new_cli_scaffolds_a_tool_that_runs_and_tests.

title: `karac new <name> --cli` scaffolds the same hello-world `src/main.kara` and placeholder test as a plain `karac new`, though `karac help` describes `--cli` as the command-line tool skeleton
detail:

title: Moving a value while a returned reference into it is live (README's `name_of` example) says `help: drop the slice borrow before moving the source`, though the borrow is a returned `ref String`, not a slice
detail:
Found in the dogfood rehearsal (karac at 57d9695f4e, release build from a fresh clone), running README.md's 'Ownership without lifetimes' example with a `main` that calls `let n = name_of(u); let v = u; println(n);`. The error matches README (`cannot move `u` while a borrow into it (a returned reference still points at it) is still live (borrowed at line 13:21)`), and its help reads `drop the slice borrow before moving the source, or restructure so they don't overlap`. There is no slice.

Expected: the help names what the borrow is (the reference `n` returned by `name_of`).
fix: 5a2a4a0b48. `check_move_of_borrowed` (src/ownership/borrow.rs) keeps the slice wording for a slice borrow. A returned reference now gets its own help, built from a new `returned_borrow_holders` map. `register_ref_return_borrows` (src/ownership/ref_return.rs) fills that map, keyed by the borrow's span, with the `let` binding that holds the reference and the function (or `.method()`) that returned it. The help reads "`n`, the reference `name_of` returned, still points into `u`: finish using `n` before moving `u`, or restructure so they don't overlap". When the holder is not a plain binding, it falls back to "the returned reference still points into `u`: ...". The error message itself is unchanged, so README's quoted line still matches. Control: the base binary prints "drop the slice borrow before moving the source". Fixture: tests/core_returned_ref_move_help.rs (function and method forms; asserts no "slice" in the output).

title: `karac lint --list`, which design.md § Built-in lints and src/lints.rs name as the way to list the lint registry, is an unknown command; design.md's v1 set also names `unused_effect`, which is not in the registry
detail:
Found in the dogfood rehearsal (karac at 57d9695f4e, release build from a fresh clone). `karac lint --list` prints `error: unknown command 'lint'`, and `karac help` has no `lint`. design.md § Built-in lints: 'The registry (name, default level, trigger, suppression) is generated from the compiler and listed by `karac lint --list`', and src/lints.rs's comments (lines 83, 627, 702) say the same. The same paragraph lists `unused_effect` (allowed by default) in the v1 set; src/lints.rs registers no lint of that name, so `#[allow(unused_effect)]` is an unknown lint.

Expected: `karac lint --list` prints the registry, and `unused_effect` is registered (or the spec drops both).
fix: cbbf20c5e9 (the `unused_effect` half; the `karac lint --list` half is Thread B's 76b022a676). `unused_effect` is registered in src/lints.rs at allow and appears in `karac lint --list`. The effect checker (src/effectchecker/unused_effect.rs) finds each function whose `with` clause names an effect its body never reaches. The body's set is the settled effects of its callees, resource methods and named function values, as inference unions them, but without the declared seed, which is why the old OverDeclaredEffect check could never fire. `writes(R)` covers a read of R and `blocks(R)` a suspension; transparent and default-permitted effects are never reported. The CLI (`report_unused_effects` in src/cli.rs) reports at the level of the function's or its impl block's attribute, else -W/-D and the manifest, else allowed. The fix-it, which `karac fix` applies, writes the clause without the unused effects and drops a clause emptied whole along with its leading space. A call through a Fn parameter or a generic bound is charged to the caller, so a declaration naming only that is reported; this is pinned as intended. Tests: tests/unused_effect.rs (7).

title: A `dyn Handler with E` stored inside `Option` (`Vec[Option[dyn Handler with E]]`) loses its declared `with E` clause: a call through `if let Some(h) = s` is charged "unknown (a call through a `dyn` value a call hands back)", so `par { r.total(1), r.total(2) }` over effect-free handlers is refused; `Vec[dyn Handler with E]` is accepted
fix: 09b4bb3178. In MIR effects (src/mir/effects.rs `slot_in`), a call through a `dyn` value made in a body whose clause names an effect variable now records the slot as traced (`Slot::traced`). For a traced slot, a value a call hands back (the reference `Vec.index` returns, which `if let Some(h)` binds into) is traced through `call_made`, as `stored_in` does for a stored function value. A value a parameter holds becomes a slot for the caller to resolve against the handlers that can flow into it, instead of every effect. Untraced slots keep the § dyn Trait rule: a plain `dyn Shape` element still has every effect (tests/mir_dyn_effects.rs is unchanged). The repro was wider than the row: `Vec[dyn Handler with E]` read through `self.routes[i]` or a `for` loop was refused the same way. Pinned in tests/mir_dyn_effect_var_elements.rs: the row's program prints `5 7`; an Option payload, an index and a `for` all run in `par` over quiet handlers; a printing handler is refused whether it is added here, by a callee the router is lent to (`fill(mut r)`), or by the function that built the router and handed it back (`make()`). The 'a call hands back' wording stays only on the untraced path.

title: E_STATEFUL_DEFAULT reached through a `dyn` method or a closure names the resource as its own caller ("`Ids` calls a `mut ref self` method of `Ids`") instead of the method or function that makes the call (`Minter.handle`)
fix: 92df153c0b. When main reached the stateful default through a value it makes (a value coerced to dyn, a closure, a function value), the needs site is the statement that makes the value, and the caller fell back to the resource's own name. The effect pass now records what that value can run that writes the resource (effects::StatefulCaller, found by Analysis::stateful_maker from the made value's instances), and stateful_default_text names it: `Minter.handle` calls ..., `bump` calls ..., or a closure in `main` calls .... A direct call keeps its callee. Pinned by tests/core_strict_check.rs::a_stateful_default_write_names_the_value_that_makes_it (the row's dyn and closure programs plus a function value, which had the same fault); the 915e6dc75d release karac printed the old text on all three. Gate green.

title: A struct's effect variable is fixed by the FIRST value bound into it, so `router.add("/hello", Hello {}); router.add("/count", Counter { .. })` (a pure handler, then one that `blocks`) is refused while the same two calls in the other order check; design.md § Effect variables says a type's instance is fixed by its construction and later bindings within the same function
detail:
Found writing an HTTP handler set from docs/ alone (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at 5a2a4a0b48. `struct Router[with E] { routes: Vec[(String, dyn Handler + CrossTask with E)] }`, `fn add(mut ref self, path: Str, h: escaping dyn Handler + CrossTask with E)`, in main: add Hello {} (no effects), Echo {}, then Counter { store } whose handle takes a Mutex lock (`blocks`). Got: "error[effect]: value coerced to `dyn Handler` has `blocks()`, outside the effect set of `E` (`{}`), which was fixed at 105:26 by the first value bound to it". Moving the Counter add first makes the program check, run and serve correctly (run == build), so the refusal depends only on statement order. design.md 5634: "Several values give the union of their sets... For a type, the instance is fixed by the value's construction and later bindings within the same function, as type arguments are inferred for `Vec.new()`." The solver (src/effectchecker/effect_vars.rs, 474c7b2a59) reads the earlier sentence "A value bound later must fit the solution" instead, and the pin corpus/core/err_effect_var_unfit encodes that reading. A union over the function's bindings is sound (a call through the value before a later binding is charged the larger set). Also in the same message: an effect with no resource prints as `blocks()`, and there is no help naming the way out (write the set on the declaration, `Router[with blocks]`). Review-thread ruling 2026-10-30 (e6f5a8211, design.md § Effect variables, How it is solved): within one function a type's instance is the union of its construction and every later binding, so order does not matter; a binding in another function must fit the set its parameter type fixes. The fix flips err_effect_var_unfit to that cross-function shape, and spells an effect with no resource without the empty parentheses.

Owner: kata thread (src/effectchecker/effect_vars.rs).
fix: 09b4bb3178. Per the review-thread ruling e6f5a8211a (design.md § Effect variables, How it is solved), src/effectchecker/effect_vars.rs no longer lets the first binding fix a value's set. Within one function the instance is the union of the construction and every later binding, so nothing there refuses a binding, and the call through the value is charged the whole set where it is named. A written type argument still fixes the set, whether on the value's `let` or on the parameter another function sees it through (`fn add_note(bus: mut ref EventBus[with writes(OrderDb)])`). A binding outside it is refused naming the type argument ("which was fixed at L:C by its type argument"). corpus/core/err_effect_var_unfit takes that cross-function shape. An effect with no resource prints bare (`blocks`). The help naming `Router[with blocks]` is moot now: the order no longer matters within a function, and the cross-function message names the type argument. Tests: tests/core_effect_vars_solving.rs (either order, union charged to a pub fn, construction joins the union, written let and param refuse) and tests/effects_dyn.rs (pure-then-printing `dyn` in one function checks, through a `Router[with reads(Stdout)]` parameter refused).

title: An element of a tuple literal did not coerce into its `dyn` slot: `routes.push((path, Hello {}))` into a `Vec[(String, dyn Handler)]`, `let t: (String, dyn Handler) = (.., Hello {})`, `Some((1, Hello {}))` and a nested tuple were refused as `found '(String, Hello)'`, while `Some(Hello {})` and a struct field coerced
detail:
Found writing an HTTP handler set from docs/ alone (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at 5a2a4a0b48. design.md § dyn Trait: a value coerces where the expected type is a `dyn` type (a let with a type, an argument, a field, an element of a collection whose type is written). The check typed a tuple literal whole in synthesis mode and compared `(String, Hello)` with `(String, dyn Handler)`, so no element was asked for its slot; the `Some(Hello {})` payload and the struct field paths check against the slot and coerce. A `Map` value and an array literal of tuples already coerced through other check-mode paths.

Owner: Thread A.
fix: 6c744eaf84: the check-mode tuple-literal arm (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) checks an element against a `dyn` slot, and a nested tuple holding one, recording the coercion at the element as an argument or field coercion is; `Vec.push` (src/typechecker/method_vec_mutation.rs) and an `Option`/`Result` payload send a tuple with a `dyn` slot through that arm. An element that does not implement the trait is named: "expected 'dyn Handler', found 'i64': `i64` does not implement `Handler`". Test: tests/core_dyn_tuple_element_coercion.rs (push, let, Some payload, nested tuple, array literal; interpreter and compiled at -O0/-O2 with drop order checked). Control: karac at 5a2a4a0b48 refused the let and push forms as found '(String, Hello)'.

title: `karac fix` applies a cascaded suggestion from a mistyped import: with `import text.stats.analyse;` (the item is `analyze`) the import's E0113 suggests `analyze` and the use's E0100 suggests `analyse`, the broken import's name, and `karac fix` applies both, leaving the program broken the other way round
detail:
Found in the multi-file package rehearsal (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at f82117c9c3: `karac new wordstat --cli`, split into src/main.kara, src/report.kara, src/text/{helpers,tokenize,stats}.kara with `pub` items and imports, tests in report_test.kara, text/tokenize_test.kara and text/stats_test.kara, written from docs/ alone. In src/main.kara, `import text.stats.analyze;` mistyped as `analyse`, with `analyze(text, 3)` used below. `karac check --output=json` reports E0113 "unknown item `analyse` in module `text.stats`, did you mean `analyze`?" at the import and E0100 "undefined name 'analyze', did you mean 'analyse'?" at the use, both machine-applicable. `karac fix src/main.kara` prints "applied 2 fix(es)" and the file then imports `analyze` and calls `analyse`: E0100 "undefined name 'analyse', did you mean 'analyze'?". Expected: a name bound only by an import that failed to resolve is not a suggestion candidate, so the use site gets no fix (or no error once the import is fixed), and one `karac fix` pass leaves the program checking.

Owner: Thread A (karac fix / resolver suggestions).
fix: e11ef9ce09: the resolver records each failed import whose E0113 carries a machine-applicable replacement, keyed by module and the suggested name (`failed_import_fixes`). A use of the misspelled name in that module raises no E0100/E0101/E0102 of its own (the import's fix makes it resolve), and the bound names of a failed import are left out of every "did you mean" list, so `karac fix` applies the import's fix alone. One `karac fix` pass now mends `import text.stats.analyse;` and its uses compile. Pinned by tests/package_fix_and_diagnostics.rs (one_fix_pass_mends_a_mistyped_import_and_its_use_is_left_alone, a_use_of_the_misspelled_name_is_corrected_once_the_import_is); the pre-fix binary swapped analyse/analyze in the rehearsal.

title: `karac fix` with no file inside a package fails with `error: missing file argument`, so the Mend loop's fix step runs one file at a time while `karac check --output=json` reports the whole package

title: `karac fmt` prints source that does not mean the same or does not parse: a test's name loses its quotes (`test analyze counts {`), `{{` in an f-string becomes `{`, a char literal `'\n'` is printed as a raw newline and `'\''` as `'''`, and `///` doc comments are dropped

On `let t = f"x{1} {{y}} \"q\""; let c = '\n';`, fmt prints `f"x{1} {y} ..."` (now an interpolation of `y`: E0100 undefined name 'y') and a char literal with a literal newline between the quotes. `c == '\''` prints as `c == '''`. `/// Splits ...` doc comments vanish, like the `//` comments of B-2026-10-30-16. fmt also adds `;` after every block-statement `if`/`for`/`while` (`};`), which no other formatter does and which is not canonical source. title: `karac fmt` has no package mode and no check mode: with no file it fails (`karac fmt requires a file argument`), `--check` is read as a file name, and it only prints to stdout, so a package cannot be formatted or checked for formatting in CI
detail:
Found in the multi-file package rehearsal (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at f82117c9c3: `karac new wordstat --cli`, split into src/main.kara, src/report.kara, src/text/{helpers,tokenize,stats}.kara with `pub` items and imports, tests in report_test.kara, text/tokenize_test.kara and text/stats_test.kara, written from docs/ alone. In the package root, `karac fmt` prints `error: karac fmt requires a file argument`; `karac fmt --check` prints `error: cannot read '--check'`. `karac fmt <file>` writes the formatted text to stdout and leaves the file alone. design.md § Command phasing puts `fmt` in the first phase with `build`, `check` and `test`, which all work with no file in a package; § Canonical formatting describes one canonical form for agent diffs. Expected: `karac fmt` formats every `.kara` under `src/` in place, and `karac fmt --check` exits nonzero listing the files that would change (the gofmt -l / cargo fmt --check shape).

Owner: Thread B (fmt).

Outside a package the bare form exits 1 with E0227 asking for a path. Unknown flags are refused rather than read as file names. Help text and design.md § Canonical formatting updated. title: `karac build` in a package writes the binary to the package root (`./wordstat`), not to `dist/` as design.md § Build cache says, so the scaffolded `.gitignore` (`/dist/`) does not ignore it
detail:
Found in the multi-file package rehearsal (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at f82117c9c3: `karac new wordstat --cli`, split into src/main.kara, src/report.kara, src/text/{helpers,tokenize,stats}.kara with `pub` items and imports, tests in report_test.kara, text/tokenize_test.kara and text/stats_test.kara, written from docs/ alone. `karac build --release` prints a project banner (project, edition, root, entry, the five modules) and "Built: <root>/wordstat"; nothing is written under `dist/`. design.md § Packages and manifests, Build cache: "Each package's own output goes in `dist/` (in the default `.gitignore`; `karac clean` removes it)", and `karac new` writes `.gitignore` = `/dist/`. Expected: the binary at `dist/<name>` (or the doc and the .gitignore changed together).

Owner: Thread B (CLI).
fix: FIXED by 710e7be317. A bare `karac build` in a package now writes `<root>/dist/<name>` (with `.exe` or `.wasm` per target), creating `dist/` as needed. That is where design.md § Build cache puts it, `karac new`'s `.gitignore` ignores it and `karac clean` removes it. `-o` still names any path, and a file build still writes `<stem>` in the current directory. `karac install` now copies the binary from `dist/`, and `karac build --help` says `<root>/dist/<package name>`. Pinned by tests/build_v2.rs `build_v2_builds_a_package`, which asserts dist/pkg runs and no `pkg` is written at the root, and by the path-dependency case. The project-build tests in tests/cli.rs, tests/mir_network_provider.rs and tests/mir_wasm.rs now read dist/. Control at e5dbfa991c: the 2 build_v2 and 8 cli project-build tests fail.

title: `karac check --output=json` in a package names a file two ways: resolver diagnostics (E0111, E0112, E0113) carry an absolute path, typecheck ones `src/<module>.kara`; and E0223 (circular module dependency) carries no file or line at all
detail:
Found in the multi-file package rehearsal (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at f82117c9c3: `karac new wordstat --cli`, split into src/main.kara, src/report.kara, src/text/{helpers,tokenize,stats}.kara with `pub` items and imports, tests in report_test.kara, text/tokenize_test.kara and text/stats_test.kara, written from docs/ alone. With a private item imported across directories, E0111's `file` is `/tmp/.../wordstat/src/report.kara`; with a type error in text/stats.kara, E0200's is `src/text/stats.kara`. The text renderer does the same (a warning prints `src/text/stats.kara:3:5` in one run and the absolute path in another). A cycle `report -> text.stats -> report` gives E0223 with `file`, `line` and `column` null in JSON, though the text form lists both files; the import that closes the cycle has a span. Expected: one form for every diagnostic (relative to the package root, as typecheck does), and E0223 located at the import that closes the cycle. A tool that groups `--output=json` diagnostics by file (the Mend loop, an editor) sees two files today.

Owner: Thread A (check --output=json).
fix: e11ef9ce09: resolver, typecheck and parse diagnostics in `karac check` / `build` all name the file through one helper (project_v2::shown), relative to the working directory. E0223 now carries the file, line and column of the import that closes the cycle (`Cycle::closing_import`) in JSON and text. A resolver `help:` reads "did you mean" only when it carries a replacement. Pinned by tests/package_fix_and_diagnostics.rs (resolver_and_typecheck_diagnostics_name_files_one_way, an_import_cycle_is_located_at_the_import_that_closes_it).

title: A failed `assert` / `assert_eq` in `karac test` reports "assertion failed" / "assertion failed: left != right" without the assertion's source text, and its `test_fail` event has no `assertion` field (design.md § Assertions, Runner output)
detail:
Found in the multi-file package rehearsal (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at f82117c9c3: `karac new wordstat --cli`, split into src/main.kara, src/report.kara, src/text/{helpers,tokenize,stats}.kara with `pub` items and imports, tests in report_test.kara, text/tokenize_test.kara and text/stats_test.kara, written from docs/ alone. With `assert_eq(s.words, 7)` failing, the event is `{"type":"test_fail",...,"message":"assertion failed: left != right","left":"6","right":"7"}`; a failing `assert(is_word_char(..) and false)` gives `"message":"assertion failed"`. design.md § Assertions: `assert(cond)` fails with "assertion failed: <source text of cond>" (the compiler captures the source expression) and `assert_eq` with "assertion failed: a == b\n  left: ..."; § Runner output lists an optional `assertion: string`, the assertion's source text. The text is fixed in src/mir/lower.rs (the `("assert_eq", _) => "assertion failed: left != right"` match). Expected: the source text in the message and in `assertion`.

Owner: Thread B (MIR builder).
fix: FIXED by 710e7be317. The MIR builder (src/mir/lower.rs) captures each assertion's source text, rendered by the formatter on one line. A failed `assert(cond)` panics with `assertion failed: <cond>` (a literal message still wins). `assert_eq(a, b)` panics with `assertion failed: a == b`, then its `left:`/`right:` lines, and `assert_ne(a, b)` with `assertion failed: a != b`, then `value:`, as design.md § Assertions specifies. `karac test`'s `test_fail` event carries the text as `assertion`, next to `message`, `left` and `right` (§ Runner output). The row's case now reads `"message":"assertion failed: s.words == 7","assertion":"s.words == 7"`. Pinned by tests/test_v2.rs `test_v2_reports_each_case` (`double(2) == 5`), tests/mir_build.rs (struct, call and `v.len() != 3` operands, on the interpreter and at -O0 and -O2), a plain `assert(x > 3 and x < 9)` in lower.rs's `aborts_report_their_message_and_place`, and tests/cli.rs `test_test_jit_bare_assert_false_emits_null_left_right` (`assertion failed: false`). Control at e5dbfa991c: all of them fail.

title: `prelude_shadow` warns that a user `struct Stats` shadows a prelude type, though `Stats` is the post-v1 `kara-data` type and not in the prelude (library/README.md), so a package's own `Stats` warns on every check, build and run
detail:
Found in the multi-file package rehearsal (Thread A, 2026-10-30), karac at f82117c9c3: `karac new wordstat --cli`, split into src/main.kara, src/report.kara, src/text/{helpers,tokenize,stats}.kara with `pub` items and imports, tests in report_test.kara, text/tokenize_test.kara and text/stats_test.kara, written from docs/ alone. `pub struct Stats { .. }` in src/text/stats.kara: every `karac check`, `build` and `run` prints "warning[prelude_shadow]: declaration of 'Stats' shadows the prelude type of the same name; built-in paths keyed on 'Stats' no longer apply to this type". library/README.md lists the prelude types (`Option`, `Result`, `Ordering`, `String`, ... `Entry`) and puts `Stats` in data.md, the post-v1 `kara-data` package ("not `std` and not the prelude"). src/prelude.rs still lists `Stats` in its scope-0 names (and `Server`, `Request`, `Client`, `Response`, which are `std.net` but documented as prelude-reachable). Expected: the lint fires for the documented prelude only; `Stats` is a common name for a user type.

Owner: Thread A.
fix: e11ef9ce09: the removed library types (Base64, Hex, Url, Stats, Column, DataFrame, LazyExpr, Tensor) are one list, prelude::REMOVED_LIBRARY_TYPES, read by both the library-call refusal and `warn_prelude_shadow`, so a program's own `Stats` warns nothing. Pinned by tests/package_fix_and_diagnostics.rs (a_programs_own_stats_shadows_no_prelude_type).

title: `karac query ownership` reports a parameter declared `s: own String` as mode "ref": the mode it prints is inferred from the body's use of the parameter, not the declared D5 mode that decides how callers pass it
detail:
Found while pinning B-2026-10-30-17 (karac at 76b022a676; the base build 57d9695f4e does the same). `fn grab(s: own String) -> i64 { s.len() }` then `karac query ownership app.kara.grab` prints `{"name":"s","mode":"ref","representation":"ref (borrow)"}`. README's query table says `ownership` reports parameter modes, and under D5 the declared mode (bare = borrow, `own T`, `mut ref T`) is the calling convention. src/ownership.rs (the `Infer parameter modes` loop before `self.param_modes.insert`) maps ParamUsage::Unused/Read to Ref, Mutated to MutRef and Consumed to Own, ignoring the declaration. An agent reading the query would conclude `grab` borrows its argument when the caller must give it away.

Expected: `mode` is the declared mode, with the inferred usage reported separately if it is still wanted (for example a `used_as` field, so an `own` parameter only read can carry a fix-it suggesting the bare borrow).

Owner: Thread A (ownership pass).
fix: d21c0ecf97: the ownership pass records each parameter's declared mode (`own T` own, `mut ref T`/`mut Slice` mut_ref, bare or `ref T` ref; bare is own with KARAC_D5=0) as `declared_param_modes`, beside the inferred `param_modes`, which the passes that use it keep reading. `karac query ownership` prints the declared mode, and parameter representations follow it. No `used_as` field: the inference does not count a write through a method call (`v.push(n)` on a `mut ref` reads as "ref"), so it would mislead. Pinned by tests/query_ownership_declared_modes.rs, which fails on the previous binary (grab's `s` and look's `v` both "ref").

title: kata 74's closed binary search over a flattened matrix (`while lo <= hi`, `m[mid / cols][mid % cols]`) runs 1.32x legacy's instructions on the MIR backend, and it is not B-2026-10-28-41's midpoint mechanism
detail: MEASURED 2026-10-30 on the M5 Pro (Kara/mir_screen/screen2.tsv, exact instructions via scripts/pmc.c, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0). bench/search_a_2d_matrix.kara: legacy (dd86e3955) 3.272G, MIR at a1cb9f4419 4.312G. B-2026-10-28-41's midpoint facts (b8ad892458) do not apply: the guard is `lo <= hi`, and stating the sound closed-interval fact `lo <= mid <= hi` there (tried, then reverted) fired on 2 sites and changed nothing (4.3117G either way), since the index is `mid / cols` and `mid % cols`, whose bounds need `mid <= rows * cols - 1` carried through a division. The ledger row -41 had listed 74 in its cluster because a second default<O2> alone helped it 0.92x; what that second run folds here is unattributed. Next step: IR-edit attribution per Kara/mir_screen/RECIPE.md.
fix:
e95c0028a0: a checked `/` or `%` whose divisor is a local assigned once by a native `len` (src/mir/guard_bounds.rs `length_locals`) is lowered as the plain division: a length is `>= 0`, so `MIN / -1` cannot happen, and the divide-by-zero check is the MIR's own and stays. Without the overflow test's `select(o, 1, y)` divisor, `mid / cols` and `mid % cols` share one `idiv` again. `KARAC_MIR_LENGTH_DIVISORS=0` keeps the check.

MEASURED on Linux x86 (this container), kata 74's bench (bench/search_a_2d_matrix), KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, cachegrind instructions: 6.86G with the knob off -> 4.46G on; legacy (dd86e3955) 4.17G, so 1.07x remains. Output identical to legacy's. Not re-measured on macOS.

Pins: tests/mir_length_divisor.rs (the search's IR has no select on its divisor with the pass on and has it with the knob off; a user `len` returning -1 still reports integer overflow; a zero length still reports division by zero; interpreted and built).

title: tests/mir_panic_free_floor.rs fails 3 of 4 on macOS arm64: a print/Vec, an overflow-abort and a Map/Set program's binaries still contain std's panic-hook marker `RUST_BACKTRACE`, so the floor B-2026-10-28-36 / B-2026-10-29-41 measured on Linux does not hold on Apple
detail: Found 2026-10-30 in the local `cargo test --features llvm` gate (M5 Pro, macOS 25.6). mir_print_and_vec_program_links_no_panic_hook, mir_overflow_abort_reports_without_the_panic_hook and mir_table_program_links_no_panic_hook fail with `std's panic hook is linked` on freshly rebuilt lean + full archives, and identically with KARAC_MIR_MIDPOINT=0 KARAC_MIR_MIDPOINT_REOPT=0 (codegen then equal to its base), so it is not b8ad892458. Either something on the Apple link path still reaches a Rust panic, or the marker test is Linux-specific; unknown which. CI is Linux, so CI stays green while the Mac binary carries the hook and its symbolizer.
fix:
FIXED by 333f5427d4 (with 22920fb08b). There were two roots, both found with ld64.lld -why_live on an arm64 link of each floor program against the aarch64-apple-darwin archive.

(1) Print/Vec and overflow programs. On Apple, std::sync::Mutex is a lazily boxed pthread mutex whose init and lock assert. The pool's shared program state and stdout's buffer (OUT_SHARED) took that Mutex, which kept std's panic hook live. 22920fb08b adds runtime/src/mir_task.rs PoolLock: std's Mutex off Apple, os_unfair_lock on Apple, which cannot fail. A contended 8-task print bench measured no slower than std's Mutex, and the TSan lane was clean.

(2) The Map/Set/SortedMap program. karac_hash::walk_index reduced a * i + c through u128. That lowers to compiler_builtins' __umodti3, whose Mach-O unwind entry names rust_eh_personality, which keeps panic_cannot_unwind and the panic hook live through karac_mir_map_walk_at. 333f5427d4 computes the index in words instead: directly while n <= 2^32 (as the compiled in-line walk already does), else by doubling without overflow. hash's walk_index_matches_the_wide_product checks it against the 128-bit product on both sides of 2^32.

Locally, the RUST_BACKTRACE markers in the table program's arm64 link went from 3 to 0. CI run 41266206892 (d8f218afe9, a descendant of 333f5427d4) passed "Panic-free floor (arm64)" with all 4 tests. Its Windows red is tests/fmt_package_mode.rs, which is unrelated.

title: A resolve error inside a `_test.kara` file is reported against its production sibling (`src/main.kara:42:43` for a line of `src/main_test.kara`), by `karac test` and now by `karac check`
detail:
Found while landing the ruling that `karac check` checks a package's test files (9b94711cc), karac at 710e7be317. Repro: `karac new wc1 --cli`, then append `test "broken" { assert(undefined_fn(1)); }` to src/main_test.kara (its line 42). `karac test` emits `{"type":"resolve_error","code":"E0100","file":"src/main.kara","line":42,"column":43,...}`, and `karac check` prints `error[E0100]: src/main.kara:42:43: undefined name 'undefined_fn'`. main.kara has 36 lines. The line and column are the test file's; the file is not. The cause: `build_program_tree_with(merge_test_companions: true)` folds the companion's items into the sibling module (`Module::test_items_start`), and `ModuleResolveErrors` names the module's `file`. A type error in a test file comes out right, because the v2 check of the combined source maps each span back to its file (tests/package_check_tests.rs). Expected: the error names src/main_test.kara. Either key the resolve error to the item it is in (items past `test_items_start` belong to `test_file`), or resolve the companion's items with their own file.

Owner: Thread B.
fix: FIXED by 1bc60ed3f0. A merged `_test.kara` companion used to share its production sibling's span offsets, so a resolve error in the test file was reported against `src/main.kara` at the sibling's line. The merge in src/module.rs now gives the companion its own `test_span_base` past the end of the production items and shifts every test item and import span by it; `resolve_modules` (src/cli/build_cmds.rs) splits the errors and the fix edits by that boundary and reports each half against its own file. `karac check` and `karac test` now print `src/main_test.kara:<line>:<col>: undefined name ...` and the JSON `"file":"src/main_test.kara"`. Pinned by tests/package_check_tests.rs `a_resolve_error_in_a_test_file_names_the_test_file`, which fails at the parent commit.

title: MIR still stores the call site into `karac.site` / `karac.site.len` before every library call that can abort, two stores a loop trip where legacy passed the site statically to a cold per-site abort path: kata 38 runs 1.18x legacy's instructions on that alone
detail: Residual of B-2026-10-28-43 after e1bd415c72 removed its thread-local lookups (count_and_say 1.80G -> 1.26G; legacy dd86e3955 1.07G). B-43's IR-edit arm that deleted every store reached 1.05G, below legacy (re-checked 2026-10-30 under the real target header: as emitted 1.84G, no thread_local 1.30G, no stores 1.14G). Fix direction, unchanged from B-43: give the abort path the site as a constant (a hidden argument of the library bodies that can abort, forwarded library-to-library, with a shim where a function value names one), so nothing is stored on the hot path and B-2026-10-26-7's per-thread requirement holds without a thread-local at all.
fix:
a4ea53a5ee: a library body that can abort (not in the program's source, and `may_abort`) is lowered as a located function, `<symbol>.at`, which takes the place of the call into it as two trailing arguments (ptr, len). A call from the program's source passes its line as a constant, a located body forwards its own to the located bodies it calls, and the plain-convention `fns` / `vfns` functions that function values, shims and the runtime call are always-inline wrappers passing no place. `karac.site` / `karac.site.len` and every store into them are gone, and with them mir_aot.rs's `address_site_globals_once` (`KARAC_MIR_SITE_TLS_ONCE`), which existed only for those globals. A body registered for hot swap takes no place.

MEASURED on Linux x86 (this container), kata 38's bench (count_and_say), KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, cachegrind instructions: 901.0M with a control karac built from d059343bbc (main just before) -> 783.7M; legacy (dd86e3955) 908.4M. Output identical. Kata 5, 74, 131, 139 and a 14-bench sample are unchanged (kata 387's apparent +2.3% was hash-seed noise: identical at KARAC_HASH_SEED=1). The row's own numbers are from the Mac and were not re-run there.

Behaviour change: a library abort reached through a function value or a runtime callback reports no place, where it reported the program's latest direct call into the library (often another line). Pins: tests/mir_site_argument.rs (no site global in the IR; `unwrap` and `swap_remove` called with a constant place; an abort inside `swap_remove`'s body reports the program's line, interpreted, built and on the JIT); tests/mir_site_thread_local.rs (no site global; four workers, built and `karac run` x5).

title: An auto-par task's counter is known to lie in the loop's constant range (30e4af977d) but LLVM 18 still divides in 64 bits: kata 4's `k % R` in the task is an unsigned 64-bit magic division where the in-order loop, exiting at the constant `k < 10M`, uses a 32-bit one
detail: MEASURED on Linux x86_64 at 30e4af977d, release, kata 4's bench (binary_search_partition), objdump and opt-18 -O3 on the KARAC_MIR_LL dump. The task clamps its run to smax(lo, 0) and smin(hi, 10000000), and the optimized task loop has `urem i64 %k, 1000` (`shr $3; mulx; shr $4; imul; sub`) where the in-order loop has the 32-bit `imul $0x10624dd3; shr $0x26`. The task's exit test is `k < hi'` with hi' a non-constant smin, and LVI/CVP narrow a urem only from a constant bound, so the 32-bit form needs a dominating test against the constant (or range metadata on the counter). Worth about 1 to 2 instructions per iteration here. The rest of the task's gap to the in-order loop (855.6M vs 599.7M instructions at two workers) is the wide sum's register pressure, B-2026-10-28-35. Suggested remedy (unverified): when the end is a constant, test the counter against it in the loop's exit as well, or have the backend put !range on the counter's loads.
fix: 287a18e111: an auto-par task whose i64 counter runs from a non-negative constant start to a constant end also tests the counter against that end as unsigned (src/mir/lower.rs, `range_cap`, read by `range_loop`). Beside `k < hi` it is a no-op, since the run's hi is already clamped to the end, but it puts a constant on the loop's back edge. LLVM 18's CVP narrows `k % R` from that, as it does in order. Tried first on the opt-18 dump: an `llvm.assume(k < 10M)` before the urem leaves it 64-bit, while an `icmp ult k, 10M` and-ed into the latch narrows it to `urem i32`. MEASURED on Linux x86_64, release, kata 4's bench (binary_search_partition), callgrind, two workers: 855.6M -> 795.6M instructions, against 599.7M in order, with the in-order loop's `imul $0x10624dd3` in the task. Pinned by tests/mir_auto_par_range_facts.rs (the `icmp ult` cap in the first task's IR, none where the start is unknown, none under KARAC_AUTO_PAR_RANGE=0). The rest of the gap is B-2026-10-28-35's wide-sum register pressure.

title: An effect clause cannot root a resource at `self`: `with sends(self)` and `with writes(self.n)` are parse errors (`Expected identifier`), though design.md § Value-rooted resources writes `writes(self.cache)` and docs/library/concurrency.md and io.md declare `Sender.send`, `Receiver.recv`, the socket, TLS, WebSocket and `Child` methods `with sends(self)` / `receives(self)`
fix: FIXED by 181b03c625. `parse_resource` takes `self` and a `self.field` path as a resource root; the resolver admits it in a method with a `self` receiver, and a function without one gets "the resource `self` is rooted at `self`, and this function has no `self` receiver". In the front-end effect checker a `self` root on a channel endpoint (`impl Sender[T]`) is the channel, collapsed like a channel parameter; on any other type the clause states the resource and callers inherit nothing, because values are keyed by the MIR effect pass from the body (src/mir/effects.rs). Pinned by tests/effect_value_roots.rs: a method rooting at `self` and `self.n` checks and runs; two `par` branches calling a `sends(self)` method on two values do not conflict and on one value do (`sends(Channel @ l4.0)` twice). docs/library/concurrency.md:24, io.md:268, :351 and :577 now conform under scripts/library-conformance.py; concurrency.md:80 is left as a fragment (`T` and `Duration` come from outside the block). Control: 5 of the 6 new tests fail on the pre-fix source.

title: examples/protobuf_schema.kara passes `karac check` but `karac run`, `karac build` and `karac __mir-run` all stop with `error[mir]: resolve: ... \`i8\` is a primitive type name and cannot be bound as a value` at 67:24 of a file that is not the example's (span offset 1002001831)
detail: MEASURED at a54f99f726. The example (`#[proto_schema]` const plus `#[derive(Message)]` comptime codegen, runtime/stdlib/protobuf.kara) is accepted by `karac check examples/protobuf_schema.kara` with no diagnostics; every executing surface fails before running, with the resolver's ReservedIdentifier error printed as a Debug struct: `ResolveError { message: "`i8` is a primitive type name and cannot be bound as a value (design.md § Primitive type names); as a path's first segment it always names the type", span: Span { line: 67, column: 24, offset: 1002001831, length: 2 }, kind: ReservedIdentifier, ... }`. Line 67 of the example has no `i8`, and no checked-in library `.kara` source has `i8` at 67:24, so the binding is most likely in comptime-generated source (derive_message's output, or the schema expansion) that only the MIR pipeline resolves. Two defects: (1) the run/build pipeline resolves something check does not, so check's verdict is wrong about this program; (2) the error escapes as `error[mir]: resolve: ResolveError { .. }` with a span pointing at no file. Fix shape: find the generated binding (dump the comptime expansion), rename it, and make check resolve what the MIR lowering resolves; render a MIR-phase resolve error as a diagnostic with its file. The example has no .expected; its header comment gives the run command.
fix: 9797536787. The protobuf derive named a repeated field's loop counter `i` + its field number, so field 8 bound `i8` (16, 32, 64 and 128 would have too), a primitive type name; runtime/stdlib/protobuf.kara now names it `ix` + the number, and examples/protobuf_schema.kara checks and runs on __mir-run (its library-conformance baseline entry is removed: "1 conforms"). Why check passed: `drop_library_diagnostics` (src/cli.rs) dropped every diagnostic whose span lay past the user's source as the library's, and the derive's generated items sit there too, in the comptime splice windows (new `comptime::is_spliced`). Resolve errors in generated code are now kept at the derive's site, which their spans carry, prefixed "in the code generated here: ", with no fix-it into text no file holds. Type errors there are still dropped, deliberately: strict typing refuses serde's generated calls, which carry no `mut` markers (three core_strict_check / core_payload fixtures went red when they were kept). So a type error in a library derive's output would still pass check and fail the build; inferred from the code, not probed, and not reachable from user code today since derives are library-defined. The MIR front end printed the resolve error as a Debug struct; it is now `resolve: line:col: message` (and `comptime: line:col: message`). Pins: tests/comptime_generated_errors.rs (check reports a reserved-name derive error at the derive; __mir-run names it without the Debug struct; a protobuf schema with a repeated field 8 checks and runs). Gate: fmt, both clippy legs, wasm clippy, test --all 10036 passed, --features llvm 10138 passed, 0 failed.

title: A `#[derive(Debug)]` type has no callable `fmt_debug`: `u.fmt_debug()` is `no method 'fmt_debug' on type 'User'`, though design.md § Display and Debug declares `trait Debug { fn fmt_debug(self) -> String; }`; `dbg(u)` prints the derived form, so only the trait method is missing
detail: MEASURED at a54f99f726 while checking docs/library/secret.md's `// prints:  User { name: "alice", token: <redacted> }` claim (the claim holds: `dbg(u)` prints `u = User { name: "alice", token: <redacted> }`). Repro: `import std.secret.Secret;` `#[derive(Debug)] struct User { name: String, token: Secret[String] }`, then `println(u.fmt_debug());` in main: `karac check` reports `typecheck: no method 'fmt_debug' on type 'User'`. design.md (§ Display and Debug, the `trait Debug` block) names `fmt_debug` as the trait's method, and `{x:?}` is reserved, so a program has no way to get the Debug text as a String other than through `dbg`'s stderr line. Fix shape: give the derived impl (and the library's Debug impls) a callable `fmt_debug`, or change design.md if the method is not meant to be public.
fix: 103da49c5f (Thread A). The checker types `x.fmt_debug()` as `String` on a concrete type that is `Debug` with no `fmt_debug` of its own (`TypeEnv::debug_text_is_builtin`, intercepted in `infer_method_call` beside `ref_eq`): a derived struct or enum, Option/Result, the collections, String and the primitives. The MIR builder lowers that call, and the same call under `T: Debug` at such a type, to the `debug_string` native `dbg` and `assert_eq` already use (`Lowerer::debug_text`), so the text is exactly `dbg`'s: strings quoted, fields named, `Secret` as `<redacted>` (the row's `Login { name: "bob", token: <redacted> }`). A program's own `fmt_debug` still wins, directly and through a generic; a type that is not `Debug` keeps `no method 'fmt_debug'`. Pinned by corpus/core/debug_text_fmt_debug (expected_from spec), which the pre-fix binary refuses with the row's error and mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-build pass alike. Remainder filed: `dbg` still ignores a hand-written `fmt_debug` (B-2026-10-31-12).

title: `karac build` (and `karac run`) runs the whole front end twice: `check_v2`'s pipeline, then `build_source_in_order_later` parses, resolves, typechecks and ownership-checks the program and its library again from source; FIXED in wall time only: since 6777e6ea51 the two run at once, so the repeat now costs CPU and not latency, and the shared front end itself is B-2026-10-31-16
detail: MEASURED at 6bae6aa8d2, kata 2 iterative.kara, release `--features llvm`, `KARAC_MIR_TIME=1 karac build`: the check pass reports check typecheck 31 ms and check ownership+mir 10 ms, then the build's own `frontend()` reports parse 9, prepare ~9, resolve ~5, typecheck 54 and ownershipcheck 14 ms, before any LLVM work. `src/cli/build_v2.rs` `build()` calls `super::run_v2::check_v2` for the diagnostics, then `crate::mir::lower::build_source_in_order_later(&source)`, which re-runs `frontend(src, false)` (`src/mir/lower.rs`). The two front ends differ: check leaves the library's bodies unchecked (B-2026-10-19-21), the build checks them, so sharing one needs the check's typed program carried into lowering with the library bodies checked. Roughly 40-50 ms of a 330 ms build of a small kata is the repeated work.
fix: FIXED by 6777e6ea51, in wall time. `karac build` and `karac run` (JIT path) now run `check_v2` on a second thread (`run_v2::checked_alongside`, 16 MiB stack like the CLI thread) while the MIR builder lowers the same source on the CLI thread; the check is joined before the builder's result is read, so a check error still ends the command with the check's diagnostic and never the builder's, and the check's pipeline is dropped on its own thread instead of living through code generation. The builder's closure stops before LLVM, since a check error exits the process from the check thread. Kata 2 (iterative), debug binary, five runs each: build 474-613 ms before, 370-457 ms after; run 319-390 ms before, 235-299 ms after. Guards in tests/check_alongside_build.rs: a type error reports `error[typecheck]` and no `error[mir]` on five repeats of each command, and a built program's JSON success object still carries the check's warnings. The CPU repeat is B-2026-10-31-16.

title: Every `karac` process starts at 10-12 ms (shipped static PIE) and the link step of a small kata's `karac build` is its largest phase at 72-102 ms: PIE kept by decision (non-PIE would save about 3 ms but drop ASLR), bfd kept (lld and gold rejected); the allocator experiment split to B-2026-11-11-82
detail: MEASURED at f7f2075954 and again at 6bae6aa8d2 on the cloud box (fork/exec/wait4 peak RSS, medians of 9-15): `karac --version` 15-20 ms, 46.6 MB. The release binary loads libLLVM.so dynamically (dyn-llvm default) and carries the runtime, so a third of `karac build`'s 115 MB peak and half of `karac check`'s 85 MB is there before the front end starts; massif puts check's heap peak at 31.8 MB. `KARAC_MIR_TIME=1 karac build` on kata 2 iterative.kara: opt passes 31-39 ms, object emission 16-19 ms, link 72-102 ms. B-2026-10-28-37's July baseline (92 ms, 24 MB on the M5 Pro) predates both. Numbers sent to the shared drop schedule thread (owner of src/backend/) 2026-10-31. 2026-10-31 drop schedule, at 2543d62eaa on the cloud box, medians of 21 `karac --version` runs (fork/exec/wait4): the 46.6 MB / 15-20 ms above is the DEV build (`--features llvm`, dynamic libLLVM). The shipped build (scripts/package-release.sh: `--no-default-features --features llvm,llvm-static`) is a static PIE: 10-12 ms, 52 MB, 10.0M instructions, 2,245 minor faults, two thirds of the instructions in ld.so applying 288,656 relative relocations (LLVM's vtables, 4.9 MB of .data.rel.ro) and most of the rest LLVM's cl::opt constructors (2.9M). Packed relocations (`-z pack-relative-relocs`): 6.8 MB smaller file, startup unchanged (9.8M instructions; the relocations are still applied). NON-PIE (`RUSTFLAGS="-C relocation-model=static -C link-arg=-no-pie"`, which needs `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` so proc macros stay PIC): 7.4-7.9 ms, 43 MB, 6.2M instructions, 1,190 faults; `karac build` and `karac run` of kata 2 match expected.out, and corpus mir-llvm (JIT) on 431 entries gives the same 430 pass / 1 fail as the dev karac. Its effect on release: Linux only (macOS arm64 requires PIE); package-release.sh gains the RUSTFLAGS and `--target`, so its output path becomes target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release (aarch64 likewise); karac and karac_jit_runner lose ASLR for their own code. Not landed: a security trade-off for Gowtham. LINK, kata 2 (static karac, KARAC_MIR_TIME): 75-90 ms, all of it `cc`/bfd ld against the 13.5 MB lean archive (9 MB of it one LTO codegen unit); strip -x is 5 ms; dropping the gcc LTO plugin or `--no-keep-memory` changes nothing. ld.lld links in 50 ms but keeps 234 KB of std's panic hook, backtrace symbolizer and fs code that bfd's --gc-sections drops (kata 2: 71,824 -> 311,392 bytes), so it is not adopted; gold 59 ms, untested for size. PROGRESS 24e4faf691 (Thread A, 2026-11-02): a default build installs its CPU baseline in-process (`set_target_cpu_override` / `set_target_features_override`) instead of a child `karac __list-target-cpus` probe; a user CPU still goes through the validated override. tests/cpu_baseline_registry.rs pins that every baseline name for v1..v4 on x86_64 and aarch64 is in LLVM's CPU list. Linking with gold or lld instead of bfd was measured on kata 2 and rejected (lld 40 ms vs bfd 72 ms link, but 311 KB vs 71,720 B stripped, since lld keeps std's panic/backtrace path). What remains is process startup, which is on the non-PIE card; the row stays open behind it. MEASURED 2026-11-09 (Thread C, release builds without LLVM at 2ec5518d64, cloud box, hyperfine -N, 40 runs; /usr/bin/time -v): `--version` 2.4 ms against 4.9 ms for the static llvm build, so LLVM's load is the whole of what laziness could take from `--version` and `fmt` (fmt --check on a 3-line file 2.2 ms vs 6.0 ms), and that is the non-PIE card above. `check` on a 3-line file is 66 ms and 45 MB on both builds: callgrind puts 293M instructions in the standard library's parse (~60M, 40M of it the STDLIB_PROGRAMS LazyLock), typecheck (89M), ownership check (53M) and library_prune (15M), with malloc/free about 37% of all instructions. Nothing there is eager by accident: every `check` checks the whole library, and making that lazy is caching or demand-driven library checking, a design-scale change. An allocator swap (mimalloc 0.1 as #[global_allocator], experiment only, not landed): tiny `check` 66 -> 48 ms, RSS 45 -> 78 MB (55 MB and 52 ms with MIMALLOC_ARENA_EAGER_COMMIT=0); mini_parsy `check` 575 -> 417 ms, RSS 127 -> 175 MB. Sent to the review thread as a decision. REVIEW 2026-11-09: mimalloc is not landed (a new dependency of the shipped compiler, for ~14 ms and ~10 MB more RSS on a small check, most of whose allocation is the library re-check); re-measure it after the library cache, B-2026-11-09-28. SPLIT 2026-11-11 (drop schedule, routed by the review thread): the allocator experiment (mimalloc) moved to B-2026-11-11-82, relocated to docs/deferred.md § Pre-checked Standard Library and Package Interfaces (7cdc0fadd4), which records that it waits for the library-cache stages. This row keeps process startup and the link step. The link step has nothing left: bfd is kept, lld and gold were measured and rejected above. Startup is the static PIE's relocation and LLVM's cl::opt constructors; the one measured remedy is non-PIE (7.4-7.9 ms vs 10-12 ms, Linux only, no ASLR for karac's own code), a security trade-off that waits on Gowtham's decision, and nothing else remains to try before v1.
fix: eee8e42fc4 (ledger split, no code change). WONTFIX by decision. The link step was measured to a standstill: bfd is kept, since ld.lld (40-50 ms against bfd's 72-90 ms) keeps std's panic hook, backtrace symbolizer and fs code that bfd's --gc-sections drops (kata 2 stripped 71,824 -> 311,392 bytes), and gold (59 ms) was rejected with it; strip -x, dropping the LTO plugin and --no-keep-memory change nothing. Process startup of the shipped static PIE (10-12 ms, 52 MB; ld.so applying 288,656 relative relocations plus LLVM's cl::opt constructors) has one measured remedy, a non-PIE Linux build (7.4-7.9 ms, 43 MB). Gowtham declined it on 2026-11-12 to keep ASLR for karac's and karac_jit_runner's own code, for about 3 ms of startup: PIE kept, a deliberate divergence from the measured-fastest build. The allocator experiment was split to B-2026-11-11-82 (relocated). Nothing else is left.

title: An effect clause cannot root a resource at a parameter that is not a channel endpoint: `with receives(listener)` on a `listener: TcpListener` and `with writes(f)` on a `File` are `'listener' is not an effect resource (it is a variable)`, though design.md § Value-rooted resources writes `writes(f)` and docs/library/io.md declares `WebSocket.accept(listener: TcpListener) … with receives(listener)`
fix: FIXED by 181b03c625. The resolver admits any parameter as a resource root except a scalar's (`ast::value_root_param_names`): `writes(log)` / `writes(log.lines)` on a `log: mut ref Log` and docs/library/io.md:375's `receives(listener)` on a `listener: TcpListener` resolve, and `sends(x)` on an `x: i64` is still "is not an effect resource" (`a_non_channel_param_is_still_not_an_effect_resource`). A channel-endpoint parameter keeps collapsing to `Channel`; any other parameter root is stated by the clause and not charged to callers by the front-end checker, as for a `self` root (B-2026-10-31-4). Pinned by tests/effect_value_roots.rs `a_parameter_of_any_non_scalar_type_roots_a_resource` and `a_scalar_parameter_still_roots_no_resource`.

title: git_fetch and registry_proxy lib tests fail on a second run that reuses a pid: their temp dirs are named by pid and a counter and never removed, so a later process finds an earlier run's upstream repo (`git commit` has nothing to commit) or package cache (a miss served as a hit)
detail: MEASURED on Linux x86_64 at 28e7ca8d8c. One `cargo test --features llvm` leg had 6 reds: git_fetch::tests::{clones_default_branch_and_resolves_head, checks_out_a_specific_rev, checks_out_a_tag, missing_manifest_is_an_error} (`git ["commit", "--quiet", "-m", "init"] failed:` with an empty stderr; git prints `nothing to commit` on stdout) and registry_proxy::tests::{cache_miss_fetches_then_hit_serves_without_refetch, corrupted_cache_entry_is_refetched} (inner fetch counted 1 where 2 was expected). Re-run alone they passed. Cause: `temp_dir` (src/git_fetch.rs) and `temp_cache_root` (src/registry_proxy.rs) name their directories `kara-gitfetch-<tag>-<pid>-<n>` and `kara-regcache-<pid>-<n>`, create them with create_dir_all, and never remove them. /tmp held 1,485 and 456 such directories, some pids twice. Deterministic repro: run the lib test binary twice under `unshare -pf --mount-proc` (pid 1 both times). The second run fails exactly these 6, and no other lib test fails that way. Shipping code is not affected: GitCliProvider only clones and checks out, and the fixture sets its own git identity, so no ambient identity is needed.
fix: e9c07ff635 (its message names B-2026-10-31-8, an id another session filed at the same time for an unrelated row; this is that commit's row): each fixture removes its directory before creating it, and the fixture's git helper prints git's stdout as well as stderr. Verified: three consecutive same-pid runs (`unshare -pf --mount-proc <lib test binary> git_fetch registry_proxy`) pass 72 of 72 over the directories the failing runs left. Before the fix, the second same-pid run failed all 6. Gate at e9c07ff635: fmt, both clippy legs, test --all 10019 passed, test --features llvm 10119 passed, 0 failed.

title: `t.to_string()` under `T: Display` at a `#[derive(Display)]` type does not build: `the method call .to_string with no resolved callee is not lowered yet`; the same call on the type itself works
detail: MEASURED at 6bae6aa8d2 while working B-2026-10-31-6: `#[derive(Display)] struct P { x: i64, s: String }`, `fn show[T: Display](t: T) -> String { t.to_string() }`, `println(show(p))` is refused by `karac run` and `karac build` with `error[mir]: build: 8:5 in show[P]: the method call .to_string with no resolved callee is not lowered yet`. `p.to_string()` prints `P { x: 1, s: a }`, and a hand-written `impl Display` works through the generic. The no-resolved-callee branch of the method-call lowering (`src/mir/lower.rs`, the B-2026-10-29-31 `display_bound` block) sent a `Display.to_string` bound to the builtin conversion only for a non-ADT receiver.
fix: 103da49c5f (Thread A). The no-resolved-callee branch of the method-call lowering sent a `Display.to_string` bound to the builtin conversion only for a non-ADT receiver; it now does so for a derived-Display ADT too (a hand-written `impl Display` is still taken by the bound lookup above it). `show(u)` with `fn show[T: Display](t: T) -> String { t.to_string() }` prints `User { name: alice, age: 3 }`, as `u.to_string()` does, on run and build. Pinned in corpus/core/debug_text_fmt_debug.

title: `dbg(x)` and a failed `assert_eq` ignore a hand-written `impl Debug`: `dbg(p)` with `impl Debug for Pt { fn fmt_debug(self) -> String { f"Pt<{self.x}>" } }` prints `p = Pt { x: 4 }`, the derived field form, though `p.fmt_debug()` gives `Pt<4>`
detail: MEASURED at 6bae6aa8d2 on `karac run` (the shape is the same on `__mir-run`): design.md § Display and Debug makes `Debug` the trait `dbg` and `assert_eq` messages use, so a hand-written `fmt_debug` should be what they print, at every depth (`dbg([p])` too). The `debug_string` and `dbg` natives render through `display_typed` with `debug_render` set (`src/mir/interp.rs`), which honours `Secret`'s redaction and a user `Display` only when not rendering Debug, and never calls a user `fmt_debug`; the LLVM backend's `debug_string` (`src/backend/mir/call.rs`) has the same gap. The fix needs the renderer to call the program's `fmt_debug` for a type that has one, as it calls a user `to_string` for Display.
fix: 5fd7621902 (Thread A). A program's own `fmt_debug` now wins wherever a Debug text is rendered (`dbg`, a failed `assert_eq`'s operands, `x.fmt_debug()`): on its own, as a field of a derived Debug, a Vec element, an Option or enum payload, a tuple part. The MIR builder queues the `fmt_debug` body of every type a `dbg`'d or debug-rendered value contains (`queue_nested_debugs`, the Debug twin of `queue_nested_displays`, `src/mir/lower.rs`); the interpreter's `display_typed` (`user_debug`, `src/mir/interp.rs`) and the backend's `fmt_adt` (`src/backend/mir/fmt.rs`, agreed with the drop schedule) call it as they call a user `to_string` for Display. The body renders by Display, so a String it interpolates is not quoted (`fmt_user` clears the debug flag around the returned text). The row's program: `dbg(p)` prints `p = Pt<4>`; `assert_eq` shows `left:  Pt<1>` / `right: Pt<2>`. Pinned by corpus/core/debug_user_impl_at_depth (spec; mir-interp, mir-llvm, mir-build) and tests/debug_user_impl.rs (dbg and assert_eq stderr on the interpreter and compiled at -O0 and -O2); control without the change: 0 passed, 2 failed. Found alongside: a builtin method straight on a unit-variant path does not build (B-2026-10-31-17).

title: `karac check` refuses moving a binding after a closure literal passed as a call argument (an `own MutFn` parameter, `with_provider`) that writes it: "moved inside a loop" with no loop around the move; both MIR backends accept the program and print the right answer
fix: 6f3c7e976e: a closure literal passed straight as an argument to a resolved call (a free function, `with_provider`) and not recorded as escaping runs within that call, so `src/use_classifier.rs` `record_statement_closures` now counts it among the statement's closures the way it already counted a method chain's (B-2026-10-29-43). Its writes to a capture end with the statement, and a later move of the capture is an ordinary move, not "moved inside a loop". The refusals that must stay are pinned beside the accepted shapes in tests/core_call_closure_write_before_move.rs: accepted are the row's `own MutFn` program and the `with_provider` shape; refused are a move inside a real loop ("is moved inside a loop"), a closure that escapes ("moved into an escaping closure") and a use after the move ("moved here, used again here"). examples/weave now gets past `enriched` and stops only at B-2026-10-31-14. Gate green (gate133); corpus and kata sweeps show no new failures against the control.
