title: A bare (borrowing) parameter of a refinement type does not take its argument the way a parameter of the base type does: an owned `NonEmpty[T]` (`type NonEmpty[T] = Vec[T] where self.len() > 0`) is refused ("expected 'ref NonEmpty', found 'NonEmpty'"), `p * 2` on a `p: Pos` (`i64 where self > 0`) is refused ("type 'ref Pos' does not implement trait Mul"), and a non-generic Vec refinement passes `karac check` but MIR refuses it ("a type that failed to check is not lowered yet")
fix: FIXED by a4cbb4119a. A bare parameter of a refinement now borrows exactly as a parameter of its base does, a copy base included, and the refinement adds only its predicate. (1) D5 (src/d5_params.rs) counts a non-generic type alias over a copy type as copy-like, so `p: Pos` (`i64 where self > 0`) is a copy and `p * 2` checks. (2) A method call or an index on a `ref`/`mut ref` of a refinement goes to a borrow of its base when the refinement has no method of its own (expr_method_call.rs receiver strip; types.rs `strip_refinement_through_ref` at the index object); this was case 3's MIR refusal. (3) A generic refinement is instantiated at each use: the synthetic `try_from` is generic in the alias's parameters (env_build.rs) and the assoc-call path passes them (expr_call.rs); inference collects, instantiates, resolves and unifies through `Type::Refinement`, and `types_compatible`/`is_subtype` compare two of the same refinement by base; the predicate of a generic alias is typed in the alias's own generic frame (items.rs). The MIR builder runs that predicate with the alias's arguments read off the value's type (`TyCtxt::match_params` in src/ty.rs, `refinement_args` in src/mir/lower.rs), so `NonEmpty.try_from(v)` and `w as NonEmpty[i64]` check `self.len() > 0` on a `Vec[i64]` or `Vec[String]`. The row's three programs print 6, 6 and 2 under check, __mir-run, run and build; pins in tests/refinement_params.rs (5 tests; control arm on the parent tree: 0 passed, 5 failed).

title: A closure that consumes a captured iterator (`for line in lines` over a `split` captured from outside) and is called once passes `karac check`, but the MIR builder refuses it ("cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place"), so check accepts what neither backend can run
fix: 6b6b058afa. The MIR builder's capture walk (src/mir/lower.rs, mv_expr's For arm) treated every `for` iterable as a borrow, so a closure looping over a captured `Iterator` captured it by `ref` and the loop's move out of it was refused. It now treats an iterable whose type is an ADT implementing `Iterator` as consumed (core §4.6, §9.1), so the capture is by move; a `for` over a captured `Vec` still borrows it. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_closure_consumes_captured_iterator (spec), which the pre-fix binary refuses with the row's error and the fix passes on interp and JIT. weave's remaining check errors are B-2026-10-31-13 and -14; its conformance-baseline reason no longer names this row.

title: `karac build` and `karac run` still do the front end's work twice in CPU: `check_v2` and the MIR builder's `frontend()` now run on two threads at once (6777e6ea51), but each parses, resolves, typechecks and ownership-checks the program and its library
detail: Remainder of B-2026-10-31-7. At 6777e6ea51 `src/cli/build_v2.rs` `build()` and `src/cli/run_v2.rs` (JIT path) run `check_v2` on a second thread (`run_v2::checked_alongside`) while `build_source_in_order_later` / `build_source` lower the source on the CLI thread, so the build's latency drops by about the check's time (kata 2 iterative, debug binary: build ~530 to ~410 ms, run ~350 to ~260 ms), but the CPU work and the two front ends' combined peak memory remain. Sharing one front end needs the check's typed program carried into lowering with the library bodies checked: check leaves them unchecked (B-2026-10-19-21), and its pass order differs from `frontend()`'s (prepare_for_resolve, D5 bare-param borrows, resolve_v2, typecheck with the pruned library, comptime, rewrite_ufcs, ownershipcheck). The interpreter path of `karac run` (`--interp`, or a build without llvm) still runs the two in sequence. PROGRESS e9682e92f8 (Thread A, 2026-11-02): `karac run --interp` builds the MIR on a worker while the check runs on the main thread, and runs once the check passes (kata 2, debug: 344 -> 231 ms). Per the review thread's ruling, two steps remain: (1) make check's library-body passes as cheap as frontend()'s, landed alone with before/after numbers; (2) share one Pipeline between check and build, only if kata 2 wall time stays within noise and large programs save CPU, coordinated with Thread B first. PROGRESS 6927dcb48a (Thread A, 2026-11-02), step one: a check that keeps the library's bodies (KARAC_CHECK_LIBRARY_BODIES=1) resolves and type-checks them, then sets them aside (moved, `take_library_bodies` / `restore_library_bodies` in src/mir/lower.rs) for lower, effects, ownership, the MIR checks and the rest, and puts them back; its report is the default check's (tests/check_library_bodies_aside.rs). Median wall time with the bodies kept, before -> after: kata 2 iterative ~165 -> ~131 ms, apps/loadtest/proxy_serve ~232 -> ~198 ms, apps/prism ~396 -> ~368 ms; the default check unchanged within noise. What remains between a bodies-kept check and frontend(): the strict typecheck's extra walks over library bodies (core_ref_write, core_escape and per-function strict checks, about 36M instructions of 220M on kata 2). Step two (one Pipeline shared with the build) is next, coordinated with Thread B first.
fix: 6927dcb48a (step one, what landed). Relocated, not fixed: a check that keeps the library's bodies resolves and type-checks them, then sets them aside for the later passes, so it costs about what the builder's frontend() does (kata 2 iterative ~165 -> ~131 ms with the bodies kept; tests/check_library_bodies_aside.rs). Step two, sharing one Pipeline serially between check and build, was measured before it was built, at bd06c31fe7 (release, KARAC_MIR_TIME=1, medians), and dropped. Any serial version must wait for the check's typecheck before it can lower, and today the two overlap. On kata 2 iterative that is at least 164 + ~10 ms against a 151 ms `run` today (+15-20% wall, ~15% less CPU). On corpus/apps/cli/mini_markdown it is at least 3.2 + ~1.08 s against ~3.2 s (+34% wall, ~20% less CPU). Both fail the review's bar that kata 2's wall time stay within noise. The duplicated front end's CPU is now tracked as docs/deferred.md § Tooling, "Shared Front End for `check` and `build`". That item carries the measurements, shape (a) (one typecheck, then the check's later passes and the builder's lowering on two threads over the shared typed program; estimated mini_markdown ~2.85 s wall / ~4.25 s CPU against 3.2 / 5.4 s), and shape (b) (the build takes the MIR the check already builds for the user's bodies).
tracker: docs/deferred.md § Tooling: Shared Front End for `check` and `build`

title: A builtin method called straight on a unit-variant path does not build: `Slot.Empty.to_string()` (derived Display) and `Slot.Empty.fmt_debug()` are `the builtin Slot.to_string is not lowered yet`, though `let e = Slot.Empty; e.to_string()` works, and so does a user method (`Slot.Empty.size()`)
detail: MEASURED at 4e4233e962 plus B-2026-10-31-12's change, `karac run`: `#[derive(Display, Debug)] enum Slot { Full(i64), Empty }` then `println(Slot.Empty.to_string());` is refused with `error[mir]: build: 8:13 in main: the builtin Slot.to_string is not lowered yet`; `Slot.Empty.fmt_debug()` the same. `karac check` accepts both. The call reaches the builtin-path branch of the MIR builder's call lowering (`src/mir/lower.rs`, `_ if name.contains('.')`), which reads `Slot.Empty.to_string` as the static `Slot.to_string` and refuses it because the call's type (`String`) is not `Slot`. A user method on the same receiver (`impl Slot { fn size(self) -> i64 }`, `Slot.Empty.size()`) prints 0.
fix: 50b9950071. `Slot.Empty.to_string()` parses as a call of the path `Slot.Empty.to_string`; the MIR builder's builtin-path branch read it as the static `Slot.to_string` and refused it. A unit variant is a value, so the call is now lowered as the method call on that value (src/mir/lower.rs, `variant_method`): the same call node, with a synthetic receiver path the builder places as the variant, through the method-call lowering a binding receiver takes. Only a fieldless variant of a non-generic enum takes this route. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_method_on_unit_variant_path (spec), covering to_string, fmt_debug, clone, a user method and discriminant on the path; a pre-fix binary refuses it with the row's error and the fix passes on interp and JIT.

title: `karac check` accepts a field access on an enum value (`e.message` on an `IoError`, `e.x` on a user enum), then `karac run`/`build` refuse it as "a type that failed to check is not lowered yet"; a missing struct field is caught
fix: aa06e8793b. A field access on an enum value is now a typecheck error at `karac check`: no field 'message' on enum 'IoError': an enum has no fields; `match` on its variants to reach a payload. The access used to fall through to the imported-struct probe in src/typechecker/fields.rs (`infer_imported_field_access`), which found no struct and returned `Type::Error` with no diagnostic, so check passed and only the MIR builder refused the program ("a type that failed to check is not lowered yet"). The new `env.enums` arm in `infer_field_access_on_ty` catches it before that probe. The same diagnostic family was tidied in the same commit: a tuple or closure receiver is named by its type (`(i64, i64)`, `Fn(i64) -> i64`) instead of 'this type'; a type with no nameable fields says "which has no fields" instead of an empty "available fields:" list (`Vec`, `Map`); and a compiler-internal `__` field (Request's `__id`) is never offered. Pins: tests/field_access_no_field.rs (2 tests: user enum, IoError after fs.read_to_string, Option; tuple, Vec, Request, and a struct that still lists its fields). Control arm on the unfixed tree a98bf7648a: 0 passed, 2 failed. gate135 green.

title: kara-lsp checks a different language from `karac check`: `karac check` passes on the `karac new --cli` scaffold, but the editor shows 3 errors (no `count` on Vec, twice, and E_INDEX_MOVE_NON_COPY on `args[1]`), because `karac::check_source` runs neither `strict_core` nor the Kāra library
detail: MEASURED on a fresh clone of main at f45fdba6a0, built as the README says with KARAC_RELEASE_TAG=v0.9.0 (`karac 0.9.0+gf45fdba6a`) and freshly built runtime archives. `karac new tool --cli`, then `karac check` (and `karac check src/main.kara`): All checks passed; `karac test` 2 passed; `karac build` and the binary work. kara-lsp (built with `cargo build --release -p kara-lsp`) on didOpen of tool/src/main.kara publishes three typecheck errors: 12:18 and 15:16 `no method 'count' on type 'Vec': iterator adaptors/terminals require an explicit .iter()` (on `line.split_whitespace().count()` and `text.lines().count()`), and 32:22 `cannot move args[1] out of an index`. Cause, read from the code: the LSP's `analyze` (lsp/src/analysis.rs) calls `karac::check_source`, which is `run_static_checks` in src/lib.rs, a hand-written parse/resolve/typecheck/effect/ownership sequence; the CLI's `karac check` (src/cli/run_check_cmds.rs cmd_check) runs `Pipeline::new(..).strict_core().with_library()`. The library is where `split_whitespace`/`lines` return iterators. So every file that uses the Kāra-side library shows false errors in the editor, starting with the scaffold `karac new --cli` writes. Hover is also typed by that sequence: hovering `count` shows `Fn(StringSlice) -> Counts` for a parameter written `Str`. The web playground shares `run_static_checks`.
fix: afe068e2fe, with b363f8496a. Natively, `karac::check_source` and `karac::hover_at`, which kara-lsp calls, now build the same `Pipeline` that `cmd_check` builds: `Pipeline::new(..).strict_core().with_library()` then `run_all_checks()`, in the new src/cli/editor.rs. Their diagnostics are read back from the records `collect_diagnostics` builds for `--output=json`, with each one's byte span (a new `DiagnosticJson::spans`, kept in step with `entries`) and its fix (`replacement`, `fix_diff`, or else `fix_it`; b363f8496a stopped a typecheck fix being offered twice, since it is in the JSON as both `fix_it` and `replacement`). `PlaygroundDiagnostic` gained a `severity`, and kara-lsp shows warnings and notes as WARNING and INFORMATION. The wasm playground has no CLI and keeps `run_static_checks`. With this change kara-lsp publishes no diagnostics on the `karac new --cli` scaffold, and hovering `text.lines()` shows the library iterator rather than a `Vec`. CORRECTION to the row: hover's `Fn(StringSlice) -> Counts` is not from the editor pipeline. `type_display` renders `Str` by its internal name on both paths, and that is left as it is. Pins: tests/editor_check.rs (3 tests: every `karac new` scaffold has no editor diagnostics and passes `karac check`; the README fix-loop program gets the CLI's span, fix and severity; a library iterator hovers as one). Control arm on a98bf7648a: 1 passed, 2 failed (the fix-loop test passes on both trees). Running the real checker through check_source exposed two problems that the old pipeline had hidden: book snippets written for the pre-D5 model (fixed in a43aa893cd; book_snippets_compile now counts errors only) and `karac fmt` dropping effect arguments (B-2026-10-31-31). gate135 green.

title: Every HTTP server program prints `BOUND_PORT=8080` on its standard output (`Server.serve`/`serve_ws`, run and build alike): the test-harness line B-2026-10-15-69 removed from `TcpListener.bind` is still unconditional in the HTTP server
detail: MEASURED on a fresh clone of main at f45fdba6a0, built as the README says with KARAC_RELEASE_TAG=v0.9.0 (`karac 0.9.0+gf45fdba6a`) and freshly built runtime archives. `karac new svc` (the default backend scaffold), then `karac build` and `./dist/svc`, or `karac run`: standard output is `[info] Listening on http://127.0.0.1:8080` then `BOUND_PORT=8080`; the README's own server example (`Server.serve("127.0.0.1:8080", handle)`) prints it too. The line comes from runtime/src/lib.rs (the `serve` accept loop, ~8620-8634: `writeln!(stdout, "BOUND_PORT={}", local.port())`, commented as a smoke-test convention). The TCP and TLS listeners print theirs only under `KARAC_ANNOUNCE_PORT` and only for port 0, on stderr (runtime/src/mir_io.rs announce_port, runtime/src/mir_tls.rs), per B-2026-10-15-69: a program's own output never carries it. The server path should follow the same rule; the tests that read it back should set the variable.
fix: 3d8fe2ab97. The line came from the library server, not the runtime: `Server.__announce` (runtime/stdlib/source/http_server.kara), run by serve, serve_static, serve_tls, serve_ws and serve_ws_tls after binding, wrote `BOUND_PORT=<n>` on every bind. It is removed. The listener under each server (`TcpListener.bind`, `TlsListener.bind_tls`) already announces only for a port-0 bind under `KARAC_ANNOUNCE_PORT`, on stderr (B-2026-10-15-69), so a harness sees one line and a program none; io.md says so, and the v2 test harnesses (tests/http_server.rs, tests/mir_io.rs `exchange`) and the ws_idle_holder reap scripts set the variable. Pinned by `server_prints_no_bound_port_unless_asked_on_both_backends` (tests/mir_io.rs), which fails on the old library with `BOUND_PORT=39661` on stderr (0 passed; 1 failed). The server corpus entries pass on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-build. The tokio `karac_runtime_serve_*` entry points the row cites still hold a stdout write, but no v2 program reaches them.

title: Parse errors show the Rust `Debug` form of the token: `Expected LeftBracket, found Identifier { name: "tool", raw: false }`
detail: MEASURED on a fresh clone of main at f45fdba6a0, built as the README says with KARAC_RELEASE_TAG=v0.9.0 (`karac 0.9.0+gf45fdba6a`) and freshly built runtime archives. `karac run README.md` in a `karac new --cli` project (a new user passing the program's argument without `--`; the README there is `# tool`) prints error[parse]: README.md:1:3: Expected LeftBracket, found Identifier { name: "tool", raw: false }. The text is `format!("Expected {:?}, found {:?}", expected, self.peek_token())` at src/parser.rs:1026, with siblings at src/parser.rs:1488 (method name), :1513 (attribute argument name) and src/parser/types.rs:727 (type). A user-facing message should name the token as source text: expected `[`, found `tool`. B-2026-10-24-27 fixed the lexer's error tokens the same way.
fix: bdcc591b6d. `Token::describe` (src/token.rs) names a token as source text: punctuation, keywords, identifiers, numbers, chars and labels in backticks, a literal whose text is not the point by what it is, EOF as "the end of the file". All five `{:?}` sites use it (src/parser.rs `expect`, the unexpected-identifier fallback, the method-name and attribute-name errors; src/parser/types.rs `Expected type`), so the README case reads "Expected `[`, found `tool`". The tests that matched the old spelling now match the new (design_md_code_blocks' `;` sweep would otherwise have matched nothing). Pinned by `parse_errors_name_tokens_as_source_text` (tests/parser.rs); a pre-fix binary prints the Debug forms.

title: `karac build` refuses the project `karac new --lib` just made ("the v2 build makes an executable from src/main.kara … v2 does not build a library package yet"), and on a binary project it prints a slice-2 manifest dump (project/edition/root/target/entry/modules) before `Built:`
detail: MEASURED on a fresh clone of main at f45fdba6a0, built as the README says with KARAC_RELEASE_TAG=v0.9.0 (`karac 0.9.0+gf45fdba6a`) and freshly built runtime archives. `karac new mylib --lib`: `karac check`, `karac fmt --check` and `karac test` (1 passed) all succeed; `karac build` exits 1 with error: the v2 build makes an executable from src/main.kara, and <root> has none; v2 does not build a library package yet (src/cli/build_v2.rs:166). A fresh user gets a scaffold from the tool whose build fails, and the message names an internal milestone (`v2`). Either `karac build` on a library checks it and says there is nothing to link (what `cargo build` on a lib reports as success), or `karac new --lib`'s README/help says build is for binaries, with a message that does not say `v2`. Separately, `karac build` in the default and `--cli` projects prints project:, edition:, root:, target:, entry: bin, modules: 1 and `<crate root> <path>` (BuildV2's `print`, src/cli/build_v2.rs:466) before `Built: …/dist/<name>`. `karac --help` still describes build with "(Project-mode file walker lands in CR-24 slice 3; slice 2 only verifies the manifest.)", so the dump looks like slice-2 verification output left on.
fix: 7da6557e44. src/cli/build_v2.rs cmd_build_v2_project: a library package (src/lib.kara, as karac new --lib makes it) has no main, and 0.9 has no library artifact (--crate-type is the deferred exported C ABI), so its build runs the same package check karac check runs (run_check_cmds::cmd_check_project) and on success prints "library package `<name>`: checked, nothing to link (a library has no `main`; the packages that depend on it build it)", exit 0; a library that does not check fails with check's output and exit 1. The text-mode package summary (project/edition/root/target/entry/modules/deps) is gone: a package build prints only Built:. Its fields stay in the --output=json document, which now also names the dependency packages (deps: name, modules, src). The build's flag refusals and karac build --help say "not in 0.9" instead of v2 / M3 (the --help slice-2 text the row quotes was already gone). This deliberately reverses B-2026-10-25-18's text summary, which was restored for legacy parity, on the review thread's call; tooling reads the JSON. Tests: tests/build_library_package.rs (new: lib scaffold builds; a lib that does not check fails as check does; a bin scaffold prints no summary); tests/build_v2.rs and tests/cli.rs summary pins read the JSON document now, and project_build_wasm_target_selects_wasm_platform_module proves the platform filter by giving the native siblings a type error. Control: the pre-fix binary exits 1 on the lib scaffold with the v2 message. Gate: 10059 default, 10163 llvm, the one test that read the dump fixed and re-run on both legs, both clippy legs re-run.

title: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE (struct `invariant` stays unlowered for 0.9; `karac check` now refuses it as a later track): The MIR builder refuses every program with a struct `invariant` ("a type invariant is not lowered yet"), so examples/weave, which checks since B-2026-10-31-13/-14, still does not run, build or test on v2
detail: MEASURED on main at 8823ad9231 (debug karac, --features llvm). `karac check` in examples/weave: All checks passed. `karac run examples/weave/src/main.kara`, `karac build` and `karac test` in the package: error[mir]: build: 107:5: a type invariant is not lowered yet. 107:5 is `invariant self.row_count >= 0` on `pub struct Summary`. The refusal is deliberate (src/mir/lower.rs, the loop after the statics: "Contracts are checked at run time; until the builder emits those checks, a program with one is refused rather than run without them"). design.md § Contracts Rule 3: an invariant is checked at construction and at every pub-method exit. The README's expected output (3 ok rows, 3 skips, `summary: 3 rows, usd_total=94.48920000000001`) is the oracle once it runs. Two corpus fixtures also carry invariants (corpus/fixtures/codegen/structs/test_e2e_constructor_non_self_return_not_checked, enums/test_e2e_generic_method_checks_the_struct_invariant).
fix: FIXED by 76062d0e3a, as a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE (the review thread's ruling, 10-31): struct invariants are not lowered for 0.9. Contracts sit in deferred.md's verification track, a later track (design.md § Tracks), so the bug was that `karac check` accepted what run and build refuse. `karac check` (and every v2 command, which checks first) now refuses `invariant` and `impl invariant` by name with the new code E_DEFERRED_TRACK (TypeErrorKind::DeferredToLaterTrack): "`invariant` on `Summary` is not available: struct invariants are contracts, which are in the verification track (deferred.md § Contracts) and not in 0.9. Check the property where the value is built, in a constructor". The MIR builder's own refusal stays as a backstop. examples/weave's `Summary` now has a constructor `Summary.new` that `requires row_count >= 0`, and weave prints its README output on `__mir-run`, `karac run` and a native `karac build`. The README's `-2` became `-2.0`, which is how design.md § Printing prints floats. Running weave also turned up B-2026-10-31-29 (an ensures clause that matches on `result` moved the value out of the return place), fixed in the same commit. Pins: tests/contracts_v2.rs (3 tests; control arm on the parent tree: 0 passed, 3 failed). The 25 class-e corpus fixtures with invariants (post-m1:contract) now fail at check instead of at the MIR build; all are class e, so the M1 bar does not change.

title: `x.eq(y)` and `x.partial_cmp(y)` on a type that derives `PartialEq` / `PartialOrd` are `no method 'eq'` / `no method 'partial_cmp'` at check, though design.md § Operator traits declares both methods and `==` / `<` already compare such a type; `cmp` on a derived `Ord` resolves
detail: MEASURED with a release karac built from 50b9950071: `#[derive(PartialEq, PartialOrd)] struct P { x: i64, y: f64 }`, then `a.eq(b)` is `error[typecheck]: no method 'eq' on type 'P'` and `a.partial_cmp(b)` is `no method 'partial_cmp' on type 'P'`; on an enum and through a unit-variant path the same. `1.eq(1)` and `1.5.partial_cmp(2.0)` check and run (the scalars register builtin impls in env_build.rs), and `a.cmp(b)` on a derived `Ord` resolves through method_nominal_tail.rs's `cmp` arm. Under `fn f[T: PartialEq](a: T, b: T) { a.eq(b) }` at a derived type check accepts and the MIR builder refuses (`the method call .eq with no resolved callee is not lowered yet`), and `.partial_cmp` under `T: PartialOrd` the same. `ne`, `lt` and the other operator names are not declared on these traits in design.md and are out of scope. Found while fixing B-2026-10-31-17.
fix: b468c6c249. The checker now claims `eq` and `partial_cmp` on a named type that supports `PartialEq` / `PartialOrd` and has no method of that name of its own (src/typechecker/method_nominal_tail.rs, beside the derived `cmp` arm). The MIR builder lowers `eq` as `==` and `partial_cmp` as the derived order wrapped in `Some`, or `None` when the deciding float pair is unordered (an `unordered` flag the float compare in `cmp_places` sets; src/mir/lower.rs `partial_cmp_places`), directly and under `T: PartialEq` / `T: PartialOrd`. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_derived_eq_partial_cmp_methods (spec), which a pre-fix binary refuses at check (12 errors) and the fix passes on interp and JIT. `x.hash(mut h)` stays open as B-2026-10-31-25.

title: `x.hash(mut h)` with a user `Hasher` is `no method 'hash'` on a type that derives `Hash` and on the primitives (`7.hash(mut h)`), though design.md § Hashing declares `trait Hash { fn hash[H: Hasher](self, hasher: mut ref H); }` and says the derive generates ordinary `self.a.hash(mut hasher)` code
detail: MEASURED with a release karac built from 50b9950071: `struct Sum { total: u64 }` with `impl Hasher for Sum` (write adds the bytes, finish returns the total), `#[derive(Hash)] struct P { x: i64, y: i64 }`, then `let mut h = Sum { total: 0 }; a.hash(mut h);` is `error[typecheck]: no method 'hash' on type 'P'`, and `7.hash(mut g)` is `no method 'hash' on type 'i64'`. A table with a user `BuildHasher` already feeds a derived key to the hasher, but through glue in each backend (src/mir/interp.rs `table_hashes`, src/backend/mir/key.rs) rather than a callable `hash` method, so a fix is either a MIR-generated derived `hash` body per type (fields in order; an enum's discriminant, then its fields; a Vec's length, then its elements; the bytes collections.md § Hashing lists for each built-in type) or a lowering onto the same glue. Split from B-2026-10-31-24 because it needs that per-type body, which eq / partial_cmp do not.
fix: 56f675ddce. The checker accepts `hash` on a type whose Hash is built in or derived (src/typechecker/derives.rs hash_is_builtin; expr_method_call.rs refuses an argument that is no Hasher), and the MIR builder lowers it (src/mir/lower.rs hash_place / derived_hash / hash_seq / hasher_call) to the calls collections.md § Hashing lists: write_<width> for an integer, write_u8 / write_u32 for bool / char, a string's UTF-8 bytes then write_u8(0xff), a sequence's length by write_usize then its elements, a tuple's or derived struct's fields in order, a derived enum's variant index by write_u32 then its payload, and a hand-written Hash by its own body; the same under `T: Hash`. A type whose hashing reaches itself calls `T.hash#derived#H`, built once, as derived == does. The hasher's default write_* methods are the ones its impl carries. Pins: corpus/core/ok_hash_into_user_hasher (the spec's bytes, identical on mir-interp, mir-llvm, karac build and karac run; the pre-fix binary refuses it at MIR) and err_hash_into_non_hasher. Gate: 10049 default, 10152 llvm.

title: `Child.wait_with_output()` leaks the child's 32-byte handle on the compiled backend: the call takes `own self`, and nothing frees the `Kid` box `karac_mir_command` allocated (corpus fixtures/mir_io/PROCESSES and PROCESS_SURFACE fail the ASan lane)
detail: Found by the pre-tag ASan sweep at a894bbaf13 (drop schedule, 2026-10-31). Repro under `karac __mir-llvm-asan`: `fn main() { let b = Command.new("printf").arg("x").stdout(Stdio.piped()).spawn().unwrap(); let out = b.wait_with_output().unwrap(); println(f"[{String.from_utf8(out.stdout).unwrap()}]"); }` prints `[x]`, then LeakSanitizer: Direct leak of 32 byte(s) in 1 object(s) allocated from karac_mir_command. `spawn` + `wait()` does not leak, because the binding is dropped through `karac_mir_child_free` (src/backend/mir/drop.rs `ChildProcess`). `wait_with_output(own self)` (runtime/stdlib/source/process.kara) consumes the receiver into the native call (src/backend/mir/io.rs child_native, op 3), which takes the `Child` out of the `Kid` but never frees the box. Present before the overnight work: the same leak at f7f2075954 and d059343bbc. Proposed fix: free the handle (`karac_mir_child_free`) after op 3. Owner: Thread C (io.rs), asked 2026-10-31.
fix: 6a105f63ba. `wait_with_output(own self)` consumes the receiver into the native call, so the call is the handle's last use and nothing drops the binding after it; src/backend/mir/io.rs child_native now calls `karac_mir_child_free` on the handle after op 3 (the runtime has already taken the `Child` out of the `Kid`, so the free drops only the box). No double free: the moved binding has no drop of its own. corpus fixtures/mir_io/PROCESSES and PROCESS_SURFACE pass the ASan lane (both 86 before, at a894bbaf13, f7f2075954 and d059343bbc), the repro prints `[x]` with exit 0 under `__mir-llvm-asan`, and `__mir-llvm-run` still prints `[x]`. Pin: tests/mir_child_wait_with_output.rs (on ci.yml's llvm list). Gate: fmt, both clippy legs, wasm clippy, test --all 10049 passed, --features llvm 10153 passed, 0 failed.

title: A provider through a generic trait (`trait Channel[T] { fn send(ref self, v: T) -> T; }`, `impl Channel[i64] for Echo`) passes `v` by value where the impl body reads it as a reference: `__mir-run` stops with `deref of non-reference Int(41)`, and the built program SEGVs in `Echo.send` (corpus fixtures/codegen/generics/e2e_generic_provider_trait_bound)
detail: Found by the pre-tag ASan sweep at a894bbaf13 (drop schedule, 2026-10-31): the corpus entry fails the ASan lane with SEGV on address 0x29 in kara.Echo.send, called from push{RequestCh=Echo}. Source: `pub trait Channel[T] { fn send(ref self, v: T) -> T; } pub effect resource RequestCh: Channel[i64]; pub struct Echo { bump: i64 } impl Channel[i64] for Echo { fn send(ref self, v: i64) -> i64 { v + self.bump } } pub fn push(v: i64) -> i64 with reads(RequestCh) { RequestCh.send(v) } fn main() { with_provider[RequestCh](Echo { bump: 1 }, || { println(f"{push(41)}"); }); }`, expected `42`. `karac __mir-run`: `error[mir]: run: in main at bb0[term]: in main.c0{RequestCh=Echo} at bb0[term]: in push{RequestCh=Echo} at bb0[term]: in Echo.send at bb0[0]: deref of non-reference Int(41)`. `karac build`: the binary exits 139. Echo.send's IR takes `(ptr, ptr)`, so the body expects the trait's bare `v: T` borrowed (D5), while the call through the provider passes the i64 by value. Same at f7f2075954 and d059343bbc, so it predates the overnight work. Owner: Thread B (MIR builder, providers).
fix: FIXED by 02e3dbefde. `resource_call` (src/mir/lower.rs) types each argument at its bound method's parameter type, but a trait method has no body, so its parameters carry no typed-HIR type and the bound's arguments (`Channel[i64]`) are not kept; it fell back to the argument's own type. D5 rewrites the trait's bare `v: T` to `ref T` and every provider's impl takes that borrow position by position (`Echo.send(ref self, v: ref i64)`), but the fallback saw an i64, a Copy type, and passed it by value: `__mir-run` stopped on `deref of non-reference Int(41)` and the built program SEGV'd in Echo.send. The fallback now keeps the trait's written mode: a `ref` or `mut ref` parameter lends the argument (unless it already is a reference). Direct and generic-bound calls were never affected. Pinned by tests/provider_generic_trait.rs a_generic_trait_resource_lends_a_copy_argument_to_its_provider (the row's program, 42) and a_generic_trait_resource_passes_ref_and_mut_ref_modes_per_instance (ref + mut ref through Store[i64] and Store[String]), on __mir-run and karac run; both fail on the control arm (0 passed, 2 failed). The corpus entry fixtures/codegen/generics/e2e_generic_provider_trait_bound passes on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan.

title: A rare LeakSanitizer report on corpus programs that spawn tasks or run `par` under load (fixtures/coro_e2e/SPAWN_NONBLOCK_SRC, SPAWN_MULTI_CAPTURE_SRC, interpreter/concurrency/test_dbg_json_in_par_emits_numeric_task_id, par_codegen/test_e2e_par_join_branch_float_method)
detail: Found by the pre-tag ASan sweep at a894bbaf13 (drop schedule, 2026-10-31): each of the four reported `detected memory leaks` once in the full ASan lane (4 jobs on a 4-core box, with a cargo build alongside). Re-run alone afterwards: SPAWN_NONBLOCK_SRC leaked 1 of 8 runs, then 0 of 16 alone and 0 of 24 four at a time; SPAWN_MULTI_CAPTURE_SRC 0 of 48; the other two 0 of 8 each. The stack of the one reproduced report was not kept, so the allocation site is unknown; schedule-sensitive, and it needs a captured report before bisecting. Candidates: a task's frame or result freed on a path the pool takes only when a worker is slow, or LeakSanitizer's stop-the-world missing a pointer held in a worker's registers. Owner: drop schedule (stackless coroutines, runtime/src/mir_task.rs).
fix: 433a916e3e (measured at; nothing to fix). Re-run 2026-11-02 by the kata thread: the four named programs, 200 rounds of `scripts/corpus/run.py --backend mir-llvm-asan --jobs 4` with all four filtered in, so the four ran at once in each round on a 4-core box. That is 800 ASan runs, using karac release at 433a916e3e with its runtime archives rebuilt at that sha (after 57efe5bc2f, per-task borrow flags) and KARAC_HASH_SEED=1. LeakSanitizer reported nothing in any run. Rounds 1-37 each failed one entry on stdout only: fixtures/par_codegen/test_e2e_par_join_branch_float_method's stale expected `13` (every lane and legacy print `13.0`), fixed to the spec in 4cf1abff47. run.py puts a sanitizer report ahead of a stdout difference, so none of those failures hid a leak. Rounds 38-200 passed 4 of 4. The row's one reproduced report kept no stack, so if it recurs, the first step is to capture the full LSan report (KARAC_MIR_LL plus the binary) before bisecting.

title: An `ensures(result)` clause that matches on a non-Copy returned value (`match result { Ok(row) => row.n > 0, Err(_) => true }`) moves the value out of the return place: the MIR interpreter stops with "return with _0 not initialized" and the compiled program double-frees or trips a copy_nonoverlapping precondition
fix: FIXED by 76062d0e3a. When the return value is not Copy, return_exit now lends it to the `ensures` clauses: a shared borrow of the return place (or of the par exit variant's payload), bound to each `ensures(result)` name for the checks and restored after them. So a `match result` in the clause binds through the loan and no longer moves out of `_0`. A Copy return still reads the place directly. The row's program prints `a 1` then `empty` on `__mir-run` and `karac run`, and examples/weave's `parse_row` runs. Pin: tests/contracts_v2.rs an_ensures_clause_matching_a_returned_value_leaves_it_returned (control arm on the parent tree fails).

title: A method whose `ensures` reads `old(self.field)` is refused by the MIR builder ("a type that failed to check is not lowered yet" at the body's tail) although `karac check` passes
fix: FIXED by f06ae29b62. The typechecker gave `old(e)` no type: `old` resolved as an unknown function, so the clause's arithmetic carried an error type that `karac check` tolerated and the MIR builder refused. `check_contract_clauses` now sets `in_ensures` while it types an ensures body, and `infer_call` types `old(e)` there as `e` (one unlabelled argument), so MIR's existing `old_vals` snapshot (a clone for a non-Copy `e`) lowers it. Fixed rather than refused, per the review thread's ruling (weave and the post-m1 contract corpus use it). Pinned by tests/contracts_v2.rs old_in_an_ensures_clause_is_its_arguments_value_at_entry (method field, plain parameter, violated clause exits 101) and old_of_a_non_copy_field_snapshots_without_moving_it (Vec and String fields); both fail on the control arm. The five corpus old() fixtures pass on mir-interp and mir-llvm, one ASan-clean.

title: `karac fmt` drops a type's effect argument: `EventBus[with E]` and `EventBus[with writes(OrderDb)]` come back as a bare `EventBus`, so a program `karac check` refuses checks clean after formatting
detail: MEASURED with a debug karac built from origin/main plus B-2026-10-31-18/-19. `karac fmt corpus/core/err_effect_var_unfit/source.kara` rewrites `impl[with E] EventBus[with E]` to `impl[with E] EventBus` and `fn add_note(bus: mut ref EventBus[with writes(OrderDb)])` to `fn add_note(bus: mut ref EventBus)`; `karac check` on the source reports error[effect] 32:18 function value has `writes(Log)`, outside the effect set of `E` (`{writes(OrderDb)}`), and on the formatted text All checks passed. The parser keeps the `with ..` clause in `PathExpr::effect_args`, apart from `generic_args` (src/parser/types.rs ~899-913), and the formatter's `TypeKind::Path` arm (src/formatter/types.rs) printed only `generic_args`. tests/fmt_round_trip.rs (every_corpus_program_checks_the_same_after_formatting, formatting_a_core_pin_or_drop_program_keeps_its_output) did not see it because `karac::check_source` ran an editor-only pipeline that did not report this effect error; once B-2026-10-31-19 made check_source run `karac check`'s pipeline, both went red on this program.
fix: aba8cf09d2. title: An `unsafe extern "C"` import with an `f64` (or any float) parameter or return passes `karac check` but `karac run`, `karac build` and `__mir-run` refuse it: `a parameter or return type of the extern "C" function `sqrt` other than an integer, `bool` or raw pointer is not lowered yet` (src/mir/lower.rs:277)
detail: Found reading the book's ch18 'Calling C from Kara' example at origin/main 35a3d971c: `unsafe extern "C" { fn sqrt(x: f64) -> f64; }` then `unsafe { sqrt(2.0) }` prints 'All checks passed.' under `karac check` and stops at the MIR build on every backend. The same program with only `strlen(*const u8) -> usize` runs and builds (prints 17). Floats are a basic C type (libm), and design.md section 15 extern-c lists them, so check and run disagree on a documented surface. Fix: lower f32/f64 (and #[repr(C)] structs if cheap) across an extern import, or refuse at check naming the types that cross today. The fix also updates docs/book/src/ch18-interop.md, which says floats and #[repr(C)] structs do not cross an import yet in 0.9.
fix: FIXED by 189722227c. f32 and f64 now cross an `extern "C"` import on every backend. The lowering's `extern_ty` (src/mir/lower.rs) admits them; the LLVM backend's `c_type` (src/backend/mir/foreign.rs, cleared with the drop schedule) passes them as float / double with no extension; the MIR interpreter, which calls C through fixed prototypes, passes them in the float registers through `foreign::call_mixed` (src/mir/foreign.rs): x86-64 System V and AArch64 number the integer and float argument registers apart for a non-variadic function, so one prototype of six integer and eight double slots serves every signature that fits, an f32 travelling in the low half of its register. Other platforms keep refusing on the interpreter only. `#[repr(C)]` structs still do not cross an import (unchanged; the MIR build says so), and docs/book/src/ch18-interop.md now says exactly that. Pinned by tests/mir_io.rs: EXTERN_FLOAT (libm sqrt, sqrtf, ldexp with an i32, lrint to i64, three-float fma, atof from a pointer) runs on __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run and build --mir with output matching Python; the two tests that pinned the refusal are flipped, and both fail on the control arm (0 passed, 2 failed).

title: Under the multi-worker pool, `send` on a full bounded `channel(n)` from several producer tasks returns `Err` instead of waiting: compiled programs lose values and print a wrong sum, `__mir-run` and `KARAC_THREADS=1` are right
fix: 59a342fad1. Confirmed cause: under the pool another producer took the last slot between a send's `__ready` (`karac_mir_chan_ready`) and `karac_mir_chan_send`, which answered full, and `chan_send_result` made that Err. The socket calls' armed-call contract (runtime/src/mir_task.rs, "Armed calls") now covers channels: a ready answer from `karac_mir_chan_ready` inside a task arms the channel call it guards (a thread-local in runtime/src/mir.rs); an armed send that finds the channel full answers 3, and an armed recv that finds it empty with a sender left answers 2, having done nothing and set the again bit; codegen (src/backend/mir/cells.rs `unless_not_ready`) then leaves the value and the destination untouched, and the coroutine transform's `__io_again` retry, until now only after a descriptor call (src/mir/coroutine.rs, now `may_be_not_ready`), sends the loop back to `__ready`. Outside a task nothing is armed, so a plain full send answers as before; `BoundedChannel` refuses at once as before; the interpreter's `__io_again` is false. Repeated runs, x86-64 Linux, 4 cores: the row's program prints 619999800000 in 20 of 20 built runs and 3 of 3 `karac run`s (wrong in 3 of 3 before); four producers on channel(64) under KARAC_THREADS=4 lose nothing in 40 of 40 runs (8 of 10 lost values before). corpus mir-llvm over the par/task/channel entries: the 63 failures all failed before the change too. Pin: tests/mir_channel_send_retries.rs (8 runs under four workers, on ci.yml's llvm list). Gate: fmt, both clippy legs, wasm clippy, archives, test --all 10063 passed, --features llvm 10168 passed, 0 failed.

title: kata 38 (count_and_say) runs legacy's instruction count but 1.22-1.28x its cycles on the MIR backend, 1.44x rustc -O on wall time where legacy was 1.10x; the cause is unattributed
detail:
MEASURED 2026-10-31 on the M5 Pro, karac g6697158fa, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via scripts/pmc.c (5-run minima): 1.135G instructions, 185-195M cycles; legacy dd86e3955: 1.074G instructions, 151M cycles. NOT TESTED: code placement. KARAC_TEXT_PAD, the knob that measured arm64's 64-byte-periodic placement on legacy, does not exist in the v2 backend, so a pad sweep builds one layout (it read 185-191M, noise). Next: a cycle profile (`sample` or Instruments) of both builds, or restore a text-pad knob in the MIR driver to bound placement first. The kata README (kara-katas cd80d598) attributed the gap to B-2026-10-31-2's stores; that was wrong and is corrected to cite this row.

M5 re-bench 2026-11-03 (scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh at kara cd7fd85dec, Darwin arm64, min of 5, outputs equal): kata 38 cycles MIR 190.4M vs legacy 148.0M, 1.287x; instructions 1.068x. Still over. | 2026-11-03 (Thread B, 3d8ac8a2c5): arm64 asm (aarch64-linux, apple-m1) shows `say`'s `out` String header kept in a stack slot: the non-ASCII push path called karac_mir_string_push_char with the string's own address, so SROA could not promote it. Every ASCII push then reloaded the length the previous push had just stored (`ldp x27, x2, [sp, #0x20]` ... `str x8, [sp, #0x20]`), a store-to-load chain per push. Legacy keeps ptr/len/cap in registers. 3d8ac8a2c5 passes the runtime a copy of the header: the loop now keeps them in registers. qemu count 1.078x -> 1.058x legacy; x86 callgrind 0.87x. The cycles are what should move. Awaiting an M5 re-run: ONLY=38.

Confirmed by Gowtham's M5 re-run 2026-11-04 (scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh ONLY=<kata> at kara 26bbf303b1, Darwin arm64, min of 5, outputs equal; on battery with light background load, so ±a few %). Kata 38 cycles: MIR 165.4M vs legacy 149.7M, 1.105x; instructions 1.025x (was 1.287x cycles). The wide-char push no longer takes the String header's address, so ptr/len/cap stay in registers.

title: MIR reloads a value the previous loop iteration just stored (kata 64's `dp[c] = cost + min(dp[c], dp[c - 1])` loads dp[c-1] back through an `ldp` that overlaps the last `str`), where legacy carried it in a register: same 15-instruction loop, 1.77x legacy's cycles on the M5; katas 6 and 293 show the same instructions-vs-cycles signature; on x86 it shows on wall time too: kata 1031's prefix-sum loop reloads prefix[i] and the input Vec's buffer pointer every trip, 2.7x rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on
detail: MEASURED 2026-10-31 on the M5 Pro (Apple silicon; found by the Mac kata re-bench), karac g6697158fa vs legacy dd86e3955, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via kara scripts/pmc.c, 5-run minima. bench/minimum_path_sum.kara: legacy 5.223G instructions / 0.729G cycles, MIR 5.277G / 1.293G (1.01x instructions, 1.77x cycles). Inner DP loop, both builds 15 instructions (otool): legacy `ldr x2,[x17,#8]; cmp x2,x16; csel x16,...; adds; str x16,[x17,#8]`, keeping dp[c-1] in x16 from the previous trip; MIR `ldp x2,x1,[x16]; cmp; csel; adds x17,...; str x17,[x16,#8]`, reloading dp[c-1] (the word the previous trip's str wrote) as half of a paired load, so every trip waits on store-to-load forwarding into a load that only partly overlaps the store. In LLVM terms legacy's IR let the stored value be forwarded across the backedge (LoopLoadElimination's shape) and MIR's does not; why (aliasing of the Vec's buffer with its header, the pointer-passing ABI, or a pass ordering) is not attributed. Same signature, mechanism NOT verified: kata 6 row_buffers 0.90x legacy's instructions, 1.70x its cycles (seq lane 1.05x -> 1.69x rustc -O on wall time, kara-katas re-bench 2026-10-31); kata 293 flipgame 1.39x instructions, 2.00x cycles. Corpus-wide the cycles track the instructions (geomean cycles-ratio/instruction-ratio 0.987 over 336 sources, Kara/mir_screen/screen2.tsv), so this is a tail, not a systemic M5 effect. Linux x86 can see the IR difference (two loads per trip where legacy has one) but not the M5 cost; the cycles above are the M5 measurement. ADDED 2026-11-01 (kata thread, x86 Linux, karac 6697158faf, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0): kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1031-maximum-sum-of-two-non-overlapping-subarrays/bench/max_two.kara, 8 interleaved runs, median 0.647 s vs rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on 0.238 s (2.72x) and clang -O3 0.192 s; the same build with 0 rounds runs 11 ms in both, so the gap is in the calls. Callgrind at 10 rounds: 357M instructions vs Rust's 259M, so most of the gap is cycles. objdump of the inlined prefix loop `prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + nums[i]`: Rust is `add (%rbx,%rcx,8),%rax; jo; mov %rax,0x8(%r14,%rcx,8)`, the running sum in a register and no bounds check; MIR is `mov 0x8(%rsp),%rdx; mov (%rdx,%r14,1),%rsi; mov (%r13,%rcx,8),%rdx; add (%rsi,%rcx,8),%rdx; jo; two bounds cmp/je; mov %rdx,0x8(%r13,%rcx,8)`, reloading prefix[i] (the word the previous trip stored, so each trip waits on store-to-load forwarding) and reloading nums' buffer pointer from its header through the stack. The header reload says LLVM cannot tell the store into prefix's buffer from nums' header, which points at the aliasing explanation above; not verified by an IR experiment. Update 11-02 (Thread B): c0865d2568 loads every sequence length with `!range [0, i64::MAX)`, which folds two bounds checks in kata 1031's prefix loop and hoists `nums.buf`. The `dp[c-1]` / `prefix[i]` reload remains: the loop's only other exit is the overflow `jo` of the checked add, and replacing it with a wrapping add keeps the value in a register, so the reload is tied to the checked-arithmetic exit (inferred: LLVM 18 LoopLoadElimination declines multi-exit loops; not verified in LLVM's source). Wall time on x86 is within noise. Rust's 2.6x lead in 1031 comes mostly from the second loop's i64-index bounds checks, which Rust's usize index avoids.
fix: 4eb76cba00 (drop schedule). Cause confirmed on x86: LLVM 18's LoopLoadElimination runs only through LoopAccessAnalysis, which refuses any loop with more than one exiting block, and each checked add or index check adds one (its branch to the panic); the same loop in C with __builtin_add_overflow + abort reloads too, and takes 2.3x the time of the forwarded form. Fix: src/backend/mir_aot/carry_store.rs, run after the IR passes: in a loop that is a chain of blocks, whose only memory write is one plain store, a load of the word the previous trip stored (same root pointer, a*K bytes back for an IV stepped by K) becomes a phi of the stored value; the first trip's word is read at the end of the preheader when no exit precedes the load, or when the preheader (or the single-predecessor blocks above it) just accessed that word with no call since. Kata 64's bench on x86 (5 runs each): 549-690 ms before, 360-424 ms after, legacy dd86e3955 365-475 ms; callgrind at K=100000: 576.0M instructions after, 570.7M before, legacy 560.1M (1.03x). Still forwarded after Thread B's unroll threshold 300 (9cde7995eb): 365-410 ms at 300, 361-480 ms at 150. Katas 6 and 293 on x86 were already at or below legacy (row_buffers 178-190 ms vs legacy 208-215; flipgame 475-489 vs 525-585). Pinned by tests/mir_carry_store.rs (both binaries match the interpreter; KARAC_MIR_CARRY_STORE=report counts the forwarded loads) and the unit tests in carry_store.rs. The kata corpus through karac build fails the same 317 entries with the pass on and off. KARAC_MIR_CARRY_STORE=0 turns it off. Not handled: a loop the unroller copies (two stores), a loop with a call or a second store, an i32-indexed access. The M5 cycle counts need a Mac re-bench.

title: `d ?? Node.Leaf(0)` on a bare `d: Option[Node]` parameter, `Node` a `shared enum`, passes `karac check` and is refused by the MIR build as a move out of a borrowed place; `Option[Node]` is a handle aggregate (core-semantics §6.1), so the `??` should count the handle and run, as check already says
fix:
FIXED by f667cd24ea. Before the fix, `nil_coalesce`'s `Some` arm moved the payload out of `*d`. Now a handle or handle aggregate read out of a borrowed wrapper counts (core semantics §6.1) through the new `payload_read`. So `d ?? Node.Leaf(0)` on a bare `d: Option[Node]` runs and leaves `d` usable, and so does `h.d.clone() ?? x`.

tests/borrowed_handle_reads.rs `nil_coalesce_counts_a_handle_out_of_a_borrowed_option` checks this: check passes, and __mir-run and run both print 2/0/2/pair/pair. Control: 0 passed / 1 failed against the old src. The program is also ASan-clean on __mir-llvm-asan. `d?`, `d.unwrap()` and `d.unwrap_or(x)` already counted.

Not covered here: `karac check` still refuses `h.d ?? x` where `h` is a borrowed struct whose field `d: Option[Node]` is reached through it (typechecker `reject_nil_coalesce_out_of_borrow`, "'??' on a borrowed 'Option[Node]' would move its 'Node' out of the borrow"), although §6.1 makes that read a count too.
