detail:
MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro by the kara-katas re-bench, karac g6697158fa, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via kara scripts/pmc.c (3-run minima). Kata 252 bench/meeting_rooms.kara: MIR 1.602G instructions vs legacy dd86e3955 1.403G (1.14x), 420M vs 341M cycles (1.23x); seq 1.27 -> 1.63x rustc -O, 0.28 -> 0.36x clang -O3, 0.16 -> 0.20x Go (~1.29x relative). Kata 253 bench/min_meeting_rooms.kara: 2.173G vs 1.807G (1.20x), 724M vs 588M cycles (1.23x); seq 1.09 -> 1.33x rustc -O, 0.48 -> 0.59x C, 0.29 -> 0.35x Go (~1.2x relative). Both shuffle once, then each round copy and sort the intervals by start (the load-bearing O(n log n) step); 252 then scans adjacent pairs, 253 counts rooms with a min-heap. The shared sort is the likely common cause. This row is only the MIR-added part; the pre-existing arm64 sort gap is B-2026-08-16-9 (wontfix in the legacy ledger). Unattributed. | 2026-11-02 (Thread C, x86 valgrind against legacy dd86e3955, karac 9f3cc6a792): meeting_rooms 1.691G MIR vs 1.746G legacy (0.97x), min_meeting_rooms 2.208G vs 2.174G (1.02x), outputs equal; the sort's share is the same on both. This container has no arm64 machine or emulator to reproduce the M5 gap. RE-MEASURED 2026-11-02 on g96fca5370: 252 1.12x instructions, 1.17x cycles; 253 1.18x instructions, 1.21x cycles (whole benchmark). The excess over legacy is larger on 253 than 252 though 253 spends a smaller share of its time sorting, so the sort is probably not the only cost: 253's min-heap may have regressed too. Not attributed.

M5 re-bench 2026-11-03 (scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh at kara cd7fd85dec, Darwin arm64, min of 5, outputs equal): kata 252 instructions 1575.7M vs 1403.4M, 1.123x (within; x86 0.97x); kata 253 2122.1M vs 1807.0M, 1.174x (over; x86 1.02x). Title narrowed to kata 253. | 2026-11-03 (Thread B, 3d8ac8a2c5): qemu-aarch64 instruction counts on aarch64-linux builds at --target-cpu=apple-m1, kata 253 at rounds=1: MIR 89.5M vs legacy 74.7-76.8M (1.20x; legacy's own build varies). The sort's partition loop ran 16 instructions per element to legacy's 11, because the comparator's order reached the sort as `zext(gt) - zext(lt)`, which LLVM does not fold back to one compare (`cset; cset; sub; cmp; lsr`). 3d8ac8a2c5 builds it as `select(lt, -1, zext(gt))`: 78.4M, 1.02-1.05x; x86 callgrind 0.95x. The rest is the heap sift (a `freeze` that keeps `cset; tst; csel`, and reloads of heap[i]). Awaiting an M5 re-run: ONLY=253.
fix: 3d8ac8a2c5 (Thread B). Confirmed by Gowtham's M5 re-run 2026-11-04 (scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh ONLY=<kata> at kara 26bbf303b1, Darwin arm64, min of 5, outputs equal; on battery with light background load, so ±a few %). Kata 253 instructions: MIR 1845.4M vs legacy 1806.5M, 1.022x (was 1.174x at cd7fd85dec). The comparator order now reaches the sort as select(lt,-1,zext(gt)), which LLVM folds; kata 252 was already within.

title: The auto-par collect lowering (`#[par_order_free]` loop pushing into a Vec) holds the collected Vec twice at peak once there are two or more workers: kata 270's par build peaks at 44-49 MiB against 22 MiB at one worker, with +12.5% instructions, both flat from 2 to 18 workers
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro, karac g6697158fa, bench/bst_close.kara's default build. The punch loop is `#[par_order_free] for t in 0..total { ...descent...; parts.push((t * 1000003 + best) % 1000000007) }` over total = 2.2M, so `parts: Vec[i64]` is ~17.6 MB; the tree (three Vec[i64] of 30k) and the 100k-entry targets Vec[f64] are small and read-only. Peak RSS (/usr/bin/time -l, 2 runs each): KARAC_THREADS=1 22.2-22.3 MiB, =2 43.8 MiB, =4 43.7-44.1 MiB, =18 48.8-49.5 MiB. Instructions (scripts/pmc.c, 3-run minima): 1 worker 0.960G, 2 1.080G, 4 1.082G, 18 1.096G (+12.5% at two workers, then flat); cycles 910M / 950M / 1001M / 1132M. Doubling at exactly two workers and flat after points at one extra full copy of the collected Vec, for example per-task chunks concatenated into a fresh result rather than written in place, plus the copy's instructions. Candidate mechanism, not verified in the runtime. The B-2026-10-31-39 family (a flat-in-the-worker-count instruction excess, katas 9, 7 and 120) has the same shape on reduction loops; this one also shows it in memory. Legacy's par build of this kata peaked at 21.1 MiB (2026-08-15 feed). The published par lane is still 1.24x rayon. Platform-independent as far as known. LINUX 2026-11-02 (drop schedule, karac at 3a1355614d, getrusage maxrss): 1 worker 37.3 MB, 2 workers 38.4 MB, 4 workers 38.5 MB. The par build is not above the seq one here, because the 1-worker run already peaks near twice the 17.6 MB Vec: glibc's realloc of a growing large block copies, where macOS remaps. So the par build's doubling is the per-task chunks (17.6 MB in all) alive while the join extends `parts`, which is inherent to chunk-then-append. Getting to one copy means the tasks writing in place into a presized `parts`, or at least reserving `parts` once, for the sum of the chunk lengths, before the extends. MECHANISM (drop schedule, 2026-11-02, from lower.rs par_for_join): each task builds its own Vec from `Vec.new`, and the join calls `Vec.extend(acc, own chunk)` per handle, so each chunk is freed right after it is copied. 16 tasks make ~1.1 MB chunks; macOS serves those from the medium magazine, which keeps freed pages resident, while the 17.6 MB result is a large allocation that cannot reuse them. So the peak is all the chunks plus the result, about 2x, while Linux returns the mmapped chunks at free. Reserving once does not fix it. A fix writes in place: reserve acc by the trip count before spawning, give each task a window of it, and compact the windows at the join with memmove when a push is conditional. That needs pushes of at most one per iteration (statically), and a window Vec that neither drop, cancel nor growth may free or realloc. That is a lower.rs + runtime change, not attempted.

title: Growing a fresh Vec[i64] to 2M elements with push, once per round, runs 1.37x legacy's instructions on the MIR backend (1.13x its cycles): found in kata 283. LOCATED (x86, 2026-11-02): legacy's sequential tabulate lowering (codegen/reduce.rs try_emit_seq_tabulate_lowering) reserved once and stored directly, so LLVM vectorized the copy; MIR keeps a capacity check per push (7 instructions a push even after an exact reserve), 1.19x on x86 after 9f3cc6a792 made the reservation fire
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro by the kara-katas re-bench, karac g6697158fa, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via kara scripts/pmc.c (3-run minima). bench/movezero.kara as it stood: each of 60 rounds did `let mut work: Vec[i64] = Vec.new(); while k < n { work.push(src[k]); k = k + 1 }` (n = 2M) before `move_zeroes(mut work, mut st)`. MIR 4.155G instructions vs legacy dd86e3955 3.036G (1.37x), 2092M vs 1856M cycles (1.13x); seq 1.11 -> 1.26x rustc -O, 1.12 -> 1.27x clang -O3, 0.80 -> 0.93x Go. LOCATED to the push loop, not move_zeroes or the `mut ref` parameters: replacing it with one `Vec.filled(n, 0)` before the loop and `work[k] = src[k]` per round (which is also what the C/Rust/Go mirrors do: memcpy / copy_from_slice / copy) gives MIR 2.812G vs legacy 3.049G instructions (0.92x), 1830M vs 1877M cycles (0.97x), seq 1.10x rustc -O, flat. So the Vec push / grow path costs MIR ~1.3G extra instructions per 120M pushes here. Kata 225's B-2026-11-02-2 also has a push in its hot loop (q.data.push in the queue rotation), so the two may share this cause. Side effect, not a Kāra leak: the per-round 16 MB regrowth also drove the kata's peak RSS to 936 MiB on macOS (plain C with the same grow-free-per-round pattern does the same; `leaks` finds 0 bytes); with the buffer reused it is 33.7 MiB, level with the mirrors. Kata 283 (and kata 280, which had the same mirror mismatch) now use the reused buffer, so neither exercises the push path any more: reproduce with the loop above. | 2026-11-02 (Thread C, x86 valgrind against legacy dd86e3955): the old movezero loop measures 4.329G MIR vs 3.551G legacy (1.22x). mir::presize did not fire: the bound `n` is `let n = 2000000`, which presize read as a literal past its 1 << 20 limit; legacy treats a named binding as a variable bound. 9f3cc6a792 fixed that (4.232G, 1.19x). The rest is the push loop itself: MIR's per-push `len < cap` check stays because the grow path writes the capacity back, 840M instructions for 120M pushes, where legacy's tabulate lowering emits a reserve and a vectorized store loop (~140M). The drop schedule handed the remainder to Thread C.
fix: 11d7eb7f01 with 9f3cc6a792. Two pieces, both needed (x86 valgrind instruction counts against legacy dd86e3955; the M5 counts are not reproducible here). 9f3cc6a792: mir::presize had not fired, because the bound `n` is `let n = 2000000` and presize read a named binding a literal sets as a literal past its 1 << 20 limit; legacy treats a named binding as a variable bound, and so does presize now (4.329G -> 4.232G). 11d7eb7f01 (Thread B, B-2026-11-01-21): a presized fill's pushes become `Vec.__push_within(&mut v, x, reach)`, which skips the capacity check below the reserved length, so LLVM drops the growth path, as legacy's sequential tabulate lowering let it. The old movezero loop (bench/movezero.kara before kara-katas 5b8a643d): 4.329G -> 3.454G against legacy's 3.551G (1.22x -> 0.97x), output equal. Thread C had a parallel version of the push hint gated green and dropped it at the rebase as a duplicate of 11d7eb7f01.

title: Kata 276's par lane runs 1.44x slower than its 2026-08-28 feed while its comparators moved 1.06-1.09x and its seq lane held, so it scales 4.6x over seq where it scaled ~6.0x; there is no matched legacy par baseline
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro by the kara-katas re-bench, karac g6697158fa, exact counts via kara scripts/pmc.c (3-run minima). Default (auto-par) build of bench/paint_enum.kara: kāra par 25.51 -> 36.61 ms (1.44x) while pthreads C par went 39.79 -> 43.26 (1.09x) and Go-par 28.58 -> 30.33 (1.06x): 0.64 -> 0.85x C-par, 0.89 -> 1.21x Go-par (~1.33x relative). Seq lane flat (1.11 -> 1.03x rustc -O). Instructions are flat in the worker count (3.750G at KARAC_THREADS=1, 3.751G at 4, 3.763G at 18), so this is not the B-2026-10-31-39 excess; wall 0.16 / 0.09 / 0.05 / 0.04 s at 1 / 2 / 4 / 18 workers. NO matched legacy par baseline: legacy dd86e3955 does not parallelize this loop (173.4 ms single-threaded, 3.484G instructions, against MIR's 47.0 ms and 3.774G in the same 20-run A/B); the 25.5 ms feed came from karac 0.1.0-dev.7481 (g9b221e799, 2026-08-28), whose auto-par did fire. So the loss is relative to that build's parallel code, not to the last legacy one. Unattributed; possibly scheduling or chunking (an 18-worker run reaches only 4.6x its seq lane on 6P+12E, against 6.0x on the 2026-08-28 feed: 152.39 / 25.51 ms). LINUX 2026-11-02 (drop schedule, karac at 63ce9d6b29, 4-vCPU x86 box): seq 320 ms, 2 workers 165 (1.94x), 3 workers 117, 4 workers 110. The box's own control, four seq copies run at once, takes 498 ms, so 4 workers already scale as far as the box lets; no loss reproduces here. Shape: AUTO_PAR_TASKS = 16 and the loop has 16 trips, so each task is one `pre` and an 18-worker run's wall is one task on the slowest core it lands on. 36.6 ms is about two E-core rounds of a 9.5 ms P-core task, which fits workers being kept off the P cores (std::thread workers at the default QoS, unverified) better than chunking. NEEDS A MAC: compare KARAC_THREADS=18 with workers' QoS raised (pthread_set_qos_class_self_np at worker start) before changing anything.
fix: cd7fd85dec: measured within the 1.15x bar by Gowtham's M5 run of scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh (kara cd7fd85dec, kara-katas b755e37e, Darwin arm64, min of 5, outputs equal) on 2026-11-03. Kata 276 par lane wall: 17.6 ms against the 2026-08-28 feed's 25.51 ms, 0.692x, so the 1.44x par-lane slowdown no longer reproduces; not bisected to one commit.

title: Kata 294's memoised flip-game search (per-node successor Strings built char by char, Map[String, bool] memo) runs 1.60x legacy's instructions and 1.51x its cycles on the MIR backend: the seq lane went from 0.62x to 0.95x rustc -O
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro by the kara-katas re-bench, karac g6697158fa, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via kara scripts/pmc.c (3-run minima). bench/flipgame2.kara: MIR 8.016G instructions vs legacy dd86e3955 5.018G (1.60x), 1312M vs 869M cycles (1.51x). Seq lane 0.62 -> 0.95x rustc -O, 1.18 -> 1.86x clang -O3, 0.99 -> 1.49x Go (~1.55x relative on all three). Kernel: `can_win(s: ref String, memo: mut ref Map[String, bool])`; `next_states(s)` does `s.chars().collect()` into a Vec[char] and builds each successor `String` character by character (`String.new()` plus per-char appends) into a Vec[String], then probes and inserts the String-keyed memo. Its sibling kata 293 (flip game) is the already-listed same-signature instance in B-2026-10-31-38 (1.39x instructions, 2x cycles); 294's kernel differs (string building + map), so it is filed separately. Unattributed: the String build path and the String-keyed Map (cf. B-2026-11-02-4, B-2026-11-02-6) are the suspects.
fix: 9f3cc6a792. Located on x86 (valgrind instruction counts against legacy dd86e3955, this container; the M5 counts in detail are not reproducible here): the String build path, not the map. `next_states` grew each successor String from `String.new()` 8 -> 16 -> 32 by realloc, and `s.chars().collect()` grew its Vec[char] the same way: 6.1M reallocs against legacy's 1.1M, where legacy's AST presize gave the String `with_capacity(n)` and sized the collect from the byte length. mir::presize now reserves a `String.new()` filled by one `String.push` per trip (`String.presize`, in bytes), and the MIR builder's chars().collect() reserves the text's byte length. Kata 294's bench: 4.618G -> 3.515G instructions against legacy's 3.994G (1.16x -> 0.88x). arm64 not re-measured. Pinned by mir_presize_reserves_a_string_fill_and_a_char_collect.

title: A `shared` handle crosses tasks inside an unmarked `dyn T` that a task or `par` branch only VIEWS: `fn mkd(s: own S) -> dyn Bump` and two `TaskGroup.spawn` closures calling `d.bump()` pass `karac check` and race (397329328 of 600000001 at KARAC_THREADS=4). The view carve-out for `dyn` captures is unsound; an unmarked `dyn T` may not reach a task or a branch even as a view
detail:
SPLIT from B-2026-11-01-26 case (e) on the review thread's ruling (2026-11-02): drop the `dyn` view carve-out. An unmarked `dyn T` may not reach a task or a `par` branch even as a view. `dyn T + CrossTask`, and a `dyn` of a trait with `CrossTask` as a supertrait, may be viewed as before.

MEASURED at 3139c3c5bf (release build with llvm, this container). Program: `shared struct S { mut n: i64 }  trait Bump { fn bump(ref self) -> i64; }  struct D { s: S }  impl Bump for D { fn bump(ref self) -> i64 { self.s.n = self.s.n + 1; self.s.n } }  fn mkd(s: own S) -> dyn Bump { D { s: s } }  fn main() { let d = mkd(S { n: 0 }); let g = TaskGroup.new(); let a = g.spawn(|| { let mut i = 0; while i < 300000000 { d.bump(); i = i + 1; } 0 }); let b = g.spawn(|| { ...same... }); a.join(); b.join(); println(d.bump()); }`. `karac check`: All checks passed. `karac build`, then the binary: KARAC_THREADS=1 prints 600000001, and KARAC_THREADS=4 prints 397329328 (real 2.19 s, user 4.02 s, so both workers ran). At 100000 iterations per task the race did not show in three runs; the larger count is what makes it visible.

WHERE: src/typechecker/cross_task_check.rs. In the spawn capture loop, a capture whose CrossTask path ends in `DynCrossTask` is recorded in `core_dyn_task_captures` and skipped, and the ownership pass (src/ownership/rc_promote.rs) refuses only a capture the task MOVES. The par-branch loop skips `DynCrossTask` outright. Both carve-outs go. A `dyn` of a trait with a CrossTask supertrait already lowers with its mark (src/typechecker/dyn_trait.rs).

Owner: Thread A. Before implementing, count the corpus and apps refusals as for -26, and send the list to the review thread if it is more than a handful outside err_ pins.
fix: bc157b9903. As ruled by the review thread, with the doc side at 1c98ebdf7 (design.md § Crossing tasks, core semantics §6.3): a plain `dyn T` is not CrossTask, so a task or a `par` branch may not reach one even as a view. Both carve-outs in src/typechecker/cross_task_check.rs are removed: the spawn capture loop's deferral of a `DynCrossTask` capture to the ownership pass, and the par-branch skip. A plain `dyn T` capture is now E_NOT_CROSS_TASK. `dyn T + CrossTask`, and a `dyn` of a trait with CrossTask as a supertrait, cross as before. The fix-it writes ` + CrossTask` where the binding's `dyn` type is declared, after the trait and before any `with` (the parser records the point), as for an erased function type (B-2026-11-01-26). The ownership pass's move-only refusal (DynMovedIntoTask, B-2026-10-30-13) and the typechecker's deferred-capture table were removed, because nothing reaches them now. The row's program is refused at check. Pins: effect_dyn_clause_par_apart, effect_dyn_par_apart and err_effect_dyn_clause_par_shared now mark their `dyn`. err_dyn_view_unmarked_spawned and err_dyn_view_unmarked_par are new and pin the unmarked views. tests/core_dyn_moved_into_task.rs now pins move and view refusal, the marked forms running, and the fix-it. A corpus and apps check sweep of 20,851 files refuses nothing beyond those three pins. The test fixtures that view a `dyn` across tasks declare it `+ CrossTask`: tests/mir_dyn.rs, mir_dyn_effects.rs, mir_dyn_effect_var_elements.rs, and the v1_service package with its test file. Control on origin/main: core_dyn_moved_into_task fails 2 of 3. Gate148 on the rebase: fmt, both clippy legs and `cargo test --all` (10123 passed) were green. `--features llvm` passed 10235 and failed 3, all in the v1_service test file's own `Vec[dyn Handler]` fixtures. Those were re-marked, after which mir_v1_service ran 5 of 5 under `--features llvm`, and fmt and both clippy legs were re-run green before the push.

title: A 0.8.0 program giving a `Vec[dyn Handler]` or `Vec[Fn(..)]` where the `+ CrossTask` form is expected gets a bare E0200 mismatch (dyn) or an opaque E_NOT_CROSS_TASK (Fn) that names neither the missing marker nor where to write it
detail: The first thing a 0.8.0 user upgrading to 0.8.1 meets under B-2026-11-01-26 / B-2026-11-02-12: `let mut routes: Vec[dyn Handler] = Vec.new(); ... Router { routes: routes }` with the field written `Vec[dyn Handler + CrossTask]` was refused as plain `expected 'Vec[dyn Handler + CrossTask]', found 'Vec[dyn Handler]'`, with no word on why the unmarked form does not convert and no fix-it; the `Fn` form (`Vec[Fn() -> i64]` into `Vec[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask]`) was refused by the function-environment pass with no fix-it either. Asked for by the review thread (2026-11-02): have E0200 add a note naming the missing marker, with the same fix-it at the declaration that the B-2026-11-01-26 refusals carry.
fix: 9dc35df0a8. A plain `dyn` value given where the `+ CrossTask` form is expected (`Vec[dyn Handler]` into `Vec[dyn Handler + CrossTask]`, or a bare `dyn Handler`) is now refused as "a `dyn` type without `+ CrossTask` does not become one with it, since nothing checked that the value behind it may cross tasks (core semantics §6.3)", with "help: write `+ CrossTask` on the `dyn` where the value's type is declared" and a machine-applicable fix-it at the local's declaration (`refuse_missing_dyn_marker` in src/typechecker.rs, keyed through the new `local_ident_uses`). The `Fn` form's E_NOT_CROSS_TASK refusal (src/typechecker/fn_env_cross_task.rs) carries the same fix-it at the parameter type, `let` annotation or callee return type the value was declared with. tests/cross_task_marker_upgrade.rs runs `karac fix` on both forms and checks the result is clean.

title: A `shared` handle crosses tasks through a COLLECTION of unmarked `Fn` values coerced into a `+ CrossTask` slot: a `Vec[Fn() -> i64]` a call hands back, or a local `let mut hs: Vec[Fn() -> i64]` filled by `push`, enters `Vec[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask]` unchecked and two tasks race on the handle
detail: Remainder of B-2026-11-01-26 (fixed 3139c3c5bf). The function-environment pass (src/typechecker/fn_env_cross_task.rs) took an erased function value from a call, field or element as out of sight only when its type was an unmarked `Fn` at the top: a `Vec[Fn() -> i64]` (or a tuple or payload holding one) was not, and the `+ CrossTask` mark takes no part in type equality, so `Bus { hs: mk(S { n: 0 }) }` with `fn mk(s: own S) -> Vec[Fn() -> i64]` pushing `|| { s.n = s.n + 1; s.n }` checked clean. Measured at aead696b20, KARAC_THREADS=4, two tasks each calling `(b.hs[0])()` 300000000 times then one more call: printed 362045262, expected 600000001 (lost updates on the `shared` handle). Second shape, same result on check: a local `let mut hs: Vec[Fn() -> i64] = Vec.new(); hs.push(<that closure>); Bus { hs: hs }` - `push` on an unmarked receiver does not join the argument's environment into `hs`, so `hs` carried an empty environment into the marked field.
fix: 9dc35df0a8. The function-environment pass now takes a value as out of sight when its type holds an unmarked erased function ANYWHERE (`is_unmarked_fn_type` is deep: Named args, tuples, arrays, slices, refs, Arc/Rc/Weak), so a `Vec[Fn() -> i64]` from a call, field or element is refused when coerced into a `+ CrossTask` slot; and a `let mut` (or `let mut x: T;`) whose type holds one, not a bare `Fn` (whose reassignment the pass already follows), starts out of sight, since `push` and element writes are not followed. The fix the diagnostic offers is `+ CrossTask` on the local's declaration, which then checks each push (pinned: a leaking push onto a marked local is refused at the push). Pins: corpus/core/err_fn_vec_call_result_marked, corpus/core/err_fn_vec_local_push_marked; tests/cross_task_marker_upgrade.rs. Control at origin/main 7c9894f84d: 5 of the 6 tests fail (the sixth, the marked-local push, already held). Check-only sweep over corpus, katas and apps (20851 files): no new refusals outside err_ pins.

title: An unmarked `Fn` reaches a `+ CrossTask` slot through a GENERIC parameter (`collect()` into `Vec[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask]`, `id[T](mkf(..))`, `mem.replace(mut f, mkf(..))`): `karac check` passes and two tasks race on the captured `shared` handle
detail:
Re-probe of §6.3 at e762753ac (after -26, B-2026-11-02-12 and -14 landed), 52 cells, check plus `karac run` at KARAC_THREADS=4. 48 refuse/ok cells are right: Option[Vec[Fn]] from a call, struct field Map[i64, dyn Bump], marked Map insert/entry().or_insert, channel send, extend/append, reassignment (direct, branch, shadow), element write/insert, Wr[T] wrappers, Option/Result/tuple/Array/SortedMap, depth 3, OnceFn, mut ref param push, field assign, par. Four are accepted by check, all where the unmarked value enters through a generic type parameter that was instantiated with the marked type. Prelude: `shared struct S { mut n: i64 }`, `fn mkf(s: own S) -> Fn() -> i64 { || { s.n = s.n + 1; s.n } }`, `fn race2(f: Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask) -> i64` spawns two TaskGroup tasks that each call f 100000 times and returns a.join()+b.join()+f(), which is 200001 with no race.
(1) `let v: Vec[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask] = (0..1).map(|i| mkf(S { n: i })).collect(); println(race2(v[0]));` check: All checks passed. run x3: 158651, 192522, 192721.
(2) same through a closure literal bound to `let c: Fn() -> i64 = || { t.n = t.n + 1; t.n }` inside the map, then collected: 156234, 190954, 163640.
(3) `fn id[T](x: own T) -> T { x }` and `let f: Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask = id(mkf(S { n: 0 }));`: 181217, 184930, 153064.
(4) `let mut f: Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask = || 1; let old = mem.replace(mut f, mkf(S { n: 0 }));` passes check (then hits invalid MIR, filed separately as B-2026-11-02-16).
Spec §6.3: a value whose type holds an unmarked function type is out of sight, and coercing it into a marked type is refused. Here the coercion happens at the generic call's argument (or at FromIterator's element), where T was inferred as the marked type, so the argument-to-T step is not checked as a coercion. Cells: probe-core/gen63.py (s63/r07, r07b, r11c, r30) in the shared folder.
fix: 37030edcb2. Per the review thread's ruling (a type parameter solved as the marked type from where a call's result goes does not mark the argument; unmarked to marked happens only at a coercion site, which checks the value), in the function-environment pass (src/typechecker/fn_env_cross_task.rs): a call to a generic function whose return type names a type parameter reaches what its arguments reach, so `id(mkf(..))` into a marked `let` is out of sight and `id(|| <captures a shared handle>)` names the capture; `collect()` into a collection of `+ CrossTask` function values takes each item as a push would, so an item type that is not marked (read through the receiver's `Item`) is out of sight; and an argument written `mut` whose type is marked is a place a generic or bodiless callee may write the other arguments into, so `mem.replace(mut f, g)` and `mem.swap(mut f, mut g)` coerce `g` into it. All four probe cells (r07, r07b, r11c, r30) are refused; marked collect, id, replace and swap still check. title: `mem.replace(mut f, g)` on a local of an erased `Fn` type is refused after check with `error[mir]: invalid MIR: assigning Fn() -> i64 to _6 of type closure#N()`, marked or not
detail: Found re-probing §6.3 at e762753ac. `karac check` passes; `karac run` and `__mir-llvm-run` both stop with invalid MIR. Minimal: `fn main() { let mut f: Fn() -> i64 = || 1; let old = mem.replace(mut f, || 2); println(f() + old()); }` gives `main: bb3[3]: assigning Fn() -> i64 to _6 of type closure#1582()`. Same with the replacement from a call (`fn two() -> Fn() -> i64 { || 2 }`, `mem.replace(mut f, two())`: bb4[0], _5) and with `Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask`. Expected 3. Looks like the local keeps the initializer's closure type instead of the declared erased type, so the generic `mem.replace[T]` instantiation picks the closure type for T. Possibly the same root as the T inference in B-2026-11-02-15.
fix: 66c81328c7. A `let mut` declared `Fn` that another function value may replace (assigned, or lent `mut` to anything but a parameter declared `mut ref` / `ref` of a function type, which the callee is specialised to per B-2026-10-19-68) now holds the declared, erased type: the closure is built as for an undeclared binding and erased into the local (src/mir/lower.rs `let_fn_replaced`, `replaced_lets`). One only called or lent to such a parameter keeps the closure's own type, since an erased value's drop keeps its borrows live and would refuse `let mut h: MutFn() = || { calls += 1; }; h(); println(calls)` (mir_build's B-2026-10-19-68 fixture). The row's program prints 3 on run and build; pinned with an assignment, an assignment in a branch, a call result and a CrossTask-marked local in tests/mir_declared_fn_local.rs.

title: After B-2026-10-31-39, an auto-par task's loop still ran about 10% more instructions than the in-order one on kata 9 (Linux): the buffer reload and kata 7's signed-term prefix compares are fixed; the bounds check and the range cap's back-edge test stay on purpose (versioning them moved no wall time)
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 (drop schedule, karac at f117a8f69f, x86-64 Linux, callgrind, kata 9's bench with K cut to 5M): 297.7M instructions in order (karac.main.seq), 332.8M at two workers (was 352.8M before f117a8f69f), so 7 more instructions an iteration. The task's hot loop versus the in-order one: (1) `cmp len; jae` on inputs[k % n], because the task no longer knows the Vec's length, which the in-order loop's LLVM derives from its with_capacity + push fill; (2) a reload of the buffer pointer each iteration (`mov (%rdx),%r9`). The load follows the bounds check, and the captured reference carries no dereferenceable fact, so LICM cannot hoist it. (3) The range_cap `k < K` back-edge test of B-2026-10-31-3, which is deliberate (2 instructions). (4) Two register moves around the checked add's rebase path. Kata 7 (bench/reverse.kara) adds `r as i64` with r an i32 that can be negative, so B-2026-10-31-39's rising-term rule does not apply and its task keeps both prefix compares. Candidates: mark loads of captured references dereferenceable/nonnull in the task (backend); for (1), version the loop on `n <= len` when the index is `k % n` with n captured; for a signed term, find the prefix extremes at the join by replaying only when the run's sum lands near a bound. Not attempted. M5 numbers (the +75% the parent row measured) need a Mac re-bench. UPDATE 2026-11-02 (drop schedule): item (2) FIXED in e888029d05: a reference's load now carries !nonnull, !dereferenceable <pointee size> and !align, so LICM hoists the captured Vec's buffer load out of the task loop; kata 9 at K=5M on two workers goes from 332.8M to 327.8M instructions (5.0M, one per iteration; KARAC_MIR_REF_LOADS=0 is the control and the opt-out), pinned by tests/mir_ref_loads.rs. The remaining 30M (6 per iteration) are (1) the bounds check and (3) the range-cap test, plus a register move. A third run of LLVM's O3 pipeline over the task takes it to 293.0M, below in order, by turning the inlined is_palindrome's signed divisions by 10 into unsigned ones (x is non-negative there); the in-order loop keeps the signed form too, so that is a further gain for both, not part of this gap. Items (1), (3), (4) and kata 7's signed terms are open. UPDATE 2026-11-02 (drop schedule): item (1) MEASURED, not worth building. Versioning the task loop on `1024 <= len` (the bounds check rewritten as `idx <u len or (m <=u len and idx >= 0)`, then LLVM's non-trivial unswitch with its threshold raised from 50 to 1000 by hand) drops the check from the hot copy: 327.8M to 317.8M instructions at K=5M on two workers (10.0M, 3%). At K=50M on two workers the wall time does not move (eight runs each, 144-175 ms before, 146-188 ms after). karac's default O2 runs no non-trivial unswitching, and the default threshold refuses this loop at O3, so doing it in karac means duplicating the task's loop in MIR; for no measured time that is not attempted. Item (3) is the deliberate range cap (an llvm.assume does not narrow kata 4's remainder, 287a18e111). Kata 7's signed terms are taken by the apps thread. UPDATE 2026-11-02 (apps thread, at the drop schedule's hand-off): kata 7's signed-term prefix compares FIXED in eb485e6e83 for a sum that cannot overflow however the loop runs: it starts at a constant, the range is constant, and each term is bounded (a cast from a narrower integer type such as kata 7's `r as i64` with `r: i32`, a literal, an `if` of such arms, or a name an immutable `let` binds to one), so the task keeps neither compare (Bx::sum_cannot_overflow). Kata 7 at K=5M, two workers, callgrind x86: 1650.7M to 1630.6M instructions (4 per iteration), against 1610.5M in order. KARAC_AUTO_PAR_BOUNDED_SUM=0 is the control and the opt-out; pinned by tests/mir_auto_par_bounded_sum.rs. A sum that starts at a non-constant or within reach of its type's end keeps both compares. Remaining for kata 7: the bounds check, the range-cap test and the register moves (items 1, 3, 4).
fix: e888029d05 (drop schedule) and eb485e6e83 (apps thread). Item (2), the per-trip reload of the captured Vec's buffer: a reference's load now carries !nonnull, !dereferenceable and !align, so LICM hoists it (kata 9 at K=5M on two workers: 332.8M to 327.8M instructions; tests/mir_ref_loads.rs). Kata 7's signed terms: a sum from a constant start over a constant range whose every term is bounded (a widening cast, a literal, an if of such) cannot leave its type, so the task keeps neither prefix compare (Bx::sum_cannot_overflow; 1650.7M to 1630.6M at K=5M, in order 1610.5M; tests/mir_auto_par_bounded_sum.rs; KARAC_AUTO_PAR_BOUNDED_SUM=0). Left as they are, deliberately: item (1), the bounds check on inputs[k % n]: versioning the loop on n <= len removes it (327.8M to 317.8M) but moves no wall time at K=50M (144-175 ms against 146-188 ms), and needs either non-trivial unswitching (not in O2; its threshold refuses this loop at O3) or duplicating the task loop in MIR; item (3), the range cap's back-edge test, which B-2026-10-31-3 added on purpose (an llvm.assume does not narrow kata 4's remainder); item (4), two register moves.

title: After the B-2026-11-02-15 fix, five more generic paths still let an unmarked `Fn` into a `+ CrossTask` slot and race: a generic impl's `Bx.new(x)`, `fold` with a marked init, `Option.unwrap_or_else`, `mem.take` on an unmarked `Option`, `Option.get_or_insert_with`
detail:
§6.3 round 3 at 667d19a39 (review thread's ask after 37030edcb2), 45 cells, check plus `karac run` at KARAC_THREADS=4. Prelude as in B-2026-11-02-15 (`shared struct S { mut n: i64 }`, `mkf(s: own S) -> Fn() -> i64` captures s and bumps it, `race2(f: Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask)` runs f 100000 times in each of two tasks and returns 200001 without a race). 34 refuse cells are right, including Bx[T] put, trait methods returning T or Self, generic fns returning wrappers, two-param pick, into_iter/map/collect, filter_map, chain, extend from an iterator, collect into a Map, Option.replace/get_or_insert, Option.take, mem.swap and mem.replace on locals and Vec elements, a marked maker returning an unmarked Fn, and dyn methods returning Fn or Vec[Fn]. Accepted by check, with race values over three runs:
(1) `struct Bx[T] { x: T }` with `impl[T] Bx[T] { fn new(x: own T) -> Bx[T] { Bx { x: x } } }`, `let b: Bx[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask] = Bx.new(mkf(S { n: 0 }));` 171225, 199637, 196248. (A free `fn bx[T]` of the same shape IS refused, so it is the associated fn on a generic impl.)
(2) `let init: Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask = || 1; let f = (0..1).fold(init, |acc, i| mkf(S { n: i }));` 190227, 200001, 192550. (With an untyped `|| 1` init it is refused.)
(3) `let o: Option[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask] = None; let f: Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask = o.unwrap_or_else(|| mkf(S { n: 0 }));` 193611, 195624, 200001.
(4) `let mut src: Option[Fn() -> i64] = Some(mkf(..)); let o: Option[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask] = mem.take(mut src);` 184267, 145309, 200001. (`src.take()` is refused.)
(5) `let mut o: Option[Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask] = None; o.get_or_insert_with(|| mkf(..));` 168481, 159905, 199888.
The common shape: the unmarked value is produced by a closure or method body whose return type is a type parameter instantiated with the marked type (FnOnce() -> T, MutFn(A, Item) -> A, an associated fn's T), or it arrives through a by-`mut ref` generic (mem.take). Cells g01, i02, i10, m01, m05 in probe-core/gen64.py.
fix: 0d618d8646. Per the review thread's structural rule (a value is coerced wherever it flows into a slot whose type holds the marker once the call's type parameters are solved), in the function-environment pass (src/typechecker/fn_env_cross_task.rs), fed the typechecker's per-call solved type arguments (node_call_subs): each call argument, for free functions, methods and a generic impl's associated functions alike, is coerced into its parameter's solved type where a value sits (not inside a function type's parameters or return); a closure literal's result is coerced into its solved return type (`f: OnceFn() -> T` with T marked), as is the result of every closure whose own return type is marked; a call whose return type names a solved parameter reaches what its arguments reach; and a callee with no body here (`mem.take`, `mem.replace`) returns what its arguments reach and writes them into a marked `mut` argument. All five cells (g01 Bx.new, i02 fold, i10 unwrap_or_else, m01 mem.take, m05 get_or_insert_with) are refused. Acceptance: gen63 and gen64 rerun in full on the check lane, 97 cells: every refuse cell refused, every run cell checks (the interp failures left on o03 and o06 are B-2026-11-02-16/-19's, and reproduce on the binary before this fix). Pins: corpus/core/err_fn_solved_{closure_result,impl_new}; tests/cross_task_solved_param.rs. Control at origin/main 6927dcb48a: 3 of the 4 tests fail. Check-only sweep over corpus, katas and apps (20851 files): no new refusals outside err_ pins.

title: Generic std ops on erased `Fn` values miscompile when a closure LITERAL is involved: `mem.swap` of two `Fn` locals is a no-op, and `Option[Fn].replace(|| ..)` stores an empty aggregate that segfaults when called; a `mem.swap` with one call-initialized side is falsely refused (E0516)
detail:
Found by the ok controls of §6.3 round 3 at 667d19a39; no CrossTask needed, every surface agrees, check passes. Expected values from the spec of mem.swap / Option.replace.
(1) `let mut f: Fn() -> i64 = || 1; let mut g: Fn() -> i64 = || 0; mem.swap(mut f, mut g); println(f()); println(g());` prints 1 0 on run and __mir-llvm-run; expected 0 1. Same with a capturing `|| k`. mem.swap on i64 locals is right.
(2) `let mut o: Option[Fn() -> i64] = None; let _ = o.replace(|| 5); let f = o.unwrap(); println(f());` karac run exits 139 with no output; a capturing `|| k` variant reports `fatal runtime error: stack overflow` on run and __mir-llvm-run; __mir-run says `call through Agg([]), which is not a function value`. Same from `Some(|| 1)`. `o.replace(mk())` with a call result, get_or_insert(|| 5), get_or_insert_with and mem.take are right.
(3) `fn mk() -> Fn() -> i64 { || 7 }`, `let mut f: Fn() -> i64 = mk(); let mut g: Fn() -> i64 = || 0; mem.swap(mut f, mut g);` is refused by check: `cannot end g while f still holds a borrow of it` [E0516]; expected f() = 0.
Likely the same root as B-2026-11-02-16 (mem.replace on an Fn local: invalid MIR `assigning Fn() -> i64 to _6 of type closure#N()`, still at 667d19a39): the local or argument keeps the closure literal's own type rather than the declared erased Fn type when the generic T is instantiated.
fix: 66c81328c7, with B-2026-11-02-16. (1) mem.swap of two declared `Fn` locals: both are now erased (lent `mut` to a generic parameter), so the swap moves values of one type; prints 0 1. (3) The false E0516: borrowck's call transfer let a callee given `mut ref Fn(..)` store the other `mut ref` argument itself; it now receives what that argument's pointee holds (src/mir/borrowck.rs `held_behind`), since a closure stored there captures by move and cannot take a borrowed parameter (§9.3); `f = mk()` swapped with `|| 0` prints 0 and 7. (2) `Option[Fn].replace(|| ..)` erases the closure it keeps, as `v.push` does (lower.rs `stored_fn`); prints 5, and the capturing form `|| k + 1` prints 5 with no stack overflow. All on run and build in tests/mir_declared_fn_local.rs (swap, swap_with_call, option_replace).

title: `(Fn() -> Fn() -> i64) + CrossTask` is a parse error (`Expected =, found +`); §6.3 says to parenthesize to mark the outer function type, and only `Fn() -> (Fn() -> i64) + CrossTask` parses
detail: At 667d19a39. §6.3: the marker binds to the nearest function type, so `Fn() -> Fn() + CrossTask` marks the inner one; parenthesize to mark the outer. The natural reading, a parenthesized whole type followed by the marker, does not parse in a let annotation or a parameter type: `let mk: (Fn() -> Fn() -> i64) + CrossTask = || mkf(S { n: 0 });` gives error[parse] Expected `=`, found `+`. The form that works parenthesizes the inner return type: `Fn() -> (Fn() -> i64) + CrossTask`, which check then treats as marking the outer (a capture of the result is refused as unmarked). Either accept the first form or have the spec show the second and the parse error suggest it.
fix: 04ae52b256. A parenthesized function type followed by `+ CrossTask` now takes the marker (src/parser/types.rs, parenthesized-type arm), so `(Fn() -> Fn() -> i64) + CrossTask` marks the outer type in a let annotation, a parameter and a return type, as §6.3 says. A parenthesized return type of a function type, `Fn() -> (Fn() -> i64) + CrossTask`, still leaves the marker to the outer type, as before (the parser records where a function type's return type starts). The formatter printed that second form as `Fn() -> Fn() -> i64 + CrossTask`, which re-parses as marking the inner type; a marked function returning a function type now prints whole in parens, or with its return type in parens when its own `with` follows the marker. tests/cross_task_paren_marker.rs runs each form through check and __mir-run as written and after formatting, so a marking the formatter moved flips the verdict, with the inner-marked and unmarked forms as refused controls.

title: `*a = || 9` through a `a: mut ref Fn() -> i64` parameter is refused with E0517 "cannot write to `a`: it is reached through a shared `ref`", though `a` is `mut ref`; the same write through `mut ref Vec[Fn]` or a struct field is accepted
detail: Reported by Thread B while fixing B-2026-11-02-19 (shape `fn set(a: mut ref Fn() -> i64, b: ref i64) { *a = || *b + 1; }`), reduced here at 667d19a39. Minimal: `fn set(a: mut ref Fn() -> i64) { *a = || 9; }` `fn main() { let mut f: Fn() -> i64 = || 0; set(mut f); println(f()); }`; check refuses at the `*a =` with E0517 and §5.9; expected 9. Same with `mut ref (Fn() -> i64)` and with a non-capturing or a copy-capturing closure, so it is not about the borrow of `b`. Accepted and printing 9: `fn set(a: mut ref Vec[Fn() -> i64]) { a[0] = || 9; }`, and `struct H { mut f: Fn() -> i64 }` with `fn set(h: mut ref H) { h.f = || 9; }`; `*a = ..` through `mut ref i64` and `mut ref String` also pass. For comparison `mut ref dyn Bump` gets its own diagnostic, E_DYN_REPLACE_THROUGH_VIEW (design.md § dyn Trait); the spec states no such rule for erased Fn, and the Vec-element and field writes show the value is replaceable in place. Either the write should be accepted, or, if the dyn rule is meant to cover Fn, the diagnostic should say so instead of naming a shared `ref` that is not there.
fix: 206d1362de fixes it in the MIR builder, not the typechecker: the E0517 came from the MIR borrow check. `let mut f: Fn() -> i64 = || 0` kept its initializer's closure type, and the call `set(mut f)` specialised `set` to it as `set{ref closure#N}`, which dropped the `mut` (so `*a = ..` read as a write through a shared ref) and tied the slot to one closure type. A function item passed the same way (`let mut f: Fn() -> i64 = zero; set(mut f)`) passed check and stopped the interpreter ("a function-value place holds Fn(..zero)"). `let_fn_replaced` (src/mir/lower.rs) now counts a lend to a `mut ref Fn` parameter as a replacement when the callee writes through it (`*a = ..`, or `a` lent `mut` onward; new `writes_through_param`), so the local holds the declared, erased type and the callee is built for it. A callee that only calls the parameter still gets the closure's own type (`mir_a_closure_through_a_mut_ref_function_parameter_keeps_its_writes` and `mir_declared_fn_local`'s `kept_mut_borrow` hold). Measured: the row's program prints 9 under check, `__mir-run`, `__mir-llvm-run` and `__mir-llvm-asan`; so do a capturing closure, a function item, the row's `*a = || *b + 1` shape (42), a forwarding `twice(mut a)`, and `*c = || 100` through `mut ref MutFn`. Pinned by tests/mir_fn_param_written_through.rs (7 programs: check clean, run and build), added to CI's codegen-e2e line. Gate at e9b2b744e8 plus the fix: fmt, both clippy legs, `cargo test --all` 10151 passed, `cargo test --features llvm` 10282 passed, 0 failed; mir_build, mir_declared_fn_local and the new suite re-ran green after the rebase.

title: The drop-soundness fuzzer was deleted with the legacy pipeline at M3 and has no v2 port: nothing fuzzes drop elaboration against ASan/LSan and a drop-token oracle
detail: FOUND 2026-11-02 by the drop schedule thread triaging Fuzz run 41439333367 (job 125256953201): fuzz.yml's drop-soundness job exited 127 ('scripts/drop-fuzz.sh: No such file or directory') on every nightly since M3 (9ed792e373, 10-24) deleted src/bin/drop_fuzz.rs and scripts/drop-fuzz.sh. The review thread removed the dead job from fuzz.yml (same commit as this row). The legacy fuzzer generated well-typed heap-core programs, built them through the AOT path under ASan+LSan, and compared a drop-token log on the interpreter, which is the only instrument that sees a user Drop body running twice or not at all. WANTED: a v2 port that builds through MIR (karac __mir-llvm-asan) and checks the drop-token log on the MIR interpreter, wired back into fuzz.yml nightly. Owner: drop schedule (drop elaboration). Not a 0.8.x item.
fix: 041a8ce231: scripts/fuzz/drop_fuzz.py is the v2 port, a Python driver over karac rather than a Rust binary, so it has no build or clippy surface of its own. Its generator keeps the legacy one's heap-core shapes (Strings, Vecs, Maps, Sets, Arrays, tuples, Options, Results, user and generic enums, user `impl Drop` values displaced, moved through variants and matched with `_`, and values moved into `par` branches and spawned tasks), written in today's language: `own` parameters, qualified variants, `into_iter()` for owned loops, and a `sync` struct into `par`. A program is judged only once `karac check` accepts it (rejections are tallied per error code, and a run that judges nothing exits 2). Each program then runs on the MIR interpreter and through `karac __mir-llvm-asan` with auto-par off and on (four workers), judged by ASan + LSan, a per-tag N/D drop-token balance on every surface, and stdout agreement with the interpreter (as a multiset of lines for a program with par or tasks), with KARAC_HASH_SEED=1. Findings are shrunk by line deletion. `--canary` plants a Drop body that runs twice and must be reported on all three surfaces, which it is. A shrink of that canary reaches a single construction line. Measured 2026-11-02 on the tree of e888029d05 before its rebase: 500 programs (seeds 1000-1199, 20000-20299) judged clean on all three surfaces, at about 1 s per program, with 300 of 300 generated programs accepted by check. fuzz.yml's drop-soundness job builds the runtime archives and karac, runs the canary, then runs 600 programs nightly on a seed derived from the date, and uploads the report and repros.

title: Kata 71's simplify-path runs 1.40x legacy's instructions and 1.42x its cycles in the seq lane on the MIR backend, and its par lane slipped from 0.91x to 1.06x rayon between g6697158fa and g96fca5370 while seq held at 0.90x rustc -O
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro, karac 0.8.0-dev.14215+g96fca5370 vs legacy dd86e3955. KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via kara scripts/pmc.c (5-run minima): bench/simplify.kara 4.067G vs 2.900G instructions, 607M vs 428M cycles. The kata still beats rustc -O in seq (0.90x, flat), which is why the sweep's ratio flags never raised this: both figures are against legacy. Par lane, g6697158fa -> g96fca5370: 0.91 -> 1.06x rayon, 14.02 -> 18.32x C-par, 6.77 -> 7.59x Go-par, at 49.3 ms against seq's 156.6 ms (3.2x). Separate from B-2026-11-01-17 (slower at exactly KARAC_THREADS=2, which still reproduces: 0.30-0.40 s against 0.14-0.15 s at one worker). Per-iteration work allocates: a Vec[char] snapshot, two Vec[i64] stacks and an f-string append per output char. Unattributed.
fix: 791fe05de0. MEASURED x86 callgrind (release at 7310a8f945 vs legacy dd86e3955, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs equal): 1.949G vs 1.505G, 1.295x. ATTRIBUTED: MIR made 5.625M mallocs to legacy's 4.375M, 1.25 more a call, which is exactly the Vec[char] snapshot doubling from its first 8 slots over the 8 inputs (6, 32, 21, 12, 21, 8, 17, 10 chars: 10 reallocs per 8 calls); the two stacks never pass 8 and `out` doubles 0.375 a call on both backends; memcpy 52M vs 17M was the same reallocs. Legacy's src/presize.rs reserves SRC.len() for a `for c in SRC.chars()` fill (iterable_len_bound); mir::presize only took counting while/range loops. FIX: plan_chars in src/mir/presize.rs takes a loop whose header is `o = StrChars.next(&mut it)`, whose only way out is the switch on o's variant, and which pushes to v once on every trip, with `it = String.chars(&text)` on the chain and nothing after it touching v; it reserves `String.len(&text)` more right after the iterator is made, and the pushes become __push_within. AFTER: 1.680G vs 1.505G, 1.116x (callgrind, release at 791fe05de0's tree). The par lane's slip (0.91x -> 1.06x rayon on the M5) was not re-measured here, as there is no rayon lane in this container; the same 1.25 mallocs a call leave every worker's iterations. Pinned by mir_presize_reserves_a_chars_walk (reserve, push_within, capacity = seed + text bytes on a non-ASCII text, and two off-shape loops left alone).

title: Kata 38's seq binary stays at 312 KiB on g96fca5370 where the B-2026-10-28-36 fix took 12 other kata seq binaries to 52-69 KB
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 on the M5 Pro, karac 0.8.0-dev.14215+g96fca5370 vs legacy dd86e3955. bench/count_and_say.kara, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0: 319,808 bytes. In the same 13-kata set the other seq binaries are 52-69 KB and par binaries 386-403 KB. The kernel uses `f"{k + 1}"`, `f"{acc}"` and `s.chars()`; whether one of those still reaches std's panic or formatting machinery is not attributed (B-2026-10-28-36's fix describes that class). `ld64 -why_live` on this binary would name the root. SECOND INSTANCE: kata 282's seq binary is also 312.3 KiB on g7310a8f94.
fix: ad984ef96b: measured on Linux, before the rebase that made ad984ef96b. Kata 38's in-order binary was 363 KB and kata 282's 346 KB, each linking std's panic hook and backtrace symbolizer, from two roots, found by walking the debug binary's call graph to rust_begin_unwind. (1) Kata 38: karac_mir_panic_set (reached from `char.try_from(..).unwrap()`) held the message in a String behind a RefCell and stored the full-report pointer of B-2026-10-28-36, so a program whose unwrap or panic(msg) may fire took the full report. The message now lives in a LeanVec set without a panic; karac_mir_abort_at's plain report writes it; only the parts that need the full report (error trace frames, held logs, a panic handler) select it. (2) Kata 282: karac_mir_str_slice / karac_mir_str_view (substring, slice, s[a..b]) built their messages with format! (core's integer Display keeps a bounds panic) and lossy text with String::from_utf8_lossy. Messages are now written into a LeanVec (the {:?} quoting through str::escape_debug, a single quote left as Debug leaves it) and lossy text is a LeanVec from utf8_chunks. karac_mir_vec_alloc's expect became vec_reserve's fatal write. After: kata 38 70 KB, kata 282 86 KB, same output. Abort reports stay byte-identical to the interpreter's. tests/mir_panic_free_messages.rs fails 0 of 5 on the old runtime and passes 5 of 5. The M5 numbers need a Mac re-measure.

title: 128 nested `{` followed by a statement keyword (`if`, `let`, `while`, ...) runs the parser out of memory: the refused statement is retried forever, one diagnostic per turn
detail: FOUND 2026-11-02 by the scheduled Fuzz run 41439333367 (03:45 PST, fa3579844): fuzz_parser reached 2 GB peak RSS on a 255-byte unit of about 200 nested `{` plus garbage (job 125256952974). Minimized by Thread C (and independently by the drop schedule) to exactly 128 `{` then `if`: `karac check` aborts with `memory allocation of 2147483648 bytes failed` after a few seconds, while 127 `{` + `if` or 129 `{` alone give a normal diagnostic in 0.02 s. Cause: at MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH (128) a block statement that begins with a keyword fails in `enter_recursion` without consuming a token; `parse_block` then calls `synchronize_to_stmt`, which stops at statement keywords, i.e. at that same `if`, and the loop retries the statement, pushing a `nesting too deep` diagnostic each turn until the error Vec's growth fails. The nesting limit does cover block braces (129 `{` alone reports it); only the recovery made no progress.
fix: 1d2fc6d232. Block recovery now takes at least one token when synchronize_to_stmt made no progress (Parser::recover_stmt), so a statement the recursion budget refuses is stepped past instead of retried. 128 `{` then `if` now gives its diagnostics and returns in 0.02 s like 127 or 129. Pinned by tests/parser_depth_recovery.rs: every statement keyword (if, while, for, loop, match, let, return, break, continue, and two full statements) at depths 127, 128, 129 and 200, at most depth + 8 diagnostics each within 30 s, plus the fuzz unit verbatim. Without the fix the test binary aborts on the allocation. The libFuzzer corpus is gitignored (fuzz/.gitignore), so the unit lives in the test instead.

title: A `Vec.with_capacity(n)` filled by a counting push loop runs 12.6x legacy's instructions on x86: mir::presize only takes a `Vec.new()` start, so every push keeps its capacity check and LLVM cannot turn the fill into a copy; after the fix the fill is one memcpy, which callgrind counts at 1.60x legacy's inline vector copy (all of it inside glibc's __memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms) at equal wall time, the same as a `Vec.new()` start
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-02 by Thread C (x86 valgrind callgrind, karac 7310a8f945 vs legacy dd86e3955, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs equal at 120000180): `let n = 2000000; let src: Vec[i64] = Vec.filled(n, 3); 60 rounds of { let mut work: Vec[i64] = Vec.with_capacity(n); let mut k = 0; while k < n { work.push(src[k]); k = k + 1; } sink = sink + work[r] + work.len(); }` runs MIR 0.841G instructions vs legacy 0.067G (12.6x), about 7 instructions a push against legacy's vectorized copy. The same loop on a `Vec.new()` start is presized (9f3cc6a792, 11d7eb7f01) and its pushes become `__push_within`, which drops the capacity check; presize.rs requires the vector's start on the chain into the loop to be `new` with no arguments, so `with_capacity(n)` (the spelling a programmer who knows the count reaches for) gets nothing. Probable fix: accept `with_capacity(_)` (Vec and String) as a fresh start too; presize's reserve is a no-op on capacity already there and still returns the room the pushes need.
fix: 791fe05de0. mir::presize took only a `new()` start as a fresh fill; it now takes `with_capacity(n)` too (src/mir/presize.rs, the chain walk in plan), and the reserve asks for what `n` does not already hold. The counting fill's pushes become `__push_within` and LLVM turns the fill into a memcpy, as from `Vec.new()`. MEASURED x86 callgrind, release at 791fe05de0's tree vs legacy dd86e3955, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, outputs equal: 0.841G -> 0.107G (12.6x -> 1.60x). The remaining 1.60x is all inside glibc's __memcpy_avx_unaligned_erms (99% of the run) against legacy's own inline vector loop, at equal wall time (0.11 s vs 0.10-0.12 s over two runs each), and a `Vec.new()` start of the same fill counts the same 0.107G, so nothing here is specific to `with_capacity`. Pinned by mir_presize_reserves_a_with_capacity_fill (reserved, within, and capacity/output for a start below and above the trip count).

title: `tx.send(s)` on a `Sender[ref String]` with a plain `String` local passes check, though §5.7 forbids a view in a channel; at run the receiver reads garbage: `panic: out of memory` on run and llvm, ASan global-buffer-overflow, interp leak
detail: §5 probe at head (after bd06c31fe). Minimal: `fn main() { let (tx, rx): (Sender[ref String], Receiver[ref String]) = channel(1); let s = "x".to_string(); let _ = tx.send(s); println(rx.recv().unwrap()); }`. check: All checks passed. karac run and __mir-llvm-run: `panic: out of memory`. __mir-llvm-asan: `AddressSanitizer: global-buffer-overflow ... READ of size 8 ... thread T1`. __mir-run prints x then `leaked at exit: a1 (count 1)`. Expected: refused under §5.7 (a view may not flow into a channel). The explicit form `let r = ref s; tx.send(r)` IS refused ("a view of a temporary value is stored in ... a channel"), so the miss is the implicit borrow at the `own T` argument where T = ref String; the crash suggests the argument is also lowered as the String value rather than a reference to it. Same with the send inside an inner block that drops s. Cell r41 in probe-core/gen5.py.
fix: 5c73fea787. The argument of a library method whose parameter is `ref T` (Sender/Channel send and try_send, Option.replace, Vec/VecDeque insert and fill, Set/SortedSet insert, contains and remove) is now typed `ref T` in MIR lowering's lib_param_tys, so an owned place is lent, not moved. The typechecker records the lend for VecDeque push_back/push_front and insert, so §5.7 applies: the minimal `tx.send(s)` on a `Sender[ref String]` is refused by MIR borrowck (E0509, a view stored in a channel), the shape the explicit `ref s` already got. Pins: corpus/core/err_send_owned_place_on_ref_channel and ok_owned_place_into_ref_slot (interp, llvm and ASan agree). Remainders are their own rows: a LITERAL into a library `ref` slot (no §5.3 static promotion in the native store path), and llvm natives for `ref` element types (Vec.fill, SortedSet iteration).

title: A method with a `self` receiver that returns a reference may return a borrowed ARGUMENT (`fn pick(self, k: ref String) -> ref String { k }`): §5.4's receiver rule says the result borrows `self` only and the body is checked against it, but check accepts, so a caller can keep the result past the argument
detail: §5 probe at head. `struct Pool { tag: String }` `impl Pool { fn pick(self, k: ref String) -> ref String { k } }` is accepted. A caller then legally does `let r = { let k = "q...".to_string(); pool.pick(k) };` and prints r after k is dropped: check passes because the result borrows only `pool`. It printed the old contents on run, llvm and ASan (no report) in my run, so the dangling read is latent here, but the spec states the body check explicitly (§5.4: 'The body is checked against the rule'). Expected: an error at the `k` return. Cell r13 in probe-core/gen5.py.
fix: 77d7baa2b1 (message refined in 921054b432). Under the core rules, a method with a `self` or `mut ref self` receiver counts only `self` as a source for its returned borrow (§5.4), so `fn pick(self, k: ref String) -> ref String { k }` is refused with "a method with a `self` receiver returns a borrow of `self` only (core semantics §5.4)". That message is used only when an argument would otherwise have lent the result; a dangling local keeps the dangling-reference message. The core_strict_check fixture `or(self, d) -> ref String { self.items.get(0) ?? d }`, which pinned the wrong answer, is flipped to a rejection. Pin: corpus/core/err_receiver_method_returns_argument. A check-only sweep of the corpus and katas found no other program this refuses.

title: Returning `m.get(k) ?? ""` from a function is refused (E0516 'cannot drop the temporary value'), and so is `let o = m.get(k); o ?? ""` ('returned borrow does not originate from a ref parameter'), though §5.3 names `m.get(k) ?? ""` as a static fallback that may be kept and returned
detail: §5 probe at head. `fn pick(m: ref Map[String, String], k: ref String) -> ref String { m.get(k) ?? "" }` is refused at the `m.get(k)` with E0516 citing §5.5. With the Option bound first, `let o = m.get(k); o ?? ""`, it is refused as a borrow that does not originate from a ref parameter. Accepted and printing the value: `m.get(k).unwrap_or("")` returned the same way, `match m.get(k) { Some(v) => v, None => "" }`, and `let r = m.get(k) ?? "";` inside main. So only `??` in a returned position is affected: its result appears to take the Option temporary as its origin instead of the Option's payload origins (m) unioned with the static literal. Spec §5.3: 'm.get(k).unwrap_or(""), counts.get(k).unwrap_or(0) and m.get(k) ?? "" may be bound, kept and returned.'
fix: 77d7baa2b1. The ref-return check accepts a local bound to a method call or `??` whose result borrows only what the parameters lend (`let o = m.get(k); o ?? ""`), and MIR lowering of `??` with a value fallback into a shared-ref destination promotes a literal fallback to a static (§5.3) instead of taking a temporary's address. Pin: corpus/core/ok_nil_coalesce_literal_fallback_returned (interp, llvm and ASan agree).

title: Two `TaskGroup` tasks that write DISJOINT fields of one local (`p.x` and `p.y`) are refused: 'a task of `g` captures `p` by `mut ref`, which no other task of the group may capture'; §9.1 captures places, and the same pair is accepted in `par {}` and as two plain closures
detail: §9 probe at head. `struct Pt { mut x: i64, mut y: i64 }` and `let mut p = Pt { x: 0, y: 0 }; { let g = TaskGroup.new(); let a = g.spawn(|| { p.x = 1; 0 }); let b = g.spawn(|| { p.y = 2; 0 }); a.join(); b.join(); } println(p.x + p.y);` is refused at both spawns with the §9.5 message naming the whole binding `p`. Expected 3: §9.1 infers capture modes per captured place with disjoint field capture, §5.6 says distinct fields do not overlap, and §9.5's rule is about a place another task already captured. The interpreter, llvm and ASan lanes all print 3 with no report. Accepted and printing 3: `par { { p.x = 1; 0 }, { p.y = 2; 0 } }` and two local closures `|| { q.x = 1; }` / `|| { q.y = 2; }`. So the TaskGroup capture check widens a field capture to its root. Cell c15 in probe-core/gen9b.py.
fix: 77d7baa2b1. The strict task-group exclusivity pass records each capture's place paths (field projections; an index ends the path) and reports a conflict only when two tasks' paths overlap (one is a prefix of the other), so tasks writing DISJOINT fields of one struct are accepted (§9.5). Pin: corpus/core/ok_tasks_write_disjoint_fields.

title: A non-escaping `Fn` parameter may be captured by a closure the callee returns (`fn wrap(f: Fn() -> i64) -> Fn() -> i64 { || f() + 1 }`); §9.3 lets the callee only call it or pass it to another non-escaping parameter
detail: §9 probe at head. `fn wrap(f: Fn() -> i64) -> Fn() -> i64 { || f() + 1 }` and the same through a struct (`fn wrap(f: Fn() -> i64) -> H { H { f: || f() + 1 } }`) pass check. §9.3: storing or returning a function-typed parameter requires `f: escaping Fn(..)`; a returned closure capturing it stores it. Expected: an error at the capture with the `escaping` fix-it, as for `fn ret(f: Fn() -> i64) -> Fn() -> i64 { f }` and pushing it into a Vec, which ARE refused. No wrong value found: the caller side compensates (passing `|| s.len()` from a block that drops s is refused with E0516, and through the struct form the argument closure took `v` by move and printed 9, ASan clean), so this is a missing callee-side check rather than an observed dangling read. Cell c25 in probe-core/gen9b.py.
fix: 77d7baa2b1. core_escape refuses a closure that captures a non-escaping function parameter when the closure itself escapes (returned, stored, or sent; anything but being the call's result): "parameter `f` is a non-escaping function value and cannot be captured by a closure that is ...". Pin: corpus/core/err_returned_closure_captures_non_escaping_param.

title: A closure stored in a field of a LOCAL struct or tuple (`Hm { f: || { n = n + 1; n } }`, `(1, || ..)`) captures a `Copy` place by copy instead of by `mut ref`, so its writes are lost and `n` reads 0 after two calls (expected 2); every lane agrees
detail:
§9 probe at head, ruled a bug by the review thread (2026-11-02 20:10Z): §5.7 does not list a plain local struct among the places a view may not go, so a struct or tuple held in a local is a local view; storing the closure in its field does not escape (§9.3), the capture of `n` is `mut ref`, and printing 0 is the silent stale read §9.1's Copy rule exists to prevent. Only when the containing value itself is returned, stored or sent does the capture become a move.
Wrong value on run, __mir-run, __mir-llvm-run (check passes):
(1) `struct Hm[F] { f: F }` `fn callm[F: MutFn() -> i64](h: mut ref Hm[F]) -> i64 { (h.f)() }` `let mut n = 0; { let mut h = Hm { f: || { n = n + 1; n } }; callm(mut h); callm(mut h); } println(n);` prints 0, expected 2.
(2) Non-generic `struct Hb { f: MutFn() -> i64 }`, calls `(h.f)(); (h.f)();` inside the block: 0, expected 2.
(3) `let mut h = Hb { f: || { n = n + 1; n } }; (h.f)(); println(n);` with h not used after the call: 0, expected 1.
(4) Tuple: `{ let mut t = (1, || { n = n + 1; n }); (t.1)(); (t.1)(); } println(n);` 0, expected 2.
Control that must keep by-move capture (correct today): `fn mk() -> Hb { let mut n = 0; let h = Hb { f: || { n = n + 1; n } }; h }` then two calls on the returned value print 1 and 2 (`a * 10 + b` = 12).
Likely code: src/core_escape.rs (escape classification of a closure stored into an aggregate literal) and src/ownership.rs (capture-mode inference). Cells c30 in probe-core/gen9b.py.
fix: 102ed9f295: invalid, premise refuted. A closure stored in a field of a struct, a local one included, escapes by design: design.md § Escaping function values calls a function type in a field or collection element "escaping by nature", the corpus/core pin err_escaping_capture_reused has refused reuse of a capture moved into a local `Holder { f: || .. }` (E0500) since the spec was approved on 2026-10-06, and core-semantics §9.3 now says so explicitly (102ed9f295). So the closure captures `n` by move, the `Copy` counter is copied in, and `n` reading 0 is the specified result on every lane. The review thread's 2026-11-02 20:10Z ruling read "not a local view" in §9.3 as an exemption and was reversed at 20:26Z. Side observation, not this row: a local tuple holding a closure that captures a non-Copy place by ref (`{ let t = (1, || s.len()); (t.1)(); } println(s);`) passes check but fails MIR's move check ("use of _1, which may have been moved"), since check treats a let-bound tuple element as non-escaping while MIR lowering erases it as escaping.

title: Coercing a struct whose trait method uses a provider-rooted resource into `dyn At` reports E_NO_PROVIDER ('no provider for Clk ... main takes no hidden provider parameter') instead of E_DYN_PROVIDER naming the resource and suggesting a generic parameter
detail: §14 probe at head. `effect resource Clk: ClkP;` and `trait At { fn at(self) -> i64; }` `struct S {}` `impl At for S { fn at(self) -> i64 { Clk.now() } }` with `fn main() { let d: dyn At = S {}; let r = with_provider[Clk](F { t: 9 }, || d.at()); println(r); }` is refused at the `S {}` coercion (col 29) with error[effect] E_NO_PROVIDER. Refusing is intended (review-thread ruling 2026-11-02 20:12Z; design.md § dyn Trait: a dyn value uses the providers in scope where it was coerced, and a coercion reaching a provider-rooted resource is E_DYN_PROVIDER at the coercion; §14.5 says so since a0ee54a6c). The E_DYN_PROVIDER text ('`S` as a `dyn At` cannot carry a provider, and its `at` uses `Clk` ... take a generic parameter (`[T: At]`) instead') exists at src/mir/providers.rs:1306 but this coercion path (let with a dyn annotation in main, outside any with_provider) reaches the generic no-provider check first. Cell p27 in probe-core/gen14b.py.
fix: 55c64b1eca. `main` needs a resource with no default, so providers::specialise never rewrites it and its refuse_dyn never saw main's coercions; effects' no-provider check for `main` reached the coercion first and reported E0419. That check (src/mir/effects.rs, the `main` loop at the end of analyze_with) now asks providers::main_dyn_refusal whether its site is a coercion to `dyn` whose method uses the resource, and if so records the E_DYN_PROVIDER refusal (E0423) with the text refuse_dyn writes, now one function, providers::dyn_provider_text. src/mir/lower.rs keeps these refusals ahead of the ones specialise finds (it extended rather than replaced report.refused). The probe's cell p27 now reports one E0423 at 21:29, `S` as a `dyn At` cannot carry a provider, and its `S.at` uses `Clk`, which has no default ... take a generic parameter (`[T: At]`), and __mir-run refuses it with the same text. tests/mir_dyn_provider_in_main.rs pins it, with two controls: `s.at()` called directly in main stays E0419 at the call, and the coercion in a callee under with_provider stays E0423.

title: A local moved BEFORE an `if`/`match` and reassigned in EVERY branch is refused at the later use ('value s moved here, used again here'), though §3.4 makes it initialized again; one reassignment after the move, or a move inside the branch, is accepted
detail: §3 probe at head. `let mut s = "a".to_string(); let t = s; let k = 1; if k > 0 { s = "b".to_string(); } else { s = "c".to_string(); } println(s);` is refused by check (error[ownership] at the println, 'moved at' the `let t = s`). Same with a `match` whose arms all reassign s. Expected: accepted, prints b; __mir-run prints b. Accepted today: a straight `s = ..` after the move; `s = if k > 0 { .. } else { .. };`; moving inside the then-branch and reassigning in both branches; reassigning in one branch when the other returns. So the ownership pass's join after a branch keeps the pre-branch moved state when every branch reinitializes. Spec §3.4: assigning to a moved place makes it initialized again; §3.5: a place is maybe-moved only if moved on some path reaching the use. Cell m07 in probe-core/gen34b.py.
fix: 25b7bffde2. The use-after-move witness kill counted a reassign only when it dominated the use, so a rebind in every branch of an `if`/`match` (none of which dominates the join) left the earlier consume live. uam_witnesses_for_binding now also applies reassign_kills_by_reachability, the check the RC predicate already used: a consume is dead at a use in another block when every CFG path between them threads a rebind of what it took. A rebind on only one path, a use inside a branch before its rebind, and a rebind only in a loop body are still refused. Pins: corpus/core/ok_reinit_in_every_branch (if and three-arm match) and corpus/core/err_reinit_in_one_branch_only. A check-only sweep of 27,386 corpus, example, test and kata files changed the verdict of no other file.

title: `return` inside a `par for` body is refused ('`return` may not cross out of a `par for` body'), though §11.7 makes `return` in a branch the same early exit as `?`, with `par for` taking the earliest exit in iteration order; `return` in a `par {}` branch and `?` in `par for` are accepted
detail: §11 probe at head. `fn f() -> i64 { par for i in 0..4 { if i == 1 { return 3; } } 0 }` and `fn h() -> Result[i64, i64] { par for i in 0..4 { if i == 2 { return Err(7); } } Ok(0) }` are refused by the typechecker at the `return` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs, ExprKind::Return, the `par_barrier` check). Expected per §11.7 (review-thread ruling 2026-10-22, B-2026-10-21-68 follow-up): `return` in a branch ends that branch, the iterations after it are cancelled, and the function returns the earliest-in-iteration-order exit's value: 3 and e7. Only `break` and `continue` may not leave a branch. Accepted today: `return 5` inside a `par {}` branch (corpus-style `let (a, b) = par { { if true { return 5; } 1 }, 2 }`) and `?` in a `par for` body (earlier probe cell p10, earliest iteration wins). Cell t15 in probe-core/gen11b.py.
fix: 1ca64acaf0. The typechecker's `par_barrier` check in ExprKind::Return (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) refused `return` in a `par for` body; it is gone, and `break` and `continue` stay refused. The MIR lowering already treated the `return` as `?`'s early exit: with the check removed, the interpreter, the compiled build, the ASan lane and a build at 1, 2, 4 and 8 workers (5 runs each, all identical) return the earliest iteration's value, including the row's two shapes, an `i64` return and an `Err` return. corpus/core/par_for_return_earliest pins it (expected_from spec, §11.7): one exit, none, the earlier of two exits winning, an `Err` return through a Vec walk, and an owned String live at the exit. tests/typechecker.rs's par_for_is_a_vec_and_keeps_jumps_inside pinned the refusal and now accepts `return` in a `par for` in both a value and a unit function. design.md § `par {}` and syntax.md said `return` may not cross out; both now follow §11.7, and CHANGELOG 0.8.1 Diagnostics notes it.

title: Two `par` branches calling a generic `fn ap[F: Fn(i64) -> i64](x: i64, f: F)` with pure closures or a pure named fn conflict as 'unknown (a function value that cannot be resolved)'; §12 computes a generic call's effects on the monomorphised instance, and the non-generic `f: Fn(i64) -> i64` form is accepted
detail: §12 probe at head. `fn ap[F: Fn(i64) -> i64](x: i64, f: F) -> i64 { f(x) }` with `let (a, b) = par { ap(3, |x| x * 2), ap(4, |x| x * 2) };` (or `ap(3, dbl), ap(4, dbl)` with `fn dbl(x: i64) -> i64 { x * 2 }`) is refused: 'branches 1 and 2 of the par conflict: unknown (a function value that cannot be resolved) and unknown (...)' (§11.2). Expected: accepted, prints 14. §12: 'The effects of a generic call are computed on the monomorphised instance', and a call through a non-escaping function-typed parameter has the argument's effects, charged to the caller. Accepted today: the same with a non-generic parameter `f: Fn(i64) -> i64` (closures or dbl), and one branch `ap(3, dbl)` beside a plain `dbl(4)`. So the generic instance's call `f(x)` through a type-parameter-typed value keeps default 1 (every effect) instead of resolving to the instantiated closure or fn item. Cell y09 in probe-core/gen1213b.py.
fix: 8876b6f720: fn_value_bodies (src/mir/effects.rs) now resolves a value of erased Fn type. A generic fn instantiated at an erased Fn is passed `&f` where `f = closure as Fn (Erase)`; the new erased_fn_bodies follows the operand back through single-assignment copies and borrows to a local whose every assignment erases a closure or fn item (refusing a local lent mut, written by a call, or erased from an already-erased Fn), and charges those bodies' effects, as core-semantics §12 computes a generic call's effects on the instance. Two par branches calling ap[F: Fn(i64) -> i64] with pure closures (also capturing a Copy local) or a pure named fn now pass and print 14 / 14 / 6 10; a printing closure or fn item still conflicts by name (writes(Stdout)). Pinned by corpus/core/ok_par_generic_call_with_pure_fn_value (mir-interp and mir-llvm) and tests/generic_fn_value_par_effect.rs (2 tests). Gate before the rebase: fmt, both clippy legs, cargo test --all 10159/0, cargo test --features llvm 10304/0. After rebasing onto 9 commits: clippy --features llvm clean, cargo test --all 10163/0, corpus core on mir-interp 152/0. On mir-llvm, 152 passed and 1 failed: katas/798 bench/best_rotation, which pre-dates this change. Its class-e expectation (error:codegen) is stale because it now builds and runs.

title: A string or integer LITERAL stored into a library `ref` slot (`v.push("lit")` on `Vec[ref String]`, `tx.send("lit")` / `tx.send(7)` on `Sender[ref T]`) has no §5.3 static promotion: interp leaks, ASan global-buffer-overflow, llvm prints nothing or OOM
detail: Remainder of B-2026-11-02-27, which 5c73fea787 fixed for a named place (the owned local is now lent into the ref slot, or refused when it would escape). Not fixed there, and pre-existing at the control: a literal argument into a library method whose parameter type is `ref T`. Shapes measured at 5c73fea787: (1) `let mut v: Vec[ref String] = Vec.new(); v.push("lit"); println(v[0])`; (2) `let (tx, rx): (Sender[ref String], Receiver[ref String]) = channel(1); let _ = tx.send("lit"); println(rx.recv().unwrap())`; (3) the same with `Sender[ref i64]` and `tx.send(7)`. __mir-run prints the value then `leaked at exit: a2`; __mir-llvm-asan reports `global-buffer-overflow`; __mir-llvm-run prints nothing (2, 3) or `panic: out of memory`. check passes all three, which is right: §5.3 promotes a literal to a static view. The miss is that the native store path receives the literal by value (or a pointer into its constant) rather than a promoted static reference.
fix: def3886d61. MIR lowering's expr_into asks literal_ref with the destination's type, so `let r: ref String = "lit"` binds a static String instead of building an owned one into the reference local; a literal argument a library method stores into a `ref` slot (`v.push("lit")`, `tx.send("lit")`, `tx.send(7)`, `d.push_back(7)` on a `VecDeque[ref i64]`) takes its slot's static the same way (§5.3), where it passed the raw literal. Pin: corpus/core/ok_literal_into_ref_slot (interp, llvm and ASan agree; the control leaks four allocations on the interpreter). An interpreter run over corpus core, apps and katas fails exactly what the control fails.

title: llvm natives for `ref` element types: `Vec[ref String].fill(r)` panics out of memory (ASan global-buffer-overflow), and iterating a `SortedSet[ref String]` prints nothing while `len()` is 1
detail: Found while fixing B-2026-11-02-27 (5c73fea787 added the `ref T` parameter types for Vec/VecDeque insert and fill and Set/SortedSet insert/contains/remove in lib_param_tys, so check and MIR now agree). The interpreter is right on both; the native lane is not, and it is pre-existing at the control. (1) `let s = "a".to_string(); let r = ref s; let mut v: Vec[ref String] = Vec.new(); v.push(r); v.fill(r); println(v[0])`: __mir-llvm-run `panic: out of memory`, __mir-llvm-asan global-buffer-overflow. (2) `let s = "a".to_string(); let mut t: SortedSet[ref String] = SortedSet.new(); t.insert(ref s); println(t.len()); for x in t { println(x) }`: interp prints 1 then a; llvm prints 1 and nothing else; ASan is clean. Backend territory (src/backend/, drop schedule): the natives appear to size or compare the element as a String value rather than a pointer.
fix: ebfe307c38 (drop schedule). Two backend causes, both in src/backend/mir. (1) Vec.fill (seq.rs) read through every reference on its value, so with a `ref String` element it reached the String and cloned its first word (the buffer pointer) as each element; it now stops at the element type. (2) A set's `entry_at` and a map's lent values (index, entry, keys/values, or_insert; table.rs `lend_value`) stored the address of the slot holding the reference, where the MIR, like the interpreter's collapse_ref_of_ref, reads the reference itself (a borrow of a borrow is the borrow): iterating a SortedSet[ref String] printed an empty string, and Map[i64, ref String] indexing ran out of memory. Both now copy the reference out, as Vec's index already did through store_ref. The row's two programs, plus a Set, Map, SortedMap (ref keys and values), VecDeque and Vec.filled of references, and a map's values/keys/entry/index, print the interpreter's output on __mir-llvm-run and are clean under __mir-llvm-asan; before the fix programs (1) and (2) and the Set/Map probe differed. Pinned by tests/mir_ref_element_natives.rs (4 programs, built and run against the interpreter and an expected literal).

title: A closure in an element of a let-bound tuple is treated as non-escaping by `karac check` (core_escape gives tuple elements tail_of(pos)), so a non-Copy capture read after it passes check and is refused later by MIR's move check, with the wrong error
detail: `let s = "abc".to_string(); { let t = (1, || s.len()); println(f"{(t.1)()}"); } println(s);` passes `karac check`; `__mir-run` fails with `move check main: bb15[0]: use of _1, which may have been moved or never initialized`. A tuple element is a positional field, and core-semantics §9.3 (as of 102ed9f295) says a closure in a struct, tuple or collection escapes, so the closure captures `s` by move and `karac check` must report E0500 at `println(s)`, as the err_escaping_capture_reused pin does for a struct. MIR lowering already erases the element as escaping and is right; src/core_escape.rs walks Tuple elements at tail_of(pos), which leaves a let-bound tuple's closure non-escaping. Ruled by the review thread 2026-11-02 20:27Z.
