(2) karac check --output=json on a package with several targets prints one object, {"targets":[{target,success,total_errors,diagnostics}],"shared_diagnostics":[..],"success"}, the shape a file check already had (split_target_json serves both); a finding on every target is reported once under shared_diagnostics. Pinned by tests/check_project_targets_json.rs. (3) --targets=all (and --target=all) checks the v1 set, native and wasm_wasi, plus any target an item in the file or package is gated on, so a gated body is still checked where it is written for; hello world passes. The gpu hint keeps naming #[target(...)]: the review thread made §4 name it as the interim spelling until #[cfg] lands (3ed4c214a1). (4) [profile.release] target-cpu, target-features and cpu-baseline are the manifest rung of each precedence chain; the older [release] spelling is still read with a warning, and a key in [profile.release] wins; [profile.dev] keys warn by name. (5) --target-cpu=help and --target-features=help print on stdout. (6) A wasm link finds wasi-libc in the bundle's lib/<triple>/, then the active rustc, then karac's build toolchain; the release bundle ships the wasm archives and wasi-libc; tests/build_wasm_bundle.rs, run by CI's wasm-e2e job (6100da885c). Release dry run 42027008632 built and ran a wasm hello from the bundle on x86_64-linux, aarch64-linux and aarch64-macos clean runners. Gate on c48ad61f26's tree: fmt, both clippy legs, cargo test --all 10350 passed, --features llvm 10517 passed, 0 failed.

title: `--output=jsonl` (check and build) never emitted a `diagnostic` event for resolve, typecheck, effect or ownership errors, so a client could not rebuild the batch document from the stream (design.md §17 Streaming phase events, invariants 1 and 2); fixed for a single file, package mode is B-2026-11-05-26
detail: Repro: a.kara = `fn main() { let s = String.from("a"); let t = s; println(s); let x: i64 = "q"; }`. `karac check --output=json a.kara` lists d1 E0200 and d2 E0500. `karac check --output=jsonl a.kara` (and `build --output=jsonl`, and package `karac check --output=jsonl`) prints build_start, phase_start/phase_complete pairs with typecheck errors:1 and ownership errors:1, and build_complete total_errors:2, but no line with "type":"diagnostic". src/cli/diag_json.rs run_pipeline_jsonl emits entries only for parse errors, and prints them as the raw batch entry with no "type" field, so even those are not `diagnostic` events. Further gaps in the same function: build_start has no build_id and "timestamp":""; build_complete has no build_id; every phase_complete reports warnings:0 (a deprecated warning is never counted); phase_skipped after a parse error hardcodes blocking ["d1"] and after resolve errors blocking []; the 20-per-file truncated marker is absent (see the batch roll-up row). `karac check --output=jsonl big.kara | head -1` panics in run_pipeline_jsonl with `failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe` (the batch --output=json path does not). Spec: every batch diagnostic appears in the stream as a `diagnostic` event with a `phase` field, and the client decides when to stop.
fix: 984142c99a, for a single file (check and build). `run_pipeline_jsonl` now runs the checks through `Pipeline::run_all_checks_observed`, the sequence the batch document uses, and at each phase boundary emits that phase's `collect_diagnostics` entries as `{"type":"diagnostic",...}` events with the batch ids (a phase's entries go out only once every phase listed before it is done, so the ids are the batch's). phase_complete counts errors, warnings and notes from the entries' severities; build_complete.total_errors is their sum and total_warnings is real; phase_skipped's `blocking` is the ids of the errors so far; build_start carries a ULID build_id, an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp and the echoed arguments, and build_complete the same build_id. Lint and comptime report as their own phases (design.md § Observable phases now says so); the skip set follows the phases' own guards, so after a resolve error the effect checker runs and is reported, as in the batch. Every write is EPIPE-safe (`print_stdout_line`: `| head -1` exits 141 quietly). Verified: stream diagnostics equal the batch `diagnostics` array, entry for entry, on 480 programs (210 corpus err/core/design pins, 270 katas and apps), with invariant 3 holding on each. Tests: tests/jsonl_stream_and_closed_stdout_check.rs; tests/cli.rs's two skip-count pins updated to the phases that really skip. Package mode (`karac check --output=jsonl` on a package member, `karac build --output=jsonl` in a package) is not the §17 stream yet: B-2026-11-05-26. The cascade cap is B-2026-11-05-17's.

title: `karac fmt` drops the trailing comma of a one-element tuple TYPE, so `(i64,)` becomes `(i64)` and the formatted program no longer typechecks (and a second fmt is not idempotent)
detail: Repro: `fn f() -> (i64,) { (4,) }\nfn g(t: (String,)) -> i64 { t.0.len() as i64 }\nfn main() { let v: Vec[(i64,)] = [(1,), (2,)]; println(v.len()); println(f().0); println(g(("ab",))); let t: (i64,) = (1,); println(t.0); }` runs and prints 2, 4, 2, 1. `karac fmt a.kara > b.kara` writes `fn f() -> (i64) {`, `t: (String)`, `Vec[(i64)]`, `let t: (i64) = (1,);` while keeping the expression `(1,)`. `karac run b.kara`: E0200 expected 'i64', found '(i64)' and `tuple index on non-tuple type 'String'`. Formatting b.kara again changes it further. The expression form `(4,)` is preserved; only the type printer loses the comma. 50 other round-trip shapes (precedence parens, casts, ranges, strings and raw strings, comments in every position, closures, labels, let-else, par, generics with where, attributes, doc comments, unicode positions) were idempotent and kept their output. design.md §17 Canonical formatting: the formatter normalizes layout, not meaning.
fix: 0dcb18ba9e. The formatter writes the comma of a one-element tuple type and tuple pattern (src/formatter/types.rs, patterns.rs), so `(i64,)` round-trips instead of becoming the parenthesised `(i64)`; the typechecker's type display prints `(T,)` too. Pinned by tests/fmt_one_element_tuple.rs (type and pattern round-trip, idempotent).

title: kara-lsp treats a file inside a package as package-less: `import util;` in src/main.kara of a package with kara.toml gets a false `unknown module util` error, so every multi-file package shows red in the editor
detail: Repro: pkg/kara.toml `[package]\nname = "app"`, pkg/src/util.kara `pub fn f() -> i64 { 1 }`, pkg/src/main.kara `import util;\nfn main() { println(util.f()); }`. `karac check` in pkg passes. Drive target/release/kara-lsp over stdio: initialize with rootUri file:///.../pkg, didOpen file:///.../pkg/src/main.kara with the same text. publishDiagnostics: severity 1, code resolve, range 0:0-0:12, `unknown module `util`: this file belongs to no package, so the only modules it can import are the library's (`std.*`); a program of several files is a package, with a `kara.toml` beside its `src/``. The kara.toml is on disk beside src/. Single-file documents work: diagnostics, didChange clearing, hover, definition, formatting, UTF-16 columns with astral characters, unknown-method -32601 and shutdown/exit were all correct. Minor, same surface: the LSP diagnostic `code` is the phase name (typecheck, parse, resolve) rather than the E-code `karac check --output=json` gives, so `karac explain` cannot take it.
fix: 8dff1b2177. kara-lsp checks a file inside a package with its package: lsp/src/analysis.rs maps the document URI to a path (percent-decoded, localhost and Windows drive forms), and `karac::check_source_at` runs the package check with the editor's unsaved buffer laid over that file (`build_program_tree_with_overlay` in src/module.rs, `package_check_with_buffer` in src/cli/build_cmds.rs), then keeps the parse, cycle, resolve and type diagnostics of that file. A lone file or a package's lone entry keeps the old single-file path. Pinned by lsp/tests/package_member.rs (sibling import resolves, unsaved buffer used, a real unknown module still reported, a lone file unchanged).

title: In a package, `karac check` drops the cross-module `deprecated` warning unless the check also has an error; `karac build` reports it, and a single file reports it
detail:
Repro: kara.toml `[package]
name = "app"`; src/util.kara `#[deprecated(note: "x")]
pub fn old() -> i64 { 1 }`; src/main.kara `import util;
fn main() { println(util.old()); }`. `karac check`: `All checks passed.` with no warning; `karac check --output=json`: `{"diagnostics":[]}`; `karac check src/main.kara`: same. `karac build`: `warning[deprecated]: src/main.kara:2:31: use of deprecated item `old`` (caret on the closing paren, col 31, not on `old`). Add `let q: i64 = "s";` to main and `karac check` now prints the E0200 AND the deprecated warning. Merged into one file (no package) the warning appears with no error present. So the clean-check path of the package checker loses lints from cross-module uses; `#[expect(deprecated)]` on such a use is reported fulfilled either way. A warning-free `karac check` is the authoring loop's success signal, and `-D warnings` CI on check would pass code that build rejects.
fix: 8b95f3e4b1. A package's karac check runs the v2 check of its combined source, as run and build do, but a passing check dropped that pipeline's warnings. Only the per-module warnings printed, and a module's own check cannot see another module's deprecated item. cmd_check_project (src/cli/run_check_cmds.rs) now prints the combined check's warnings in text mode, and adds them to --output=json, in place of the per-module ones. So check prints what build prints, with no duplicates. Pinned by a_clean_package_check_warns_of_another_modules_deprecated_item (tests/package_pipeline_parity.rs), which covers check, check --output=json and build. The caret on the closing paren in util.old(), wrong in build as well, is B-2026-11-05-24.

title: §17 tooling roll-up: batch JSON lacks the 20-per-file cascade cap; `--emit-timings` unknown; explain rejects the symbolic codes the text prints; tool-namespaced attributes accepted silently; lint-level edge cases (statement `#[expect]` under a fn `#[allow]`, unknown `-D` names, doubled level labels); the larger items (concept ids, derivations, hint shape, style lints, fmt method order) split to B-2026-11-05-28..32
detail: Each item checked against design.md §17 at b289acf29. (1) No diagnostic carries `concept` (rule 4, required for errors and warnings). (2) 25 E0200s in one file are all reported as primaries with no `truncated` marker (rule 3). (3) E0400 for `fn inner() { println("x"); } fn mid() { inner(); } pub fn top() { mid(); }` has only message/class: no derivation chain (rule 5), no inferred_effects/declared_effects, no hint; `karac fix` leaves it ("no fixable diagnostics") though the message names the exact clause. A match missing a variant is not fixable either. §17 names effect annotations and missing pattern arms as the routine mechanical fixes. (4) Hint shape: single-file JSON carries `replacement: {offset,length,text}` beside a prose hint, package JSON carries `fix_it` and `fixes[].edits[]`; neither is the spec's `diff {file,line,old,new}`. Package-mode --output=json is `{"diagnostics":[...]}` with no program_effects key (null required when not reached). (5) `karac fix` style lints: counter while to for, `x = x + e` to `+=`, final `return e;` to `e`, redundant `.iter()`, redundant `ref` on a parameter: none fires and none is in `karac lint --list` (the registry lists every other v1 lint the spec names). (6) `--emit-timings=t.json` is an unknown flag. (7) `karac query effects f.kara.top` and `query ownership` answer without a `derivation` ("each answer includes a derivation chain"); `karac query queries` with no target is a usage error. (8) `karac explain ownership/move-semantics` (the spec's own concept id) is unknown (supported: closures, operators, module-state, stable-hash); `karac explain a.kara.top` (item: effects with derivation, would-be mode) is unknown. Text output prints names like `error[E_DUPLICATE_LINT_LEVEL]`, `E_UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE`, `E_FORBIDDEN_LINT_ALLOW`, `E_NOT_CROSS_TASK` that explain rejects; JSON gives E0121/E0247/E0248 that work, but E_DUPLICATE_LINT_LEVEL's JSON code is the generic E0001 with no class. (9) Re-probed after the 219b88a4a2 spec change (karac::proto and karac::field are legal compiler-namespace attributes; other multi-segment paths and unknown karac:: names are errors): `#[karac::proto]` and `#[karac::field]` are accepted correctly, but `#[karac::bogus]`, `#[foo::bar]` and `#[a::b::c]` are still accepted silently on a fn, and E0121's hint still suggests `#[your_tool::name]`. (10) `#[allow(unfulfilled_lint_expectation)]` on a fn does not silence an inner `#[expect(deprecated)]` that does not fire. (11) `-D no_such_lint` is accepted silently (an attribute gets unknown_lint). Text labels mix levels: `warning[unknown_lint]: ... error[E_UNKNOWN_LINT]`, and unfulfilled_lint_expectation prints its `warning[...]` prefix twice. (12) `karac fmt` does not sort methods (`zeta` stays before `alpha`; imports are sorted). Checked fine: fmt --check lists files and exits 1 writing nothing, package/dir in place, single file to stdout, --write; lint levels allow/warn/deny/expect, E_DUPLICATE_LINT_LEVEL, E_EXPECT_ON_UNFULFILLED, -F with inner allow refused, -D warnings, `#[name = v]` and `key = v` refused with good messages; run/test exit codes 0/1/7/101; EPIPE on run, interp and built binaries.
fix: 8039f0b7dd and c9f058b0f1; the five large items are their own rows. (2) The cascade cap: `cap_cascade` (src/cli/diag_json.rs) drops a file's errors past its 20th primary error from `--output=json` and the JSONL stream, and each phase that dropped some reports the count in `{"phase":…,"truncated":{"file":…,"suppressed_primary_errors":N}}` after its last entry; warnings are never capped; batch and stream carry the same markers (design.md §17 rule 3 now says where the marker sits). 25 E0200s plus a deprecated warning give 20 errors, the warning and a marker of 5. (6) `--emit-timings=<file>` (any command, before `--`) writes the `phase_time` phases and the wall-clock total as JSON, rewritten after each phase, nothing on stdout. (8) `karac explain` reads a catalogued `E_*` name as a code and catalogues E_NOT_CROSS_TASK, E_UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE, E_FORBIDDEN_LINT_ALLOW, E_EXPECT_ON_UNFULFILLED and E_DUPLICATE_LINT_LEVEL, which has its own parse code E0006 in place of the generic E0001. (9) Per the review thread's ruling (219b88a4a2, 7098ae42a2): a multi-segment attribute path is E_UNKNOWN_ATTRIBUTE unless it is `karac::proto` / `karac::field` or in `diagnostic::`; E0121's hint no longer offers `#[your_tool::name]`. A `karac::` helper on a fn is accepted like `#[serde(...)]` on a fn: derive-helper placement is not validated for any helper. (10) A statement-level `#[expect]` sees the levels of its function, impl and enclosing statements. (11) `-A/-W/-D/-F NAME` naming no lint warns `unknown_lint` on stderr; the unknown-lint and unfulfilled-expectation messages carry one level. (4, part) package-build JSON carries `program_effects`. Split out: (1)+(8 concepts, items) B-2026-11-05-28; (3)+(7) B-2026-11-05-29; (4) B-2026-11-05-30; (5) B-2026-11-05-31; (12) B-2026-11-05-32. Package-mode JSON/JSONL is B-2026-11-05-26 (Thread B). Tests: tests/lint_and_explain_edges_check.rs, tests/resolver.rs (tool path refused), src/cli/explain.rs unit tests. gate174 green (10361 + 10529, 0 failed).

title: §17 panic record and debugger contract are not emitted: no JSONL panic event on stderr under `karac run`/`karac test`, no record `kind`, so `karac debug` has nothing to read; `std.runtime` (has_debug_metadata, list_tasks, list_par_blocks) is an unknown module
detail:
design.md §17 Panic record: under karac run and karac test the runner asks the program for the record as one JSONL event on stderr, with kind (explicit, index_out_of_bounds, overflow, div_by_zero, unwrap, borrow_conflict, assertion, alloc_failure, unreachable, deadlock), message, file:line:col and the error-return trace. Measured: `fn main() { let v: Vec[i64] = []; println(v[3]); }` under `karac run` and `--interp` exits 101 with stderr `runtime error: index out of bounds
  at a.kara:1:43
Error return trace:
  a.kara:1:43` and nothing else; same shape for div_by_zero and panic("boom"). No JSON line, no kind. `karac test` reports a panic as test_fail with message only. src/crash_report.rs says `std.panic does not emit yet`; `karac debug` therefore has no producer. A plain panic also prints an `Error return trace` naming only the panic site, though nothing propagated through `?`. Debugger contract: `import std.runtime;` is `unknown module std.runtime` on all backends, so has_debug_metadata(), list_tasks() and list_par_blocks() (which must return empty lists in a binary without metadata) cannot be called; deferred.md extends element 4 but does not defer it. Panic location, track_caller, the 101 exit, the handler order and release stripping of the error-return trace were all correct.
fix: fe1f97379f (std.runtime), 16b7a99fda (panic record), da5cd420c7, 4ac5c26c17. (1) `std.runtime` is a gated library module (runtime/stdlib/std_runtime.kara) whose has_debug_metadata(), list_tasks() and list_par_blocks() reach the Runtime builtins. Its types (Runtime, TaskInfo, ParBlockInfo, WaitTarget) are its globals. It can be imported whole (`import std.runtime;` + `runtime.list_tasks()`) or item by item. Pinned by corpus/design/ok_std_runtime_introspection on interp, llvm and asan, and by tests/package_std_imports.rs in a package. (2) The panic record's kind, per the ruling at 2d8332469a: under --output=json/jsonl, karac run sets KARAC_PANIC_RECORD. The interpreter, and the runtime once karac_jit_runner enables it, then write {"type":"panic_record","kind":K} after the human report, and the runner folds it into its runtime_error event without passing it through. karac test always asks, and puts the kind on test_fail. Text mode and built binaries keep the human report alone. The kind comes from the panic site, because expect("x") and panic("x") print alike: a panic_kind native that the MIR builder emits for assertions and unreachable(); a library __karac_panic_kind call in Option/Result unwrap/expect/unwrap_err/expect_err and the library's bounds checks; otherwise the abort reason (overflow, also for a shift out of range; div_by_zero; index_out_of_bounds, also for string slices). tests/panic_record.rs pins every producible kind on JIT and interp, text mode's silence, the built binary, and karac test. Spawn-site metadata (has_debug_metadata() is false even in dev) and the three kinds no v2 path raises are B-2026-11-05-34.

title: Parallel assignment (`a, b = b, a`, `v[i], v[j] = v[j], v[i]`) in ANY package panics the compiler: `entered unreachable code: StmtKind::MultiAssign is removed by the desugar pass before reaching this phase` (src/resolver/resolve_block.rs:155) on check, run, run --interp and build
fix: 8b95f3e4b1. A package's per-module resolve and type checks (resolve_modules, typecheck_modules in src/cli/build_cmds.rs) run on each module's own items, before the flattened program is desugared, so a StmtKind::MultiAssign reached the resolver's unreachable arm. They now run desugar::desugar_multi_assigns first. It rewrites each parallel assignment with expand_multi_assign, the same function the whole-program desugar calls (6e3b08f011 documents why only the walk is separate). tests/package_pipeline_parity.rs runs every desugared form in a package and in a lone file: a binding, element and field swap, a struct spread, user Add and Index[(i64, i64)], a trait default method, an impl Trait argument and a named default. It also covers a swap in another module and one in a test file under karac test.

title: A `for` over an open range `lo..` wraps silently past the type's MAX on JIT, debug and release AOT (`for i in (i64.MAX - 1)..` yields MAX-1, MAX, MIN, MIN+1; `for b in 254u8..` yields 254, 255, 0, 1), and the MIR interpreter dies with `unchecked Add overflowed; the builder must use CheckedBinaryOp`
detail: Repro: `fn main() { let mut n = 0; let mut last: i64 = 0; for i in (i64.MAX - 1).. { n += 1; last = i; if n > 3 { break; } } println(n); println(last); let mut k = 0; for b in 254u8.. { k += 1; println(b); if k > 3 { break; } } }`. karac run, karac build (debug) and karac build --release: `4`, `-9223372036854775807`, `254`, `255`, `0`, `1`, exit 0. karac run --interp: exit 3, `error[mir]: run: in main at bb11[0]: unchecked Add overflowed; the builder must use CheckedBinaryOp`. Expected (Numeric semantics: integer overflow panics; RangeFrom is `[lo, inf)`): a panic of kind overflow, exit 101, once the counter passes MAX; the loop must never produce a value below lo. The iterator path is right: `((i64.MAX - 1)..).take(3).collect()` panics `integer overflow` on every backend, so only the `for` lowering of RangeFrom uses an unchecked step (the interpreter's check names the builder). Bounded ranges at the edges are right on all four lanes: `(i64.MAX - 1)..=i64.MAX` (2), `0u8..=255` (256), `(u64.MAX - 2)..=u64.MAX` (3), `120i8..=i8.MAX` (8), `i64.MIN..=(i64.MIN + 2)` (3).
fix: 479d7a3253. design.md § Ranges (97de1386e2) has `lo..` as `[lo, inf)`: the type's largest value is in the range, and asking for the one after it overflows. The `for` lowering of an open range (range_loop with no end) stepped with an unchecked BinaryOp Add; it now steps with the checked add every other integer `+` uses, after the body, so `for b in 254u8..` runs for 254 and 255 and then panics with overflow (exit 101) on every backend, and the interpreter no longer refuses the loop. RangeFrom.next stepped before giving its value out, which overflowed one value early ((254u8..).next() twice panicked); it now steps on the following call, latched by a new `given` field the range literal starts false (range_value), and `contains` reads the latch. Bounded ranges keep their unchecked step, which cannot overflow (`..` stops below b <= MAX; `..=` steps only below MAX since 9b61847653). Pinned by corpus/core/panic_range_from_overflows_after_the_type_max: i64 and u8, `for`, `take` and `next`; interp, mir-llvm and ASan agree. Gate: 10322 + 10488 passed, 0 failed.

title: In a package, every user operator-trait impl (`impl Add for V`, `impl Index[(i64, i64)] for Grid`, ...) is refused with E0108 `user-defined impl Add for V is not supported in 0.8; operator traits are stdlib-only`; the same file outside a package compiles and runs
fix: 8b95f3e4b1. The package's per-module resolvers never set with_user_operator_impls, which every v2 pipeline sets, so they refused a user operator-trait impl with E0108. Both per-module resolvers (resolve_modules and typecheck_modules, src/cli/build_cmds.rs) now set it. Pinned by tests/package_pipeline_parity.rs: user Add and Index[(i64, i64)] in a one-module package, and an Add impl in one module used by another.

title: Definite assignment ignores diverging paths: `let x: i64; if k > 0 { x = k; } else { return 0; } x` and the same with `panic(..)` in the else or in a match arm are refused `use of uninitialized binding`, and so is a `loop` whose only `break` follows an assignment inside an `if`
detail: design.md §6 Definite assignment: the compiler tracks whether the binding is assigned on every path that READS it; a `loop` body that assigns x on every path before every break makes x assigned after it. Refused by karac check (error[ownership] use of uninitialized binding, help `assign to x before reading it`), all of which run correctly on interp, llvm and ASan: (1) `fn f(k: i64) -> i64 { let x: i64; if k > 0 { x = k; } else { return 0; } x }`; (2) `fn w(k: i64) -> i64 { let x: i64; if k > 0 { x = k; } else { panic("neg"); } x }`; (3) `fn g(k: i64) -> i64 { let x: i64; match k { 0 => { x = 1; } _ => { panic("no"); } } x }`; (4) `let z: i64; let mut i = 0; loop { i += 1; if i == 3 { z = i * 10; break; } } println(z);`. Accepted correctly: both branches assigning, every match arm assigning, a loop whose two breaks each follow an assignment in sequence, and let-else with a diverging else. Refused correctly: one branch assigning, assignment only in while/for, a break before the assignment, field-wise struct and slot-wise array init, uninit capture, compound op on an uninit `let mut`.
fix: c519e4b881. src/ownership/expr_check.rs: an `if` branch or `match` arm that diverges (`return`, `break`, `continue`, or a call typed Never such as `panic`, directly or through a block, `if` or `match` that diverges on every way out) is left out of the definite-assignment join, so the other branch decides; src/ownership.rs apply_loop_break_dominance: a bare `loop`'s break-site states decide post-loop assignment even when the body's fall-through path leaves the binding unassigned, since the code after a `loop` is reached only through its breaks. All four shapes check and print 3/0/4/1/10/30 (pin corpus/design/ok_definite_assignment_skips_diverging_paths, on interp, llvm and ASan); a branch that falls through unassigned, a second break before any assignment, and a break ahead of the assignment are still refused (tests/assert_borrow_and_definite_assignment_check.rs).

title: §6 expressions roll-up: `if c { 5 }` in statement position is accepted; an unparenthesized struct literal in an `if` condition is accepted; `u == ()` is `comparing this type is not lowered yet`; RangeTo/RangeToInclusive/RangeFull are undefined type names; `ambiguous_not_comparison` never runs; a discarded tuple of Results warns nothing (item 8, multi-assign order, is CONFORMANT per the 43518f58d7 decision: values first)
detail: Checked against design.md §6 at 6ae884a05. (1) `let c = true; if c { 5 } println("x");` passes check and prints x; spec: a value-producing if without else is a type error even in statement position (`let x = if c { 5 };` is refused correctly). (2) `if p == Point { x: 0, y: 0 } { .. }` is accepted and runs; spec: a struct literal in an if/while/for head must be parenthesized. (3) `let u: () = (); println(u == ());` is refused `comparing this type is not lowered yet` (also a labeled block of type () compared to ()). (4) `let d: RangeTo[i64] = ..2;` `undefined type RangeTo, did you mean Range`; same for RangeToInclusive; spec's table names six library types (the slice forms v[..n], v[..=n], v[..] work). (5) `not x == y` gives no warning: src/logical_lint.rs check_ambiguous_not_comparison has no caller, though the lint is in `karac lint --list`. (6) `par { ok(1), ok(2) };` and `(r, 1);` with Result elements discard silently; spec §6 says a discarded par tuple of Results warns (a bare discarded Result warns correctly). (7) `0..3..5` is reported as `range bounds must have same type` rather than ranges-do-not-chain. (8) Settled, not a bug: `v[ix(0)], v[ix(2)] = v[ix(2)], v[ix(0)]` evaluates the right-hand values before the target place operands, which the review thread's decision 43518f58d7 makes the rule (values first, then each target's places and write, left to right). Everything else of §6 (176 single-file cells x 4 lanes, 13 package cases) matched: block values, statement-ending block-likes with the parenthesize fix, shadowing and drop order, let mut patterns, all compound ops, parallel swap/rotate/fields/Drop types, if let / else if let / or-patterns, let-else divergence and scrutinee temporary drop points, labels and labeled blocks, loop value typing, ranges at type edges, precedence table, comparison through refs, ??, defer/errdefer, and left-to-right order of fields, f-string parts, receiver/args, index base/index.
fix: a78baaf0dd. Items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 are fixed; item 4 is split to B-2026-11-05-37; item 8 was already conformant (decision 43518f58d7). (1) An `if` without `else` whose block produces a value is refused at check (typechecker/exprs.rs refuse_valued_if_without_else), in statement position and as a `let` initializer alike; three legacy drop fixtures that discarded such a value now pin the refusal (expected_from spec). (2) A struct literal in the head of `if`, `while`, `if let`, `while let` or `for` is a parse error with a machine-applicable fix that adds the parentheses (parser/exprs.rs parse_struct_literal_body_generic). A block expression in a head lifts the rule inside its braces. `karac fmt` keeps the parentheses (formatter in_head). Five test programs and seven corpus programs that had a bare literal in a head are parenthesized with `karac fix`. (3) MIR equality on a unit type is true (mir/lower.rs eq_places), on the interpreter and compiled. (5) ambiguous_not_comparison runs on the compile path (cli/diag_json.rs lint_entries_for_compile_path); it reads operators, so it walks a parse of the program's text taken before lowering rewrites them into calls. It warns on a `not` before the comparison only, as § 6 words it; `x == not y` has one reading and kata 1053 writes it. (6) A discarded tuple holding a Result or Option warns, a `par { .. }` tuple included (must_use_lint.rs). (7) `0..3..5` is "ranges do not chain". Pinned by tests/expressions_s6_rollup.rs (11 tests, one compiled). Gate: test --all 10398 passed, --features llvm 10569 passed, 0 failed.

title: A use of a deprecated item through a module binding (`import util;` then `util.old()`) is warned with the caret on the call's closing paren, not on `old`; `import util.{old};` then `old()` puts it on `old`
detail: Found closing B-2026-11-05-16. Package: src/util.kara `#[deprecated(note: "x")]\npub fn old() -> i64 { 1 }`, src/main.kara `import util;\nfn main() { println(util.old()); }`. `karac check` and `karac build` both print `warning[deprecated]: src/main.kara:2:31` with the caret under the `)` (column 31); the name `old` is at columns 26-28. With `import util.{old};` and `old()` the caret is on `old` (2:21, three carets). A module binding is desugared into an item import before resolution (src/module_binding.rs, B-2026-08-20-17), so the call the typechecker sees is a synthesized `old()` whose callee span likely comes from the whole `util.old()` call or its end; pointer, not a diagnosis. The span is what an editor underlines and what a fix-it would be anchored to.
fix: 244ab1cf33. The deprecated warning was right; the column was lost mapping the package's combined source back to the file. The combined text blanks a module binding's qualifier (`util.old()` reads `     old()`), and `word_map` (src/cli/project_v2.rs), which maps a combined line's columns onto the file's line, read the run of spaces against `util.` as a word and moved every column after it by the qualifier's length, so the header said 2:31 and the caret sat under `)`. A run of spaces the file lacks is now either a blanked qualifier (one space per blanked byte, mapped onto the characters it hid) or a shorter rename's padding (no room in the file), whichever lines the text after it up with the file. Any diagnostic after a module-qualified use on its line was affected, not only deprecated. Fixtures: remap_tests::a_blanked_qualifier_keeps_the_columns_after_it (the case above, a qualifier sharing the member's first letter, a two-byte-letter qualifier, rename padding, a longer rename before a blank) and package_pipeline_parity::a_deprecated_use_through_a_module_binding_points_at_the_name (two `util.old()` uses on one line: 4:18 and 4:31 with carets under each `old`, in check, build and check --output=json).

title: The backend still emits none of the LLVM 19-22 facts B-2026-11-04-83 left: `range` attributes on parameters and returns, `icmp samesign`, and `captures(address/read_provenance)` beyond `captures(none)`
detail: The remainder of B-2026-11-04-83, which landed GEP `nuw` and `trunc nuw/nsw` (e75d97a500, 18fba62c62). Each item is an opportunity, not a bug, and a wrong fact is UB. (1) `range(lo, hi)` on parameters and returns: the MIR knows a range only from a type (char, an enum tag passed by value). Lengths and indices are plain i64/usize, whose type carries no bound, and length loads already carry `!range [0, i64::MAX)` (drop.rs load_len). (4) `icmp samesign`: LLVM 22 InstCombine infers it from known bits. On kata 28's kmp, `opt -O3` marked 3 of 13 icmps samesign from the IR as emitted, so the front end would add it only where it knows signs LLVM cannot see. The bounds check cannot carry it: a negative index cast to usize has the other sign bit. (5) `captures(address)` for pointers that are only compared: no candidate site identified. Measure on the frozen set (scripts/corpus/bench.py against m2-bench/bench-2026-11-05-bd14c35815-llvm22.json, about 2% geomean noise, re-time any mover 3x) before landing any of them. For scale, the GEP nuw facts changed 5 of 502 frozen-set binaries, and every mover over 1.14x vanished when re-timed.
fix: 049261c58f: a by-value function's bool (i8) parameters and return carry `range(i8 0, 2)` (src/backend/mir/mod.rs mark_range_params; `KARAC_MIR_RANGE_ATTR=0` turns it off; tests/mir_bool_range_attr.rs). Measured on the frozen set (707 programs): 50 binaries changed, geomean 0.999. same_tree 0.905/0.914/0.905 and is_symmetric 0.93 over three timings; with KARAC_MIR_ALIGN_BRANCHES=1 they stay at 0.90 to 0.907, and callgrind counts are identical (same_tree 3123770708 both), so the gain is block layout, not fewer instructions. valid_parentheses' 1.10-1.12x vanished aligned (0.988); maximum_swap 1.044 persists at -0.1% instructions. title: package mode: `karac check --output=jsonl` on a package member prints `type_error` lines (no `type` stream, no ids) and stops at typecheck, `karac build --output=jsonl` in a package prints raw batch entries, and package `check --output=json` has no ids or `program_effects` (design.md §17; remainder of B-2026-11-05-13)
detail: Remainder of B-2026-11-05-13, whose single-file fix (984142c99a) streams §17 events from `run_pipeline_jsonl`. A package takes two other paths. (1) `karac check --output=jsonl src/main.kara` in a package goes through `cmd_check_package_member` (src/cli/run_check_cmds.rs), the module-aware front, which prints `parse_errors_jsonl` / `cycles_jsonl` / `resolve_errors_jsonl` / `type_errors_jsonl` lines (`{"type":"type_error",...}`), no build_start, phase events or build_complete, and exits at a type error, so the ownership error of `import util; fn main() { let s = String.from("a"); let t = s; println(s); let x: i64 = "q"; util.hi(); }` never appears. Its `--output=json` is `{"diagnostics":[...]}` with entries that carry no `id` or `primary` and no `program_effects` key. (2) `karac build --output=jsonl` in a package reaches `check_v2_or_exit`'s `(Jsonl, Some(a))` arm (src/cli/run_v2.rs), which prints each batch entry, remapped to the package's files, with no `type` field and no phase events. Spec: the stream is one shape for every build, a superset of the batch document, and the batch document carries `program_effects` (null when not reached). Likely shape: give `JsonlStream` a remap hook so the amalgam pipeline streams through `run_all_checks_observed`, and route the package-member check's phases through the same events.
fix: 532e17a65b. (1) `karac check --output=json|jsonl` on a package member now checks the package's combined source as `karac build` does (check_package_machine, src/cli/run_check_cmds.rs), so every phase runs: the row's program reports its type error, the util module's undeclared effect and the ownership error, each naming its file. The text report stays scoped to the named file. (2) `karac build|run --output=jsonl` in a package streams through run_pipeline_jsonl_remapped (JsonlStream remaps each entry, build_start lists the package's files), and `--output=json` is the full batch document (emit_json_output_remapped: ids, program_effects, public_function_effects, cascade cap). (3) A refusal only the module boundaries carry (parse error, cycle, refused import) and project-mode `karac check` render through emit_found_entries: ids and `primary` in phase order, the stream's phase events with the phases after an error skipped and blocking ids, and program_effects when the combined check ran (null otherwise). tests/package_jsonl_stream.rs pins member, build, refusal, clean member and project-mode reports, each stream's diagnostics equal to the batch document's. Platform/target sweeps keep their per-run shapes. Gate before the rebase onto 792981e84a: fmt, both clippy legs, cargo test --all 10356 passed, --features llvm 10524 passed, 0 failed; the rebase conflicted with Thread A's cascade cap in emit_json_output, resolved to cap the remapped document too, and the affected suites (cli 552, run_v2, build_v2, lint_and_explain_edges_check, jsonl_stream_and_closed_stdout_check, package_jsonl_stream) and non-llvm clippy re-ran green on the merged tree.

title: x86, host-dependent: min_stack (155) ran about 3.5x slower on LLVM 22 than on LLVM 18 because a four-case switch with an unreachable default became a jump table, fixed by a jump-table floor of 5; hsearch (275), 2x on a Cascade Lake host on 11-05, is at parity at HEAD on an Emerald Rapids host (its unfolded bounds check is B-2026-11-10-37); the M5 read 0.904x and 1.056x legacy
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-05 on the 4-core x86 cloud container, best of 5, outputs equal: main at ce0cf3209b (LLVM 22.1.8, with the dereferenceable `ref T` parameters that fixed teemo) against c420c96612 (the last LLVM 18 commit): min_stack 951 ms vs 444, hsearch 1074 vs 526. The dereferenceable parameters change neither (953 and 1097 without them). HSEARCH: `h_index_prefix`'s binary search inlined into main. LLVM 18 emits a `jge` branch for `if citations[mid] >= n - mid { hi = mid } else { lo = mid + 1 }` and no bounds check on `citations[mid]` (the midpoint assume of B-2026-10-28-41 folds it); LLVM 22 emits two cmovs (cmovge/cmovl) and keeps the bounds check (`cmp $0x3ffff; ja`). On a 2 MiB array the branch wins: the predicted path lets the next load start early, which the cmov's data dependence forbids. Running karac's pipeline under opt with drop-unnecessary-assumes removed changes neither the cmovs nor the check, so the assume is lost or unused elsewhere. MIN_STACK: the reverse, LLVM 18's main has 4 cmovs and LLVM 22's none; not yet attributed. Next step: diff each version's post-pass IR (KARAC_MIR_CARRY_STORE=report KARAC_MIR_OPT_LL) on the hot loop, as for teemo, then find which pass decides. scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh carries both under this id. ATTRIBUTED 2026-11-05 (later): MIN_STACK is the post-pass IR, not llc: llc-22 on LLVM 18's post-pass IR runs 469 ms, llc-18 or llc-22 on LLVM 22's 916/912 ms (assembled and linked by hand against libkarac_runtime_min.a). The IR differs in one place that matters: LLVM 22 proves `op = (state / 1024) % 4` is in [0, 3] (it drops the `& 2147483647` mask as known), so the `if op == 0 ... else if op == 1 ... else if op == 2 ... else` chain becomes a four-case switch with an unreachable default, which x86 lowers to a jump table (one indirect jump on random data); LLVM 18 kept three cases and a default, lowered to compares. -min-jump-table-entries=5 removes the jump table but gives 800 ms, so the compare tree LLVM 22 then builds is still slower than 18's chain. HSEARCH: LLVM 22 puts nsw on the midpoint's `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` (its checked add proven not to overflow), and instcombine then rewrites karac's `assume(mid >= lo)` to `assume(hi - lo > -2)`, which says nothing about `mid`. LLVM 18 kept `mid >= lo`, and its IPSCCP (the pass that removes the check, found with -print-after-all) derived mid in [0, 262143] from it and folded `citations[mid]`'s bounds check. With the check gone the loop is one block and x86's cmov converter turns the two selects into the branch that wins here. Tried by hand on LLVM 22: freezing mid folds the check but leaves the checked add's overflow branch; adding assume(lo >= 0) or assume(mid >= 0) does not fold it. M5 2026-11-05 (Gowtham's run at 7c63217740, Darwin arm64, 5 runs, vs legacy, relayed by the review thread): min_stack cycles 0.904x (instructions 0.787x), hsearch cycles 1.056x (instructions 1.173x), both within the 1.15x bar with the same sinks. Kept OPEN for x86 Linux, a release target where the 2x stands; both causes are LLVM 22 choices (the switch's jump table, instcombine weakening the midpoint assume) with no karac-side cure found yet.
fix: 787f0559a5 sets LLVM's -min-jump-table-entries to 5, GCC's x86 floor, in the AOT pipeline's options (src/backend/mir_aot.rs; KARAC_MIR_JUMP_TABLE_MIN=<n> sets another). MEASURED 2026-11-10 on a second x86 host (4-core cloud container, Intel family 6 model 207, Emerald Rapids; the row's host was Cascade Lake), best of 7 to 11, outputs equal, against the last LLVM 18 karac (c420c96612, built here against Ubuntu's LLVM 18.1.3) as the control. MIN_STACK: the four-case switch with an unreachable default was still a jump table at HEAD, 666 to 726 ms against LLVM 18's 180 to 199 and legacy's 184 to 233; llc on HEAD's own post-pass IR with the switch rewritten as compares ran 264 to 275 ms; with the floor at 5, 200 to 248 ms. Rust (rustc on LLVM 22.1.6, -O, overflow checks) runs it in 705 ms, so the jump table is LLVM 22's choice for every front end. HSEARCH: at parity on this host at HEAD, 277 to 323 ms against LLVM 18's 316 to 359 (legacy 413, clang-18 C 386). Its loop no longer has the two cmovs the row describes: HEAD branches (jge) and keeps the bounds check (cmp $0x3ffff; ja), a predictable branch. The binary is identical at floors 4 and 5. Cascade Lake was not re-measured; the unfolded check is filed as B-2026-11-10-37. A/B over the 707 frozen-set programs on this host (floor 4 against 5, min of 5 interleaved, the outliers re-timed at 15): 580 build byte-identical, 127 differ with equal output, 0.979x geomean, best 0.38x (155), then 0.72x (28 brute force), 0.82x (270, 126); worst 1.11x (394), 1.10x (6), 1.09x (224), 1.08x (228, 340), where a jump table over predictable text beat the compares. aarch64 keeps its own floor: min_stack's aarch64-apple-darwin object is byte-identical at 4 and 5, so the M5 rows do not move. Pinned by tests/mir_jump_table_floor.rs, which builds the dispatch at the default and at 4, requires the same output, no indirect jump in main by default, and one at 4.

title: diagnostics carry no `concept` id, and `karac explain` knows no concept ids from the diagnostic taxonomy (`ownership/move-semantics`) and no items (`karac explain a.kara.top`) (design.md §17 rule 4, `karac explain`)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-05-17 items (1) and (8). design.md §17's batch example gives every error and warning a `"concept": "ownership/move-semantics"` / `"effects/public-function-declaration"`; no diagnostic carries the field. `karac explain ownership/move-semantics` is unknown (the supported concepts are closures, operators, module-state, stable-hash), and `karac explain <file>.<item>` (the spec: the item's inferred effect set with its derivation, and the would-be parameter mode beside the declared one) is unknown. Needs a concept taxonomy keyed from codes/classes (src/cli/explain.rs CODE_TABLE is the natural home), the field in DiagnosticJson::add, and the item target in explain.
fix: 7966b30c9e and 91ba688886. (1) Concept ids: `explain::concept_for(phase, code, class, lint)` gives every diagnostic a concept from design.md's concept table: the code's catalogue row (the compiler's own error kind, finest key: E0516 is classed a type mismatch but is a borrow conflict), else the class, else the phase, so none goes without one. DiagnosticJson::add writes `concept` after `category`; the package check's resolve/type/late-phase/parse/cycle records and the manifest, walker, dependency, toolchain-pin, lockfile, cache, update, MIR-build and monomorphization-budget records carry it too. The table grew from the spec's two ids to 45, each against the sections that specify it (the retired and deferred rows stay). `karac explain <concept-id>` names the sections (doc#anchor) and the codes that carry the id, --format=json likewise; `karac explain <code>` names the code's concept. (2) Items: `karac explain a.kara.top` (a method `a.kara.Type.method`) reports each effect with its derivation, the `with` clause and each parameter's declared mode beside the weakest mode the body needs. The derivation is `effect_graph::derivation(effects, function, effect, file) -> Vec<DerivationStep>` (+ derivation_json), following TracedEffect.origin call by call, each step at the call's line; a library callee closes the chain on its call; a function with a `with` clause ends at the clause, which the checker trusts (its set is seeded from the declaration). Thread A reuses it for E0400 / query effects (B-2026-11-05-29). Fixtures: explain::tests::concept_ids_match_the_design_table (table == CONCEPT_IDS, every heading resolves), every_catalogued_code_has_a_concept, tests/concept_ids.rs (batch + stream for five diagnostics, a package's, explain for every id), tests/explain_item.rs (chain, declared clause, would-be modes, method, errors).

title: E0400 carries no `derivation`, `inferred_effects` or `declared_effects` and `karac fix` cannot add the missing clause; a match missing an arm is not fixable either; `karac query effects` / `query ownership` answer with no `derivation` (design.md §17 rule 5, Structured compiler output, Compiler query API)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-05-17 items (3) and (7). For `fn inner() { println("x"); } fn mid() { inner(); } pub fn top() { mid(); }` the E0400 record has message/class only: no derivation chain (top calls mid, mid calls inner, inner has writes(Stdout)), no inferred_effects/declared_effects, no hint, and `karac fix` says "no fixable diagnostics" though the message names the clause to add. A non-exhaustive match has no machine-applicable arm insertion. §17 names effect annotations and missing pattern arms as the routine mechanical fixes. `karac query effects f.kara.top` and `query ownership` answer without the `derivation` chain the Compiler query API requires of every answer, and `karac query queries` with no target is a usage error.
fix: 49c047aa9a. E0400's JSON record carries `inferred_effects`, `declared_effects` (`[]` with no clause) and a `derivation`, the call chain of each undeclared effect from Thread C's effect_graph::derivation (design.md §17 rule 5). Its fix appends the effects to the `with` clause, or writes the clause after the return type, before the body. The fix is one edit per function, sorted, attached to that function's first E0400, so `karac fix` resolves the row's `top` / `mid` / `inner` program. There is no edit for `main` (its fix is to drop `pub`), for an `Fn` return type, or for a library function. A non-exhaustive match on an enum, a bool or a tuple of them, borrowed parts included, gets one edit with every missing arm: exhaustive::missing_match_witnesses adds each witness as a row until the arms are total. Before, an enum got one arm per run and a bool got none. `karac query effects` answers with the derivation of each inferred effect. `query ownership` answers with why each parameter has its body-level mode (the ownership pass records the statement that first moved or wrote it) and why each counted binding is counted. `karac query queries` with no target reports the package in the current directory (src/main.kara, or src/lib.kara), and outside a package it says so. Pinned by tests/derivation_and_fixes.rs (5 tests). Gate 180 was green: 10436 + 10611 passed, 0 failed. The fix found B-2026-11-06-5: the query pipeline is built without the library, so a program using `WsMessage` fails every query kind though `karac check` passes it.

title: fix hints have two shapes, neither the spec's `diff {file, line, old, new}`: single-file JSON gives `replacement {offset, length, text}` beside a prose hint, package JSON `fix_it` and `fixes[].edits[]` (design.md §17 Structured compiler output)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-05-17 item (4). The spec's hint is `{"description": ..., "diff": {"file", "line", "old", "new"}}`. `karac check --output=json` on one file emits `replacement`/`fix_diff` (offset-based) next to `hints[].description`; the package path emits `fix_it` and `fixes[].edits[]`. `karac fix` reads the offset forms, so a migration needs both readers or a shared emitter. The package JSON's missing ids and `program_effects` are B-2026-11-05-26.
fix: 7449bc90ba and 90d3c8b4b2. Every machine-applicable fix in JSON output (file and package, json and jsonl, every phase) now carries a hint whose diff is {file, line, old, new} over the source lines the fix touches, one diff per fix, built by a post-pass (src/cli/diag_json.rs add_hint_diffs) from the record's own edits. The edits keep one shape on every path: replacement {offset, length, text} for one edit, fix_diff [...] for several. The type checker's duplicate fix_it object and fixes array are dropped, and the editor bridge (src/cli/editor.rs fixes_of) no longer falls back to them; kara-lsp and the VS Code extension read neither. In a package the diff is re-derived from the diagnostic's own file after the remap (90d3c8b4b2), so a line with a module-qualified call shows its qualifier; a fix with an edit in another module gets no diff. CHANGELOG 0.8.1 Changed notes the drop; design.md 17 'One fix shape' states the rule. Pinned by tests/fix_hint_shape.rs (one edit, several edits, package, qualified call) and the diag_json unit tests.

title: `karac fix` has none of the five style lints (counter `while` to `for`, `x = x + e` to `+=`, a final `return e;` to `e`, a redundant `.iter()` / `.to_string()` on a literal, a redundant `ref` on a parameter), and `karac lint --list` lists none of them (design.md §17 `karac fix`, Lint levels)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-05-17 item (5). design.md § `karac fix` and `karac explain` lists five style lints, each with a machine-applicable fix, and § Lint levels says the registry includes them. None fires on the shapes named and none is in the registry (src/lints.rs STARTER_LINTS).
fix: 2f7442d85a adds the five lints in src/style_lints.rs: counter_while_loop, manual_compound_assign, needless_return, redundant_literal_method and redundant_ref_param, each with a machine-applicable fix that `karac fix` applies. They are `allow` in check, build and run, and on in `karac fix`. `-W NAME` or `#[warn(NAME)]` reports them anywhere (W0295 or E0295, with a `fix_diff`), and `#[expect]`, `-D` and `-F` follow the lint-level rules. They stay silent on a program with its own type errors. Each rewrite holds only where the meaning provably does not change. The `while` becomes a `for` only when the counter is local, an unannotated integer, stepped once at the end with no `continue`, unused after the loop, and the bound is invariant. `+=` only on numeric or String `+`. A `return` is dropped only before a value that does not start with a block. `.iter()` is dropped only when the body does not deref the item. `ref` is kept on function-typed parameters, deref'd parameters, destructured parameters, trait impls and functions used as values. Verified by tests/style_lints_check.rs (8 tests), and by a corpus sweep that applied only these edits to every corpus program and compared `run --interp` output before and after. The remaining differences were the pre-existing B-2026-11-05-38 crash and timeouts under load. The sweep found B-2026-11-05-39 and -40, the reasons `ref` stays on function-typed and destructured parameters.

title: `karac fmt` does not sort methods (an impl's `zeta` stays before `alpha`; imports are sorted) (design.md § Canonical formatting: methods sorted, imports sorted)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-05-17 item (12). § Canonical formatting says declarations are canonicalized, methods sorted and imports sorted. Imports are; methods are left in source order. Sorting moves doc comments and attributes with each method and reorders every existing kata on its next format, so it wants a decision on the order (alphabetical, or by kind then name) before the change.
fix: a81fc12853: `karac fmt` prints each `impl` and `trait` body in canonical order, as Gowtham ruled (option b; spec f8410beba3, design.md § Canonical formatting). Associated types come first, then functions without `self` (constructors such as `new`), then methods, each group alphabetical. Doc comments, comments and attributes travel with their item. A comment after the body, or at the end of a line inside a method, stays where it was. Pinned by tests/fmt_member_order.rs (4 tests), and the pin in tests/fmt_comments.rs is flipped. Against the previous formatter, over all 6561 corpus, stdlib, example and kata programs with an impl or trait, the output has the same lines and is a fixed point. The reformat is its own commit, 7b2867f02e: kata 716's corpus copy and three stdlib files, the only in-repo programs that were already fmt-clean and change under the new order. kara-katas fd13633d has the same change for kata 716.

title: The v2 backends emit none of the debugger contract's runtime metadata (design.md § Debugger contract, elements 1-3): no spawn-site ids per `par {}` block, no parent-frame reference per worker, no await-chain `WaitTarget`; so `std.runtime.has_debug_metadata()` is false even in a dev build and both lists are always empty
detail: Found closing B-2026-11-05-18, which made `std.runtime` importable (fe1f97379f). Its three functions reach `Runtime.has_debug_metadata` / `list_par_blocks` / `list_tasks`, which return false / empty on interp, JIT and build: the legacy codegen's `KARAC_SPAWN_SITES*` tables (record_spawn_site) and `KaracFrame` chain were not carried to the MIR backend, and karac_jit_runner's publish_spawn_sites finds no such symbols. The spec has the metadata on by default in `[profile.dev]`; an empty answer is the contract's degraded mode, not the dev default. Repro: `import std.runtime;\nfn main() { let (a, b) = par { 1, 2 }; println(runtime.has_debug_metadata()); println(a + b); }` prints false under run and build. Also not producible today, so not yet exercised by the panic record: the `borrow_conflict`, `alloc_failure` and `deadlock` kinds (no v2 path raises those panics).
fix: FIXED by 12215de11b (pins repinned e03db5523a). A compiled dev build now carries elements 1-3 and the two lists of element 4. `TaskGroup.new` for a `par` block passes its place and branch count to `karac_mir_group_new_at` (src/backend/mir/mod.rs par_group_sites, cells.rs); a coroutine spawn passes its place to `karac_mir_task_spawn_at` (task.rs). The runtime (runtime/src/mir_task.rs) keeps the site on the group or task: `list_par_blocks()` returns each live block with its FNV-1a spawn-site id, file:line:col, worker count and the parent task; `list_tasks()` returns each suspended task with its id, parent, place and `WaitTarget` (Running, PeerTask, IoHandle(fd), Sleep). `has_debug_metadata()` is true in a dev build. `karac build --release` sets KARAC_STRIP_DEBUG_METADATA, so the release answer is false with both lists empty (the contract's degraded mode). The backend checks the library's row layout (runtime/stdlib/runtime.kara) against the runtime's before the call. The interpreter keeps the degraded answer. Pins: tests/mir_debug_metadata.rs (dev and release, both lists), corpus/fixtures/codegen/enums/wait_target_matches_every_variant, corpus/fixtures/codegen/attrs_ir/test_has_debug_metadata_returns_true_when_gate_on (1 on mir-llvm), the interpreter pins now mir-interp only. Repro from the row prints true under build and run. Left for B-2026-11-05-36: the kara.toml key, each worker's file:line, the effect summary, and the peer task's id in WaitTarget.PeerTask.

title: x86 host-dependent: a jump across a 32-byte line costs kata 661 1.5x on one Cascade Lake host and nothing on another; aligning branches is 0.914x geomean there and loses kata 207 2.3x here, so it is opt-in (KARAC_MIR_ALIGN_BRANCHES=1); the over-2x list was a cross-host artifact
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-05 on the 4-core x86 cloud container (Intel Xeon @ 2.80GHz, family 6 model 85 with avx512_vnni: Cascade Lake). (1) The 33 frozen-set benches over 2x legacy in m2-bench/bench-2026-11-05-bd14c35815-llvm22.json compare today's mir times with legacy times copied from the 10-29 baseline, taken on another host. Head to head on one machine (legacy dd86e3955a vs main 2281e06f53, min of 9): only hsearch is over 2x (2.02x, B-2026-11-05-27), then min_stack 1.97x (-27), image_smoother 1.81x, bst_iterator 1.59x, is_symmetric 1.51x; the rest of the 40 under 1.5x. (2) image_smoother (661): its pixel loop's checked add has a 6-byte jo crossing a 32-byte line (0x2e1d..0x2e23), Intel erratum SKX102, whose microcode fix stops caching the decoded uops of such a line. Removing either overflow check in the post-pass IR, or assembling the same IR with -x86-align-branch-boundary=32 -x86-align-branch=fused+jcc+jmp, took 0.49 s to 0.32 s (legacy 0.29). Hoisting the row pointer load bought nothing. (3) A/B over the 707 frozen-set programs, same karac, alignment off vs on, interleaved, min of 3: nop padding 0.914x run geomean, 226 programs 10%+ faster (277 celebrity 0.52, 343 integer_break 0.55, 322 coin_change 0.57), size +0.05%. (4) About an hour later the same unaligned 661 binary ran 0.27 s (it had run 0.48), and a second A/B with clang's exact setting (-x86-branches-within-32B-boundaries, prefix padding) gave 0.985x geomean, 72 faster and 33 slower by 10%+: kata 207 course_schedule 0.19 s off vs 0.43-0.46 s on, with both nop and prefix padding, re-timed 3x; its queue loop is the same instructions shifted by 0x90 with one nop. The container's behaviour changed under us (the VM reports microcode 0x1, so the host's is unknowable from inside), which also means x86 timings taken at different hours are not comparable. So alignment is a host lottery, kept OPT-IN as KARAC_MIR_ALIGN_BRANCHES=1 (src/backend/mir_aot.rs, tests/mir_branch_align.rs checks every jump of a compiled program and that without the knob some jump crosses). Open for: a remedy that does not depend on the host (e.g. aligning only jcc in hot loops, or per --target-cpu), and for anyone measuring x86 perf: re-time the control in the same minute.

title: `(0..n).step_by(2).rev()` is "no method 'rev' on type 'IterStepBy'": Rust's `StepBy` walks back over a range, Kāra's has no `next_back` and the diagnostic names no other way
detail: Found by kata 1054's mutation testing (an iter-arm edit taking the even places from the back). `let back: Vec[i64] = (0..7).step_by(2).rev().collect();` is refused by `karac check` with E0236 "no method 'rev' on type 'IterStepBy'" and no fix. Rust accepts it (`StepBy<I>` is `DoubleEndedIterator` when `I: DoubleEndedIterator + ExactSizeIterator`, ranges among them) and prints [6, 4, 2, 0]. In runtime/stdlib/source/iter.kara `IterStepBy[I]` implements only `Iterator`; walking back needs the number of items left, which Kāra's iterators do not expose generically. Either a `DoubleEndedIterator` impl for a step over a range (the length is `(end - start)`), or the diagnostic pointing at `(0..n).rev()` with a computed start, would close it.
fix: 9ad19508aa. IterStepBy implemented only Iterator, so .rev() and .next_back() were refused (E0236 no method 'rev' on type 'IterStepBy'). runtime/stdlib/source/range.kara: IterStepBy[I] is now a DoubleEndedIterator when I: StepBack, a private trait Range[T] and RangeInclusive[T] implement. Each takes the last value the step reaches (a new RangeStep.last_step_within, one per integer type) and shrinks its end past it, so both ends of one step meet in the middle as Rust's StepBy does: (0..7).step_by(2).rev() is [6, 4, 2, 0]. StepBack stands in for two direct impls, which the coherence check refuses although their headers do not unify; that false positive is B-2026-11-06-6, and StepBack is to be replaced once it is fixed. docs/library/iterators.md lists a step over an integer range among the DoubleEndedIterators. Pinned by corpus/design/ok_step_by_over_a_range_walks_back (exclusive, inclusive, negative, u8 to 255, i128, empty, alternating ends, a step already started) on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan.

title: The v2 debugger metadata lacks two pieces of the contract: `list_tasks()` rows carry no effect summary, and `WaitTarget.PeerTask` does not name the task waited on (the kara.toml key and per-worker file:line landed at 0652164cf8)
detail: B-2026-11-05-34 (12215de11b) gave compiled dev builds the spawn-site ids, parent task, place and WaitTarget, stripped by `--release`. design.md § Debugger contract also asks for: (1) `runtime_debug_metadata = true|false` in `[profile.dev]` / `[profile.release]` (design.md § Build profiles); src/manifest.rs refuses it as an unknown key (its test at the `unknown key `[profile.dev].runtime_debug_metadata`` assertion), so the only switch is `--release` or KARAC_STRIP_DEBUG_METADATA=1; (2) each worker's `file:line` in a `list_par_blocks()` row (today the row has the block's place and worker count only); (3) the effect summary of each `list_tasks()` row; (4) element 3's pointer to the peer task (`WaitTarget.PeerTask` carries no id; Wait::Task in runtime/src/mir_task.rs knows it). The MIR interpreter answers the degraded mode (false, empty), which the contract allows. UPDATE 2026-11-06: 0652164cf8 landed (1) the `runtime_debug_metadata` key in both profiles (src/manifest.rs parse_debug_metadata_keys, src/cli/build_v2.rs) and (2) `ParBlockInfo.worker_locations`, each branch's file:line, found through the closure each branch runs (src/backend/mir/mod.rs branch_closure), pinned by tests/mir_debug_metadata.rs. Left: (3) the effect summary, which runtime/stdlib/runtime.kara puts after v1 because effect sets are not values yet; (4) the peer task's id: the runtime does not know it, since codegen works out a join's readiness and passes only a flag (karac_mir_ready), so the backend would have to pass the joined handle's task id; a channel wait has no single peer and a mutex wait's holder is in HELD.
fix: FIXED by 7241c6d35a (with 0652164cf8). 0652164cf8: kara.toml's `runtime_debug_metadata = true|false` in `[profile.dev]` and `[profile.release]` overrides the default (on in dev, off in release; src/manifest.rs parse_debug_metadata_keys, src/cli/build_v2.rs), and `ParBlockInfo.worker_locations` lists each branch's `file:line`, found through the closure each branch runs (src/backend/mir/mod.rs branch_closure). 7241c6d35a: a join's readiness goes through `karac_mir_ready_join`, which keeps the joined task's result block in `Wait::Task`, and `list_tasks()` maps it to that task's id, so `WaitTarget.PeerTask(task_id)` names the task waited on (0 for a channel, lock or pool, or a joined task that is running); the variant took its payload before any release carried the unit form. Pins: tests/mir_debug_metadata.rs (three tests: blocks with worker lines, tasks with a join naming task 4, both kara.toml overrides), corpus/fixtures/codegen/enums/wait_target_matches_every_variant. The task listing was the same over 50 runs, 20 of them at KARAC_THREADS=4. Not done here: the effect summary per `list_tasks()` row, which runtime/stdlib/runtime.kara puts after v1 (effect sets are not values yet) and docs/deferred.md § Debugger Contract Extension for Parked Tasks already carries as part of element 4.

title: `RangeTo[T]`, `RangeToInclusive[T]` and `RangeFull` are undefined type names, and `..2`, `..=2` and `..` as values are `the expression kind Range is not lowered yet` (design.md §6 range table; the slice forms `v[..n]`, `v[..=n]`, `v[..]` work)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-05-23 item (4). design.md §6's range table names six library types, and says all six implement a common `SliceIndex[T]` contract. The library (runtime/stdlib/source/range.kara) defines Range, RangeInclusive and RangeFrom only. `let d: RangeTo[i64] = ..2;` is `undefined type RangeTo, did you mean Range`, and the same for RangeToInclusive and RangeFull. Without an annotation, `let d = ..2;` (and `..=2`, `..`) passes the typechecker and is refused at MIR lowering with `the expression kind Range is not lowered yet`. Only the index position works today, through a special case in lowering. The fix needs the three library types (with `contains` for the bounded two), the value lowering for an open-start range, and the SliceIndex contract the spec names; that is a library plus MIR change, larger than the roll-up's other items. Measured at the roll-up's fix commit's parent with `karac check` on the debug build.
fix: 28d010faad. runtime/stdlib/source/range.kara defines RangeTo[T] and RangeToInclusive[T] (an `end` field and `contains`) and RangeFull, all Copy, none an iterator (design.md § 6: only the forms with a start iterate; `for x in ..3` is refused as not iterable). MIR lowers an open-start range value to its bounds (mir/lower.rs range_value). Indexing by a stored range: a Vec, array or slice indexed by a stored `..=n` ends after `n` (slice_view_by read only RangeInclusive as inclusive), and a string is sliced by a stored range of any form (string_range_by; `let r = 1..3; s[r]` was also not lowered). A range of bare integer literals takes its element type from an annotated range type in check mode, so `let r: RangeInclusive[u8] = 1..=200;` is accepted where it was refused as an i64 range. The spec's "common SliceIndex[T] contract" is met as behaviour: every sequence that takes `items[Range]` takes the other five forms, written in the brackets or held in a binding; no nameable SliceIndex trait exists, and none is named anywhere else in the spec. Pinned by corpus/design/ok_open_start_ranges (interpreter, mir-llvm and ASan lanes; karac run == karac build) and err_open_start_range_is_not_iterated. Gate: test --all 10403 passed, --features llvm 10576 passed, 0 failed (4 TSan tests passed after rebuilding a stale TSan archive).

d70e6d474a lowers an integer `cmp` as one three-way compare (`(x > y) - (x < y)` as an i8, llvm.scmp, then one switch) instead of two branches, so the two-key sort_by comparator inlined into the sort's fused partition loop no longer branches on the less test. x86: 0.70 s -> 0.53 s (rustc -O 0.52 s). M5 (review thread's m5-rows run at 4471044a8a, 5 runs): 757.1M cycles against legacy's 793.9M, 0.954x, at 0.824x the instructions, so the legacy half is closed. The arm64 gap to rustc -O (1.360x cycles) remains and is filed as B-2026-11-06-8. Kata 642 builds differently under the fix and reads 4% slower by the clock on x86; its hot function does identical instructions and branches and moved 0x50 bytes, which is layout: do not re-file it from a frozen-set pass.
title: Kata 354 runs 0.81x legacy's instructions but 1.46x its cycles on the MIR backend; FIXED d70e6d474a (integer cmp as one scmp): M5 0.954x legacy's cycles; the arm64 gap to rustc -O (1.36x) is B-2026-11-06-8
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-06 on the M5 Pro, karac 0.8.0-dev.14606+g162ee7a0e vs legacy dd86e3955, bench/russian_doll.kara, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, exact counts via scripts/pmc.c (3-run minima): 1.902G vs 2.340G instructions, 1158M vs 794M cycles, so the loss is in IPC, not instruction count. First M5 run: 2.05x rustc -O, 2.04x rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on, 0.73x clang -O3 (qsort) and 0.11x Go. The kernel is `order.sort_by(|a, b| ...)` on (width, height) pairs with a two-key comparator, then a patience-sorting LIS with binary search. Compare B-2026-11-01-22 (kata 116) and B-2026-11-01-42 (kata 147), the earlier IPC-loss rows. Not attributed. UPDATE 2026-11-06 (Thread B, x86 container): callgrind branch-sim put the loss in mispredicts, 55.2M vs rustc's 28.1M: the sort's fused partition loop (33.7M vs 5.9M) and the LIS binary search (17.2M, x86's cmov converter turning a select back into a branch). Cause of the sort half: lower.rs scalar_cmp built an integer `cmp` as two MIR branches, so the inlined two-key comparator stayed branchy. d70e6d474a computes `(x > y) - (x < y)` as an i8 (llvm.scmp) and switches once: kata 354 0.70s -> 0.53s on x86 (rustc -O 0.52s, interleaved, same hour), and the apple-m4 llc output of the fused loop now takes the less test with csel; the remaining branch is the user's own `a.0 != b.0`. Frozen set: 2 of 707 programs build differently, 354 1.31x faster and 642 4% slower by the clock, which is layout (its hot function does identical instructions and branches, moved 0x50 bytes): do not re-file 642 from it. A global `-x86-cmov-converter=false` was measured and rejected (frozen-set geomean 1.029, kata 540 2.8x slower). Left open for the M5 re-run (scripts/bench/m5-rows.sh), which decides the close.

fix: 8f6325386f and f5ddd049b4. Two roots kept std's panic hook and backtrace symbolizer in a binary that prints a float or formats a hole with a spec. First, core's float formatting (Grisu, Dragon, the even-tie rule's parse), format! and Vec<char> in the spec parser, and the spec cache's thread-local destructor: src/float_text.rs (Ryu shortest digits, exact half-even fixed places) now writes every float the interpreter and the runtime print, checked against core on all 2^32 f32s, 200M f64s and 20M fixed cases (8f6325386f). Second, on Mach-O only: the u128 digit loop's __udivti3, whose unwind entry names rust_eh_personality, which ld64 -dead_strip keeps live; write_magnitude now divides 32 bits at a time (f5ddd049b4). Linux: 379,088 -> 100,640 B. M5 re-run (Gowtham, kara 6e709e5fdd, Darwin arm64): kata 346 83 KiB vs 328 KiB before, 0.253x, within the seqfix 0.5 bar. Pinned on Linux by tests/mir_panic_free_natives.rs mir_float_printing_and_format_specs_link_no_panic_hook; the Darwin half is pinned only by m5-rows.sh's row.
title: Kata 346's seq binary is 336,240 B on g162ee7a0e, after 5984ed3080 and e8466b1435 took the seven B-2026-11-04-31 katas to 83-99 KB
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-06 on the M5 Pro, karac 0.8.0-dev.14606+g162ee7a0e, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 build of bench/moving_average.kara: 336,240 B. Same compiler, same day: 297 85,064 B, 315 85,168, 332 85,304, 394 85,056 (all fixed by B-2026-11-04-31), and the other 24 katas of this batch 68,496-101,840 B (349 101,840 and 350 101,800 are a size class between). The kernel computes a moving average with f64 division and prints an f64 sink (`291716447.836`), so float formatting is the first suspect for the root that still links std's panic and backtrace machinery. Not attributed. ATTRIBUTED AND FIXED ON LINUX 2026-11-06 (8f6325386f): every program that printed a float or formatted a hole with any spec ({x:.3}, {n:>5}) kept std's panic hook: core's float formatting (Grisu/Dragon asserts and indexing), the parse the even-tie rule read back with, format! and Vec<char> in FormatSpec::parse, and the spec cache's thread-local destructor registration. src/float_text.rs (Ryu shortest digits, exact half-even fixed places) replaces them, shared by interpreter and runtime; checked against core on all 2^32 f32s, 200M f64s and 20M fixed cases. Linux, same output: 346 379,088 -> 100,640 B; a bare float print 358,160 -> 83,848; {12:>5} 374,744 -> 96,304. Open until the M5 re-run (m5-rows.sh row B-2026-11-06-2, seqfix:336240). M5 RE-RUN 2026-11-06 (Gowtham, kara a3df76e55c): 296 KiB vs 328 KiB, 0.902x, OVER the 0.5 bar. Darwin cause (f5ddd049b4): spec formatting's u128 digit loop called compiler_builtins' __udivti3, whose EH frame names rust_eh_personality; ld64 -dead_strip keeps what a live function's unwind entry references, so std's panic handler and symbolizer stayed. Reproduced with a cross link through ld64.lld (__TEXT 294,912 B; -why_live chain _main -> karac_mir_fmt_spec -> write_magnitude -> __udivti3 -> EH frame -> rust_eh_personality -> panic_fmt). Dividing 32 bits at a time: cross-linked __TEXT 49,152 B, no panic_fmt. Open until the next M5 run.

title: A Rust `Vec<usize>` element type, once `karac fix` spells it `Vec[Vec[usize]]`, draws four `i64`/`usize` coercion and comparison errors with no fix; the fix is to write `i64` (design.md §5: `usize` is for FFI)
detail: Found by kata 1055's binary-search arm, written the way Rust writes it: `let mut places: Vec<Vec<usize>> = vec![Vec::new(); 26]; for (i, c) in source.bytes().enumerate() { places[..].push(i); }` and then `list.partition_point(|&p| p < pos)`, `pos = list[k] + 1`. `karac fix` rewrites the spelling to `Vec[Vec[usize]]` and stops. `karac check` then reports, with no fix: 'implicit coercion from 'i64' to 'usize' would narrow or change sign' at the push, 'cannot compare 'usize' and 'i64'' in the predicate, and 'implicit coercion from 'usize' to 'i64'' twice at the `pos =` stores. design.md §5 says `isize`/`usize` are for FFI only and Kāra code uses `i64` for every size, length, count and index, and the existing B-2026-10-25-10 family already drops a Rust `as usize` cast with that reason. The written type is the one thing to change: `Vec[Vec[i64]]` checks clean and the arm prints the mirror's output. A remedy would be a fix on a `usize` (or `isize`) written in a type outside an FFI signature (an `extern` block, a `ptr.*` value) that rewrites it to `i64`, or a fix on these coercion errors that points at the annotation the `usize` came from. The kata's arm writes `i64` by hand and its README cites this row.
fix: 52c81c1375 (with 7b8a0de80f). A `usize` or `isize` written in a type outside an FFI item (an extern function or block, a struct with a `repr` attribute), in a program where such a type meets `i64` (a widening or narrowing coercion, a mixed-sign compare, a `collect` item that differs only there), now draws one diagnostic per written spelling: "this type mixes with `i64`, and `usize` and `isize` are for FFI signatures: Kāra writes sizes, lengths, counts and indices as `i64` (design.md §5), so write `i64` here", whose machine fix rewrites it to `i64` (src/typechecker/pointer_ints.rs; spellings recorded in lowering.rs, mixes noted in exprs.rs and expr_ops.rs). A `usize` that meets nothing draws nothing, and an `as usize` cast keeps its own drop-the-cast fix (B-2026-10-25-10), which 7b8a0de80f restores after the first commit's gate showed two `core_strict_check` reds. The row's own shape, `Vec[Vec[usize]]` pushed `enumerate()` indices and compared with an `i64` through `partition_point`, now mends to `Vec[Vec[i64]]` and prints its answer (tests/kata_1057_check_gaps.rs, `kata_1057_usize_mixed_with_i64_becomes_i64`), and kata 1057's heap arm, written the Rust way with `Vec<(i64, usize)>`, reaches `Vec[(i64, i64)]` through `karac fix` alone. Gate on the same tree before its final rebase onto 09c0261046: fmt, both clippy legs, `cargo test --all` 10455 passed, `cargo test --features llvm` 10625 passed, 0 failed.

title: `m.get_or(k, "lit")` on a `Map[String, String]` stops the MIR interpreter with `a String place holds no box` when the default is a string literal, hit or miss; a `let d: String = "x"` default works
detail: Found by the B-2026-11-05-31 corpus sweep: `karac fix` removing `.to_string()` from a literal default (spec-equivalent: a string literal is a `String`, design.md § String literals) turned corpus/fixtures/memory_sanitizer/map_set/asan_map_insert_duplicate_heap_value_discarded_no_leak and .../strings/asan_map_get_or_string_value_owned_copy_no_double_free into crashes. Minimal: `fn main() { let mut m: Map[String, String] = Map.new(); m.insert("k", "v"); println(m.get_or("k", "x")); }` -> `error[mir]: run: in main at bb12[term]: a String place holds no box`, exit 3, before printing; with key "z" it prints `x` and then stops at bb24. `let d: String = "x"; m.get_or("z", d)` prints `x`, exit 0. The native is src/mir/interp.rs `("get_or", [key, default]) if is_map`; the literal argument presumably reaches it as a static Str place where a String is expected. The compiled lanes were not measured (the release binary here has no backend).
fix: 8a9475c0f8. A literal get_or default was lent as a view of static text, the way a borrowed text argument is; but the default is the value a miss returns, so the interpreter's native dropped it as a String on a hit (a String place holds no box) and returned it as one on a miss, and the compiled lane copied the 16-byte view into a 24-byte String (ASan stack-buffer-overflow, measured on the pre-fix release binary). src/mir/lower.rs now lowers a literal get_or default as the String the checker typed it, which the native drops or returns. Pinned by corpus/design/ok_map_get_or_takes_a_literal_default (Map[String, String] hit and miss, Map[i64, String], SortedMap, a String binding default) on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan.

title: Passing a struct's `Fn` field to a bare `Fn` parameter is refused as a move out of a borrowed place (`apply(self.f, 1)` with `fn apply(f: Fn(i64) -> i64, ..)`); the same call to `f: ref Fn(i64) -> i64` is accepted, though a function-typed parameter is non-escaping and borrowed (design.md § Parameter modes, core-semantics §9.3)
detail: Found by the B-2026-11-05-31 corpus sweep (corpus/apps/cli/mini_sortedcontainers: `sort_by_key_stable(items, self.key)` after `key: ref Fn(V) -> K` became `key: Fn(V) -> K`). Minimal: `fn apply_bare(f: Fn(i64) -> i64, x: i64) -> i64 { f(x) } struct S { f: Fn(i64) -> i64 } impl S { fn go(self) -> i64 { apply_bare(self.f, 1) } }` -> `error[borrow_projection_copy]: cannot move a non-`Copy` value out of a borrowed place. This type has no `.clone()`...` at `self.f`. With `fn apply_ref(f: ref Fn(i64) -> i64, ..)` the program checks and runs (prints 2). A bare parameter borrows (design.md § Parameter modes), and a function-typed one is non-escaping by default (core-semantics §9.3), so the argument should be borrowed, not moved. The style lint `redundant_ref_param` stays silent on function-typed parameters until this is fixed.
fix: 34cb06e29c: the call-argument move check (src/typechecker/exprs.rs check_call_args_with_substitution_full) skips a function-typed argument whose callee parameter is bare and not `escaping` (items.rs d5_borrowed_fn_params, set per call in expr_call.rs and method_user_impl.rs), since that parameter is a shared borrow (core semantics §9.3, §9.6) and the MIR already passes it borrowed (lower.rs def_call, fn_arg). Free, generic, method and `Type.f` static calls all take `apply(self.f, 1)` now, on interp and llvm. `own` and `escaping` parameters still refuse it as a move out of a borrowed place. Pins: corpus/core ok_fn_field_to_bare_fn_param, err_fn_field_to_escaping_fn_param. Full interp corpus: no new failures. Not changed: style_lints.rs `redundant_ref_param` still exempts function-typed parameters citing this row; lifting that is Thread A's call.

title: A pattern over a bare parameter binds differently from one over a `ref` parameter: `match arg { E.R { xs, ms } => (xs, ms) }` reached through `fn get(e: E)` of a `shared enum` is refused (`cannot move 'xs': it borrows its value`), and the same body under `e: ref E` is accepted (design.md § Parameter modes: a bare parameter borrows)
detail: Found by the B-2026-11-05-31 corpus sweep (corpus/apps/cli/mini_tsdb `eval(self, e: ref Expr, ..)` after the `ref` was removed). Minimal: `shared enum E { R { xs: Vec[i64], ms: i64 }, F { arg: E }, N }` and `fn get_bare(e: E) -> i64 { match e { E.F { arg } => { let (xs, ms) = match arg { E.R { xs, ms } => (xs, ms), _ => return 0 }; xs.len() + ms } _ => 0 } }` -> `error[borrow_projection_copy]: cannot move 'xs': it borrows its value (a bare `for` element, a `ref` binding, or a binding into a borrowed place)` at the tuple; the identical `get_ref(e: ref E)` checks clean. One of the two is wrong, since design.md § `karac fix` says `x: ref T` means the same as `x: T`. A one-level `match e { E.A { xs } => xs }` returning `xs.len()` behaves the same under both. The style lint `redundant_ref_param` stays silent on any parameter a pattern takes apart until this is settled.
