title: A `let` after a `#[derive]`d type had no hover type and no inlay hint: derived items were spliced in numbered from 0, so lowering's renumbering moved the program's own later nodes off the ids the type tables are keyed by
detail: Found by the inlay-hint sweep over corpus/apps (lsp/tests/incremental.rs, hints compared incremental vs full): 16 failures in task_runner, flag_eval and kv_http, every one a `let` after a derived type whose type hint was missing. `comptime_mir::splice` inserted the derived impls as parsed, with node ids starting at 0; `lower`'s `assign_node_ids` then renumbered the program's own later nodes as duplicates, away from the ids `typed.node_types` was built against, so hover and the hint lookup found nothing. The retyped typecheck also saw duplicate ids; no wrong answer was observed from that, so wider risk is a hypothesis. Pinned by lsp/tests/signature_hints.rs `a_let_after_a_derived_type_keeps_its_type`.
fix: b6179e77bc: `comptime_mir::splice` now numbers the spliced derived items from fresh ids above the program's maximum (`node_ids::next_free_id` + `number_items_from`), so lowering no longer renumbers the program's own nodes and the type tables stay keyed correctly. The corpus/apps incremental sweep went from 16 hint failures to 0 over 1,422 edits; the derive suites (comptime_mir, comptime_generated_errors, core_derive_lists, derive_helper_position_check, fix_derive_partial_eq) pass. Pinned by lsp/tests/signature_hints.rs `a_let_after_a_derived_type_keeps_its_type`.

title: Under `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` a write through a `mut Slice` view of a `Vec` is lost: `poke(mut w[2..4])` with `xs[0] = 99` leaves `w` as `1 2 3 4` in a program that has any `for` loop; `as_slice_mut()` in a tuple field and `iter_mut()` over a range view lose theirs too (the same cause as B-2026-11-10-2: the views were lowered on a shared borrow and literal_tables made the Vec a static)
detail: v1 gate re-check at 8f7933cf20, the M4b auto-par-off comparison (mir-llvm with and without KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, 21220 entries): 11 verdicts differ and 6 are this, all passing with auto-par on and wrong with it off: fixtures/codegen/iter_range/test_e2e_mut_sub_range_slice_writes_through_to_the_backing_buffer and _of_a_mut_slice_forwards, fixtures/codegen/slices/test_e2e_index_through_a_slice_typed_tuple_field (`2 1 2` for `2 9 2`), fixtures/core_strict_check/check_write_through_a_read_only_slice_4, design/ok_slice_iter_mut (JIT exits 101 with no output; the built binary prints `[1, 2, 3, 4]` twice where `[11, 12, 13, 4]` and `[11, 12, 26, 8]` are expected). The interpreter is right either way, and `karac build` with KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 is wrong too, so the benchmark lane (bench.sh builds that way) is affected. Minimal: `fn poke(xs: mut Slice[i64]) { xs[0] = 99; }` and a main that pokes `mut w[2..4]` on `let mut w: Vec[i64] = [1, 2, 3, 4]`, prints it, then has any `for x in r { .. }`: off prints `1 2 3 4`, on prints `1 2 99 4`; without the loop both are right. The elaborated MIR of main is the same in both modes except the Record build's extra gotos, and it borrows the Vec SHARED for the mutable view (`_6 = &_1; _5 = Vec[i64].slice(move _6, 2, 4)`, from slice_view(.., mutable: false) at the non-place Index arm of src/mir/lower.rs), so the likely cause is LLVM trusting the shared borrow and forwarding the Vec's old contents; the auto-par build's block layout hides it. Hypothesis, not bisected.
fix: ba29c00d5c (B-2026-11-10-2) fixed this; 9e055f2e50 adds the pin. The views were lowered on a shared borrow (`_6 = &_1; Vec.slice(..)`, and `as_slice_mut` through the generic method path), so src/mir/literal_tables.rs took the Vec of literals for one only read and made it a read-only static: writes were lost, and an in-place sort (fixtures/interpreter/slices/test_slice_sort_and_reverse, the exit 101) wrote to read-only memory. Auto-par's recording build skipped the promotion, which is why only KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 showed it. ba29c00d5c lowers `as_slice_mut` as a mutable view and has the table pass refuse a table whose shared borrow goes to a call returning a `mut Slice`. Lowering the range view on a `mut` borrow instead (tried here first) makes MIR borrowck refuse fixtures/codegen/slices/test_e2e_slice_equality_compares_contents, which is B-2026-11-10-4. Checked at 9e055f2e50: the row's five corpus entries, test_e2e_slice_equality_compares_contents and test_slice_sort_and_reverse pass on mir-llvm with KARAC_AUTO_PAR 0 and 1; tests/mir_mut_slice_view.rs (a range, a range value, an inclusive range, a tuple-held as_slice_mut view; interpreter and built binary, auto-par off and on) passes, and printed `[1, 2, 3, 4]` / `[1, 2, 3]` on a compiler before ba29c00d5c. Of the kara-katas benches, the four that pass a `mut` range view or call as_slice_mut (843, 832, 702, 792) print the same before and after, so no M5 row ran through the affected shape.

title: Every bad format spec of an f-string is reported at the f-string's closing quote: `println(f"x {a:?} y {b:?}")` gives two "format spec `?`: `?` is Debug formatting" errors at one column, the `"`, so the two holes read as one place reported twice
detail: Building the http_cache app: a self-test line printing `{d.max_age:?}` and `{d.s_maxage:?}` gave both diagnostics at 614:204, the end of the literal. The f-string hole carries its own offset, line and column (the lexer records them for re-parsing the expression), and `foreign_spec_letter` (B-2026-11-09-68) already places its diagnostic inside the hole, but the general path called `self.error(&msg)`, which takes the current token: the whole interpolated literal, already consumed. Remedy: report each bad spec at the spec's own text in its hole (`hole_span`). Kept without a machine fix for `?`: `{x}` needs a `Display` the parser cannot see, as tests/mend_rustisms.rs's descriptive cell says.
fix: FIXED by e922bfc642. src/parser/exprs.rs `report_bad_spec`: a format spec that fails to parse is reported at the spec's own text in its hole (`hole_span`, from the hole's recorded offset, line and column), not with `self.error` at the consumed f-string token. `{x:?}` keeps no machine fix (`{x}` needs a `Display` the parser cannot see; tests/mend_rustisms.rs's descriptive cell). Pinned by tests/http_cache_gaps.rs `each_bad_format_spec_is_reported_at_its_own_hole`.

title: A field named by a structural marker (`struct Directives { private: bool }`, a Cache-Control parser's natural field) says "Expected identifier, found `:`" at the colon, and a struct literal naming it fails and cascades past its closing brace ("Expected expression, found `;`"); neither says that `private` cannot name a field, which `r#` cannot rescue
detail: Building the http_cache app. design.md § Raw identifiers: structural markers (`self`, `pub`, `private`, `mut`, `ref`, `own`, ...) cannot be escaped, so no spelling of such a field exists. At a declaration the field parser eats `private` as the field's visibility and then expects a name; in a literal, `expect_identifier` gives E0003's "'private' is a reserved keyword" without a remedy and returns None, and a literal whose FIRST field is `private:` is not even recognised as a struct literal (`looks_like_struct_literal_body_at` wants an identifier). Remedy: before a field declaration's visibility and a literal's field name, a marker directly followed by `:` is reported once ("`private` cannot name a field: it is a structural marker, which `r#` does not escape, so give the field another name") and retyped as the name, so the struct and its uses parse as written; the literal lookahead accepts it. Member access (`d.private`) was already legal.
fix: FIXED by e922bfc642. src/parser.rs `recover_marker_as_field_name`: a structural marker that `r#` cannot escape, directly before a `:`, at a field declaration (items.rs `parse_struct_fields`, generics.rs's struct body) or a struct literal's field (exprs.rs), is reported once ("`private` cannot name a field: it is a structural marker, which `r#` does not escape, so give the field another name") and retyped as the name; `looks_like_struct_literal_body_at` accepts it as a first field. `priv`, reserved for future use as well, keeps its "'priv' is reserved" message. Pinned by tests/http_cache_gaps.rs `a_structural_marker_as_a_field_name_is_named_once` (three errors, no cascade).

title: A program's own `struct Entry` loses its own methods: `impl Entry { fn age(self, ..) }` then `e.age(now)` is "no method 'age' on type 'Entry'", because method dispatch hands every `Entry` receiver to the map entry's (`or_insert`, `and_modify`, ...); the prelude_shadow warning says the opposite, that built-in paths no longer apply
detail: Building the http_cache app, whose cache entry is `struct Entry` (as in most caches and logs). typechecker/method_mapset.rs dispatched `Type::Named { name: "Entry" }` to `infer_entry_method` whatever declared it, so every user method was unknown (`require_known_method`). design.md § Module System: prelude names are not reserved, and the prelude_shadow lint says built-in paths keyed on the name no longer apply to the user's type. Remedy: when the program declares its own `Entry` (a struct, or an enum without `Occupied`), only the map entry's four names (`or_insert`, `or_insert_with`, `and_modify`, `or_default`) go to the map entry, so `Map.entry(k).or_insert(v)` still works in the same program. MIR and both backends key their natives on those names, so nothing else changed; the app and the fixture run on the interpreter and compiled.
fix: FIXED by e922bfc642. src/typechecker/method_mapset.rs: when the program declares its own `Entry` (a struct, or an enum without `Occupied`), only `or_insert`, `or_insert_with`, `and_modify` and `or_default` dispatch to the map entry; every other method goes to the program's impl. `Map.entry(k).or_insert(v)` still works beside it. Pinned by tests/http_cache_gaps.rs `a_users_entry_keeps_its_own_methods` and `_compiled`, and by the http_cache app on all four backends.

title: `opt ?? "" == value` (`??` binds loosest, so it is `opt ?? ("" == value)`) gives three type mismatches (`expected 'String', found 'bool'`, the closure's return type, the closure's type) and no word on precedence or fix
detail: Building the http_cache app: `self.vary.iter().all(|(name, value)| req.header(name) ?? "" == value)`. design.md says `??` has the loosest precedence of all operators, as in C# and JavaScript (Swift's binds tighter than `==`), so a reader from Swift or Kotlin's `?:` meets it. Remedy: when a `??` fallback is a comparison and the payload is no `bool` (so the comparison cannot be the fallback), one error names the precedence ("`??` binds more loosely than `==`: `a ?? b == c` is `a ?? (b == c)`, whose `bool` fallback cannot stand in for the 'String' it unwraps; write `(a ?? b) == c` to compare the value") with the edit adding the parentheses, and the expression is typed as `bool` so nothing cascades. An `Option[bool] ?? a == b` is left alone.
fix: FIXED by e922bfc642. src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs `infer_nil_coalesce`: a fallback that is a comparison, under a payload that is no `bool`, gets one error naming the precedence with the edit `(a ?? b) op c`, and the expression is typed `bool` so nothing cascades; `Option[bool] ?? a == b` is untouched. Pinned by tests/http_cache_gaps.rs `a_comparison_after_nil_coalesce_is_parenthesized`.

title: A `ref Str` (an element of `pairs.iter()` over a `Slice[(Str, Str)]`) handed to a `String` parameter gets "expected 'String', found 'ref Str'" with no fix where a `Str` gets `.to_string()`; to a user function the ownership pass offers `.clone()`, which leaves a `Str`
detail: Building the http_cache app: `for (k, v) in headers.iter() { b = b.header(k, v); }` with `headers: Slice[(Str, Str)]`. The typechecker's Str-to-String fix (B-2026-10-12-7) matched a found type of exactly `Str`. Remedy: a `ref Str` / `mut ref Str` takes the same `.to_string()` edit, and the message names the found type; for `take(k)` the `.to_string()` now wins over the ownership pass's `.clone()` at the same span.
fix: FIXED by e922bfc642. src/typechecker.rs: the Str-to-String `.to_string()` fix (B-2026-10-12-7) also takes a `ref Str` / `mut ref Str`, and its message names the found type; for a user function's `own String` it now wins over the ownership pass's `.clone()`. Pinned by tests/http_cache_gaps.rs `a_borrowed_str_where_a_string_is_wanted_gets_to_string`.

title: A tuple of borrowed elements moved where owned ones are wanted (`for (k, v) in headers { out.push((k, v)); }` with a bare, so borrowing, `headers: Vec[(String, String)]` parameter) gets "expected '(String, String)', found '(ref String, ref String)'" with no fix, where the one-element form gets `.clone()`
detail: Building the http_cache app's `with_label`. The single-binding form (`for n in names { out.push(n) }`) gets the strict-core "a borrowed value cannot be moved out of what it borrows" with a `.clone()` edit, and a local bound out of a parameter gets `own` on the parameter (kata 2046); the tuple form reaches the plain mismatch. Remedy: `own` on the parameter when the tuple's elements come out of a bare parameter's iteration, or `.clone()` on each element; the app took `own` by hand.
fix: 18c7e2b429: check_assignable reads a tuple literal's elements (recorded by span as it is typed, `tuple_literal_elems`) and gives the one-element form's remedy element by element (src/typechecker/exprs.rs reject_borrowed_tuple_elements): "`k` and `v` are borrowed, and a borrowed value cannot be moved out of what it borrows. Take owned copies with `.clone()`", with a multi-edit fix adding `.clone()` after each borrowed element, or, when every one is bound out of the same bare parameter, that parameter's `own` (kata 2046's rule). A `for` element over a bare parameter takes the `.clone()` form, as the one-element `for n in names { out.push(n) }` already did; the app's hand-written `own` + `.into_iter()` is two fixes away and stays the author's choice. Pinned by tests/http_cache_diagnostics.rs a_tuple_of_borrowed_loop_elements_takes_clone_on_each, a_tuple_with_one_borrowed_element_clones_only_that_one, a_tuple_bound_out_of_a_bare_parameter_takes_its_own.

title: `req.header("X-Purge-Token") != Some(PURGE_TOKEN)` (an `Option[String]` against an `Option[Str]` of a constant) is refused with "cannot compare 'Option[String]' and 'Option[Str]'" and no remedy; `String == Str` compares, and the library has no `as_deref`
detail: Building the http_cache app (2 sites: the purge token, an origin's `If-Modified-Since`). Rust refuses the same pair and its answer is `.as_deref()`; Kāra's `Option` has `as_ref` and `cloned` but nothing that views an `Option[String]` as an `Option[Str]`, so the diagnostic cannot name one. Remedy: an edit for the literal form, `Some(x)` -> `Some(x.to_string())` (what the app did by hand), or compare `Option[String]` with `Option[Str]` as their payloads compare, or an `Option[String].as_str()`; a spec call between the last two.
fix: 18c7e2b429: report_compare_mismatch (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs option_str_some_fix) answers an `Option[String]` against `Some(<Str>)` with the row's first remedy: "an `Option` compares items of one type, so the `Some` of a `Str` does not meet an `Option[String]` (a `String` and a `Str` compare only bare); `.to_string()` makes its item a `String`", fix `Some(TOKEN.to_string())`, for a constant, binding, literal, field, index or call in the `Some`. A literal `Some("x")` already checked. The row's other two remedies (comparing `Option[String]` with `Option[Str]` by their payloads, or an `Option[String].as_str()`) are a spec question left to the review thread. Pinned by tests/http_cache_diagnostics.rs an_option_string_against_some_of_a_str_constant_takes_to_string.

title: A `Str` view of a parameter passed through a closure combinator is refused as returning a borrow of a temporary: `fn unquote(s: Str) -> Str { s.strip_prefix("\"").and_then(|t| t.strip_suffix("\"")).unwrap_or(s) }` is E0509 "the result borrows a temporary value, which this function owns", as are `.map(|t| t.trim())` and `split_once(..).map(|p| p.0)`; the same chain without a closure, or a `match`, passes
detail: Building the http_cache app's Cache-Control parser. MIR borrowck (src/mir/borrowck.rs): the Option's payload is a view of `s`, and the closure captures nothing, so the result borrows only `s`. Probes: `s.strip_prefix(x).unwrap_or(s)` passes; `.and_then(|t| ..).unwrap_or("")`, `.map(|t| t.trim()).unwrap_or(s)`, `.and_then(..) ?? s` and `s.split_once("=").map(|p| p.0).unwrap_or(s)` all fail at the chain's first call. Suspect the call-result rule counting the closure temporary (or the moved Option temporary) as an origin of the result. The app wrote the `match` form by hand.
fix: 1a5b6091e7: the row's suspect held. MIR lowers `map`'s closure argument as `_6 = &_5`, and a call result carried every argument's origins, so `Option.map(copy _3, move _6)` borrowed the closure local and returning it was E0509. src/mir/borrowck.rs arg_origins: a `ref` / `mut ref` closure argument gives the result what the closure holds (held_behind), as a call through a reference already did, unless the result's type has a place for a closure (`may_hold_closure`, shared with B-2026-11-10-24's pointee rule). A closure that lends one of the function's own locals into the result is still refused (E0516 on the local). Pinned by tests/http_cache_diagnostics.rs a_str_view_through_a_closure_combinator_is_returned (the row's four probes, `??` included) and a_closure_lending_a_local_into_the_result_is_still_refused; core pins 271/271.

title: A `let` inside a block outlived it for the `let mut` rule: `let mut q = 7; if c { let q = 3; } q = 8;` was refused as a write to the inner, immutable `q`
detail: Found building unused_mut (B-2026-11-09-55). The ownership pass keys `immutable_lets` by bare name and never restored it at block exit, so an inner immutable `let q` stayed recorded after its block and the outer `let mut q`'s later write drew "cannot reassign `q` — `q` is declared without `mut` at line 3:16". The field's doc called the bare-name model an under-report only; this direction is a false positive. Repro: `fn main() { let mut q = 7; if q > 0 { let q = 3; println(f"{q}"); } q = 8; println(f"{q}"); }`.
fix: df878ae40f: check_block saves `immutable_lets` on entry and restores it at exit, so a `let` inside a block ends with it. A match arm's or a `for` pattern's binding still clears the name past its scope, which can only under-report. tests/unused_mut_lint.rs an_inner_block_let_leaves_an_outer_let_mut_writable.

title: A method's `mut ref` argument needs no `mut` marker, so an immutable binding is written through it unreported: `let s = String.new(); r.fill(s);` with `fn fill(ref self, buf: mut ref String)` checks clean and fills `s`
detail: design.md §7 (call-site markers): a missing marker at a `mut ref T` parameter is an error, and method receivers are the only exemption; the marker does not grant mutability, so the place must be `let mut`. check_call_site_marker runs for free-function calls only (ownership's MethodCall arm says "Part 1½: only free-fn args mark"), so `r.fill(s)` is accepted without a marker and without `let mut s`, and the write lands in an immutable binding. A free-function call `fill2(u)` gets the marker error. Since B-2026-11-09-55, a MARKED method argument on an immutable binding (`r.fill(mut t)` with `let t`) is refused like a free-function one, and an unmarked one at a `mut ref` parameter counts as a write for unused_mut, so the lint never removes a `mut` such a call needs. Left: requiring the marker on method arguments (with its fix), which will touch corpus programs that pass buffers to library methods unmarked (`r.read_to_string(s)` in apps/cli/cron_sched).
fix: e705e5be7e, per the review thread's 0.8.x ruling: an unmarked argument at a method's `mut ref` parameter, where the method resolves to its own signature, warns `deprecated` with a machine-applicable fix inserting `mut ` (src/ownership/borrow.rs note_unmarked_method_mut_arg, src/cli.rs report_unmarked_method_mut_args), once the program has no errors; a forwarded `mut ref` / `mut Slice` needs no marker, as for a free function, and `#[allow(deprecated)]` silences it. The 606 corpus calls resolved only by method name keep today's behaviour. Sources migrated with `karac fix`, outputs unchanged: 40 corpus programs (mir-interp 48/48 on the touched entries), their 16 kara-katas app originals (kara-katas d2537c3f, extracted_src follows), the embedded programs in tests/mir_io.rs and mir_serde.rs, selfhost/src/parser.kara, two doc lines, and the desugared hash-byte wrapper (`k.hash(mut s)`). Pinned by tests/method_mut_marker.rs an_unmarked_method_mut_ref_argument_is_deprecated_and_fixed and allow_deprecated_silences_the_unmarked_method_argument. The compile error at the next minor release is tracked by B-2026-11-10-36.

title: The `let mut` rule misses receiver writes its hand-written method table lacks: `let w: VecDeque[i64] = VecDeque.new(); w.push_back(1);` checks clean
detail: The ownership pass decides that a method writes its receiver from `method_self_modes` (program impls) and `stdlib_method_self_borrow_kind` (a table naming Vec, Map, SortedMap, Set, SortedSet and String methods). Library types outside the table (VecDeque, and any baked impl it does not list) never draw "cannot call `push_back` on `w`" on a non-`mut` binding. The strict typecheck's `method_writes_receiver` (src/typechecker/core_ref_write.rs) already knows: it reads baked impls' first parameter from the env and fell back to the mutating-builtin names. Since B-2026-11-09-55 it records each such call in `TypeCheckResult::receiver_write_calls`, which unused_mut reads as a write; the remedy is for the immutability rule to read it too, measured over the corpus for programs it newly refuses.
fix: e705e5be7e: the strict check's receiver_write_calls now records whether a receiver write is known (program impl self modes, baked library impls' first parameter, Atomic/Option) or only guessed from the method name, and the ownership pass's receiver rule (src/ownership/expr_check.rs) refuses a known write on a plain `let`, with the `let mut` fix. The name-only guess counts only for the builtin collections (Vec, VecDeque, String, Map, Set, SortedMap, SortedSet, PriorityQueue), so `Vector.reverse` on a program's own type is not misread. Corpus sweep: 11 fixtures newly refused (VecDeque.push_back, Map.entry on a plain `let m`, BufReader.read_line), all migrated to `let mut` with outputs unchanged; the same `let mut` went into the programs in tests/mir_io.rs, mir_collections.rs, mir_isolating_built.rs (`split_off`), buffered_io_sources.rs, buffered_sockets.rs, buffered_provider_socket.rs and buffered_tls.rs (their owners told). Pinned by tests/method_mut_marker.rs a_vecdeque_push_back_on_a_plain_let_is_refused_and_fixed and a_reading_library_method_on_a_plain_let_stays_accepted.

title: A plain `karac build` whose auto-par verdicts parallelize nothing shipped the recording lowering, which puts a block between every statement of a block, not the in-order program: kata 1088's bench, where every candidate is refused, ran 15% slower than its `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` build (1.223 s against 1.065 s), on one core
detail:
MEASURED on the 4-core cloud box, kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1088-confusing-number-ii/bench (400 random n up to 10^9, each answered by a recursive walk over the digits 0, 1, 6, 8, 9; output `400 n up to 10^9: 345592512 confusing numbers, checksum 529503063` in every build). Medians of 12 interleaved runs: `karac build` 1.223 s (user 1.205, so nothing ran in parallel), `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build` 1.065 s. The two binaries differed (cmp: first difference at byte 265), though the build parallelized nothing.

CAUSE: `build_renamed_source` (src/mir/lower.rs) lowers the program once with `AutoPar::Record`, takes the cost gate's verdicts, and lowers again with `AutoPar::Apply` only when some verdict accepts. When none does, it returned the Record lowering (`Ok((first, None))`). The Record lowering delimits each candidate by ending a basic block between every statement of a block (`auto_par_record_stmts` / `candidate_branch_end`), so the MIR handed to the backend had extra blocks and jumps the in-order lowering does not, and LLVM's optimized output for the hot recursion differed.
fix: ba29c00d5c: `build_renamed_source` (src/mir/lower.rs) no longer returns the recording lowering when the cost gate accepts nothing; it drops it and lowers the program again with `AutoPar::Off`, so a plain `karac build` that runs nothing as tasks is the in-order program, with the literal-table and presize passes the recording lowering skipped. Kata 1088's bench binary from a plain build is now byte-identical to the `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` one. Pinned by tests/kata_1088_auto_par_in_order.rs (the ★ walk and a `main` like the bench's: no tasks, groups or reductions, and every MIR body equal to `build_sequential_source`'s); on the previous lower.rs it fails (the two builds' bodies differ). Turning those passes on for plain builds exposed B-2026-11-10-2, fixed in the same commit.

title: `v.as_slice_mut()` and a range view passed `mut v[a..b]`, on a `Vec` of literals, lowered on a shared borrow, so the literal-table pass made the `Vec` a static: on a compiled backend a write through the slice was lost (`bs[0] = 7` left `[9, 8, 3, 1, 2]`) and a sort through it crashed writing to read-only memory, in every `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0` build and, after B-2026-11-10-1, in plain ones
detail:
FOUND by the full gate on B-2026-11-10-1's fix: tests/core_strict_check.rs `every_argument_to_a_mutating_parameter_is_marked` printed nothing under `__mir-llvm-run` (exit 101). Reduced: `let mut b = [9, 8, 3, 1, 2]; let mut bs = b.as_slice_mut(); bs.sort(); println(f"{b}")` segfaults under `__mir-llvm-run` and `karac build` (ASan: SEGV on a WRITE in karac_mir_sort_int, at an address in the binary's image); with `bs[0] = 7` instead it prints `[9, 8, 3, 1, 2]`. `__mir-run` prints the right answers. `KARAC_MIR_LITERAL_TABLES=0` makes both right.

CAUSE: the method-call lowering in src/mir/lower.rs turns `as_slice` / `as_mut_slice` on a `Vec` or array into a slice view of a `Shared` / `Mut` borrow, but not `as_slice_mut`, the spelling docs/library and the tests use. That went through the general method path as `Vec[i64].as_slice_mut(move _4)` with `_4 = &_1`, a shared borrow (the backend and interpreter both answer `as_slice_mut`, so it ran). src/mir/literal_tables.rs promotes a `Vec` built from literals whose every other mention is a shared borrow, so `b` became a static. The record lowering a plain auto-par build used to keep skips that pass, which is why only the sequential lane showed it before B-2026-11-10-1.

The range view: a full mir-llvm corpus run with the `as_slice_mut` part fixed, against the same entries on a compiler without either fix, found 4 entries red only with the fix (corpus/design/ok_slice_iter_mut, fixtures/codegen/iter_range/test_e2e_mut_sub_range_of_a_mut_slice_forwards and _slice_writes_through_to_the_backing_buffer, fixtures/core_strict_check/check_write_through_a_read_only_slice_4), each a `mut v[a..b]` argument on a `Vec` of literals whose write was lost. The range-index lowering in src/mir/lower.rs takes every range view through a shared borrow and the call `Vec[T].slice`, whose result is typed `mut Slice` when the view is written through. Borrowing mutably there instead fixed the four but made MIR borrowck refuse fixtures/codegen/slices/test_e2e_slice_equality_compares_contents (B-2026-11-10-4), so the literal-table pass now refuses a table whose shared borrow is handed to a call returning a `mut Slice`.
fix: ba29c00d5c: the method-call lowering in src/mir/lower.rs takes `as_slice_mut` with `as_slice` / `as_mut_slice` into `slice_view`, mutable unless the method is `as_slice`, so `v.as_slice_mut()` borrows `v` mutably. src/mir/literal_tables.rs refuses a table whose shared borrow is handed to a call returning a `mut Slice` (`lent_to_mut_slice`), which covers `mut v[a..b]`, whose lowering still borrows shared (B-2026-11-10-4). Pinned by tests/kata_1088_as_slice_mut.rs (the lowered `main` takes `&mut` for `as_slice_mut`; a write through `as_slice_mut`, a sort through `split_at_mut`, and a sort through `mut d[1..4]`, each on a `Vec` of literals, print the right lists under `__mir-run` and `__mir-llvm-run` with `KARAC_AUTO_PAR` 1 and 0); with the `as_slice_mut` hunk reverted both tests fail. A full mir-llvm corpus run, compared entry by entry with a compiler at 0142335972, showed no entry red only with the fix.

title: A `flat_map` closure whose body is an `if`/`else` or a `match` giving a list from each branch (`|x| if x == 0 { [0, 0] } else { [x] }`, as Rust's `flat_map` takes any `IntoIterator`) is refused with "iterate it with `.into_iter()`", but `karac fix` has nothing to apply
detail:
FOUND writing kata 1089's iterator-chain arm (kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1089-duplicate-zeros/duplicate_zeros_chain.kara): `arr.iter().flat_map(|x| if x == 0 { [0, 0] } else { [x] }).take(n).collect()`. `karac check` reports E0200 `trait bound `OutV: Iterator` is not satisfied: `Vec[i64]` is a collection, not an `Iterator`; iterate it with `.into_iter()``; `karac fix` says `no fixable diagnostics`.

CAUSE: `record_into_iter_sites` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs, B-2026-10-20-33) finds where the fix's `.into_iter()` goes with `value_end`, which follows a closure to its body and a block to its last expression, and knows only the ends of a name, a call, a field, an index or a list. An `if` or `match` had no end, so the hint carried no fix.
fix: ba29c00d5c: `value_end` in `record_into_iter_sites` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) gives a closure whose body is an `if` or `if let` with an `else`, or a `match`, the end of that whole expression, so the `.into_iter()` fix goes after it (`|x| if x == 0 { [0, 0] } else { [x] }.into_iter()`). Only the closure's own body takes it: the last `if` of a block body would end the statement at its `}`. Pinned by tests/kata_1089_flat_map_if_into_iter.rs (an `if` and a `match` body: refused with the hint, `karac fix` writes `.into_iter()` after the expression, the result checks clean and prints `[1, 0, 0, 2]`). Before the fix `karac fix` reported `no fixable diagnostics` on the kata's arm. Kata 1089's chain arm is the text `karac fix` now gives.

title: A range view passed `mut v[a..b]` is lowered on a shared borrow of `v` (`_r = &v; Vec[T].slice(move _r, a, b)`), so MIR borrowck does not see it write: corpus fixtures/codegen/slices/test_e2e_slice_equality_compares_contents mutably lends `a[0..2]` while `let s1: Slice[i64] = a[0..2]` is still read later, and is accepted
detail: FOUND fixing B-2026-11-10-2. In the range-index arm of the expression lowering (src/mir/lower.rs, `ExprKind::Index` with a `Range` index), `slice_view(object, Some(range), t, false)` always borrows shared, even when `t` is a `mut Slice` (an argument marked `mut`). Passing the view's mutability instead (`HK::Slice { mutable: true, .. }`) made the fixture fail MIR borrowck: `24:28: mutable borrow of _1 while it is borrowed (borrow at bb25[1] at 14:26) [E0516]`, line 14 being `let s1: Slice[i64] = a[0..2];` and line 24 `cmp_mut(mut a[0..2], mut c[0..2])`, with `s1` read again at line 39 (`as1 == s1`). The front end's ownership check accepts the program. Whether that program is meant to be accepted (the fixture's expected output says it runs) or is an aliasing violation core-semantics.md §5.6 should refuse is the open question; the lowering's shared borrow under a written view is wrong either way, and B-2026-11-10-2 had to work around it in the literal-table pass.
fix: 8819ec4dff: a range passed for a `mut Slice` parameter (`f(mut a[x..y])`, `a[x..=y]`, a range value `a[r]`) is now viewed with `slice_mut` through a `mut` borrow of `a` (`arg_operand_here` in src/mir/lower.rs; `slice_view_by` takes the mutability), so MIR borrowck refuses it with E0516 while a read view of `a` is live, as core-semantics §5.6 requires (review's ruling 2026-11-10: a live `ref` borrow forbids a mutable borrow of the place, and an index projection overlaps the whole collection). `karac check` reports it (`cannot mutably borrow `a` while `s1` still holds a borrow of it`); the front end's ownership check still accepts it, and MIR borrowck carries the refusal. corpus/core/err_mut_range_view_while_read_view_live pins the refusal (accepted before). fixtures/codegen/slices/test_e2e_slice_equality_compares_contents pinned the wrong acceptance: its `cmp_mut(mut a[0..2], mut c[0..2])` now runs before `s1` is taken, printing the same output (passes on mir-interp, mir-llvm and mir-llvm-asan, KARAC_AUTO_PAR 0 and 1). A sweep of the 106 corpus entries and the kara-katas programs that pass a `mut` range view, `karac check` before and after, found no other new E0516. With the view's borrow now `mut`, the literal-table pass's refusal from ba29c00d5c (a shared borrow handed to a call returning a `mut Slice`) no longer has a range case to catch; it is kept.

title: `karac run` of apps/cli/mini_tldextract (21.8k lines) takes 92 s on one core, where `karac build` takes 16 s wall (42 s CPU over four units) and the interpreter 4.3 s
detail: v1 gate re-check at 8f7933cf20: the entry was the one mir-llvm timeout (60 s under 4 jobs); it passes with --timeout 300. Unloaded on the 4-core container, release karac with the shared libLLVM: `karac __mir-llvm-run` 91.7 s and 517 MB peak, `karac run` 92.0 s wall / 92.1 s user, `karac build` 15.8 s wall / 42.0 s user / 1.46 GB peak, `karac __mir-run` 4.3 s; the built binary runs in 0.03 s. So the JIT path compiles the whole program as one module on one thread at roughly twice the build's total CPU, which makes `karac run` the slowest way to run a large program. KARAC_MIR_TIME on the build shows its four units at 5 to 9 s each. Measured, not profiled; whether the JIT can take the build's unit split (or its optimisation level) is the open question.
fix: 5f76094346: two causes, both in the JIT path, profiled with llc -time-passes on the IR the runner received. (1) The JIT pipeline's `cgscc(inline)` folded the app's ~100 single-call `data_file_*` functions into `data_files`, one function of 183,528 instructions; codegen on it took 67 of the runner's 67 s (machine scheduler 40 s, CodeGenPrepare 18 s), and with inlining off the whole run took 11 s. `src/backend/mir/inline_budget.rs` estimates each function's size with its single-call callees inlined and marks the largest of them `noinline` until it fits 10,000 instructions (`KARAC_MIR_JIT_INLINE_BUDGET`, 0 = off); it touches none of the 1,132 kata bench programs, so their code is unchanged. (2) The runner compiled the whole module on one thread. A program the build splits into codegen units is now compiled the same way for the JIT (`mir_aot::compile_jit_units` over `split::compile_parts`): one object per unit on its own thread, emitted for the JIT's own target machine (host CPU, JIT code model), and `karac_jit_runner` links the objects (`LLJITEngine::add_object_file`); the split's hidden cross-unit symbols resolve within the JITDylib. Small programs, a hot-swap module, KARAC_DEBUG_INFO and KARAC_MIR_LL keep the IR path. Release, 4 cores, unloaded: mini_tldextract 92 s -> 6.9 s (build 16 s), mini_pyasn1 30 s -> 8.8 s, mini_markdown 24 s -> 11.5 s (build 11.6 s + 0.3 s exec), mini_pyhcl 5.2 -> 3.1 s, mini_pandas 4.1 -> 2.4 s. corpus/apps on mir-llvm: 476/476. Pinned by tests/run_v2_jit_units.rs (karac run and __mir-llvm-run at 1 and 3 forced units, handoff files removed) and inline_budget's unit tests. The object path is measured on Linux x86-64 only; the arm64 CI job now runs the new test.

title: A block, `if` or `match` whose every value is an unsuffixed literal is typed `i64` at once, not as the literal variable design.md §8 says later uses fix -- FIXED for the operand form only (kata 2055's `prefix[i] + if b[i] == b'*' { 1 } else { 0 }` into a `Vec[i32]`); the binding form, `let x = if c { 1 } else { 0 }; take_i32(x)`, is B-2026-11-10-49
fix:
547252a43f (pushed 2026-11-10) fixes the operand form. As an operand of an arithmetic, comparison or bitwise operator, or of a compound assignment, an `if`, `match` or block whose every value is an unsuffixed literal now takes the other operand's numeric type when every literal fits it, as a literal written there does. Each literal's node is typed too, so the MIR reads the same. A literal that does not fit (`if c { 300 } else { 2 }` beside a `u8`) is refused as before. This matches design.md §8 "A join of literals is a literal" (eb38ac12ab). Kata 2055's `prefix[i] + if b[i] == b'*' { 1 } else { 0 }` into a `Vec[i32]` and kata 2087's `r += if hr > r { 1 } else { -1 }` over `r: i32` now check with no edit. Tests: `tests/kata_2087_literal_if_operand.rs`.

The binding form, `let x = if c { 1 } else { 0 }; take_i32(x)`, is NOT fixed here. It is filed as its own row, B-2026-11-10-49, which goes to Thread B together with B-2026-11-10-40 (the same root cause, for tuples). The title says so.

title: A user iterator over a `Str` field whose `next` spells its return `Option[Str]` (or `Option[(i64, Str)]`) instead of `Option[Self.Item]` passes `karac check`, then `collect()` on it is refused E0509 in `ItemValues[..].next`: "the result borrows (*_1).0, which the receiver owns"; the same impl written `-> Option[Self.Item]` runs
fix: 7087121aa9: whether a method's result is a view (it borrows what the receiver's value borrows, not the receiver; core semantics §5, "Items borrow what the receiver borrows") was read from the impl's own spelling of the return type (`view_result` in src/mir/lower.rs), where `Option[Str]` is not one and `Option[Self.Item]` is. A trait method's result is now also a view when the trait declares it one (the lowering records each impl method's trait, `method_trait`), unless the impl's signature writes a `ref`, which keeps the receiver's borrow as the rule says (tests/mir_build.rs `mir_by_ref_items_borrow_the_source_not_the_iterator`'s `Option[ref i64]` lending iterator still errors where it did). So `-> Option[Str]` and `-> Option[(i64, Str)]` with `type Item = Str` / `(i64, Str)` collect like the `Self.Item` spelling, and an item borrowing the iterator's own `String` is refused E0509 at the user's `next` in both spellings (it was accepted spelled out). `karac check` also reported MIR borrowck's E0509 under code E0516; a new `TypeErrorKind::BorrowOutlivesOwner` gives it E0509, and fixtures/mir_escaping_view INTO_SHARED and INTO_CHANNEL, which recorded the mislabel, now expect E0509. Pinned by corpus/core/ok_spelled_item_type_borrows_like_self_item and err_spelled_item_type_lends_from_receiver; the 34 corpus and kara-katas programs that implement Iterator print the same under `__mir-run` before and after.

title: An unannotated closure parameter used with an operator is refused at the operator (`let f = |x, n| x + n; f(1, 2)` -> "type '?T0' does not implement trait Add"), though design.md §8 lets a later use in the same body fix it; when nothing does, the message is not §8's "cannot infer closure parameter type"
fix: cb5f6da53e: infer_binary (src/typechecker/expr_ops.rs, defer_operator_on_open_vars) no longer judges an arithmetic, comparison or bitwise operator whose operands are both a variable nothing has typed (not a literal's): it unifies them, returns the operand type (bool for a comparison) and records the operator, which discharge_deferred_operand_vars judges at the end of `check`, before report_unsolved_call_vars. A number passes (an integer for a bitwise operator; a char or bool may be compared); another type is refused with "'+' on 'String': a closure parameter that a later use types takes an operator only as a number; annotate the parameter"; a parameter still unknown is left to the closure's own "cannot infer closure parameter type", now reported alone. `let f = |x, n| x + n; println(f(1, 2));` prints 3, and the `.to_vec()` of operator closures leads with its move-only refusal. Pinned by tests/closure_param_operator_later_use.rs (both executors, three refusals).

title: `BufReader.new(stream)` over a `TcpStream` (`BufReader.new(conn.try_clone().unwrap())`, then `.lines()`) passes check, though a `BufReader` wraps only a `File` or a child pipe: the interpreter fails "BufReader[TcpStream].new of a closed file" and a compiled build frees the socket as a file (ASan: attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed, in karac_mir_buf)
detail: Building the tcp_balancer app's backend, which reads its connection line by line the way Rust's BufReader::new(stream).lines() does. docs/library/io.md says a BufReader wraps a File or a child process pipe, and gives TcpStream only read/write, but `karac check` accepts `BufReader.new(conn.try_clone().unwrap())` and `for line in reader.lines()` with no diagnostic. Under `__mir-run` the call fails at run time with "BufReader[TcpStream].new of a closed file" (the interpreter looks the descriptor up among files). Compiled (mir-llvm, mir-build), the program crashes with "free(): invalid size" or "double free"; under mir-llvm-asan, "attempting free on address which was not malloc()-ed" inside karac_mir_buf: the runtime treats the stream handle as a File box. Repro: a listener on 127.0.0.1:0, a client that writes two lines and shuts its write side, the accepted side wrapped in BufReader and read with .lines(). Needs a ruling first: either BufReader/BufWriter over TcpStream (and TlsStream) is supported, as in Rust and Go (bufio.NewReader(conn)), which a line-based service wants, or check refuses it with a help naming the manual line split. The app splits lines itself over conn.read.
fix: FIXED by e1523f1438. Ruling (a) from the review: BufReader and BufWriter take a connected TcpStream. src/typechecker/exprs.rs E0297 accepts a TcpStream and still refuses every other source (d5307a5abd). Interpreter (src/mir/interp.rs): a socket buffer is a staged Buf::Provided over the descriptor (socket: true), read and flushed through the socket; Wait::Buffered reads what the socket holds without waiting until a read has some bytes, a line or the end, by the read timeout, so a read inside a task suspends; dropping the buffer closes the connection (Sockets::close). Compiled: runtime/src/mir_bufsock.rs (a Read/Write over the descriptor through mir_sock::drive) and karac_mir_ready_buf, built by ops 13/14 of karac_mir_buf; src/backend/mir/task.rs readies socket reads and LinesIter[TcpStream].next. LinesIter is generic over its reader, socket buffer calls carry sends/receives(Network) in MIR and front-end effects, and a TcpStream passed to a library `own` parameter moves in. Fixtures: tests/buffered_sockets.rs (echo over tasks, timeout and reset as IoError, fill_buf; interpreter and compiled at 1 and 4 threads), tests/buffered_io_sources.rs. tcp_balancer reads its backend connections through BufReader lines again (kara-katas 096de59d). Remainder (TlsStream, a Network-provider socket, generic wrappers): B-2026-11-10-28.

title: The interpreter's readiness peek for a waiting socket read swallowed a pending socket error: a reset TCP connection read as an end of stream (`Ok(0)`) and a refused connected-UDP `recv` waited out its timeout, where a compiled build reports `os error 104` / `connection refused`
detail: Found by the tcp_balancer app: a 503 closed with the client's line unread makes the kernel reset the connection. A compiled build and Python read the answer, then ECONNRESET; `karac __mir-run` read the answer, then 0 (eof). Cause: src/mir/interp.rs, the Wait::Read and Wait::Datagram readiness checks peek the socket without blocking (MSG_PEEK) and treat any error but WouldBlock as ready, but a peek that fails takes the socket's pending error (SO_ERROR) with it, so the read that follows finds nothing wrong. For TCP that read returns 0; for a connected UDP socket whose datagram came back refused (ICMP port unreachable) the recv blocks until its read timeout and reports TimedOut. Control at origin/main 08f3580ac2+: RESET prints "got 4\neof", REFUSED prints "err timed out"; compiled prints "got 4\nerr os error 104" and "err connection refused".
fix: FIXED by 1ca1f71e30. src/mir/interp.rs: `Sockets` gains `failed`, the error a suspended read's readiness peek took off its socket. The Wait::Read and Wait::Datagram checks keep a peek error other than WouldBlock there (and count the socket ready); `TcpStream.read` and `UdpSocket.recv`/`recv_from` report it before reading, and a dropped socket forgets it. A reset now reads `got 4` then `err os error 104`, and a refused connected-UDP recv `err connection refused`, as compiled builds do (control: `eof` and `err timed out`). Fixtures: tests/interp_socket_errors.rs (interp and compiled, both programs), on CI's codegen-e2e line.

title: A call through a path that starts at `std` (`std.mem.take(mut v)`, design.md's own example `std.fs.read_to_string(path)`) fails "undefined name 'std'" with no help, while `mem.take` and `fs.read_to_string` resolve
detail: Porting tcp_balancer, the Rust-shaped `std.mem.take(&mut g.value.events)` became `std.mem.take(mut ...)` after karac fix, and then failed: error[resolve]: undefined name 'std', pointing at `std`, with no help and no fix. docs/design.md line ~231 gives `std.fs.read_to_string` as its example of a module path in an expression. Either the full path resolves (as the design text says), or the diagnostic names the short form (`mem.take`, `fs.read_to_string`) as a machine-applicable fix. Repro: `fn main() { let mut v = [1, 2].to_vec(); let w = std.mem.take(mut v); println(f"{w.len()} {v.len()}"); }`.
fix: FIXED by 47514a3c77, on top of 3c5e8c8dc5 (kata 2076's thread), which named Rust's std path written with dots and deleted its module segments as the `::` form already did. Both forms stopped deleting only at a type, a primitive, `mem` or the last segment, so `std.fs.read_to_string(p)` (design.md's example) was fixed to `read_to_string(p)`, which does not resolve. src/parser.rs kara_module_call keeps a module Kāra's expressions name (fs, env, process, clock, rand, ptr, cpu, gpu, critical_section) when a function follows it, in both the dotted (rust_std_paths) and the `::` path: `fs.read_to_string(p)`, `env.args()`, `process.exit(0)`; a type after it (`std::fs::File::open`) still goes on alone. `std.mem.take(mut v)` is `mem.take(mut v)` (3c5e8c8dc5). Fixture: tests/rust_std_path_kara_modules.rs (both forms, karac fix output checks).

title: `format!` whose argument is an `if`, `match` or block expression (`format!("{}={}", n, if up { "up" } else { "down" })`) gets E0001 with no machine fix, because the f-string rewrite refuses any argument containing `{`, `}` or `:`, though an f-string hole takes those expressions
detail: Porting tcp_balancer's show_pool. src/parser.rs format_macro_rewrite (~line 1905) declines to rewrite when an argument's text contains a brace or a colon, so E0001 ("Kāra has no macros; `format!(...)` is Rust syntax") carries no fix and the author rewrites by hand. An f-string hole accepts `if`/`match`/block expressions (`f"{if up { "up" } else { "down" }}"` checks and runs), so the rewrite can allow balanced braces outside string literals; a `:` outside a string (a path or a type ascription) and a nested `format!`/f-string can stay refused (a nested f-string is deprecated, design.md §3).
fix: 3be914cd0e. src/parser.rs format_arg_fits_hole replaces the blanket refusal of any argument containing `{`, `}` or `:`: braces are allowed when balanced outside literals, so an `if`, `match` or block argument goes into the hole; a `:` or backslash outside a literal, a literal holding a brace, colon or escape, a nested f-string or macro, a comment and a line break still keep the call unrewritten. A block argument is written in parentheses (`{({ let k = n * 2; k + 1 })}`), since its opening brace after the hole's would read as an escaped `{{`. A format spec after the argument works (`f"{if up { n } else { 0 }:>5}"`). Pinned by tests/format_macro_block_args.rs.

title: An immediately invoked closure whose body ends in `collect()` (`let s: Set[i64] = (|v: ref Vec[i64]| v.iter().map(|x| x + 1).collect())(a);`) reports "an expression whose type does not lower (Type(UnknownParam(\"C\"))) is not lowered yet" under typecheck; the same closure bound by a `let` and called builds the `Set` (remainder of B-2026-11-09-40)
detail: Repro: `fn main() { let a = Vec[1, 2, 2]; let s: Set[i64] = (|v: ref Vec[i64]| v.iter().map(|x| x + 1).collect())(a); println(f"{s.len()}"); }`. At 86c3102afc `karac check` reports the UnknownParam("C") error at 3:24 and `__mir-run` fails at build with the same. `let f = |v: ref Vec[i64]| ...collect(); let s: Set[i64] = f(a);` prints 2. B-2026-11-09-40's fix opens the closure body's tail call's `C` only from open_unsolved_let_params, which runs for a `let` binding a closure; a closure literal in callee position never reaches it, so the tail `collect`'s type argument stays the bare parameter. Expected: the call's expected type decides the closure's result and the tail `collect` builds it, as for the let-bound closure.
fix: 3be914cd0e. src/typechecker/items.rs open_called_closure_result, called from infer_call (src/typechecker/expr_call.rs) when the callee is a closure literal: each parameter its result leaves unbound becomes a fresh variable the call's context solves, the closure body's tail call takes it (open_closure_tail_params, as for a let-bound closure), the callee node records the opened type, and the variables are judged with the other open lets, so `let u = (|v| ...collect())(a);` with nothing deciding it is "cannot infer type parameter 'C'" rather than a lowering error. `let s: Set[i64] = (...)(a)` and `take((...)(a))` with `take(v: Vec[i32])` build and run. Pinned by tests/collect_target_decided_later.rs a_closure_called_where_it_is_written_builds_what_the_call_decides.

title: `unused_mut` misses a `let mut` binding of a `mut ref` handle that is only passed as `mut child`: the call-site marker counts as a write to the binding, though the write lands in the referent and the binding needs no `mut`
detail: Found by scripts/mend/rustism_audit.py --only let_mut (19/20 after unused_mut, B-2026-11-09-99). corpus/katas/501-600/588-design-in-memory-file-system/file_system_owned/source.kara line 29: `let child = node.children.entry(names[0].to_string()).or_insert(new_node()); make(mut child, names[1..], content);` checks clean as written, so `let mut child` is never needed, yet with it the lint is silent. src/ownership.rs report_mut_marked_arg_write calls mark_mut_let_written(root) for every marked argument, and report_write_to_immutable_binding marks before its binding_is_reference_handle exemption, so a write through a reference handle (`*r = v`, `r += 1`, a field store, a `mut` marker) uses the `mut` though the error path itself exempts it. Expected: only a write that rebinds the handle (`r = other`) uses the `mut` of a reference-handle binding; check that the warning's fix then compiles before landing.
fix: 3be914cd0e. src/ownership.rs mark_mut_let_written_through: a write rooted at a binding that is not a rebind uses its `let mut` unless it lands in a referent. A sub-place write (field store, index, a method on a field) through any reference handle (`mut ref T`, `shared`, raw pointer, `mut Slice`) lands elsewhere; a lend of the whole binding (`f(mut x)`, a `mut ref self` method on `x`, an unmarked `mut ref` argument) lands elsewhere only for a `mut ref` of a non-Copy type or a `mut Slice`, which forward their borrow, while a `shared` value lent whole can be rebound by the callee (`*t = n`, kata 897's relink) and keeps its `mut`. A `let mut` initialized from a `ref T` or a `mut ref` of a Copy `T` copies the value (core-semantics.md §1.1), so its writes are its own and keep the `mut` (dropping it would turn `let mut r = m.entry(k).or_insert(0); bump(mut r)` into a write to the map). A whole rebind (`x = e`) always uses it. Corpus sweep with a release build before the whole-lend rule (which only removes warnings): 360 warnings over 245 programs, and every `karac fix` result checks clean and prints the expected output. The rustism audit's `let mut` row is 20/20. The sweep also showed an immutable `shared` binding lent as `mut` is accepted though the callee rebinds it: filed as its own row. Pinned by tests/unused_mut_reference_handle.rs.

title: `s.extend(v.iter())` on a `String`, with `v` a `Vec[char]` (an iterator lending `ref char`), is refused as ambiguous between `Extend[char]` and `Extend[String]` and told to use UFCS, where a `Vec`'s `extend` takes the same lent items
detail:
FOUND writing kata 1092's Hirschberg arm (kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1092-shortest-common-supersequence/shortest_common_supersequence_halves.kara): `out.extend(x[i..].iter())`, `out` a `String` and `x` a `Vec[char]`, adds what a word has left. `karac check` reports the call ambiguous between the two `Extend` impls a `String` has (`Extend[char]` and `Extend[String]`) and names UFCS; `karac fix` has nothing to apply.

CAUSE: the user-impl dispatch in `src/typechecker/method_user_impl.rs` keeps the impls whose item type fits the iterator's item, and `ref char` is neither `char` nor `String` exactly, so both impls stayed candidates (the `fits` filter fell through on the borrow) and the call was ambiguous. A `Vec[T]`'s `extend` reads a lent `Copy` item out through `iter_read_value`; a `String`'s had no such path.
fix: e609854dde: the user-impl dispatch's `fits` filter in src/typechecker/method_user_impl.rs also tries the item read through its borrow (`peel_borrow`), and `s.extend(it)` on a `String` whose iterator lends `char`s is claimed in src/typechecker/expr_method_call.rs by the new `extends_by_lent_chars` (src/typechecker/method_vec_mutation.rs), which infers the argument and keeps its errors only when the item is `ref char`. The MIR builder lowers that call (`string_extend_lent_chars` in src/mir/lower.rs, in the no-callee branch) through the library's new `string_extend_iter` (runtime/stdlib/source/collections.kara, on the compiler's keep list), which reads each item out with `iter_read_value` and pushes it, as a `Vec`'s `extend` reads a lent `Copy` item. An iterator lending `String`s is still refused and told to use `.cloned()`, as a `Vec`'s would be. Pinned by tests/kata_1092_string_extend_lent_chars.rs (`extend` by `v.iter()`, a slice's `iter()`, `chars()`, an owned `Vec[String]` and `iter().rev()` print `abcbcxyPQcba` on __mir-run and __mir-llvm-run; lent `String`s get the `.cloned()` message, not "ambiguous"). Before the fix `karac check` refused kata 1092's Hirschberg arm as ambiguous; the arm now runs as written.

title: LeetCode's Rust template `impl Solution { pub fn f(..) }` with no `struct Solution;` (the site supplies it) gets only "undefined type 'Solution'", and `karac fix` has nothing to apply
detail:
FOUND writing kata 1092's solution arm (kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1092-shortest-common-supersequence/shortest_common_supersequence_solution.kara), LeetCode's Rust template carried to Kāra by `karac fix`. The template for this problem is `impl Solution { pub fn shortest_common_supersequence(str1: String, str2: String) -> String { .. } }` with no `struct Solution;`. `karac check` reports E0104 `undefined type 'Solution'` at the impl and E0100 at the call, and `karac fix` says `no fixable diagnostics`, so the Mend loop stops at a declaration any reader can supply.

CAUSE: `resolve_impl_block_scoped` (src/resolver/resolve_items.rs) resolves the impl's target as any type expression; an undefined one gets the plain UndefinedType error with no replacement.
fix: e609854dde: `resolve_impl_block_scoped` (src/resolver/resolve_items.rs) hands the target's resolution errors to the new `declare_missing_impl_target`: for an inherent, non-generic impl whose single-segment target nothing declares and none of whose functions takes `self` (the type is only a namespace), the UndefinedType error says so and carries a fix that writes `struct Solution {}` and a blank line above the impl. An impl with a `self` method, which would need fields the fix cannot know, keeps the plain error. Pinned by tests/kata_1092_impl_solution_template.rs (the namespace impl is refused naming `struct Solution {}`, `karac fix` declares it above the impl, the result checks and prints 42; an impl with a `self` method is left untouched). Before the fix `karac fix` said `no fixable diagnostics`. Kata 1092's solution arm reaches a clean check in four rounds of `karac fix` from LeetCode's template, the second declaring the struct.

title: An immutable `let` of a `shared` value can be lent as `mut` and rebound by the callee: `let tail = T { v: 1 }; advance(mut tail);` with `fn advance(t: mut ref T) { *t = n; }` checks clean and leaves `tail` naming a different object, though `let` froze the handle
fix: e705e5be7e: report_mut_marked_arg_write (src/ownership.rs) refuses a `mut` marker on a bare binding that holds a `shared` value (or any reference handle) when the binding is a plain `let`, with the `let mut` fix, since the marker lends the binding itself and the callee's `*t = n` rebinds it (design.md § Call-site `mut` markers). A forwarded `mut ref` / `mut Slice` binding stays exempt (it lends the referent), and a marker on a field or element still writes through the handle (`bump(mut t.v)` with `let t` checks). Corpus sweep: one program newly refused, corpus/fixtures/codegen/concurrency/e2e_ref_atomic_param_aliases_caller_cell, migrated to `let mut c`; kata 897 already wrote `let mut tail`. Pinned by tests/method_mut_marker.rs a_shared_let_lent_as_mut_is_refused_and_fixed_with_let_mut and a_field_of_a_shared_let_lent_as_mut_still_needs_no_let_mut.

title: `while let Some(x) = it.find(|x| ..)` (or `next_if`) over `v.iter()` is refused E0516: the closure passed by reference is taken to be stored into the `mut ref` iterator (§9.5), whose type cannot hold it, so the next iteration's closure conflicts
fix: 1b5fe88816: transfer_call (src/mir/borrowck.rs) still lets a callee given a whole-local `mut ref` store the other arguments' borrows into its pointee (§9.5), but a pointee whose type has no place for a closure (may_hold_closure: no closure, erased function, `dyn`, opaque, `shared`/`weak` or `TaskGroup` part, through refs, containers and fields) now takes from a `ref closure` argument only what the closure holds (held_behind, as the erased-Fn slot already did), not the loan on the closure local. `while let Some(x) = it.find(|x| x < 5)` over `v.iter()` prints 6; a `find` in a `for` body and `Peekable.next_if` in a `while let` run too. Still refused: a pointee that can hold the closure (`Vec[ref F]`), and a closure handing back a captured `ref n` that the callee pushes into a closure-free `Vec[ref i64]` (the captured loan still lands). Pinned by tests/mir_closure_into_iterator_slot.rs (both executors, both refusals).

title: The char-pattern fix-it's `c.to_string()` allocates a String on every call: kata 2062's `"aeiou".contains(c.to_string())` vowel test makes its compiled bench 2.4x slower than the same program with a `match` (0.95 s against 0.40 s), and 2.2x Rust's `"aeiou".contains(c)`; kata 2063's bench, with the same test, is 5.8x slower
detail:
B-2026-10-20-22 settled that every string pattern parameter is `pat: Str`, and `char_pattern_for_str` (src/typechecker/exprs.rs) refuses a char with the machine-applicable edit `c.to_string()` for a char variable. That reads well, but the edit puts a heap allocation (and its free) wherever the test sits, and the usual place is the inner loop of a character-class test. Kata 2062 (Count Vowel Substrings) wrote its ★ arm's test as Rust writes it, `fn is_vowel(c: char) -> bool { "aeiou".contains(c) }`, and took the fix: `"aeiou".contains(c.to_string())`.

Measured with a release karac at 1fa08b17ca plus the slice fix-it 0556eab231, `KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0 karac build`, the bench in kara-katas leetcode/2001-2100/2062-count-vowel-substrings-of-a-string/bench (20000 words of 100 letters, an O(n^2) scan per word, one `is_vowel` call per letter visited), three interleaved runs each on a 4-core container: 0.913 / 0.995 / 0.977 s as fixed, 0.385 / 0.402 / 0.448 s with the body replaced by `match c { 'a' | 'e' | 'i' | 'o' | 'u' => true, _ => false }`. Rust `rustc -O -C overflow-checks=on` with `"aeiou".contains(c)` takes 0.43 s, C 0.14 s. Everything else in the two Kāra programs is the same. Kata 2063 (Vowels of All Substrings) uses the same test in its ★ arm, written straight in the fixed form, `if "aeiou".contains(c.to_string())` once per letter of an O(n) sum; its bench (200 windows of 100000 letters) takes 0.811 / 0.878 / 0.814 s as fixed and 0.140 / 0.139 / 0.140 s with the `match`, 5.8x, where Rust takes 0.165 s.

What would remove it, any of: a char's `to_string()` that does not allocate when the result is only borrowed by a `Str` parameter (the String is a temporary that dies at the end of the call); a `Str` view of a char's UTF-8 bytes the fix-it could write instead (`c.encode_utf8(buf)` in Rust); or a fix-it that writes a non-allocating form for a `contains` on a string literal receiver (a `match` on the literal's chars, or `"aeiou".chars().any(|v| v == c)`). The kata keeps the fixed form, as the Mend loop produced it.
fix:
380b5381f1. This follows the review ruling: a codegen remedy, with no change to the spec or the fix-it. A String local that a char's `to_string()` fills and that is only lent (every other mention is a shared borrow of the whole local, its drop, or a storage marker; never the result or an argument) gets the char's UTF-8 bytes in a 4-byte slot of the frame, with no capacity. Its drop frees nothing, and a write would copy it to the heap first. The analysis is src/mir/char_strs.rs, and the codegen is `char_string_in` in src/backend/mir/call.rs. The result's lifetime stays a temporary: a moved, returned or pushed to_string() still allocates, and coroutine resume bodies keep the heap because their locals can outlive a poll. KARAC_MIR_CHAR_STR=0 turns it off.

Benches (kara-katas bench/vowels.kara, KARAC_AUTO_PAR=0, 5 interleaved runs, 4-core container):
- 2062: 0.70-0.84 s allocating, now 0.34-0.42 s; the `match` form takes 0.26-0.40 s.
- 2063: 0.61-0.79 s, now 0.16-0.24 s; the `match` form takes 0.10-0.14 s. What remains of 2063's gap is the String.contains call itself.
Outputs are identical.

Pinned by tests/mir_char_str.rs: chars of one to four bytes against the interpreter, plus IR checks for the slot in three lent cases and for the heap in a returned one. Corpus on mir-llvm over the 116 entries that lend a to_string(): 115 pass. The one failure is 824 goat_latin bench's stale error:codegen expectation, which fails the same with the feature off. Gate: test --all 11117/0, llvm 11323/0.

title: A closure with no declared return type that returns a non-`i64` integer (`return i as i32;`) and has an unsuffixed literal tail or `return` (`0`) is refused: "closure returns conflicting types: 'i64' vs 'i32'"; `karac fix` produces this shape when it deletes Rust's `|..| -> i32`
detail: FOUND writing kata 1093's solution arm (kara-katas leetcode/1001-1100/1093-statistics-from-a-large-sample/sample_stats_solution.kara), LeetCode's Rust template carried to Kāra by `karac fix`. The Rust closure `let find = |k: i64| -> i32 { for (i, c) in count.iter().enumerate() { acc += c as i64; if acc > k { return i as i32; } } 0 };` loses its `-> i32` to the fix (a closure does not declare its return type), and the fixed program is then refused at the closure: "closure returns conflicting types: 'i64' vs 'i32'". The closure's return type is the unification of its tail with every `return`; an unsuffixed literal with no expected type is typed `i64` before the unification sees the other returns, so `0` beside `i as i32` conflicts, where a `fn` with a declared `i32` (or a `let x: i32 = if c { y } else { 0 }`) takes the literal at `i32`. Reproduces with the tail as the literal (`return k as i32; 0`) and with a `return` as the literal (`return 7 + 1;` beside a `k as u16 * 2` tail). The fix's output being refused by the checker is the worst shape a machine-applicable fix can have: the Rust arm cannot reach a clean check by fix rounds alone.
fix: 900693f6bb. A closure with no declared return type now types an unsuffixed integer literal returned or left as its tail after its other returns: the `return E` whose E is an integer literal tree is recorded by its index (`literal_returns` on `ClosureReturnFrame`, src/typechecker.rs), and the closure's return unification (src/typechecker/exprs.rs, the new `fold_closure_return` helper holding the old merge/conflict logic) folds the non-literal returns first; when they agree on an integer type other than i64, the literal returns and a literal tail are promoted to it (`promote_int_literal_operator_tree`, with the tail's block type recorded), and otherwise the literals fold in as before (all literals still default to i64). An out-of-range literal is still refused ("integer literal 300 out of range for 'u8'"), and a literal beside a non-integer return still conflicts. Kata 1093's Rust arm now reaches a clean check in three rounds of karac fix and matches the Python mirror on every lane. Pinned by tests/kata_1093_closure_literal_return.rs (literal tail with an i32 return, literal return with a u16/i8 tail, all-literal still i64, range refusal, String-vs-literal conflict, and the fix round trip from `|t: i64| -> i32`); the control compiler refuses the first, second and last.

title: `BufReader`/`BufWriter` over a `TlsStream` is refused at check (E0297, "not built yet"), and over a socket a `Network` provider opened stops at the constructor; remainder of B-2026-11-10-14, whose fix buffers a plain `TcpStream`
detail: B-2026-11-10-14's ruling (review, docs/library/io.md § Buffered I/O) is that the buffered wrappers take a connected TcpStream or TlsStream. e1523f1438 built the TcpStream half on the interpreter (Buf::Provided with socket: true, Wait::Buffered) and the compiled backend (runtime/src/mir_bufsock.rs, karac_mir_ready_buf, ops 13/14 of karac_mir_buf). Left: (1) a TlsStream: src/typechecker/exprs.rs still refuses it with E0297 citing -14; it needs a Read/Write over the TLS connection on both backends, with the same task suspension (a TLS read may need bytes the socket has not delivered yet, and a pending TLS record is not visible to a readiness peek). (2) A TcpStream a `Network` provider opened (core semantics §14.11): the interpreter returns an error at the constructor and a compiled build prints "a buffer over a socket a `Network` provider opened is not built yet (B-2026-11-10-14)" and exits 101 (runtime/src/mir_io.rs). (3) A generic wrapper (`fn wrap[R](r: own R) { BufReader.new(r) }`) is not judged by E0297, which looks at the resolved argument type at the call. Repro for (1): `import std.io.{BufReader}; fn f(s: own TlsStream) { let r = BufReader.new(s); }` fails check E0297 "buffering a `TlsStream` is not built yet". Thread C (I/O, HTTPS client) takes this row.
fix: 23ce3eab43. BufReader and BufWriter wrap a TlsStream on both backends: the runtime reads through mir_tls::TlsRead (pending bytes, then the connection under the stream's read timeout) and suspends inside a task through mir_bufsock's ready hook, which drives the handshake (mir_tls::buffered_ready); the interpreter reads and flushes through the TLS connection and Wait::Buffered asks it whether a line is ready. A TLS failure is IoError Other("TLS: <failure>"). Over a Network provider's socket the buffer calls the fake's read_stream/write_stream (runtime net_provider::ProvidedSocket; interp provided_socket_read/flush), its drop calls close, and a NetError maps to the matching IoError (ProviderUnavailable, Unsupported, TimedOut as Other("timed out")). A generic wrapper's parameter is judged at each instantiating call through generic callers (typechecker emit_buf_instance_errors), refused there with E0297. Tests: tests/buffered_tls.rs (two tasks, handshake waiting, BufWriter, timeout, unexpected close, plain peer; interp == compiled), tests/buffered_provider_socket.rs (both backends), tests/buffered_io_sources.rs (TlsStream accepted; generic wrapper refused at line 12).

title: `karac build` was ~21% slower than at f1416771a4 on the ADR-2 frozen set (0.886x legacy, was 0.734x): the in-order program was lowered after the auto-par builds instead of beside them and a method's modes were looked up by scanning every method; now 0.851x. The library growth behind typecheck, ownership and parse is B-2026-11-10-38
detail:
MEASURED 2026-11-10 at 7b70e3b10f (x86 cloud box, 4 cores) with review/adr2-dual/run-head.py against legacy-archive 741fbf08c1 `karac build --legacy` (LLVM 18), min of 3 interleaved runs, default auto-par, fresh release build: 583 of the 585 frozen benches (76 minimum_window_substring and 316 remove_duplicate_letters now refused by legacy after kata edits). Build time geomean 0.886x legacy (11-02 at f1416771a4: 0.734x), max 1.507x (3629 bfs_sieve, was 1.318x; 0.498 -> 0.569 s), stripped size 0.309x (was 0.376x), peak RSS 1.046x (was 1.115x). ADR-2 bars (1.5x / none over 2x / 1.25x) hold. Against the 11-02 file on the same benches the tip arm's build time is 1.296x and the legacy arm's 1.074x, so about 1.21x after the box's own drift. Result: review/adr2-dual/frozen-head-7b70e3b10f.json in the shared folder.

KARAC_MIR_TIME=1, kata 233 digit_one build thread (ms), against B-2026-10-31-41's split at f1416771a4: parse 13 -> 20, prepare 17 -> 11-17, typecheck 63 -> 69-90, ownership 12 -> 19-30, opt 13 -> 8 + 36 and emit 9 -> 6 + 17 across two modules (the in-order `.seq` module and the main one), link 99 -> 90. defs+node_res / typed_hir / mir_builder / finish_build run three times (2, 3 and 2 bodies) before compile_mir. An edit-compile loop pays all of it; no bar excuses it.
fix: 2991314acf. A build with auto-par on lowered its program two or three times in a row (recording, parallel, in-order); the in-order lowering now runs on its own thread beside the other two (src/mir/lower.rs build_renamed_source, InOrderBuilt), and ProgramDefs + node resolutions are built once per program (Frontend::defs_res). The ownership check and the use classifier looked a method's parameter modes up by scanning every Type.method key per argument; they now read an index by name (ownership::method_keys_by_name). Pre-optimisation IR, both modules, byte-identical on all 585 frozen benches against 7b70e3b10f; build time 0.963x and a further 0.984x. ADR-2 at 2991314acf (run-head.py, legacy 741fbf08c1, min of 3): 0.851x legacy (was 0.886x), max 1.392x (was 1.507x), size 0.309x; review/adr2-dual/frozen-head-2991314acf.json. The library growth behind typecheck/ownership/parse is B-2026-11-10-38.

title: Tracker for the next minor release: an unmarked argument at a method's `mut ref` parameter becomes a compile error; in 0.8.x it is a `deprecated` warning with a `karac fix` that inserts `mut ` (e705e5be7e, design.md § Call-site `mut` markers)
detail: Split from B-2026-11-09-100 under the review thread's ruling (2026-11-10): design.md § Call-site `mut` markers is the rule, and in 0.8.x an unmarked fresh-binding argument at a method's `mut ref` parameter warns rather than errs. e705e5be7e: ownership's MethodCall arm records each unmarked argument whose method resolves to its own signature (`resolved_method_mode_key` -> `method_param_modes` says `MutRef`) in `OwnershipCheckResult::unmarked_method_mut_args`; src/cli.rs `report_unmarked_method_mut_args` reports it as `deprecated` with a machine-applicable fix inserting `mut ` at the argument, for user code only, and only once the program has no errors (an error's own fix, e.g. a trait's `ref` replacing an impl's `mut ref`, can change the parameter). Exempt, as for a free function's strict check: an argument that forwards a `mut ref` or `mut Slice` (by its type or its root binding's); a range index (`v[0..2]`) is not exempt, since its `mut Slice` is made at the call. `#[allow(deprecated)]` or `expect` on the function or its impl silences it. NOT covered, as ruled: the 606 corpus calls resolved only by method name (no precise signature), which keep today's behaviour; and library sources (runtime/stdlib), which are not reported. Migrated in e705e5be7e with `karac fix`, outputs unchanged: 40 corpus programs, their 16 kara-katas app originals, the programs in tests/mir_io.rs, mir_collections.rs and mir_serde.rs, selfhost/src/parser.kara, two doc lines, and the desugared hash-byte wrapper (`k.hash(mut s)`). At the next minor: turn the warning into an ownership error (E-code with the same fix), decide whether the name-only calls join it, and flip tests/method_mut_marker.rs `an_unmarked_method_mut_ref_argument_is_deprecated_and_fixed` and `allow_deprecated_silences_the_unmarked_method_argument`. title: LLVM 22 keeps hsearch's (275) bounds check on `citations[mid]` in a binary search: instcombine rewrites karac's `assume(mid >= lo)` into `assume(hi - lo > -2)`, so IPSCCP no longer folds the check; costs nothing measurable on Emerald Rapids at HEAD, Cascade Lake not re-measured
detail: MEASURED 2026-11-10 at 787f0559a5 on a 4-core x86 cloud container (Intel family 6 model 207, Emerald Rapids), best of 11: hsearch 277 to 323 ms against the last LLVM 18 karac's (c420c96612) 316 to 359. HEAD's inlined `h_index_prefix` loop branches on the comparison (jge) and still tests `mid` against the array (`cmp $0x3ffff; ja` to the abort), which LLVM 18 folded: B-2026-11-05-27's attribution stands, LLVM 22 puts nsw on `lo + (hi - lo) / 2` and instcombine then turns `assume(mid >= lo)` into `assume(hi - lo > -2)`, which says nothing about `mid`, so IPSCCP cannot derive mid in [0, 262143]. Freezing mid, or adding assume(lo >= 0) or assume(mid >= 0), did not fold it on 11-05. On this host the check is a predicted branch and costs nothing measurable. On 11-05 the same source on a Cascade Lake host (2.80GHz, model 85) ran 2x LLVM 18, but then the loop held two cmovs that the check kept from becoming a branch; HEAD has none, so that cost may be gone there too. Next: re-measure on a Cascade Lake host; if it still loses, give the midpoint a fact instcombine cannot weaken (an assume on `mid < hi` emitted after the nsw add, or the bound as range metadata).
fix: 5a072c1314 gives LLVM a fact about a binary search's bounds that its passes keep. `mir::monotone` now counts `hi = mid` (down) and `lo = mid` or `lo = mid + c` (up) as one-way steps when `mid` is a midpoint of this loop's `lo < hi` guard (`mir::midpoint`), written only there and before the step. `assume_midpoint` (src/backend/mir/mod.rs) then also states `lo0 <= mid < hi0` against the counters' values on loop entry. The row's attribution held at HEAD. The midpoint's `assume(mid >= lo)` became `(hi - lo) >> 1 > -1`. A header fact `hi <= hi0` folded the check under plain `default<O2>` but not in karac's pipeline: early argpromotion (KARAC_MIR_EARLY_PROMOTE) left the check standing. The direct `mid < hi0` survives both. MEASURED 2026-11-10 on the Emerald Rapids container (model 207): kata 275 hsearch went from 1,513,796,057 to 1,320,453,489 instructions (callgrind), against 1,625,467,107 for the last LLVM 18 karac (c420c96612). Its loop keeps no bounds check; wall time is within noise on this host. Over the 707 frozen-set programs (KARAC_MIR_MIDPOINT_MONO=0 against the default, min of 5, the 16 that differ re-timed at 15), 691 build byte-identical and 16 differ, all with equal output. Instructions: search_range (34) 0.86x, blackpixels (302) 0.84x, summary_ranges (352) 0.98x, kth_smallest (668) 1.00x, map_sum_pairs (677) 1.02x. Wall time ran from 0.82x (34) to 1.23x (677, 1.10x in the first pass) on a host where the identical hsearch binary varied by 15%. 302 read 1.14x in wall time with 16% fewer instructions, between 400 and 478 ms across reruns. Cascade Lake was not re-measured. Pinned by tests/mir_midpoint_entry_bounds.rs: a prefix h-index search and a search whose `lo` moves by `lo = mid; lo = lo + 1` must print a Python mirror's output on both backends, and both `v[mid]` checks fold in the built main only with the facts (two remain at KARAC_MIR_MIDPOINT_MONO=0). A search whose `hi` starts past the end still stops at the check.

title: A program that names no library method still kept and checked Iterator's min/max/sum/count/last/find/collect/cloned/take/enumerate and ExactSizeIterator's is_empty defaults in every kept iterator impl: ALWAYS_KEPT reached them though the compiler only answers those names at a spelled call (the drift since 11-02, measured as 378 -> 510 kept library methods)
detail:
Remainder of B-2026-11-10-29. MEASURED 2026-11-10 at 2991314acf against f1416771a4 (both release, x86 cloud box). `fn main() { println("hi") }` keeps 378 -> 510 library methods (KARAC_MIR_PRUNE_DEBUG=1, both threads' prunes counted) and executes 603M -> 893M instructions (callgrind, whole build): TypeChecker::check 238M -> 324M (check_impl_block_inner 120M -> 199M, the kept library bodies), OwnershipChecker::check 73M -> 128M, Parser::parse 68M -> 91M, lower_typed_parts 47M -> 119M (two lowerings now, each of more bodies). runtime/stdlib/source grew 8240 -> 10213 lines (collections.kara +937, iter.kara +300, priority_queue.kara +309, serde.kara +267, range.kara +171). Over 30 frozen benches the build thread's typecheck is +22 ms a build, ownership +9, parse +7 (KARAC_MIR_TIME=1, min of 3).

What an empty program keeps beyond what it names: every impl of a library trait method without a default body (`RangeStep` for 12 integer types x 4 methods), the free functions that take no library type (`repeat`, `once`, `successors` and their iterator impls), and through them the names their bodies use (`String`/`StringSlice` `split`, `lines`, `trim`, `strip_prefix`, ... kept for a program with no strings). The levers named in B-2026-10-31-41 stand: prune by type-directed reachability rather than by word, or typecheck only the library bodies the MIR builder reaches.
fix: 5244494204. src/mir/library_prune.rs: `ANSWERED_WHEN_SPELLED` names the eleven ALWAYS_KEPT names the compiler answers only at a call the program or a kept library body spells (min max sum count last find collect cloned take enumerate is_empty). They are held out of the `reached` seed. A library trait's default of one of those names (`Method.trait_default`: the trait's body or an impl's definition of it) is kept only when the name is spelled; every other method of those names (Vec.last, i64.max) stays always kept, and free functions keep it too. Before, each default was kept for every program and desugar copied it into about 26 kept iterator impls, each copy typechecked, ownership-checked and lowered on both the check and build threads. Thread A checked the Vec.from_iter -> collect rewrite: the MIR path does not take it (lowering.rs `lower_program` is not called there, and expr_call.rs's synthetic collect is gated on !library_methods_from_source). tests/library_prune_answered.rs pins that program (`3 6`) and inherent methods of answered names; unit tests an_answered_name_keeps_a_trait_default_only_when_spelled and answered_names_are_always_kept_names. MEASURED over the 585 frozen benches against 2991314acf (min of 3, interleaved): build time geomean 0.881x (median 0.883, p90 0.941), exit codes identical; pre-optimisation IR (KARAC_MIR_LL, .ll and .seq.ll) byte-identical on 573, and the other 12 (katas 56, 252, 253, 354, 435, 436, 452, 675, 757, 761, 973, 1665, all sort_by users) identical once `closure#\d+` is normalised: fewer bodies lowered renumber the library's sort_by closure (#1818 -> #1686).
